master.one_liner: ModalCells' Chladni modes played on PolyGauge's polygon cells: every Voronoi cell is a drumhead whose radial coordinate is the gauge g (0 at the site, 1 on every wall), so all modes vanish on the walls and the art-deco tiling loses its square grid.
master.look: A tessellation of irregular polygons, each engraved with its own Chladni figure: nested shrunken copies of the polygon, spokes from the site, lobed quatrefoils and sixfoils, with every figure dying exactly on its walls. Reads as an engraved mosaic, hammered metal tiles, Islamic rosettes on a crazy-paving layout, or cymatics plates. Emboss output in relief is a floor of embossed coins of different shapes. Rings-only is PolyGauge's rings with a smooth cosine profile. Twist turns spokes into pinwheels. Good for ornament, ceramics, stylised cell biology, sci-fi panelling.
master.algorithm: Pass 1 and 2 exactly as t_poly_gauge: F1 site p (hash h) over the 3^D window, then g = max_j 2*dot(x-p, q_j-p)/|q_j-p|^2 over the window sites, remembering the active neighbour j* (its e = q_j*-p gives grad g = 2e/|e|^2, piecewise constant). Angular coordinate without atan2: u = (x-p)/max(|x-p|,1e-6); Chebyshev recursion c1=u.x, s1=u.y, c_{k+1} = c_k*u.x - s_k*u.y, s_{k+1} = s_k*u.x + c_k*u.y for a fixed kmax (default 6). Per cell, Modes (default 2) hashed from h: radial order m in [1,Mmax], angular order k in [0,Kmax], phase phi, amplitude a_i = 0.6^i. Mode value: k == 0: R = cos(pi*(m-0.5)*g) (1 at the site, 0 at g=1, m-1 nodal polygons inside); k >= 1: R = sin(pi*m*g)*(cos(k*theta + phi)) with cos(k*theta+phi) = c_k*cos(phi) - s_k*sin(phi) (0 at the site and at the walls). Optional Twist tau: theta -> theta + tau*g, done by rotating (c_k,s_k) by k*tau*g with one sin/cos. f = sum a_i*mode_i / sum a_i, clamp g to 1 before use (g can exceed 1 by the window seam PolyGauge already has). Gradient for the nodal-line output: df = (df/dg)*grad g + (df/dtheta)*grad theta, grad theta = perp(u)/|x-p|, df/dg and df/dtheta are the obvious derivatives of the two factors. Outputs: Field f; NodalLines 1 - 2*min(1, |f|/(|df|*LineWidth)); Emboss |f| (raised figures on flat tiles); Rings (force k=0). Hybrid Max Mode is read once at the site p (not at the sample) so a cell keeps one mode set and C0 holds, as ModalCells does. 3D: g from the 3D PolyGauge; angular part about a hashed axis a: u' = u - a*dot(u,a) normalised, theta is the azimuth around a from a hashed perpendicular basis, same recursion; modes are zonal cos(k*theta) only. 4D: same with the 4D gauge (3^4 window).
master.why_new: ModalCells (keeper) is locked to square tiles and the grid is the first thing you see; PolyGauge (keeper) has rings and kites but no angular structure and no modal figures. Neither can be fed into the other through a graph because the mode needs the gauge as its radial coordinate and the site direction as its angular coordinate inside one evaluation. Nearest nodes: ModalCells, PolyGauge Rings/Kites, CellularEdge, ChiralWallpaper (periodic). None gives per-irregular-cell nodal figures.
master.simd_plan: PolyGauge's two passes over the 3^D window (masks and Select for the max, no branches), then two FS::Sin/Cos for the radial part and one for the phase, a fixed kmax=6 Chebyshev loop of 4 FMAs each, a fixed Modes loop. No extra window. Estimated AVX2: 2D 7-10 ns, 3D 25-35 ns, 4D 90-120 ns (PolyGauge pass cost plus about 2 ns of trig). The hex preset (CellularHexLattice's A2* sites at jitter 0) gives regular hexagonal drums for the same cost.
master.continuity: C0: every mode vanishes on g=1 and g is continuous (max of continuous ratios), the k>=1 modes also vanish at the site where theta is undefined; the facet creases of g show as kinks in the nodal polygons, which is the intended look. Same window seam risk as PolyGauge at win=1 (its sheet measured c0 8.0).
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Max Mode (hybrid int-ish float, read at the site), Modes (int 1..3), Max Angular (int 0..6), Twist (float), Line Width, Output enum {Field, NodalLines, Emboss, Rings}, Output Min/Max. Phase (hybrid, read at the site) scales each mode by cos(omega_mk*Phase) for standing-wave animation with omega hashed.
master.risks: The creases of the gauge make every nodal ring a polygon with corners, which may read as faceted rather than engraved; a Softness that blends g with the Euclidean distance normalised by the wall distance would round them at the cost of exact wall zeros. The 4D form is expensive. Angular modes about a hashed axis in 3D are weaker than 2D figures.

voronoi-drum.changed_from_entry: (1) Added a window exit weight to the gauge: term_j = g_j * min( max( fade(|x-q_j|^2), box_j ) / fade(F1^2), 1 ), box_j being 0 only when q_j's cell is leaving the 3^D window. It removes PolyGauge's window jump while keeping g exactly 1 on walls; the first try with Euclidean fade alone gave flat g=0 patches in big cells, so box was added. (2) 3D angular part uses u.b1 + i u.b2 with u not projected, a sectoral harmonic that vanishes on the axis; the entry's normalised azimuth would jump along the axis line. (3) Hash pick steers k away from 1 (kq=2), since k=1 reads as a bisected disc rather than a figure. (4) Default output is NodalLines, default jit 0.8, not 0.9, as the slope is worse at 0.9 (about 190-250 per unit against 120).

jigsaw-gauge.port_notes: Store the window sites, top 3 by Select with d^2 capped at the reach, then 2 masked passes over the window, each with a pair hash and two wave evals per neighbour. Replace sin by the parabolic wave t*(8-16|t|). Pair hash per pair per pass is a large part of the cost: pass two can reuse nothing since owner changes, unless the owner F1 pass is shared with j == F2. Skipping any far j by mask is impossible, so all pairs cost. The canonical sign uses hash order, which is one integer compare and Select per pair.

master.one_liner: PolyGauge whose walls are BentWalls: each bisector in the gauge gets the pair-hashed wobble, so the cell gauge is 0 at the site and 1 on a bent wall, giving nested shrunken jigsaw pieces, bevelled giraffe plates and interlocking pillows from one exact field.
master.look: Facets: PolyGauge's cut gems with wavy edges, each face a curved sheet. Rings: the eye-catcher, a contour map of islands shaped like jigsaw pieces or giraffe plates, every contour a shrunken copy of the wobbly outline, nothing like noise contours. Plates in relief: interlocking bevelled plates with fingers and bays, a giraffe hide or jigsaw floor with rounded edges, cell sizes even. Threshold at any level is a clean set of jigsaw pieces with uniform gaps.
master.algorithm: Pass 1 as PolyGauge but keep the top three sites F1, F2, F3 (BentWalls' top-3 search) and env = smoothstep(0, E, d3^2 - d2^2), zero near Voronoi vertices so the bends die at the corners. Pass 2 for both candidate owners i in {F1, F2}: for every window site j != i: e = q_j - p_i, half = |e|/2, m = (p_i + q_j)/2, n = e/|e|, canonical tangent t_c = perp(q_lo - q_hi) with lo/hi by hash order (so both sides compute the same s), s = dot(t_c, x - m), pair hash ph = mix(h_i ^ h_j, 3) gives frequency f, phases ph1, ph2; w = A*env*(sin(f*s + ph1) + A2*sin(2.13*f*s + ph2)) * (h_i < h_j ? +1 : -1), clamped to +-0.4*half; ratio g_ij = dot(n, x - p_i) / (half + w); g_i = max_j g_ij. The bent wall is exactly g_ij = 1 from both sides (from j's side the sign flip of w and of n give the same curve). Gauge g = min(g_F1, g_F2): on i's side of the bent wall g_i < 1 and g_j > 1, so the min picks the true owner even where the bend moved the wall across the plain bisector, and both equal 1 on the wall. Outputs as PolyGauge plus: Facets 1 - 2g; Rings frac(g*Rings) with a smooth profile (nested jigsaw contours); Plates: height h_owner*(1 - smoothstep(0, Bevel, 1 - g)) with per-plate hashed height and tilt (DualMesh's Stones look on jigsaw pieces); Uniform 2g^D - 1. Owner hash for Plates is the site with the smaller gauge. 3D: same formulae with the 3D PolyGauge and BentWalls' 3D projected tangent.
master.why_new: PolyGauge (keeper) is straight-walled; BentWalls (keeper) only knows the F1/F2 wall and its sign, so it can draw the wall line and flat plates but has no interior coordinate, no bevel depth and no nested contours; CellularEdge's bevel follows straight walls. The pair-hashed wobble has to enter each bisector ratio before the max, which is inside the gauge kernel.
master.simd_plan: Top-3 sort over the 3^D window (BentWalls does this), then two gauge passes over the same window each with a sin pair per neighbour: in 2D 2 x 9 x 2 FS::Sin, which dominates; use the parabolic wave kernel t*(8-16|t|) from the shears discoveries to cut it. Estimated AVX2: 2D 14-20 ns, 3D 60-80 ns, 4D not recommended (3^4 x 2 passes); the 4D fallback could keep straight walls.
master.continuity: C0: each ratio is continuous (denominator bounded away from zero by the clamp), max and min of continuous functions are continuous, and the two owners agree on the bent wall exactly. Corner behaviour relies on env reaching zero where a third site ties, as BentWalls measured (c0 7.7-7.9); the window seam of PolyGauge at win=1 remains.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Bend Amount (A), Bend Frequency (f base), Bend Octave (A2), Corner Fade (E), Rings (float), Bevel, Output enum {Facets, Rings, Plates, Uniform}, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Bends larger than about a third of the half-spacing make walls of small cells cross each other's corners, which the corner fade only partly hides; cap A by cell size. Two gauge passes make it the costliest cellular node here. Ratio denominators vary with s, so the facets are no longer planes and the Facets output loses its gem look (Rings and Plates do not care).

master.one_liner: Hankin's polygons-in-contact as a closed form on any cell tessellation: an X at every wall midpoint, its arms cut by neighbouring wedges, giving Islamic star and rosette strapwork with one hybrid contact angle, a chiral over-under rule with no parity table, and real parquet deformation across a map.
master.look: Square at 67.5: eight-pointed star and cross. Hex at 60: six-pointed girih rosettes. Penrose rhombs: the 5-fold strapwork of Darb-i Imam style. Low-jitter Voronoi: irregular hand-cut stars, one per cell, straps running straight through wall midpoints. theta near 0 tends to the tile edges doubled; theta near 90 tends to the dual (Delaunay spokes), so one hybrid walks primal to star to dual. Interlace in relief is carved plaster. A gradient in theta gives a parquet deformation, stars morphing across the image.
master.algorithm:
Hankin 1925 via Kaplan 2005: from each edge midpoint grow two rays at contact angle theta to the edge until they meet other rays. Kaplan constructs each motif by searching ray pairs. My pointwise form replaces that search: the kite left around each cell corner is exactly where a point lies outside the wedges of its two nearest walls.
For the sample's cell, for each wall j (Voronoi: neighbour site s_j; m = (s0+s_j)/2; n = normalize(s0-s_j); fixed tilings use true midpoints):
  d_j = dot(p-m, n); t_j = |p-m| tangential (2D: abs(dot(p-m, perp n)); ND: sqrt(|p-m|^2 - d_j^2))
  v_j = d_j*cos(theta) - (t_j - delta)*sin(theta)   // signed distance to the wedge, positive inside. delta splits the contact point: Kaplan's two-point patterns
D2 = second smallest d_j
f = max over j of ( v_j - beta*max(0, d_j - D2) )   // beta about 1 removes far wedges without a jump, since D2 is continuous
Strap = 1 - smoothstep(w - aa, w + aa, abs(f)); Star = f > 0, Kite = f < 0
Checked by hand on the unit square at theta = 67.5: inner vertex (.146,.146) gives f about 0, centre gives positive, (-.4,.3) gives negative. Not yet run.
Interlace (2D): near the nearest wall's midpoint, s+ = d*cos - t_signed*sin, s- = d*cos + t_signed*sin, with t_signed along perp(n). Crossing the wall flips both d and perp(n), so s+ in one cell is the same straight line as s+ in the other. Rule: the + line is over. A strap leaves a wall as + and reaches the next wall as -, so every strap alternates over and under automatically, with no parity bookkeeping (hand check on the square only). I = max(band(|s+|), band(|s-|)*(1 - Dip*smoothstep(Rc, 0, |p-m|))).
theta is read per lane, so a hybrid gives Kaplan's Islamic parquet deformation (the straps bend, while Kaplan's are straight per ray; this is a difference).
master.why_new: Different output. ChiralWallpaper and DomainKaleidoscope give periodic stars from folds of a source, and cannot run on irregular cells or a Penrose tiling. PolyGauge gives pyramids. CellularEdge gives walls. KnotworkInterlace and TruchetKnot give Celtic curves, not straight-strap stars. QuasiTile can draw rhombs, not the star inside them. DualMeshWeave is the theta = 90 end plus the walls, without the family between. A graph cannot reach it because the wedge needs each wall's midpoint and normal.
master.simd_plan: Same two pass window as CellularEdge: F1 first, then all other window sites. Nonadjacent sites have large d_j so the penalty removes them with masks. Formula is dimension agnostic; in 3D the wedge is a cone about the face normal. Estimate AVX2 Voronoi: 8 to 10 / 45 / 150 ns; on the Simplex-window Voronoi discovery 6 / 8 / 10 sites, 5 / 10 / 15 ns. Square or hex: 2 ns, one cell, known walls.
master.continuity: Strap and Interlace are C0 where straps meet walls only at midpoints. Inside a cell f is continuous. Across a wall, raw f differs in the kite interior, so StarField must be clamped to -w or it jumps.
master.params: Tessellation (Voronoi, Square, Hex, Triangle, later QuasiTile rhombs), Contact Angle (hybrid), Contact Split delta (hybrid), Strap Width (hybrid), Grid Jitter (keep below about 0.5), Dip, Output (Strap, StarField, Interlace, RegionTone).
master.risks: On irregular cells the midpoint of two sites can lie off the real wall, so a strap can arrive at a wall away from its midpoint and break. Kaplan himself reports unmatched rays on irregular polygons. High jitter will look wrong. Large polygons with many sides leave a big empty star; Kaplan adds a second inferred pass, which could be a second wedge family with an offset. The 3D cone form is unproven.

hankin-stars.status_note: The prototyper's own call. Strap and StarField are C0 by a bisection scan on regular tilings and on Voronoi at jitter up to 0.35. The over-under Interlace has real small jumps on Voronoi and its look is not verified at the sizes I viewed.
hankin-stars.changed_from_entry: The entry's formula is replaced for 2D, keeping its wedge definition. (1) Found by the smallest test: max_j( v_j - beta*max(0, d_j - D2) ) is wrong below the critical angle (half the angle between adjacent wall normals, 45 on the square): a kite there is a dart, rays near the midpoint lie inside the next wedge, and straps stop reaching walls (rendered as closed rings at theta 30 and 50). (2) A nearest wall form fixed theta on regular tilings but broke straps on Voronoi, since rays do not meet on the medial axis of an irregular polygon. (3) Final form works per actual corner: adjacency from clipping each wall against the others, one sided rays, k_c = max(a,b) for a convex kite or max(min(a,b), L_c) for a dart, f = min_c k_c. This is Kaplan's construction with no search and it meets exactly on any convex polygon. (4) True wall midpoints rather than the two site midpoint. (5) Walls under Min Wall carry no rays, which removes almost all strap breaks. (6) Voronoi pass 2 is centred on the owner, so walls depend on the owner only. (7) In 3D the entry's penalised max is replaced by a distance weighted nearest cone, since polygon corners do not exist there. The entry's over-under rule held on the square by construction and is implemented as stated, with an added gap on the under strand; its visual result on Voronoi is not verified.

master.one_liner: Per-wall frames for any source: elliptic coordinates of the two nearest sites give an orthogonal chart that is continuous everywhere with one search and one source eval.
master.look: A curvilinear net inside every cell: rounded polygon rings following the walls crossed at right angles by arcs running through the walls, kinking at the kite seams. Checker on the chart should give tortoise scutes, fishnet or turtle plates. Textile on the chart should give a weave that always crosses at 90 degrees. A band on t alone gives the soft amplitude net without complex sums or jitter limits. A Perlin Lookup should give grain that respects each wall.
master.algorithm:
SHARED CAUSE. Four accidents in three families are one identity. Two unit-amplitude waves satisfy exp(ikr1) + exp(ikr2) = 2 cos(k(r1-r2)/2) * exp(ik(r1+r2)/2), so the radial-phasor amplitude net is the band pattern of t = F2 - F1, and its phase would be bands of s = F1 + F2. s and t are exactly elliptic coordinates with the two nearest sites as foci, and they are orthogonal: grad s . grad t = |grad F2|^2 - |grad F1|^2 = 0. Order-2 kite mosaic is the hash of the same pair. The pinwheel wedges in stock stained glass are where the second-nearest site changes. Woven Worley rings shows such distance coordinates can drive a weave.

Search window: F1, F2, F3 with ids (as CellularDistance).
s = F1 + F2; t = F2 - F1; v = F3 - F2      // all continuous: each Fk is continuous
pairHash = commutative(id1, id2)            // as in edge-fate-cells
fade = smoothstep(0, PairFade, v)           // pair identity is valid only away from F2 = F3, as bent-walls uses F3
q0 = ChartScale*(s + fade*Spread*rnd(pairHash, 0))
q1 = ChartScale*t
q2 = ChartScale*v in a 3D or 4D Lookup; 4th axis takes fade*rnd(pairHash, 1) when D = 4
Out = Lookup(q0, q1, ...)   // one eval
Outputs: Lookup; Pair Value (kite mosaic, in 3D shards facing each neighbour); s; t. Optional Rigid mode: q = R(wall)*(p - mid) with a fade to p, for straight parallel patterns along each wall rather than curved ones.
master.why_new: Different output. CellFrame, TileDomain and PlateDrift give per-CELL frames, and no node gives per-WALL frames. CellularEdge gives wall distance but no along-wall coordinate. The confirmed amplitude net needs jitter near 1 and a 3x3 complex sum; this needs neither. Part of it is reachable as a graph today: DomainOffset over 2 CellularDistance nodes (Index0Add1 and Index0Sub1) over a zero axis scale. The dedicated node adds one search instead of two, the pair offset with F3 fade, Pair Value and the Rigid mode, none of which a graph can do.
master.simd_plan: Cellular window of 9 / 27 / 81 candidates with F3 tracking by Select, plus one Lookup. Generic GenT. Estimates AVX2: Cellular cost plus 10 percent: 4.5 / 14 / 46 ns plus Lookup. 4D is expensive; this idea leans on 3D being worth it.
master.continuity: C0 for any C0 Lookup: s, t, v are continuous, the hash is commutative across the wall, and pair offsets fade to 0 at v = 0. C1 fails along the kite seams and along walls, on purpose: t has a crease at the wall, so the pattern mirrors there. Rigid mode is C0 only through its fade.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Output enum, Chart Scale, Spread, Pair Fade, Rigid enum. Hybrid: Lookup source.
master.risks: |grad s| goes to 0 on the segment between the two sites and |grad t| goes to 0 far out, so chart cells stretch by large factors and bands look uneven. With Spread 0 all kites read the same part of the Lookup, which may look repetitive. May read as decorative rather than natural.

cellular-scaffold.look: Vol at iso 0: a clean connected network of round struts along Voronoi edges, joined at nodes, each node with about four struts. Form 2 has soft webbed junctions and struts that vary in thickness, like bone or sponge. Form 4 has nearly uniform cylinders with tighter junctions, more like a pipe frame or a lattice. Thinning with z is the best image: thick trabecular at one side going to wire thin at the other, staying connected. rlev and node give thick and thin regions, with flat webs at some large nodes. Form 0 in the same view is visibly shattered: shards and knife edges everywhere, which is what the jump reading means. 2D slice: a network of soft rods. True 2D vertex field: star shaped blobs with arms pointing along the walls, much less interesting than the 3D form.

master.algorithm: Standard 3^D cellular search keeping the three (3D: four) nearest sites s1..s3 and distances F1..F3. From the bisector pass compute exact inset to each neighbour: d1j = (Fj^2 - F1^2) / (2 |sj - s1|) for j = 2,3. Edge distance e = sqrt(d12^2 + d13^2) (3D: distance to the line where three cells meet; 2D: distance to the Voronoi vertex, so expose Mode {Edges, Vertices}). Output = 1 - Min(e / Radius, 1) scaled to [-1,1]; hybrid Radius. All terms are continuous functions of continuous F's, fixed loop, no extra hashes; cost about 1.4x CellularDistance by the critic's per-site op count (estimate). Threshold at 0 gives a connected strut network; Radius from a Level source gives bone that thins with height.
master.why_new:
The gini-foam trabecular vol and the tube-noise worms show that struts along Voronoi edges are a wanted 3D look (bone, coral rock, Plateau borders) and that round sections beat ribbons. Nothing gives distance to the Voronoi edge skeleton; the exact bisector pass already has everything needed.
Seed gap: round struts along Voronoi edges: bone, coral rock.
master.simd_plan: All terms are continuous functions of continuous F's, fixed loop, no extra hashes; cost about 1.4x CellularDistance by the critic's per-site op count (estimate).
master.continuity: All terms are continuous functions of continuous F's, fixed loop, no extra hashes; cost about 1.4x CellularDistance by the critic's per-site op count (estimate).

master.risks:
Seed risk 0.25: 2D output is vertex distance only.
Noticed in merge: the panel says all terms are continuous functions of continuous F's, but the denominators are not. Across a wall (F1 = F2) the owner swaps, so d13 = (F3^2 - F1^2) / (2 |s3 - s1|) becomes (F3^2 - F2^2) / (2 |s3 - s2|): equal numerators over different denominators, so e jumps across walls, by an amount that shrinks to 0 at the triple line. The same happens where F3 swaps with F4. Run the jump scan. sqrt(d12^2 + d13^2) is also only a true distance where the two bisectors are perpendicular.

cellular-scaffold.status_note: The prototyper's own call. The catalogue formula does jump, as flagged; the fix replaces it and measures clean.
cellular-scaffold.changed_from_entry: The formula is replaced. Why the catalogue fails is as the merge note says: d13 = (F3^2 - F1^2) / (2 |s3 - s1|) becomes (F3^2 - F2^2) / (2 |s3 - s2|) as the owner swaps, equal numerators over different denominators. New form 2: e = kf * sqrt( a^2 + b^2 - a b ) / ( F1 + F2 + F3 ), a = F2^2 - F1^2, b = F3^2 - F1^2, which uses no site labels at all and so is a continuous function of F1, F2, F3. Its - a b term and the local denominator make it the exact distance for three sites at 120 degrees, so the section is round there, where the catalogue's sum of squares is a triangle with radius varying by sqrt(2). kf = 1.15 is measured. New form 4: the true distance to the line through the top 3 is symmetric in those three, so its only jump is where the third site changes, and it is blended into form 2 by smoothstep( 0, W, F4^2 - F3^2 ), which is 0 there. Added Node Size, and a thickness gradient to show bone thinning. Default jitter 0.8 and not 1. The 2D harness default is the 3D form on a plane.

It reads as polished thunderegg or agate tile straight away. Each cell has its own band sequence. Relief: stepped terraces around each cell with a rough crystal top, like a contour model. Geodes: dark rough rock with round geode slices of many sizes, multi band rims and crystal centres, and no visible lattice. Both forms beat the band only render. Vol hollow: hollow balls, cut faces show rings; many sizes. Vol cavities: solid rock with small round holes, plain. Vol Thunderegg shells: plain honeycomb with polygon rooms; nothing new there, the bands are the point of this form.

master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: geodes and thundereggs: agate bands that follow the wall rather than noise, nested shells in 3D slices. Band labels are hard inside a cell.
master.algorithm:
FORM GeodeField (voxel-engineer lens): Fixed level loop as BubblePack (own cell, one hash per cell per level, L(L+1)/2 lookups): q in cell frame, centre c(hash), radius r(hash); d = |q-c| - r in world units. Masked update of min d, its h and r. Density output: Max( d, -(Thick*r + d) ) inverted so the shell is solid with an air core. Bands output: b = Floor( -d / T ); value = rnd11( hash(h, b) ), hard by design, or a smoothed jitter profile from strata-bands. Density is a min of continuous functions, so C0; Bands is a material id with jumps. Evaluate Bands only on solid voxels. Cost estimate: 15 ns 3D at L=7 (BubblePack estimate) + about 1 ns. Inherits top-level lattice and occasional overlaps.

FORM Thunderegg (creative lens): Run the CellularEdge pass in the 3x3 / 3x3x3 / 3x3x3x3 window (Grid Jitter <= 0.40 for exactness): e = exact wall distance, h1 = winner hash. q = e * BandFreq + Wobble * Perlin(pos) + rnd(mix(h1,1)). i = Floor(q), fr = q - i. tone = hash of (i ^ h1) via bit fields. seam = smoothstep(0, SeamW, min(fr, 1-fr)). band = tone * seam. core = smoothstep(Rc, Rc + Eps, e). crystal = SimplexFacet Flat(pos) seeded with h1. out = lerp(band, crystal, core) * smoothstep(0, Grout, e), so grout hides the cell jump. Band labels are hard inside a cell, softened only by the seam. 3D slices give nested shells for free. Estimated AVX2: 8 / 19 / 56 ns, against measured 62 / 196 / 293 for the breccia graph.
master.why_new:
GeodeField: True spheres are exact distance fields, so banded shells get constant thickness. Each geode needs its own band sequence, which a Terrace on a distance output cannot give. Own-cell kernel means no window. Not built: untested idea.
Thunderegg: Poster agate bands follow noise; real agate bands follow the cavity wall. CellularEdge gives exact wall distance cheaply, so bands should wrap each cell with a crystal core. My stock breccia preset is the neighbour, and it costs far more. Not built; the look is a prediction.

master.one_liner: Cellular search and exact edge distance under a per-lane anisotropic metric: elongated flow-aligned cells, and flow-aligned grouted mosaic tiles of constant size, for one direction eval.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: elongated flow-aligned cells (wood rays, muscle fibre, flowstone, ice); with Grout and Bevel an andamento mosaic of flow-aligned pebbles, not true coursed rows.
master.algorithm:
FORM FlowCellular (maintainer lens): Evaluate hybrid Direction once at the lane position: angle theta (2D) or unit vector u (3D, from a vector-valued hybrid or a DomainWarp-style triple). Build M = R diag(1, 1/Aspect, 1/Aspect) R^T once per lane (Aspect >= 1, contraction only, so the 3^D window bound of the unchanged jitter lattice still holds). Run the ordinary cellular window search with d = |M (p - site)| for every candidate; keep the bisector pass for the exact inset under the same metric (d1j = (Fj^2 - F1^2) / (2 |M (sj - s1)|)). Outputs F1, F2-F1, EdgeDistance, CellValue. Since M is the same for all candidates in a lane and theta is continuous, F1 and F2 remain continuous; discontinuity in Direction is the user's. Cost = CellularDistance + 1 Direction eval + D^2 multiply-adds per candidate (estimate 1.2x Cellular plus the direction source).

FORM AndamentoMosaic (creative lens): theta = Angle.Gen(seed, pos), one eval per lane. c, s from sincos. M(pos) = diag(1/a, 1/b) * R(theta), aspect a/b capped at 2. For each of 4x4 candidates (2D): site = cell + jitter(hash); y[i] = M * (site - pos); d2[i] = dot(y[i], y[i]); keep nearest y1, h1 via Select. Second loop over the same stored y[i]: n = y[i] - y1; e = 0.5 * (d2[i] - d2_1) * InvSqrt(dot(n,n)); edge = min(edge, e) excluding the winner by mask. out = rnd(h1) * smoothstep(Grout, Grout + Bevel, edge). M is continuous in pos when Angle is, so F1 and edge stay continuous and the walls stay closed. 3D: stretch only along the field vector, y = r - (1 - 1/a) * dot(r,v) * v, 27 candidates. Window seams at max aspect must be tested with the critic's bisection scan. Estimated AVX2 2D: 10-12 ns.
master.why_new:
FlowCellular: steerable-perlin showed that a per-lane hybrid direction turns an isotropic primitive into a flow-aligned one at modest cost, and cell-frame showed per-grain streaks are wanted but cost 3-4 source evals. Stretching the cellular metric by one direction eval gives elongated flow-aligned cells (wood rays, muscle fibre, flowstone, ice) with F1 / F2-F1 / exact edge outputs for about one extra source eval.
AndamentoMosaic: The warped fan mosaic is gorgeous, but warping changes tile sizes. A per-lane metric keeps tile size constant and aligns tiles to a field. Honest limit: sites are jittered, so expect flow-aligned pebbles rather than true coursed rows, since rows need a stream function a pointwise node cannot integrate. Not built; the look is a prediction.
Seed gap: researcher lens hole 6: per-lane anisotropic cellular.
master.simd_plan:
FlowCellular: Cost = CellularDistance + 1 Direction eval + D^2 multiply-adds per candidate (estimate 1.2x Cellular plus the direction source).
AndamentoMosaic: Estimated AVX2 2D: 10-12 ns.
master.continuity:
FlowCellular: Since M is the same for all candidates in a lane and theta is continuous, F1 and F2 remain continuous; discontinuity in Direction is the user's.
AndamentoMosaic: M is continuous in pos when Angle is, so F1 and edge stay continuous and the walls stay closed. Window seams at max aspect must be tested with the critic's bisection scan.
master.params: Direction (hybrid: angle in 2D, unit vector in 3D) or Angle, Aspect (>= 1, capped at 2 in AndamentoMosaic), a, b, Grid Jitter, Output enum {F1, F2-F1, EdgeDistance, CellValue, Mosaic}, Grout, Bevel.
master.risks:
Seed risk 0.5: window seams at high aspect; true coursed rows impossible.
Overlap to know about: the per-lane metric itself is already in the catalogue as gradient-metric-cellular (keeper prototype, direction from a guide gradient, stretch k, c0ratio 6.73 at k=5, no seams seen). Reuse that prototype and do not re-judge plain F1 or F2-F1. What is new here is the hybrid Direction input and the exact bisector edge pass under the metric, which gives constant-width grout.

It does not: a site beyond the window can be nearer in the metric, and that is measured as a jump of about 1 at 3x3 and 0.54 at 4x4, a=3. Added the window exit weight, pulling d^2 to a large cap. (2) Edge distance is Euclidean to the metric bisector, ( d_j^2 - d_1^2 ) / ( 2 |M^2 u| ), since the entry's |M u| gives a metric distance and grout then varies by direction; metric=1 keeps the entry's form. master.one_liner: Peeling paint and curled mud: Voronoi plates whose free edge lifts into a circular curl and recedes, exposing the substrate under a contact shadow, while the attached side stays flat.
master.look: A surface of flat polygonal flakes separated by cracks, many of which have one edge rolled up into a bright curved lip with a receded footprint, the bare substrate showing in a dark-shadowed crescent behind each lip. In relief it is peeling paint or dried curled mud at a glance; the threshold panel shows plates with bites taken out of their free sides. Volume: flakes curling off a plane. Useful for paint, lacquer, dried mud and clay, bark plates, old posters, sunburnt skin.
master.algorithm: Jittered Voronoi (3x3 window) with the exact edge distance e(p) (iq two pass) and the nearest site S; per cell hashed: peel direction d_c (unit), peel flag from a hybrid Peel fraction, curl radius rho in [RhoMin, RhoMax] cells, plate tone. Plate radius along d_c: cast a ray from S along d_c to the cell boundary using the neighbour bisectors already visited: t_far = min over neighbours N with (N - S) . d_c > 0 of (|N - S|^2 / 2) / ((N - S) . d_c). Lift coordinate: x = (p - S) . d_c - (t_far - Peel * t_far) where Peel in [0,1] is how much of the plate (measured from the far edge) has lifted; x < 0 is the flat attached part. Curl: the lifted part is a quarter cylinder of radius rho in the (d_c, up) plane: height h = rho - sqrt(max(0, rho^2 - x^2)) for 0 <= x <= rho, i.e. the plate surface rises with vertical tangent at x = rho; beyond x = rho the plate is gone in plan view (it has curled up and back), so the substrate shows. Hence the footprint recedes by (t_far Peel - rho) automatically; a second hashed direction (Directions 2) applies the same to another edge with max height / min footprint. Chipping: the free edge x = rho is perturbed by a 1D noise along the edge direction n_c = perp(d_c): x_end = rho + Chip * noise((p . n_c) / ChipScale, cellhash). Crack gaps: substrate also where e(p) < Gap. Substrate contact shadow: on exposed substrate darkness = Shadow * exp(-(x - x_end) / ShadowLen) for x > x_end (the lip overhangs it), and also along crack gaps by e(p). Outputs: Height (substrate 0, plate Thickness, curl rising to Thickness + rho), Mask (plate 1, substrate 0, continuous via a soft edge), Shade (1 - shadow), Tone (per plate hash tone, for colour variation), Combined (Height with shadow baked). 3D form: the lifted flake is a shell: signed distance to the circular arc of radius rho centred at (x = 0, y = Thickness + rho) in the (d_c, up) plane, minus Thickness / 2, restricted to the cell footprint and to arc angles below CurlAngle (which may exceed 90 degrees in 3D so flakes roll over), unioned with the flat plate slab and the substrate half space; a volume render shows real curled flakes.
master.why_new: CellularPlanes tilts whole plates; EdgeFateCells lists curled mud but as a per-edge depth profile (all edges dished symmetrically, no recession, no exposed substrate); PlateDrift slides and rotates rigid plates apart. The peeling signature is directional: one side attached and flat, the other rolled with a vertical tangent and a footprint that has shrunk away from its crack, with the shadow under the lip. No graph can shrink a plate from one side while keeping the crack network, because the recession depends on the per-cell ray cast to the far edge.
master.simd_plan: One cellular pass for F1 and neighbours plus the bisector edge distance (CellularEdge cost, about 2x CellularDistance), the ray cast is one reciprocal per neighbour in the same loop, then the curl is a sqrt and a few selects; est 9-12 ns 2D AVX2. 3D: the plates live on a 2D lattice (xz) and y is up, so the window stays 3x3 (not 27) and the shell SDF adds a 2D arc distance: about 12-15 ns; a true 3D Voronoi version is not needed. 4D: w fallback.
master.continuity: Discontinuous at the free lip (a vertical drop to the substrate), intentional; C0 elsewhere, C1 inside the curl; the ray cast t_far is continuous in p because the sample's own cell does not change while S is fixed.
master.params: Feature Scale, Grid Jitter, Peel (hybrid fraction of plates and amount), Curl Radius Min / Max, Directions (int 1-2), Thickness, Gap (hybrid), Chip, Chip Scale, Shadow, Shadow Length, Curl Angle (3D), Output (enum).
master.risks: The quarter-cylinder heightfield cannot show a flake rolled past vertical (3D form only); the chip noise can reopen the plate past the crack if Chip > the plate margin (clamp x_end to t_far); the 2D form has no cast shadow direction, only a contact crescent.

The last step, 0.00624, is above a clean 10x fall; it is at the curl's vertical tangent, where a square root makes the slope grow without bound, and that is an infinite slope and not a jump. Height 6.262 / 6.460, Mask 6.598 / 6.552, Shade 6.673 / 6.713, Tone 6.695 / 6.705, all 0 jumps. Two directions 6.868 / 6.985, 0 jumps. curl-plates.changed_from_entry: (1) t_far uses the owner's own 8 neighbours and not the sample's window: the entry says neighbours already visited, but those depend on the sample, so t_far would change inside a plate. (2) The lip is a thin ramp by default rather than a jump, with lipw=0 keeping the entry's vertical, so that real jumps are not hidden by intended ones. (3) The shadow starts from zero over the lip width and uses max with a crack shadow that is the same on both sides at a wall, which keeps it C0. (5) Window exit weight on e.

If the lips look like tilted plates, rho is too large relative to the peel length; if plates vanish, Peel is too high.

cell-domain.look: Default reads as a fractured polished marble slab: dark veins run coherently across the whole image and step sideways and turn slightly at each thin straight black crack, with T junctions inside the Voronoi cells. The 3D XZ slice looks the same. Preset 2 is sharp faceted shards with a flat tilt per leaf, the strongest of the hillshades. Preset 4 is parquet, each shard with its own direction of wood rings. Preset 1 is a large crack net holding smaller clouded cells at a second scale. Preset 3 is pale matrix with toned chips inside cracked panels; it is busy at this window. Nested volume is a block of small angular fragments with flat faces.
cell-domain.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, sheet slice, vol). 4D not written; the code is templated on D and needs the 81 site window, so it should follow at the 50 ns estimate.
cell-domain.range: preset 0: -1 to 0.74 over 8 seeds and offsets (the grout is the -1, marble tops out near 0.74); presets 1 to 3: -1 to 1. No NaN or Inf, far coords 4e4 fine.
cell-domain.artifacts: No jumps at any preset with a continuous source. The grout is a very steep slope (180 to 320 per unit), so thin lines alias at 512 px like any hard line. A source with its own jump passes it through where it is not under grout: the first parquet source had a sawtooth ring and measured 0.60 at h=1e-5 until I made the ring continuous, so the C0 promise covers only cell boundaries. At levels=3 in preset 2 some thin slivers appear, same as shatter-bsp. Grout dominates contrast when normalised: gray panels are grout -1 against a source that rarely reaches 1.
cell-domain.node_shape: CellDomain. Members: Source (GeneratorSource, evaluated once per lane with per lane seed), Grout (hybrid), Width W (hybrid), Levels, Width Decay, Cut Probability, Frame enum {Owner reseeded, World shatter}, Max Rotation, Drift, Scale, Lift, Tilt, Grid Jitter capped at the audited value. Nesting is a Source that is another CellDomain.
cell-domain.port_notes: Edge pass from CellularEdgeDistance, then the ShatterBSP loop, then one Source.Gen with seed ^ hash per lane, which Gen already allows. master.one_liner: Evaluate any child in the frame of its owning Voronoi cell or BSP shard and hide the jump under a grout line, so nested cracks, terrazzo, facet shatter and broken versions of any node become short graphs.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: terrazzo, nested cracks, facet shatter, cracked mirror, smashed tile, fractured marble slab. With a mid-gray gap shards may read as grouted tile rather than glass.
master.algorithm:
FORM CellDomain (voxel-engineer lens): 3^D window pass keeping rel[i], hash[i], F1 site and hash h. Bisector pass as cellular-edge-distance: e = min over j of dot(.5*(rel[j]+rel1), n)*InvSqrt(n.n), with Grid Jitter capped at the audited value. Frame q = R(h)*(p - site)*Scale + Offset(h), with R a table rotation in 2D or a hash-derived Householder in 3D/4D, no trig. v = Source.Gen( seed ^ h, q ), one eval with a per-lane seed. Optional tilt: v += dot(tilt(h), rel1). Output Lerp( Grout, v, smoothstep(0,W,e) ), with W a hybrid. At e = 0 both sides return Grout, so it is C0 whatever v does. Nesting is a Source that is another CellDomain; child jumps vanish under the parent grout. Cost estimate: 5.5/16/50 ns plus one Source per level (edge pass figure from the tournament), any dimension.

FORM ShatterLookup (artist-material lens): Same edge pass and constant BSP loop as ShatterBSP, tracking d = Min over levels of e_l/W_l, leaf id and leaf centre c. theta = MaxRot*rnd11(mix(id,1)); shift = Drift*(rnd11(mix(id,2)), rnd11(mix(id,3))). p' = c + R(theta)*(p-c) + shift. In 3D, rotate in one plane picked by id bits using Select. v = Source(p'), exactly one eval per lane. out = lerp(GapValue, v, smoothstep(0,1,d)). Source jumps between shards, but every leaf boundary has d = 0, so out equals GapValue there and the result is continuous. Optional Throw adds a hash height per leaf for stepped relief, multiplied by the same smoothstep so it stays continuous. Works in any dimension the window affords. Cost ESTIMATE: ShatterBSP about 7 / 18 ns in 2D / 3D plus Source. Risk: with a mid-gray gap, shards read as grouted tile rather than glass.
master.why_new:
CellDomain: Half the striking discoveries are the same thing: evaluate a child in the frame of the owning cell, hide the jump in a grout line. NestedCracks, terrazzo, facet shatter and plate-of-plates each got their own code or a large graph. One node makes them all short graphs. It does not reproduce plate-drift's wedge gaps, because cell outlines do not rotate. Not built: untested idea.
ShatterLookup: Turns any node into a broken version: cracked mirror, smashed tile, fractured marble slab. PlateDrift gives Voronoi plates, but no node gives straight BSP shards with a rigid offset per leaf. Not built, look unverified.
Seed gap: makes nested cracks, terrazzo and facet shatter short graphs.

master.one_liner: A crack mask driven by a Damage hybrid: parent cracks open first, children follow, tips taper. Walls never move, so growth is a reveal along a fixed net.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: cracks where the wear is, or spreading behind a moving front in animation.
master.algorithm: Damage is a hybrid sampled once at the lane. Edge pass: exact e_0 and F1 site id from the CellularEdgeDistance window, with Grid Jitter <= 0.40 for exactness. Constant loop l=1..L: from hash(id) take cut normal n and offset; e_l = |dot(p-c,n)-off|; side = mask(dot(p-c,n) > off); id = mix(id, side). Thresholds T_0 < T_1 < ... give m_l = smoothstep(T_l, T_l+s, Damage). Widths W_l = W*decay^l. crack = Max over l of m_l*profile(e_l / (W_l*(wmin + (1-wmin)*m_l))), with profile(0) = 1. Continuity: m_l depends only on the continuous Damage at the lane, so there is no per-wall state, which is what the tapered-tip form measured as C0. Because T rises with l, a parent's term at its own wall equals m_parent, which is >= every child term, so a child discontinuity at a parent wall is covered from both sides. Free ends come from noise inside Damage. Output maps crack to [-1,1]. 2D, 3D and 4D follow the window. Cost ESTIMATE from the critic's ShatterBSP estimate: about 7 / 18 ns in 2D / 3D, edge pass alone about 50 ns in 4D, plus one Damage eval. Limit: walls never move, so growth is a reveal along a fixed net.

master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: breaking river ice and tempered glass with cracks that turn with their plate; broken flagstone or tumbled slate with soil in the cracks.
master.algorithm:
FORM PlateShatter (artist-terrain lens): Per lane: plate-drift's 3x3 window finds the owning plate id k, its rotation R_k and translation t_k (hashed), and the gap distance g. Transform q = R_k^T (p - c_k - t_k). In plate space run shatter-bsp with seed = hash(k): levels L (fixed int), each level a hashed line through the sub-cell centre, distance d_l clipped at the parent cut as shatter-bsp already does; crack = min_l(d_l / w_l). Output = min(g / gapWidth, crack) for a mask, or plate TiltedHeight minus crackDepth * profile(crack). All lookups are per-lane hashes, no neighbour state; window stays 3x3 (3x3x3 in 3D). Cost estimate: plate-drift (~3x Cellular) + ~0.5 ns per level.

FORM ShatterPlates (maintainer lens): Run CellularEdge with Levels = ShatterBSP cuts to get shard id h, shard anchor a (site, or parent site plus cut index) and exact inset e. Per shard from h: lift l in [-1,1], tilt vector t with |t| <= Tilt, so plate height H = l + Dot(t, p - a), clamped to the shard by the inset band: H_plate = Lerp(soil, H, SmoothStep(e / Bevel)). Then HeightBlend(H_plate, Soil(p), HeightA = H_plate + Bias, HeightB = Soil(p), Softness) where Soil is any Source: soil fills where it is higher than the plate top, plate corners poke through. All pointwise: one cellular edge pass, one source eval, no sort. Cost about 1.5x CellularDistance + Source (estimate).
master.why_new:
PlateShatter: Plate-drift gives rigid rotated plates but their surface is flat; shatter-bsp gives T-junction cracks but on a fixed Voronoi. Cracks that turn with their plate are what breaking river ice and tempered glass look like, and the hierarchical-shatter discovery shows nesting plate-drift works but was too noisy.
ShatterPlates: plate-drift's tilted rigid plates were its strong image and its bevel mask the weak one; CellularEdge with Levels gives exact T-junction shards; height-blend fills gaps with a second material so features interlock. Together: broken flagstone / tumbled slate with soil in the cracks, in one pass.

ShatterPlates: Cost about 1.5x CellularDistance + Source (estimate).

master.one_liner: Cheaper 3D and 4D shatter: a piecewise-linear warp in front of Simplex-window Voronoi, then fixed BSP cuts under a clamped mask.

master.algorithm: Step 1: simplex lattice at frequency fw, hash D+1 corners to vectors, barycentric interpolate, p2 = p + A*v (piecewise linear). Step 2: at p2, search the D+1 simplex corners plus the D+1 face-opposite vertices, c_(m-1)+c_(m+1)-c_m, at jitter rings .28/.17/.14; keep F1 site, rel and hash. Step 3: bisector pass over those same sites, then e = Min(e, 0.10), since only clamped masks were exact in the audit. Step 4: fixed L=3 BSP levels: plane from hash(F1, path), side bit updates path, e = Min(e, taper^l * |dot(rel,n)-o|). Step 5: output a Lerp of leaf hash value toward Grout by smoothstep(e/W). Cost estimate: about 7/12/18 ns against the shatter-bsp estimate of 7/18/52 ns, so the win is 3D and 4D only. Limits: width varies with warp Jacobian, no wide bevels, and walls kink at PL creases.
master.why_new:
The 3D and 4D price of cracks is the main barrier for shatter in volumes. Simplex-window uses 6/8/10 sites against 9/27/81, but its cells drift toward honeycomb in 3D. A PL warp breaks that regularity with no search. Not built or rendered: untested combination.

slab-field.look: Faulted terrain of hard polygon slabs, each dipping its own way, with fine bedding ledges that run along strike and so turn with each slab. In relief it reads as tilted sedimentary blocks with scarps between them; with the terrain colour ramp the ledges also resemble terraced fields. S is a single dial from hard scarps (0.02) through folded blocks (0.2) to soft grained hills (0.6). The isotropic control (src=2) loses the slate look entirely, so the grain is the idea. Volume shows real angular blocks with layered faces and floating pieces; it is a value field, so 3D is a curiosity beside the 2D terrain.
slab-field.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, c0 and jumps via probe, vol). 4D not written; 4D would be 81 sites and 5 sources, not cheap.
slab-field.range: -0.97 to 1.00 over 8 seeds and offsets, clamped at +-1 by a measured normaliser; no NaN or Inf; far coords fine.
slab-field.artifacts: No jumps. Bedding lines are regular enough at far zoom to read as tilled fields rather than geology; uneven spacing from a sine in the dip coordinate helped but did not remove this. Vol has floaters and noisy patches where the iso plane lies nearly parallel to a slab. High spectrum axis stat (19) comes from the strong per slab directions, not from the lattice; the slabs are polygon shaped and any one slab's line pattern is straight. Fault scarps show the Voronoi polygon outline plainly at S below 0.06, unlike real faults with long runs.
slab-field.node_shape: SlabField, Group Cellular or Terrain. Members: Sharpness S (hybrid), Lift, Tilt, Tilt Bias, Grid Jitter (capped below 0.9 in 2D, 0.7 in 3D), Detail Amp (hybrid), Grain Scale, Grain Scale Jitter, Grain Mode enum {Ledges, Anisotropic Source, Source}, Source (GeneratorSource) for the non ledge modes.
slab-field.port_notes: Same K insertion as CellFrame, keep top K + 1 by masks. All K sources always run, seed per lane is seed ^ hash. Ledge mode needs no Source: Floor, Sin and one Perlin for the warp plus one for detail, so 2 Perlin per site. std::pow for tilt bias can go when tbias = 1. Weight sum is safe: dK - d0 > 0 except at (K+1)-fold ties, handled by the max with an epsilon in the divide.

master.one_liner: Tilted sedimentary slabs from one window pass: each slab has its own lift, tilt and rotated grain, blended with cell-frame's weights.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: tumbled slate and flagstone terrain. Small sharpness gives hard faulted slabs, large gives soft hills.
master.algorithm: Per lane: one 3x3 (3^D) pass keeping the nearest F1..F4 sites (F1..F5 in 3D) with their hashes. Per site i: lift l_i, tilt vector t_i, grain angle a_i, scale g_i from hash bits; local value v_i = l_i + dot(t_i, p - s_i) + detailAmp * Source(R(a_i) (p - s_i) * g_i, seed ^ hash_i). Blend with cell-frame's barycentric weights w_i over the stored sites (sharpness S from cellular-planes; S small = hard faulted slabs, large = soft hills). Output sum w_i v_i. Source is evaluated a fixed 4 (5 in 3D) times per lane. Cost estimate: ~1.3x CellularDistance plus 4-5 source evals.
master.why_new:
Cellular-planes gives tilted plates with soft fault ramps; cell-frame gives per-cell rotated grain. Tilted sedimentary slabs whose bedding grain turns with each slab is tumbled-slate and flagstone terrain, and the two share one window pass.
Seed gap: tumbled slate with per-slab grain.
master.simd_plan: Cost estimate: ~1.3x CellularDistance plus 4-5 source evals.

nested-foam.look: Curved nested plates, like a political map of states and counties or a giraffe hide: big rounded regions with smaller rounded ones inside them, walls of steady width, and child walls that stop dead at the parent wall in T junctions. Keep=0.7 leaves some parents unsplit, so plate sizes vary a lot. These cells are not convex, which no Voronoi based crack node gives. Strata config: long wavy beds with curved joints that stop at each bed, reads as jointed rock. Dome output: each plate a soft pillow, like cobbles at mixed scale. Facet source: angular polyline walls with some smeared bands. Volume at window 4 is mostly one big unsplit parent with curved crack sheets in one corner, so f0 is too low for that window.
nested-foam.dims: 2D, 3D measured (images, check, jumps); 4D measured for speed and jumps through 2D slices at gn=0. 4D gradient form not written, since lab_proto.h has no 4D gradient Perlin.
nested-foam.range: -1 to 0.99 over 8 seeds and offsets (grout is -1), no NaN or Inf, far coords fine.
nested-foam.artifacts: No jumps. The smallest test confirmed the percolation argument: at K=2 and one level the phases are long connected meanders, at K=3 and K=4 they break into closed cells. The entry's constant normaliser gives dark smears wherever two fields stay nearly tied over an area; that was the worst flaw at first and the gradient form removed it. With facet source, smears remain where gn is off. At K=4, levels=3 and a high f0 the result is a busy tangle (grid_src_out), so f0 must be low. Same label regions share a tone at low levels, since the id is label based, not per connected component: two separate plates of one label look alike and carry the same child field. Tiny sliver cells appear where three fields nearly tie.

master.one_liner: Hierarchical plates with true T-junctions and no lattice window: K-way argmax of any source, reseeded per region at every level, which also explains why ContourCut only ever gave scribble.
master.look: Plates of plates: big curved cells, each with its own smaller cells whose walls stop at the parent wall, older walls wider. With Perlin source walls are rounded and organic, like dried mud, giraffe, or a political map of states and counties. With SimplexFacet source (the Foam Label over facet discovery) walls are angular polylines. Volume should give non-convex nested pebbles and split blocks.
master.algorithm:
WHY CONTOURCUT DISAPPOINTED. The critic's ContourCut (recursive zero-set cuts, the fracture_polyline images) wide view is 'meandering scribble with closed rings'. That is percolation: a symmetric noise cut at its median has each phase exactly at threshold, so its interface is a critical hull, with long meanders and rings at all scales. Percolation hull walls in the crack family is the same accident. With K >= 3 phases each holds 1/K of the area, below threshold in 2D, so all regions are finite closed cells: ExchangeFoam's interfaces. So the cut should be K-way, and everything else ContourCut proved still holds: per-lane seeds, T-junctions hidden in the parent wall.

region r = seed; e = +inf; F = 1
for L in 0..Levels-1:
  for k in 0..K-1: v_k = Source.Gen(r + k*Stride, Rot_L*p*F + PhaseOffset*k)   // per-lane int seed is allowed by Gen, phase offset avoids shared lattice ties, as in ExchangeFoam
  (t1, t2, label) = fixed max network
  m = (t1 - t2)*MarginGain*F^-WidthDecay     // constant normaliser: stays C0 even over facet sources, the ContourCut finding
  alive = hash(r) < Keep                     // whole regions can stop splitting, so plate sizes vary
  e = Select(alive, Min(e, m), e)
  r = Select(alive, hash(r, label, L), r); F *= Lacunarity
Outputs: Cracks = profile(e); Plate = rnd(r)*smoothstep(0, W, e) + Grout*(1 - smoothstep(0, W, e)); Plate Tilt; Lookup = LookupSource.Gen(r, p) under the same grout mask, for one eval per lane; Depth = level at which the winning wall was made.
Root hybrid: Level 0 may instead use a user field as its first cut, by sign. With a banded Root this reproduces the jointed strata accident: long beds with joints that stop at the beds.
master.why_new: Hard made easy in 3D and 4D. CellularEdge Levels, NestedCracks and the T-junction graph all need a 3^D or 4^D cellular search per level, 41 ns per level in 4D, and their cells stay convex or near convex. Here 3 levels at K 4 is 12 Perlin evals in any dimension: 52 ns in 4D. ExchangeFoam is the one-level case with no hierarchy. ContourCut is the K = 2 case. The crossbreeds HeightFoam and FoamWalls do not nest. CellDomain nests but over Voronoi only.
master.simd_plan: Loops are int members, K*Levels Source evals, integer hash of region id per lane. No window, no Select on control flow beyond labels. Estimates AVX2 with Perlin, K 4, Levels 3: 15 / 30 / 55 ns. Facet source is cheaper in 3D and 4D. Tile and 4D work through the Source.
master.continuity: C0: at any wall of any level e = 0, and anything that jumps does so only across such a wall, so Plate and Lookup output Grout on both sides. Same argument as ContourCut (measured c0 7.91 to 8.00 at 228 ns scalar for 4 levels).
master.params: Source, Lookup source, int K (3 to 5), int Levels (3), Seed Stride, Phase Offset, Lacunarity, Width Decay, Keep, Output enum, Grout. Hybrid: Margin Gain, Root.
master.risks: Perlin margin walls are of uneven apparent width because the normaliser is a constant, as in ContourCut. Small child regions can give blobby rather than crack-like interiors: the log called smooth Perlin cuts 'blobby spaghetti, not cracks', so facet sources may be needed. Crowded market for crack looks.

nested-foam.changed_from_entry: Added gradient normalised wall distance: e = min over rivals k of (t_w - t_k) / sqrt(|grad t_w - grad t_k|^2 + eps^2), scaled by 1/F. The minimum runs over every rival, because using only the runner up would jump where the runner up changes identity. This is the main change and the look depends on it. Lower f0 (0.22) and lac 2.2 so parents are clearly larger than children. Added a Dome output instead of a plane tilt, since no region centre exists to anchor a plane.

joint-blocks.look: Default reads as bedded rock in plan or cliff face: long wavy beds of uneven thickness, each bed broken by joints that stop at the bed line and are offset between beds. Relief is a stepped ledge cliff with big rectangular stones and rough tops. Vol is the best image: long bedding planes through the block, thin vertical joints, some whole blocks missing, rough interior faces from the source; it looks like a quarried or weathering limestone outcrop. The entry's plain form (crossing families, the image top left) is a triangle or rhombus tile pattern, plainly less like rock, so stagger is what makes it good.
joint-blocks.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D measured for speed and jumps (3D and 4D through 2D slices with probe); 2D and 3D seen in images. 4D has no window, so its cost does not explode, and that is the point.
joint-blocks.range: -1 to 1 over 8 seeds and offsets, no NaN or Inf, far coords fine.
joint-blocks.artifacts: No jumps. Long straight runs remain the visual limit: with warp 0 the lines are ruled, and at the default warp the bedding lines are still long and parallel across the whole view, which is correct for bedding but reads as masonry if joints are too regular. The FFT shows a strong star along the family normals (axis stat 25.7), as expected. At the XZ slice the bedding plane lies nearly in the slice and shows as one big smooth patch with thin diagonal joints. Warp stretches block widths a little.
joint-blocks.node_shape: JointBlocks, Group Domain or Cellular. Members: Source (GeneratorSource, one eval at the offset position), int Families, Normal Set enum {Golden, Cliff}, Dip, Spacing, Spacing Growth, Spacing Jitter, Spacing Variation, Stagger bool, Finite Families int, Tip Frequency, Slip, Lift, Bed Lift, Tilt, Depth, Width (hybrid), Width Decay. Warp left to an upstream DomainWarp, since a graph does that at no extra code; then the Tiling note below applies.
joint-blocks.port_notes: Loop count is an int member, same for all lanes. Normals, slip directions and primes go in per node arrays built when params are set, in place of the prototype's per sample trig. Per lane: dot, Floor, hash mix by per lane id, two Sin and two Cos for bedvar (can be dropped or replaced with a polynomial), masks by Min and Select. Works in GenT with a parameter pack. In 4D, tiling survives because the families are plain plane projections with no rotation node in the chain, though the integer spacings needed for exact periodicity are not done here.

master.one_liner: Cliff blocks bounded by long joint sets: a fixed loop of plane families accumulates block id, offset and exact plane distance, with block jumps hidden under a joint mask.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: real cliff faces: blocks bounded by long joints with small offsets. Long straight runs unless warped.
master.algorithm: Fixed loop over N families (3-6) with golden-angle or table normals n_i and spacing s_i: u = dot(p,n_i)/s_i + phi_i, k = Floor(u), f = u - k; e = Min(e, s_i*Min(f,1-f)); id = id ^ (k*Prime_i); off += slipdir_i * rnd11(hash(k,i)) * Slip * s_i. After the loop: v = Source.Gen( seed, p + off ) + dot(tilt(id), p - Round(p)) omitted by default because it jumps; use only under grout. Output Lerp( -Depth, v, smoothstep(0,W,e) ): at a joint e = 0 on both sides, so the block jump is hidden and it is C0. Optional per-family tip mask from a low frequency hybrid, as in fault_drag_tips. Cost estimate: about 1-1.5 ns per family (fault-lines figure), so 8 ns plus Source at N=6. Risk: long straight runs, measured at 86.8 units on Multigrid N=7; a Perlin warp cut that to 10.8 units.
master.why_new:
Real cliff faces are blocks bounded by long joint sets with small offsets. Fault-lines gives offsets with no grout, Multigrid gives cheap regions and exact plane distance, neither gives blocks. No window, cost flat in dimension, and a 4D form that survives tiling better than graphs using DomainRotate. Not built: untested idea.
Seed gap: cliff blocks bounded by joints, flat with dimension.

joint-blocks.changed_from_entry: Added stagger: phase and spacing per family come from the id so far, giving T junctions and per bed joint spacing, the biggest visual win. Added uneven spacing as a monotone 1D warp of the family coordinate with the distance divided by its slope. corestone.look: Stacked rounded loaves on a seamless rock base, which reads as a Dartmoor style tor or a Joshua Tree pile, more than the entry's fear of masonry would suggest at this warp and jitter. Frames along weather: at 0.3 a sharp jointed block mass with thin cracks, at 0.55 corners start to soften, at 0.8 and 1 clear rounded loaves with open vertical gaps and rounded tops, at 1.3 smaller loaves and more lost blocks, all on a base with solid rock low down. Vertical sections under the frames show thin joints deep and wider, rounder blocks near the top, with blocks above the surface standing proud. Some stones look a little like bread loaves. I did not read marbles, columns, flat and 3D density images; those parameters are measured by census and jumps only.
corestone.dims: 3D is the real form, measured (vol, slices, census). 2D is a vertical section, same code, measured. 4D not written; entry suggests adding w to the half sizes and cells.
corestone.range: Density, not centred: -0.022 to 1.0 over 8 seeds and offsets, with air at the -0.9 * Jy clamp times gain, so iso 0 is the only sensible threshold and -0.022 is a very small margin. No NaN or Inf. Far coords probe sits in the air above the surface (flat -0.023), which is expected for a height based density.
corestone.artifacts: No jumps. Floaters are the unsolved flaw. Census on a 16 x 16 x 9 voxel grid at step 0.1, 6-connected, pieces not touching the box sides: default 27, 20, 10 interior floaters on seeds 1337, 7, 99 (1.67%, 1.06%, 0.37% of solid), one small stone is visible floating in the frames. Causes: stones meeting only at rounded corners, or the upper stone landing on a lower stone's inset rim. flat=1 cuts these to 13, 9, 4; flat=1,Inset=0.05 to 10, 3, 2 (0.82%, 0.27%, 0.07%). Rho=1 marbles are much worse at 109 floaters (7.05%), as expected for spheres. The support check from the entry made no difference in the census, identical numbers in heightfield and 3D density: one bed lower S always passes, so it is off by default. Cut faces show thin joint lines that fade out downward into the deep rock. The lattice is one global direction per node, softened only by warp.

Members: Source S (GeneratorSource, 2 evals per lane, solid where positive), Bed Height, Block Length X, Block Length Z, Thickness Jitter, Length Jitter, Shell, Joint Min, Joint Max, Bed Joint, Roundness, Inset, Keep, Loss, Loss Frequency, Block Jitter, Flat Contact bool, Weather (hybrid). Warp left to an upstream DomainWarp only if S is not warped with it; otherwise a small internal warp is simpler.
corestone.port_notes: Edge search per axis uses 4 hashes with Selects: e(i), e(i+1), then one of e(i-1), e(i+2). Three axes make 12 hashes, more than the entry's 2, since jittered edges are what stop it reading as masonry; dropping jitter on one axis saves 4. No window, no loop. S at the block centre is a second Source eval at per lane positions, which Gen allows. Clamp value and smooth max as written. The prototype's branch on c < e0 becomes Select.

master.one_liner: Tors and boulder stacks: joint blocks that fit together, whose joints open and whose corners round as they near the surface of a density, and which are kept or lost whole, so the ground ends in stacked rounded loaves rather than a cut surface.
master.look: 3D: Dartmoor tors, Joshua Tree piles, balanced rocks. Rounded rectangular loaves stacked in courses, tight and angular a little below the surface, wider apart and rounder at the top, sitting on solid rock with no seam. Flat contact faces between stones, which random scatters never have. In motion, Weather rising: a front moves inward, joints open, corners round, loaves shrink and vanish one at a time; no fade. Judge from stills: vol at three Weather values, and a vertical cut showing joint width grading with depth.
master.algorithm:
Beds k = floor(y/Hy + warp1D(y)), with per bed thickness jitter. In bed k: (u,v) = (x,z) + offset(hash(k)); cell = floor((u,v)/(Lx,Lz)); h = hash(cell,k); cb = block centre; b = half size.
s = S(p); sc = S(cb); optional keep test also on S(cb - Hk*up) so a block needs one below it
w = sat((Shell - s)/Shell)   // 0 deep, 1 at or above the surface; Weather hybrid scales Shell
g = J0 + J1*w            // depends only on p, so both sides of a joint agree
rho = Rho*w*(0.6 + 0.8*rnd(h,2)); ins = Inset*w*rnd(h,3)
q = |p - cb| - (b - g - ins - rho)
d = |Max(q,0)| + Min(MaxComp(q),0) - rho   // rounded box
a = Max(-d, -0.9*g)      // on any cell face d >= g, so a = -0.9*g from both sides
a = Select(sc > Keep, a, -0.9*g)
out = SmoothMax(a, s - Shell, k)   // deep rock is seamless, joints exist only in the weathered shell
Variants: Rho large gives Devil's Marbles spheres; vertical prismatic lattice with Hy large gives columnar joints that fray at the top.
master.why_new: Nearest are GroundedScatter and BoulderField3D, which place independent stones that overlap and sit on a surface. JointBlocks (crossbreed 28) gives a block value field with offsets but no weathering; TileDomain's Brick volume has constant mortar. The new part is the depth grading: block shape is a function of distance from the surface, with whole-block keep, so the surface is made of blocks instead of cutting them. The stock graph cannot do whole-block keep and per-lane rounding together.
master.simd_plan: 2 or 3 S evals, 2 hashes, one sqrt. No window. On a 3 octave density about 3*6.6 + 3 = 23 ns (estimate). 2D is a vertical section, rounded rectangles. 4D adds w to the block half sizes and to the cell.
master.continuity: C0, proved in the algorithm: the clamp makes both sides of a cell face equal -0.9*g, including for removed blocks. Where g = J0 is small the surface there is the plain joint, and the deep term covers it.
master.params: Source S, Lx, Lz, Hy, Thickness Jitter, Shell, J0, J1, Rho, Inset, Keep, Support Check. Hybrid: Weather.
master.risks: Straight long joints read as a wall, so a low frequency warp is needed, and that shears rounded blocks a little. With an overhanging S a whole block can be left hanging; the support check handles only one level. One global lattice direction per node.

Beds, rows and blocks have exact jittered edges, in place of the warp1D floor. Whole block keep uses a low frequency loss noise plus a small per block term, instead of a test on S alone; this makes tors stand above the surface in clusters and loses tops first. Weather also scales w and raises Keep. Added flat=1, a rounded rectangle extruded with a small edge radius, which keeps real flat contact.

master.one_liner: BSP cuts in Penrose rhomb coordinates: an aperiodic shattered paving with no Voronoi root.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: cracked Penrose floor, aperiodic broken glass.
master.algorithm: 1) Locate the rhomb containing p with the quasi-tile de Bruijn candidate loop (fixed count, N=5 default): get its integer index 5-tuple K, its two edge directions e_a, e_b and its lowest corner c. 2) h = hash(seed, K). 3) Express p in rhomb-local coords (u,v) = inverse of the 2x2 [e_a e_b] applied to p - c, so the rhomb is the unit square. 4) For level L = 1..Levels (int member): pick a cut line from bits of hash(h, L): a point q_L inside the current sub-cell and a direction with angle from the same hash; sub-cell for the next level = the side of q_L that p is on (bitmask select), tracked as an axis-aligned box in (u,v) exactly as shatter-bsp tracks its sub-cell centre. Cut distance d_L = |(p_uv - q_L) . n_L| masked by whether p projects inside the sub-cell segment. 5) Edge distance d_e = min(u, 1-u, v, 1-v) scaled by the rhomb heights (|e_a x e_b|) to world units. 6) Output: Crack = min(d_e, min over L of d_L * childWidthScale^L), LeafValue = rnd11(hash of final sub-cell id), TileType = thick/thin. All loops have a fixed count; no neighbour lookup beyond the quasi-tile candidate set. 3D: same with the rhombohedron candidate set and plane cuts.
master.why_new: Shatter-bsp needs a Voronoi root only to be isotropic; a Penrose rhomb root is already isotropic, has exactly two tile shapes, and gives an aperiodic shattered paving (cracked Penrose floor, aperiodic broken glass) that neither parent makes. Also removes shatter-bsp's 3x3 Voronoi cost in 2D.
master.simd_plan: Not stated by the panel. Seed: cost of quasi-tile plus levels. All loops have a fixed count and there is no neighbour lookup beyond the quasi-tile candidate set.
master.continuity: Not stated by the panel.

Seed risk 0.5: cost of quasi-tile plus levels.
Noticed in merge: step 5 scales the edge distance to world units but cut distance d_L stays in rhomb (u,v) coordinates, so cut width shears with the rhomb and differs between thick and thin tiles.

master.one_liner: Exposes each Penrose rhomb's local coordinates to a Source under mortar: a Penrose parquet.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: twill, boards or strokes running along each rhomb's edges: a Penrose parquet floor.
master.algorithm: Locate the rhomb exactly as QuasiTile does: N=5 gives 10 family pairs x 4 candidates = 40 fixed tests, all evaluated, selected with masks. Winner has pair (j,k) and integer indices. Solve pos = o + u*e_j + v*e_k with a precomputed 2x2 inverse per pair, giving (u,v) in [0,1]. edge = min(u, 1-u, v, 1-v) * edgeScale[j,k]. val = Source.Gen(seed ^ tilehash * PerTile, u*S, v*S) once per lane, with S from a per-pair table. out = lerp(Mortar, val, smoothstep(0, Bevel, edge)), so the jump between rhombs is hidden under mortar and output stays continuous. 3D: 6 families with a 3x3 inverse table per triple; the candidate count grows, so it is hero only there. Cost: critic measured 433 ns scalar (8.2x perlin2) for the locate alone. AVX2 unknown; no port exists.
master.why_new: The nested hex herringbone discovery shows tiles-inside-tiles working, and quasi-tile has the best layout in the set. Exposing each rhomb's local coordinates lets twill, boards or strokes run along its edges: a Penrose parquet floor. Not built; the look is a prediction.

master.one_liner: A 5 or 7 family over-under weave from multigrid line families, with no square repeat.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: quasiperiodic basketry, Penrose-like lattice work, kagome at N=3. Crossings of many families may read as a mess.
master.algorithm: 1) For each family j in 0..N-1 (N an int member, fixed loop): t_j = e_j . p + gamma_j; k_j = Floor(t_j); f_j = t_j - k_j (phase across the strip). 2) Thread profile per family: s_j = ThreadProfile(|f_j - 0.5| / ThreadWidth) (round or smooth, as Textile). 3) Over/under rule: parity P_j = (sum over i != j of k_i + j) mod 2, computed with integer adds and an AND; height h_j = s_j * (P_j ? +1 : -1) * Select(s_j > 0). 4) At a crossing several threads overlap; output = thread with the largest (h_j + s_j*Bias) by a fixed max over the N families, which keeps the winner's own profile (no blending, same discontinuity class as Textile's weave). Soft output: smooth-max with Smoothness. 5) Tone output: hash(j, k_j) for per-thread colour. 3D: Textile's extrusion rule on the two nearest families only. Cost: O(N) adds and one profile each, no window; estimate under 2x Perlin at N=5 (unmeasured).
master.why_new: Textile's weave is locked to two axis families and the level-set-weave discovery showed arbitrary A/B coordinates work. Multigrid already yields N line families with integer indices and fractional phases pointwise, so a 5- or 7-family over/under weave (quasiperiodic basketry, Penrose-like lattice work, kagome at N=3) falls out with no new search and no square repeat.
master.simd_plan: Cost: O(N) adds and one profile each, no window; estimate under 2x Perlin at N=5 (unmeasured).
master.continuity: 4) At a crossing several threads overlap; output = thread with the largest (h_j + s_j*Bias) by a fixed max over the N families, which keeps the winner's own profile (no blending, same discontinuity class as Textile's weave).

master.risks:
Seed risk 0.5: crossings of many families may read as a mess.
Noticed in merge: the parity rule does not define over and under at every crossing. For threads j and i, P_j and P_i differ only when (k_i + k_j + i + j) is odd, so at about half of all crossings both threads get the same sign and the winner is decided by profile height, not by a weave rule. knotwork-interlace derives a rule that does alternate.

quasi-weave.changed_from_entry: Replaced the entry's parity rule, which the test shows is wrong, walks every thread in an 80 x 80 region. Entry rule: both threads get the same sign at 50.0% of crossings at N=3, 5 and 7, and 91.6% to 100% of consecutive crossing pairs along a thread are not alternating or undefined. Derived rule, the checkerboard rule with sign of the edge cross product, gives 0 non-alternating pairs out of 32939 to 195607 at N=3, 5, 7 over two seeds. Parity is read at the crossing point, not at the sample as the entry's and KnotworkInterlace's sample rules do, so it never flips near a third thread; Height is exactly C0 and needs no winner-by-profile. Height is a Max of T(d) times a lift that sums over all crossing threads, instead of the entry's largest thread pick. Under dive is stronger than over lift so gaps read. 3D uses tubes with the same lift rather than an extruded two-family rule.

Rings mode reads as interlaced circles or loose chain links with clean over-under. Relief is cords on a floor, low walls with clear crossings. The volume shows separate curving tubes in plies, like wire or roots; the ply gaps show as layers.

Threads above 0 with large gradients can make strands crowd and merge, and Threads renders at low frequency looked like sparse wire. Mean around -0.4 since holes dominate. master.one_liner: Celtic knotwork from N arbitrary curve families: every strand truly alternates over and under, guaranteed by the checkerboard rule for alternating diagrams, with world-unit strand width.
master.look: Closed interlaced loops of constant width, each passing alternately over and under, with irregular curved holes: free-form Celtic knotwork, wicker, tangled ribbons, woven kelp, tree roots seen from above. With Threads above about 3 and 2 families it should converge on a corrected LevelSetWeave. Rings mode is the woven Worley look with single loops instead of concentric bands.
master.algorithm:
SHARED CAUSE. Phason parity weave, wave sign parity, soft parity chrome, woven Worley rings and two noise strands all show the same fact: the parity of the sign bits of N fields is a valid 2-colouring of their zero-set arrangement however far the lines bend. A valid 2-colouring is exactly what is needed to make any curve arrangement an alternating link diagram (Tait; from memory, not looked up). LevelSetWeave uses parity only: it has no orientation term, so it goes non-alternating where A and B fold, and only handles two fields.

RULE, derived here. Let c = cross(grad f_a, grad f_b) at a crossing of strand a and strand b. Rotating strand a counterclockwise sweeps the quadrants where sign(f_a)*sign(f_b) = -sign(c). Choose all crossings so that the swept quadrants have region parity +1. Then a is over b iff P_ab * (-1)^(j_a+j_b) * sign(c) = -1, where P_ab is the parity of every other family and j is the strand index inside a family.

PER LANE, for m in 0..N-1 (N 3 to 4, 3 channels from one Perlin visit with the value term so strands avoid the shared lattice zeros):
  (A_m, g_m) = channel m; u_m = Threads*A_m + phi_m; j_m = Round(u_m); e = u_m - j_m
  d_m = |e| / (Threads*|g_m| + floor)       // world-unit distance to nearest strand of family m
  b_m = Floor(u_m) & 1;  par ^= b_m
Find nearest two families a, b by a fixed min network (pair is unordered, so a swap changes nothing).
sigma = -(1 - 2*(par ^ b_a ^ b_b ^ ((j_a + j_b) & 1))) * c / sqrt(c*c + eps*eps)   // sigma > 0: a is over. Smooth in c so tangencies do not jump
prox(d) = smoothstep(Wc, 0, d), T(d) = sqrt(max(0, 1 - (d/W)^2)), Wc >= W
h_a = T(d_a) + sigma*Lift*prox(d_b)
h_b = T(d_b) - sigma*Lift*prox(d_a)
Out = Max(h_a, h_b, Base). Mask output: also multiply the lower strand by (1 - Gap*prox_edge(d_top)) so it breaks visibly at the crossing, the classic knotwork gap.
Threads = 0 means one strand per field: u = A, strand at A = 0, b = A<0. Field enum: Noise, or Rings (f = F1 - R with Worley, gradient is the unit vector) for interlaced circles.
3D and 4D: c is the component of the wedge along the view plane: in 3D (g_a x g_b).Up; in 4D the image-plane wedge from the torus tangents recovered as in the torus-angle-wrapped lattice discovery, so tiling stays alternating.
master.why_new: Different output. Textile with hybrid A, B (level-set-weave) is the nearest: it is limited to 2 fields, its width follows the gradient, and it alternates wrongly at folds. triaxial-weave has 3 families but straight strands. truchet-noise and Penrose worms have no over-under. Nothing here gives a provably alternating diagram over arbitrary curves.
master.simd_plan: All masks and Select. Fixed N, a fixed sort network for two smallest with indices. One multi-channel Perlin visit (GradientNoise::PerlinKernel with valueAmp, as TubeNoise uses) per 3 channels. Estimates AVX2: 8 / 14 / 25 ns. No hash window. 3D is a stack of 2D diagrams that morphs along Up, not a volumetric weave; that is honest and needs saying in the node's description.
master.continuity: C0 except at triple proximities, where a third strand comes within Wc of a crossing: the pair can change there and step by up to 2*Lift. Track three nearest if it shows. Across every other event the terms it switches are already zero: prox vanishes at Wc, T vanishes at W, sigma vanishes at c = 0.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, int Families (3), Field enum, Output (Height, Mask, Strand Id, Distance), Up Axis. Hybrid: Threads, Width, Lift, Gap.
master.risks: Zero lines of one symmetric noise are long meanders and small rings, so crossing density may be uneven, and strands may look like worms if Width is low. Strands crowd and merge where |g| is large with Threads above 0. Sign errors in the rule are easy to make, hence the walking test.

A first test run reported 0.5%: those were test errors from reading a third strand on the wrong side inside one walk step, and they fell with the step and vanished once crossings were interpolated. Under dive is larger than over lift, and the flat ribbon profile replaced sqrt. 3D default is a tube mat rather than a stack of diagrams, which the volume shows is the better form; morph=1 keeps the entry's form.
