truchet-knot.look: Saw clean Celtic interlace: round straps with a carved centre groove, joined by quarter arcs into closed loops of many sizes, breaking cleanly under each over strap with a dark gap. pcross 0.25 gives meanders and rings with few crossings, 0.55 is the knotwork, 0.95 becomes a plain basket weave. The plain form is visibly locked to the square lattice: straight runs, axis cross in the FFT, axis ratio 206. With warp=1.2 it turns hand drawn and woven, the strongest look of the set, though strap width then varies with the warp. Relief reads as carved or embossed leather. Volume shows smooth separate tubes that really pass over and under one another.
truchet-knot.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D is real tubes that rise and dive by a bump along each strand at crossing tiles, with plies repeating along z and their own hash. The check command's z=0.5 plane falls between plies and reads constant -1, not a fault. 4D not built, the plan is to pass w to the hash for plies; tile lattice would not tile through GenTileable2D.
truchet-knot.artifacts: Height has no jumps at any tested setting. Lattice lock is the honest limit, as the entry warned: axis 206 at warp 0. Strap width is not constant through an upstream warp. Mask and OverUnder jump by design. Tone (out=4) jumps per tile. Seed sensitivity is low (mean 0.171) since every seed has the same grid, with different tile choices.
truchet-knot.node_shape: TruchetKnot: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, hybrid P Cross (read at tile centre), Strap Width, Over Lift, Under Dive, Dip Width, Groove, Groove Width, enum Output {Height, Mask, OverUnder, Interior, Tone}, Tube Amp for 3D, Ply Height. Output Min/Max. Could also be a Crossing option on TruchetNoise.
truchet-knot.port_notes: One hash, one tile, no window. Crossing and arc branches both compute, then Select. Cos for the bump can be a polynomial on along, or smoothstep. Over bit is ( i + j ) & 1 with Select per strand. The tile decision uses the first hash bits; A or B uses a separate bit. Bump is zero on tile edges, so height matches across tiles without any neighbour lookup.

master.one_liner: TruchetFlow's arc tiles plus a crossing tile, with TriaxialWeave's consistent over-under: checkerboard parity at the crossings makes an alternating knot diagram, so the tiling becomes Celtic interlace, plaitwork and chain mail with real over-under straps.
master.look: P Cross 0: TruchetNoise's meanders. P Cross around 0.5: Celtic knotwork, interlaced straps that loop and weave with every crossing alternating, closed loops of many sizes. P Cross 1: plaitwork or a basket plait, and with Gap a sheet of chain mail. Relief is a convincing embossed leather or carved wood interlace; Interior with a fibre source gives woven cord. Threshold is a clean knot diagram.
master.algorithm: Square tiles (hex optional later). Tile (i,j) hash picks a type with probabilities from P Cross (hybrid, read at the tile centre): A = arcs N-E and S-W (quarter circles of radius 0.5 about the NE and SW corners), B = arcs N-W and S-E, X = straight strands N-S and E-W crossing at the centre. Each tile has two strands s0, s1; per strand compute the distance d (arc: | |p - corner| - 0.5 |, straight: |p.x - 0.5| or |p.y - 0.5|) in tile-local coordinates and a strand orientation class: in A/B tiles a strand entering from N or S is class V and the other class H (they never cross); in X tiles s0 = V, s1 = H. Over rule at X tiles: V is over when (i + j) is even, H is over when odd; along any strand the orientation class flips at every arc tile and the parity flips at every tile step, so consecutive crossings of one strand alternate over and under (the standard Truchet-knot construction). Strap profile h(d) = max(0, 1 - (d/HW)^2)^Shape; for the under strand multiply by dip(d_over) = smoothstep(HW, 2*HW, d_over) so it visibly passes beneath. Height = max(h_over, h_under*dip). Strands of neighbouring tiles meet at edge midpoints with matching tangents (perpendicular to the edge) by construction, so no per-sample window is needed: one tile (window 1^2). Outputs: Height, Mask (union of straps), OverUnder (+1 over, -1 under, 0 off), and Interior as in TruchetFlow: the Source sampled at (along, across) where along is the arc angle times 0.5 or the straight coordinate, across is d, for strap texture. 3D: the 2D knot in xy extruded as a solid of thickness Height around z=0 (an interlaced strap slab), or applied on each z-slab with a hashed offset for a stack; the 4D form drops w.
master.why_new: TruchetNoise and TruchetFlow (keeper) have no crossings and no over-under, so they cannot interlace; Textile (ship) and TriaxialWeave (keeper) weave straight families only; LevelSetWeave weaves two fields but cannot make closed interlaced loops. The over-under needs the tile parity and the strand class inside the same kernel as the arc distances. Known in the shader and recreational-maths community (Truchet knots), new here.
master.simd_plan: One hash per sample, 2 arc distances (one sqrt each) or 2 abs, a few Selects for type and class, two smoothsteps. No window. Estimated AVX2 2D 2-3 ns, 3D about the same plus the slab test. Cheapest idea in this file.
master.continuity: Height is C0 (profiles reach zero at the strap edge, strands match across tile edges with matching tangents, the dip is a smooth function of the other strand's distance); Mask and OverUnder are discontinuous by design. Interior is C0 along a strand and jumps between strands, like TruchetFlow.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, P Cross (hybrid), Strap Width, Shape (float), Dip Width, Gap (space between parallel straps, lets straps read as separate cords), Output enum {Height, Mask, OverUnder, Interior}, Source (for Interior), Output Min/Max.
master.risks: The alternation argument assumes every crossing is at an X tile centre with straight strands; adding curved crossing tiles would need the same class bookkeeping. On a square grid the pattern is lattice-locked by nature; a TruchetFlow-style pre-warp or hex tiles are the way to loosen it, and the hex version needs a three-strand tile set and a different parity rule.

braid-plait.look: Saw it pass the smallest test: L=3,P=1 reads at once as a hair braid, thick strands with long fibre streaks swinging over and under in an S. L=0 is a tight diagonal plait like cane or a cable knit sleeve. L=12,P=0.6 is a loose rope mat with some long straight runs, closer to a material than a diagram but still tidy and vertical. Per strand tone at L=3 lets one dark strand be followed through the braid. Relief is a chunky rope or carved plait. Volume shows fat real tubes passing around each other, clearly plaited, with the ply cut showing as flat orange ends.
braid-plait.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D is real tubes that swing lanes and rise and dive, plies along z with their own hash; z-continuity mean 0.0021, max 0.0033 for dz=1e-3. 4D not built, the plan in the entry is to scroll the row hash with w.
braid-plait.artifacts: Height has no jumps. With mode=1 a strand that goes under twice in a row surfaces between the two crossings as a small round blob, visible; this is correct for that diagram but looks spotty, so Alternating is better. Strands stay vertical, so the look needs an upstream warp or rotation to escape its axis (axis ratio 57.7). Below P=1 per strand tone falls back to a per row hash, so it changes along a strand. Default is periodic along y for a band: seed only shifts the row phase per band.

Its natural home is a third Structure in Textile next to Weave and Knit, sharing Profile and Fibre, as the entry guessed; it does not share Textile's cell kernel.

Strand identity at P=1 is integer arithmetic only. Band row phase is one hash per band. Width correction costs one sqrt per candidate; a table on t or a polynomial would do.

master.one_liner: Random braid-group words drawn as a texture: strands in lanes, rows of hashed adjacent crossings under the brick rule, so strands change lanes and pass over or under, giving plaits, cable knit and in 3D solid braided rope; probably a Structure mode of Textile.
master.look: A plait: strands that run straight, then swing one lane sideways in a smooth S and pass over or under a neighbour, with random crossings giving a loose, hand-done braid and P = 1 giving the regular hair braid or a cable-knit rib. In 3D a solid braided rope or cable with visible lay. Tiled through TileDomain it becomes braided trim, basket rims and rope borders.
master.algorithm:
Lanes L (Strands), rows of unit height along y, lanes of unit width along x, strand width W, crossing probability P.
  r = Floor(y); t = y - r; k0 = Floor(x)
  for each candidate lane k in {k0-1, k0, k0+1} (the strand that starts row r in lane k):
    pair = k - ((k - r) & 1)   brick rule: in row r the crossing pairs are (pair, pair+1) with pair = r mod 2, so every strand is in at most one crossing per row and crossings never overlap
    crossing = rnd01(hash(r, pair)) < P and 0 <= pair and pair + 1 < L   (Periodic enum wraps the lanes for a round rope; Full mode forces P = 1 for the classic plait: a 3-lane plait with P = 1 is the hair braid sigma1 sigma2^-1 ...)
    dir = (k == pair) ? +1 : -1
    xs = k + 0.5 + Select(crossing, dir*S(t), 0), S(t) = smoothstep(t) so strands never kink
    over = (rnd01(hash(r, pair, 1)) < 0.5) xor (k == pair)   handedness per crossing (Alternating enum makes every crossing alternate like a real plait)
    depth = Select(crossing, (over ? +1 : -1)*sin(pi t), 0)
    d = |x - xs|; cover = d < W/2
    keep the covering strand with the largest depth (two compares)
  out = Select(any cover, profile(2d/W)*(1 + Shade*depth), Gap), profile = sqrt(1 - s^2) for a round strand, with fibre streaks from a 1D noise along the strand if wanted.
3D: strands are tubes: zs = depth*Amp; d = sqrt((x - xs)^2 + (z - zs)^2); out = Radius - d, an SDF of a plaited cable, rope or hair braid; w can scroll the row hash for a loop.
Strand identity across rows is not pointwise (it is the product of the row permutations), so colour is per strand segment or single-tone; a 2-colour alternation by lane parity swaps at every crossing and should not be offered.
master.why_new: Textile covers weaves (threads keep their lanes) and knits (loops); triaxial-weave covers kagome. A braid is the third textile structure: strands permute lanes, which neither of those can express, and the brick rule plus a per-row hash is all it costs. Nearest look: Textile twill at a glance, but every strand wanders.
master.simd_plan: Three candidates, each a hash, a smoothstep, a Sin and a handful of flops, then two compares: ~3-4 ns 2D, ~5 ns 3D. No window beyond the three lanes; branch free; 4D by scrolling the row hash with w.
master.continuity: C0 within a strand; the winner switch at a crossing gives the over/under step that every textile node has; the S-curve is C1 so strands do not kink.
master.params: Strands L (int), Crossing Probability P (hybrid), Width W (hybrid), Shade, Amp (3D depth), Mode enum {Random, Full, Alternating}, Periodic (enum), Gap value, fibre noise amount, Feature Scale, Seed.
master.risks: Without strand identity, long-range colouring is impossible; random crossings at low P look like wires rather than a braid; the strand profile needs the same fibre shading Textile already has to look good.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, no port: 3-4 ns in 2D and about 5 ns in 3D, as the entry guessed: three candidates, each a hash, a Sin and a sqrt. Scalar measured 163.4 ns, perlin2 about 55 ns.

braid-plait.changed_from_entry: Corrected a limit the entry stated: strand identity IS pointwise at P=1, unfold the bounce with q = k or 2L-1-k and q - r names the strand, so per strand tone works in the regular plait, used in out=1. The test follows strands for 2000 rows at L=3, 5, 8 and 0: 0 name changes along a strand, and exactly L names when L > 0. Shown that Alternating works at any P: every row has one strand per lane, so lane gaps give a checkerboard, and the rule is r parity by the brick rule. Tested: 0 non-alternating of 272665 to 1599600 pairs per run over L=3, 8, 0 and P=1, 0.6, 0.25, against about 50% for Random. Measured width across the strand (d / sqrt(1 + slope^2)) so the swing keeps its width. Height is a Max of C0 terms rather than the entry's winner by depth, which removes the entry's over-under step. Added Band Gap with a per band row phase, since P=1 otherwise has no seed dependence at all (seed sensitivity read 0.000 before this, 0.161 after).

origin.smallest_test: L = 3, P = 1, Alternating: it must look like a hair braid. Then L = 12, P = 0.5, Random, and judge whether loose random plaits read as a material (cable sweaters, rope mats) or as a diagram.
origin.confidence: medium-high for the look (it is constructive); medium for being worth more than a mode of Textile.

dual-mesh-weave.look: Saw what the entry feared: two nets drawn on top of each other. Star shaped rods meet at each vertex with 6 or more spokes, and short polygon rails wander between them. The crossings are there, with a small break where one passes under, but at this density the eye reads a tangle of twigs or cracks, not a weave or a lashed trellis. The short tie form reads as rods with tick marks and some floating ticks. Region is dark polygons cut by spokes with smeared bright patches. Relief is a low fussy mesh and adds little. The 3D volume is the one strong result: a cage of pale curved looking plates and rods, like an organic scaffold or bone, with visible stair stepping on near flat plates at this ray step.
dual-mesh-weave.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D is a different structure, plates pierced by rods, on Kuhn tets with J clamped to 0.33; z-continuity mean 0.0067, max 0.0396 for dz=1e-3. 4D not built.
dual-mesh-weave.artifacts: No jumps in Height or Region. RodRail (out=2) jumps by design. Stair stepping on plates comes from sampling, steep plate sides at this step. Lattice rhythm of the jittered grid shows as vertices of regular spacing. Rods at a vertex overlap into a star hub, which hides the over-under near the vertices. The 3D volume is also.

Every edge costs 2 segment distances and a radial distance. The 3D rod loop uses a static table of 98 unique Kuhn edges, a squared distance per edge, one sqrt at the end.

master.one_liner: CellularDualMesh's two edge sets woven together: every Delaunay rod crosses exactly its own dual wall once, so a hashed over-under per pair is always consistent, giving a random lashed trellis of straight rods and polygon rails.
master.look: A random trellis: a triangle net of straight rods lashed to a polygon net of short rails, each rod tied where it crosses its rail, with the rails over some rods and under others. Reads as a wattle fence, bamboo scaffold lashings, a garden trellis, or a random kagome; thresholded it is a dense two-family lattice with small triangular and kite holes. In relief the lashings stand out as knots. 3D volume is a cage of polygon plates skewered by rods.
master.algorithm: From t_cellular_dual_mesh: the 3x3 corner window, 8 locally Delaunay triangles, per triangle the three half walls (centroid G to edge midpoints M_ab) and, new, the three primal edges (a, b) as capsule strands. For each primal edge (a, b) with symmetric pair hash he: the primal rod is the segment a-b; its dual rail is the union of the two half walls meeting at M_ab from the two triangles sharing the edge; they cross at M_ab (the rail is perpendicular-ish to the rod there because the centroid dual wall passes through the edge midpoint). Over bit = he & 1: rod over rail or rail over rod at that crossing. Each rod has exactly one crossing (with its own rail) and each rail segment pair has exactly one crossing (with its own rod), so there is no alternation constraint to satisfy and any bit assignment is a valid weave. Per sample: d_rod = min over the 8 triangles' edges of segDist minus rod width (each edge appears in two triangles, fine for min); d_rail = min over half walls minus rail width; at the crossing the under strand is dipped: h = max(h_rod * dip_rod, h_rail * dip_rail) where dip_rod = over_bit ? 1 : smoothstep(W, 2W, d_rail_of_the_same_pair) and vice versa; this needs the pair-local distances, so the dip is computed per edge inside the loop before the min, keeping (h_over, h_under) per candidate and taking the max of the two heights over candidates. Window reach as the proto (margin (1-J)/2) clamps distances for C0. Outputs: Height, Mask, RodRail (+1 rod, -1 rail), Region value (per polygon, from the proto). 3D: Delaunay edges of the Kuhn tets are rods and dual faces are plates; a rod pierces its own dual face once, so the over-under becomes a pierced plate (a hole where the rod passes): a cage of plates skewered by rods, same bookkeeping.
master.why_new: CellularDualMesh (keeper) draws only the dual walls (with removal and width); TriaxialWeave (keeper) weaves straight families only; BondGraph has no second family; the woven Worley rings discovery weaves two fields but with no explicit crossings. The pairing of a rod with the one rail it crosses is a property of the dual mesh that only exists inside its kernel.
master.simd_plan: The proto's 8-triangle loop with 3 extra capsule distances per triangle and one smoothstep per edge; all fixed, masks only. Estimated AVX2: 2D 15-20 ns, 3D 50-80 ns with the plate-and-rod form (48 tets).
master.continuity: Height is C0 (capsule profiles reach zero, clamped at the window reach as the proto, dips are smooth functions of distances); Mask and RodRail are discontinuous by design.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Rod Width, Rail Width, Width Jitter, Dip Width, Rod Density, Rail Density (per-pair presence as the proto's density), Output enum {Height, Mask, RodRail, Region}, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: The honest doubt is the look: two superimposed nets may just look busy. The crossing is near, not exactly at, a right angle and not at the rod's centre for skewed triangles, so ties can look misplaced. Lattice rhythm of the jittered grid shows in the rods, as in DualMesh.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate from the entry, no port: 15-20 ns in 2D, 50-80 ns in 3D. Scalar measured in 2D only: win=3 543.1 ns, win=4 1144.6 ns, perlin2 about 51 ns. 3D speed not measured.

dual-mesh-weave.changed_from_entry: Dip is radial about M_ab rather than from the rail distance. The rail's two half walls live in two triangles, and one triangle cannot read the partner half, so a rail distance would not dip the rod consistently; radial agrees across both triangles. Added Lash, the entry's suggestion taken further: rails shrunk to ties around the crossing. 3D uses a unique edge table instead of per tet edges. hinge-tile.look: Saw a working mechanism. In the angle sweep, triangles start as kagome with hexagon holes, twist into pinwheels and stars, and close to a clean triangular floor at the top of the range. Driven by noise, a patch of closed triangle floor bursts into open star holes, which reads as expanded metal or a kirigami sheet flexing. Squares go from a close fitting grid to a checker of diamonds, and a gradient reads as a sheet being stretched open. Corner contact holds where the angle is steady; where Opening changes fast, gaps appear between neighbours, as predicted. Source in frame carries fbm per plate clearly, and each plate turns with its texture. Relief reads as chunky hinged plates at varied heights. The volume is stacked slabs of pivoting plates, tidy and plain.
hinge-tile.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 3D is the plain form the entry expected: plates in slabs, each with its own seed and the checker flipped, not a true 3D mechanism. 4D would pass through the extra axis, not built.
hinge-tile.artifacts: No jumps at any tested setting. Lattice is plain and periodic, with an axis cross, axis ratio 37.95. HoleMask (out=1) jumps by design. Fast changing Opening leaves visible corner mismatch rather than overlap, because each tile always fits its own cell. It looks manufactured by nature.
hinge-tile.node_shape: Two new Patterns on TileDomain, {Rotating Squares, Rotating Triangles}, plus a hybrid Opening read at the tile centre. TileDomain's current Rotation enum is discrete and cannot hold the corner relation, so this needs Opening as a real member. Output {Bevel, Hole Mask, Source in Frame}, as TileDomain has. As a separate node: Lattice, Opening, Bevel, Gap Value, Height Jitter, Source.
hinge-tile.port_notes: One cell, no search or window. Sin and Cos of Opening per lane when it varies, a pair of constants when it does not. Triangles locate by a simplex style skew and one compare. The hybrid must read at the cell centre, so one extra source evaluation per lane at another position, which the execution model allows. Tile fit does not depend on neighbours' angles, which is why a fast Opening gives gaps and never a seam.

master.one_liner: Auxetic and kirigami hinge tilings as a tile frame: rigid squares or triangles that stay touching at corners while a hybrid opening angle spreads them apart, giving rhomb and star holes that open across a map, and carrying any source in each tile's frame.
master.look: Laser-cut metal or expanded panel where rigid plates pivot as you move across the image, holes opening from slits to diamonds; a parquet deformation. A gradient input gives a sheet being stretched open. A Simplex input gives patches of open mesh in closed plate. In relief, chunky hinged plates.
master.algorithm:
Rotating-square mechanisms are known from Grima and Evans 2000 and used for deployables by Konakovic-Lukovic et al. 2018 and IsoGami 2026. I read abstracts and snippets only; the geometry below is my own.
Squares: lattice pitch 1, cell c, f = p - c - 0.5; s = (-1)^(c.x + c.y); alpha = Opening(cell centre) in [0, pi/4]; a = 1/(cos(alpha) + sin(alpha))
q = Rot(s*alpha)*f; d = max(|q.x|, |q.y|) - a/2
A square of side a rotated by alpha has a bounding box exactly a*(cos + sin) = 1, so it fits its cell and needs no window, and its corners touch the neighbours' corners on cell edges when alpha matches. alpha = 0 is a closed floor, alpha = pi/4 is a checker of diamonds on square holes.
Triangles: honeycomb centres with neighbour distance D, opposite rotation on the two sublattices, circumradius rho = D/(2*cos(alpha)), alpha in [0, 30 degrees]; alpha = 0 is kagome, 30 degrees closes to a triangular floor.
Output: TileBevel = sat(-d/Bevel)*Height(hash), HoleMask, or Source(q*SourceScale + rnd(hash)) inside the tile, Gap value outside.
Hybrid read at the cell centre, one eval. With alpha varying, corners mismatch slightly; that is a gap, not a jump in any tile.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. TileDomain's Rotation enum is discrete, so it cannot hold the corner-touch relation. ChiralWallpaper keeps symmetry but makes no holes. PlateDrift rotates Voronoi plates but they do not touch or tile. Nearest graph: none, since rotation per cell with a matching size is not expressible.
master.simd_plan: One cell, 2 nodes in the rhomb for kagome, no search. sin and cos of alpha per lane, or a table when Opening is constant. 3D: columns stacked in slabs with a per-slab phase, which is honest but plain; real 3D rotating cubes are not a single-mechanism lattice. 4D: pass through. Estimate 2 ns plus hybrid in 2D.
master.continuity: Discontinuous at tile edges when Gap differs from the bevel's base value; C0 with bevel to Gap. A varying Opening does not create value jumps beyond those edges.
master.params: Lattice (Square, Kagome), Opening (hybrid at cell centre), Bevel, Gap Value, Source (hybrid, optional, read in tile frame), Height Jitter, Feature Scale. Could be a TileDomain Pattern and Rotation entry rather than a node.
master.risks: Reads as manufactured, so limited to a mode. A fast-changing Opening gives visible corner mismatch. Lattice is plain: rectangular periodic, unless warped upstream, and warping breaks rigidity. Likely verdict: mode of TileDomain, not a node.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate, no port: 2 ns plus the Opening source, as the entry guessed, at about 2 Perlin reads for the built in noise Opening. Scalar measured: triangles 249.2 ns, squares 268.6 ns, Source in frame 517.5 ns, constant Opening 152.0 and 162.0 ns, perlin2 about 51 ns. At constant Opening the ratio is 2.99.

hinge-tile.changed_from_entry: Corrected the triangle range: the entry says alpha in 0 to 30 degrees with 30 closing the floor. From rho = D / (2 cos alpha), rho = D, the closed floor's circumradius, needs cos alpha = 1/2, so it closes at 60 degrees. The sweep shows angle=0.5 (30 degrees) as half way, and the closed floor at angle=1 (60 degrees). Used a triangular tiling skew, whose cells are exactly the Voronoi cells of the honeycomb, to locate tiles. Default lattice is triangles since they gave the strongest image; squares stay at lat=0.

At a border whole pavers and pebbles stand proud of their neighbour, rock fills the low joints of the pavers, and sand fills first. Next to the hard label version, where borders slice straight through stones, the difference is obvious, and next to a plain soft fade, which shows ghosted double exposures of both materials, it is obvious too. Above lock 0.8 it turns to confetti, with stray stones far from the border; at tau 0.3 it turns back into a fade. The relief reads as broken slabs with rock and grass between them. The volume render at out=3 was nearly all cut face and showed nothing, so no the volume is kept.

height-foam.port_notes: Compact kernel w_k = Max(score_k - best + Depth, 0) needs no Exp, and is the exact N-way form of the HeightBlend parent's weights. All materials always evaluate. Weight per material must offset each material's mean height or the shares drift: measured shares went from 19 / 17 / 29 / 35 percent to 25.5 / 24.3 / 24.4 / 25.9 percent (out of a 1/4 target) after subtracting the means 0.42, 0.50, 0.75, 0.87. master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: up to four materials in curved foam regions; at a border pebbles stay whole and sand fills first.
master.algorithm:
FORM HeightFoam (artist-material lens): Four fixed GeneratorSource members H_0..H_3 and one Field source. Constant loop k=0..3: F_k = Field(p, seed + k*Stride); v_k = H_k(p); score_k = F_k + HeightLock*v_k + Weight_k. best = Max of score. w_k = Exp((score_k - best)/tau), normalised by their sum, with tau > 0; the subtraction stops overflow. Output enum Value = sum(w_k*v_k), Label (argmax, jumps by design), Margin (best minus second best). Continuous for tau > 0. All 8 evals always run, as the execution model requires. Same code for 2D, 3D and 4D if the sources tile. Cost ESTIMATE: 4 Perlin fields about 4.4 ns, 4 FS::Exp about 1 ns, plus the four materials. Honest rival: nested HeightBlends with a foam Margin as Control. Ship this only if that graph's borders look wrong.

FORM FoamBlend (maintainer lens): Evaluate K control fields c_k (K fixed int, one Source at K seed offsets, or K sources). a = argmax c_k, b = second, margin m = c_a - c_b >= 0 (continuous, zero on the border). Evaluate the two winning material sources S_a, S_b only (2 evals, selected per lane by masks over a fixed loop of the N materials: everything costs its worst case, so N materials = N evals in SIMD; document that). Blend w = SmoothStep((H_a + m * Gain) - H_b, Softness) with H the materials' own heights (their value, or a Height input); out = Lerp(S_b, S_a, w). Away from the border m is large and the winner dominates; on the border the height difference decides, so the seam follows the features. Discontinuity only where argmax changes, where m = 0 and w is decided by heights alone, which is continuous in H. Cost K + N source evals + a few ops (estimate).
master.why_new:
HeightFoam: Up to four ground materials competing in foam-shaped regions, with borders that follow the stones and cracks instead of fading across them. ExchangeFoam has the regions and HeightBlend has the border, but the graph needs many nested nodes. Not built, look unverified.
FoamBlend: exchange-foam gives the best region labels, height-blend gives the best material transition, and biome-blend failed because its borders were cell-scale scallops. Combining label margin with height-driven blending gives biome transitions where pebbles stay whole and sand fills first, from the K evals already paid.
Seed gap: biome borders that follow the stones.
master.simd_plan:
HeightFoam: Cost ESTIMATE: 4 Perlin fields about 4.4 ns, 4 FS::Exp about 1 ns, plus the four materials.
FoamBlend: Evaluate the two winning material sources S_a, S_b only (2 evals, selected per lane by masks over a fixed loop of the N materials: everything costs its worst case, so N materials = N evals in SIMD; document that). Cost K + N source evals + a few ops (estimate).
master.continuity:
HeightFoam: Output enum Value = sum(w_k*v_k), Label (argmax, jumps by design), Margin (best minus second best). Continuous for tau > 0.
FoamBlend: a = argmax c_k, b = second, margin m = c_a - c_b >= 0 (continuous, zero on the border). Away from the border m is large and the winner dominates; on the border the height difference decides, so the seam follows the features. Discontinuity only where argmax changes, where m = 0 and w is decided by heights alone, which is continuous in H.

foam-walls.look: Line art of even weight around organic, non-convex plates, with no polygons and no lattice in sight. In the same frame the naive margin wall shows fat black blobs where the top two fields run parallel and hairlines elsewhere. Plate output: stepped mesas, five levels with a shoulder at each crack, which read in the relief as flat stacked plateaus with cut cliffs. Winner output at oct=3 reads as cracked weathered rock, plates keeping their own relief. In 3D the out=6 shell is a real open-cell membrane foam of constant thickness, a look I have not seen from any earlier node. At oct=4 the outlines get crinkled and small closed loops appear; those loops are real label islands, not specks.

master.algorithm: Fixed loop k<K (default 5): (s_k, g_k) = Perlin value + analytic gradient at p + offset_k with seed + k*stride. Masked update of winner value s1, its gradient g1 and label. Second fixed loop over j<K: d = (s1 - s_j) * InvSqrt( |g1 - g_j|^2 + eps ); e = Min( e, Select( j==label, +large, d ) ). This is a min over all fields rather than a rank-2 pick, so there is no jump when rank 2 changes, and e reaches 0 from both sides at a winner change. Outputs: Wall smoothstep(e/W), Plate rnd11(hash(label)) lifted by bevel(e), Winner value under grout, all C0 except raw Label. Cost estimate: K * about 1.3x Perlin + K InvSqrt: about 8 / 16 / 30 ns (2D/3D/4D) at K=5, against 3N source taps for FD. Keep the per-field offset, since Perlin ties at vertices. Risk: specks where a field difference has a saddle near a tie, as FoamBlend v2 showed.

Cracks around non-convex organic plates with constant world-space width. Voronoi cannot do non-convex; Foam Margin blurs where the top two fields run parallel. Analytic gradients avoid FoamBlend's 3N evaluations. Not built: untested idea.

grained-regions.look: Stripe: a polycrystal zebra. Each curved region carries its own straight or slightly bent stripe direction, with a thin grey seam at constant width between regions. The wide view reads as dazzle camouflage with no visible lattice. Threshold shows a clean mosaic of striped patches. In 3D the stripes become stacks of plates in differently oriented blocks, like martensite or a cut Widmanstatten pattern. Contour: closed ring contours of the winner's field, with the walls almost lost among them; reads more as a topographic marble than as grains. Steerable form: patchwork of short brushed streaks, region borders soft and only just readable at fr=1.2 with tone; the ridged version showed visible horizontal lattice rows, so it stays off by default. The steerable form is far more expensive and less striking than the stripes.
grained-regions.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D range -1.000 to 1.000, z step 0.0297 at dz 1e-3). 4D not built. Stripe mode reads raw position, so it does not tile through 4D. Contour mode reads only the field values, so it can.

grained-regions.artifacts: No jumps. With K=5 there are only five directions per seed, so distant regions with the same label share a direction, which is visible as a limited palette if you look for it. Steerable form: a 2x2 corner window limits the aspect, because the k=0.5 eigenvalue floor from the parent applies, so grain stays short. The 3D slice has wide bands where a region's direction is nearly normal to the slice, which is correct and not an error.
grained-regions.node_shape: GrainStripes: K, Seed Stride, Field Octaves, Output {Stripe, Contour, Label}, Frequency, Bend (W), Gap Width, Contour Gain, per-label direction and phase hashed from seed. Share the walls' kernel with foam-walls: Distance is already computed there, and Stripe is one Cos plus a table lookup on top.
grained-regions.port_notes: The field and gap kernel is foam-walls. Stripes need one table lookup by label through masks, one Cos. The steerable form needs K(K-1)/2 InvSqrt (one per pair, the pair distance is symmetric in its denominator), a symmetric matrix accumulated with K FMAs per entry, and a 2^D corner octave. Blending projector matrices is far simpler than blending angles: the entry's normalise and its fallback at opposite angles both vanish, and the metric stays exactly trace preserving.

master.one_liner: Each exchange-foam region gets its own grain or stripe direction, giving polycrystal looks with curved grain boundaries and no lattice.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: metal grains, mineral thin-sections, brushed patchwork, a polycrystal zebra with curved grain boundaries. The gap at walls may read as cells.
master.algorithm:
FORM GrainedRegions (graphics-researcher lens): 1) Evaluate K label fields s_k (exchange-foam, with the per-field offset so no lattice ties), K a fixed int. 2) Winner w = argmax s_k and runner-up by a fixed max network; border weights per label from FoamBlend v2: d_k = max_j (s_j - s_k) / |grad s_j - grad s_k| using the fields' analytic or 3-tap gradients, weight a_k = smoothstep(1 - d_k / Width). 3) Direction vector v = normalise(sum_k a_k * (cos th_k, sin th_k)) with th_k = hash angle of label k; where |sum| is near zero (opposite angles) fall back to isotropic by the same |v|-weighted anisotropy as CurlSteeredGrain. 4) Evaluate steerable-perlin octaves with direction v and Aspect; output grain, or Label, or grain + label tone. 5) Vector-blending angles means grain rotates smoothly through borders instead of popping. 3D: angle pairs per label, same blend. Cost: K label fields (about K x Perlin, with gradients K x 1.5) plus steerable octaves; K=4 default.

FORM GrainStripes (creative lens): For k in 0..K-1 (fixed int): v[k] = Source.Gen(seed + k*Stride, pos). Track top1, top2 and label idx with Max and Select. dir = table[idx], phi = table2[idx], both per node arrays computed when a param is set. Stripe mode: c = cos(tau * f * dot(dir, pos) + phi + W * top1); W bends stripes along the region's own field. Contour mode: c = cos(tau * f * G * top1 + phi), which uses no raw coordinates, so it can tile through 4D if Source does. g = smoothstep(0, Gap, top1 - top2). out = c * g. Output is 0 on both sides of every wall, so it is continuous by construction. Estimated AVX2 with K=5 Perlin: about 8 / 14 / 26 ns (critic estimate for the foam plus about 1.5 ns, unverified).
master.why_new:
GrainedRegions: Cell-frame gives per-grain brushed direction but with Voronoi grains; exchange-foam gives blob regions of varied size with enclaves. Steering the grain by the region's hashed angle, blended at borders by the pairwise distance weights from FoamBlend v2, gives metal grains, mineral thin-sections and brushed patchwork with soft isotropic borders, all region shapes instead of polygons.
GrainStripes: lattice-phasor shows square cuts where orientation changes, and exchange-foam has beautiful curved walls with no lattice. Giving each foam region its own stripe direction should give a polycrystal zebra with curved grain boundaries. Not built; the look is a prediction.
Seed gap: polycrystal looks with curved walls.
master.simd_plan:
GrainedRegions: Cost: K label fields (about K x Perlin, with gradients K x 1.5) plus steerable octaves; K=4 default.
GrainStripes: Estimated AVX2 with K=5 Perlin: about 8 / 14 / 26 ns (critic estimate for the foam plus about 1.5 ns, unverified).
master.continuity:
GrainedRegions: Not stated by the panel.
GrainStripes: Output is 0 on both sides of every wall, so it is continuous by construction.
master.params: K (fixed int, 4 or 5), Source, Seed Stride, Width, Aspect, Octaves, Output enum {Grain, Label, Grain plus Tone}; GrainStripes form: Mode {Stripe, Contour}, f, G, W, Gap, direction and phase tables.
master.risks: Seed risk 0.25: gap at walls may read as cells.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured. Stripe at K=5, fo=1: about 8 / 16 / 30 ns (foam-walls' own estimate) plus one Cos per lane. Stripe at fo=2 roughly double. Steerable form about 25 ns in 2D, a guess from the scalar ratio.

grained-regions.changed_from_entry: Gap uses foam-walls' first order distance instead of the margin (gap=1), so the seam has constant width and no blobs; the margin form is still gap=0. The steerable form blends the metric tensor (a weighted sum of d_k d_k^T) rather than direction vectors, so it needs no normalise, and opposite angles go isotropic by themselves: this removes the anisotropy fallback the entry asked for. Added a ridged option, not adopted. Added a separate field octave count (fo).

cellular-multi.look: Material: rounded stones with deep clean joints of constant width, each with its own tone, a slight dome, and a broad shade that runs across many stones from the lookup at the site, so neighbours relate to each other. Relief reads as laid cobbles or dry stone paving. The volume is solid cobble blocks with clean flat cut faces and grout channels, a look that costs four searches per sample today. Foam plates: curved mesas at five levels that each keep their own bumpy relief, with cliffs between; the relief has a real tableland character, water-level basins and high flat tops. The comparison shows the five inputs next to each other.
cellular-multi.dims: Kernel 2D and 3D measured (Material 3D range -1.000 to 0.840, z step 0.0217 at dz 1e-3; Foam plates 3D -0.460 to 0.947). 4D not built. The saving should be largest at 4D, where a search costs 41 ns.
cellular-multi.range: Material -1.000 to 1.094 over 8 seeds and offsets (needs a clamp or a smaller lookup weight). Foam plates -0.758 to 1.338. No NaN.
cellular-multi.artifacts: None in the look. No jumps: every per-cell value is multiplied by a bevel that reaches 0 on the cell border, so CellValue's and Lookup's jumps stay hidden. Plain CellValue and Lookup channels do jump at cell borders by design. Material can exceed 1 slightly, because the lookup sum is not normalised. Foam plates has steep cliffs. The pattern's runtime risks (one memo slot thrashing when two hosts alternate, StencilFilter interleaving) cannot be shown in a scalar test and were not tested.
cellular-multi.node_shape: Host: CellularMulti with the usual Cellular members (Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Distance Function). Tap: Source = host, Channel enum {F1, F2, F2-F1, EdgeDistance, CellValue, CellId, SiteOffsetX/Y/Z/W, F1Angle}. ExchangeFoamMulti: Phases, Seed Stride, Source, channels {Label, Margin, WinnerValue, RunnerUpValue, WinnerIndex}.
cellular-multi.port_notes: Memo compare is 1 pointer plus 1 + D vector compares. Second pass runs over the stored window, no extra hashes. SiteOffset needs only the F1 site's relative vector with a masked update per cell. A Tap for 'Lookup' can be left to the graph, since p + offset is the site: a DomainOffset fed by offset taps, one per dimension. That graph is only cheap with the memo, which is the reason to build this.
cellular-multi.params_text: mode=0,zoom=1.3,jit=0.437,bw=0.14,R=0.8,dome=0.35,tint=0.3,look=0.55 (defaults: Material). Foam plates: mode=1,K=5,oct=3,rel=0.55,g=0.02. One channel: chan=0 F1, 1 EdgeDistance, 3 CellValue, 4 Lookup at site, 5 Dome, 6 SiteOffset x.

master.one_liner: A multi-output node pattern (one evaluation, N channels read by sibling Tap nodes through a GeneratorCache-style memo), first for Cellular (F1, F2, edge distance, cell value, site offset) and ExchangeFoam (label, margin, winner value), which makes the 'Foam plates' look and one-search 3D cellular materials possible.
master.look: Foam plates, recorded in the discoveries as needing the winner value no node exposes: stepped mesas where each ExchangeFoam label sits at its own level and keeps its own relief (Label tap through a Remap, plus WinnerValue tap). Cellular materials that today cost three window searches, per-cell tint (CellValue) + bevel (EdgeDistance) + dome (F1) + per-cell lookup at the site, at one search: roughly 12 ns instead of 36-48 ns in 3D, so bevelled, tinted, dome-topped cells become affordable in volumes and in 4D tiling. Phasor amplitude as a free taper mask for stripe ends.
master.algorithm:
PATTERN: a MultiOutput node keeps, exactly like GeneratorCache, a thread_local memo { generator ptr, seed[lanes], pos[D][lanes], channel[N][lanes] }. A Tap node has Source = the MultiOutput node and a Channel enum; its Gen calls host->Channel( c, seed, pos... ): memo hit (same ptr, seed, positions) returns channel c in ~10 ops, miss runs the full evaluation once, stores all N channels and returns c. Results never depend on the memo; only cost does.
CellularMulti channels from one 3^D CellWindow search with CellTopK<2>: F1, F2, F2-F1, EdgeDistance (iq second pass: min over sites of dot( 0.5(s_i + s_1) - p, normalize(s_i - s_1) )), CellValue (rnd11 of the F1 hash), CellId (F1 hash & 0xFFFF as float), SiteOffsetX/Y/Z/W (p - s_1 in cell units, so p - offset is the site: any Source sampled there is a free CellularLookup), F1Angle (2D).
ExchangeFoamMulti channels: Label, Margin, WinnerValue, RunnerUpValue, WinnerIndex.
PhasorMulti channels (if PhasorNoise ships as a node): Phase, Amplitude, Orientation.
master.why_new: A graph has to re-run the window search per output and nothing exposes the winner value, the runner-up, or the site offset vector. The memo is the library's own GeneratorCache mechanism, so no core change, only a convention and a Tap node. Nearest: cellular-edge-distance, cellular-lookup, exchange-foam, GeneratorCache.
master.simd_plan: Memo compare = 1 pointer + (1 + D) vector compares. A Tap miss costs the host's full search, hits ~10 ops. Siblings in the same batch hit as long as nothing interleaves a different position (a StencilFilter over a Tap interleaves and recomputes; still correct, just slower). 2D/3D/4D as the host.
master.continuity: As the host's outputs (EdgeDistance C0, CellValue discontinuous, Label discontinuous, WinnerValue C0 within a plate).
master.params: Host: the usual Cellular members (Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Distance Function) or ExchangeFoam's (Phases, Seed Stride, Source). Tap: Source (the host), Channel enum.
master.risks: One TLS slot per host type thrashes if two instances alternate within a batch (correct, slow); the Node Editor should draw Taps hanging off the host; encoded trees serialise Tap->host as an ordinary source link.

climate-diagram.look: A categorical biome map with curved, non-convex regions and small enclaves, reading like a Minecraft biome map. thumb_nearest shows the same layout with grassland down at a fifth of the map; The thumbnail has it at the requested 40 percent, and the other biomes shrink, so the effect of the shares is visible. Blend output is a small world with green plains, desert dune fields (I cut their scale after the first render, they were too big), ridged ice peaks, lumpy forest and a jungle valley running through it, with soft borders. The wide view is an even patchwork with no lattice. Volume of the grassland mask is a porous solid and not worth much as an image. It is a selection node, and in a still it looks like what a nested graph could look like; the value is in the numbers.
climate-diagram.dims: 2D and 3D measured (shares above; Blend 3D range -0.821 to 0.970, z step 0.0189 at dz 1e-3). 4D not built; only the axes and biome sources see the position, so it works and tiles if they do. Only 2 axes tested; 3 and 4 axes not built.
climate-diagram.range: Value -0.800 to 1.000 (the table). Blend -0.973 to 0.975 over 8 seeds and offsets. No NaN.
climate-diagram.artifacts: Value and Index jump at borders by design. Borders follow axis contours, so their world-space width in Blend varies with the axis slope: fat where both axes run flat, thin elsewhere, as the entry warned. Small enclaves appear, because FBm axes wander over small climate distances. Sub-pixel slivers near triple points, see adjacency_measured. Weights solved for one axis marginal are off by up to 1.8 points on another. Correlated axes would break the shares, not measured.
climate-diagram.node_shape: Axis A, B, C, D (hybrid, 2 to 4 used), Axis Distribution {Gaussian, Uniform}, Axis Std, Biome Count, per biome: Point, Share, Weight, Value, hybrid Source; Output {Value, Index, Margin, Mask, Blend}, Selected, Blend Width. Weights are plain float members, so an encoded tree needs no solve.
climate-diagram.port_notes: K fixed loops of n multiplies, Min with masked index, table lookup through a permute. Phi by polynomial, or a cheaper logistic since calibration absorbs the error: calibrated weights make Phi's accuracy almost irrelevant. Blend: test AnyMask( W_k > 0 ) per biome before calling its source. Compact weights mean a skipped source contributed exactly zero, so parity between skip and no skip is exact. Solve lives in the Node Editor, offline.

master.one_liner: Minecraft-style biome selection by nearest point in climate space, made into a power diagram whose weights are solved so each biome gets the map share you asked for, while desert can only touch what its climate cell touches.
master.look: A categorical map of curved, non-convex regions whose borders are level sets of the axes, like a Minecraft biome map, except that the shares are what you typed and forbidden neighbours never meet. Blend output: biome terrains fading through each other.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: 2 to 4 hybrid axes. Each axis is normalised to [0,1] by a chosen marginal: u = Phi(a/sigma) for Gaussian axes such as FBm, u = (a+1)/2 for Uniform. Table of K <= 16 biomes: Point P_k in [0,1]^n, Share f_k, Weight w_k, Value v_k or Source S_k.
Solve, not at Gen time: Q = 1024 R2 points in [0,1]^2 (or a 16^3 grid for 3 axes), w = 0. Repeat 64 to 200 times: label each q by argmin_k |q-P_k|^2 - w_k, then w_k += eta*(f_k - count_k/|Q|) with eta about half the squared mean point spacing. This is semi-discrete optimal transport, the objective is convex, so simple ascent converges. Weights are stored as plain float members so an encoded tree needs no solve and Gen has no state.
Gen, per lane:
  e_k = |u - P_k|^2 - w_k  for all k
  best = Min e_k, second = next lowest, by masks
  Value / Index: v[best]. Margin: second - best. Mask(j): smoothstep( (min over k != j of e_k - e_j) / Blend ).
  Blend: W_k = max(0, 1 - (e_k - best)/Blend)^2, normalised over k. For each k: if AnyMask(W_k > 0) evaluate S_k, else skip it for the whole batch. out = sum W_k S_k.
Adjacency: the axes are continuous, so moving across the map moves continuously in climate space, so two biomes can only share a border if their power cells share a facet. The designer controls which borders can exist by where the points sit.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Nearest real node ExchangeFoam: exact shares with no calibration, but labels have no climate meaning and any pair can touch. Nearest catalogue idea BiomeBlend (dropped): solves transition width, not selection. Nested SplineRemap reaches any 2D table but with no share control and a hand tuned cut per axis. Evidence read: Minecraft uses a closest match in 6 parameter space and uneven level widths such as temperature level 0 spanning -1 to -0.45, so a biome's area is a side effect of those numbers. Red Blob's elevation and moisture table warns that thresholds need tuning for each project. FN2 issue 16 asks for 80/15/5 percent distributions directly. The Riverheim mod lists budgeted biomes as a feature. FN2 issue 163 and discussion 162 ask for Fade to skip inputs it does not need, and Auburn says it is possible when no lane in the register needs that side; the Blend output does that per source, so 8 biomes cost about 2 in coherent batches.
master.simd_plan: K fixed loops of n multiplies with Min tracking. Dimension agnostic through GenT, since position only reaches the axis and biome sources, so 2D, 3D and 4D all work and tile if the sources tile. Estimate: 2-3 ns for K=8 over the axis cost, plus Phi. Blend pays for only the sources with an active lane. Scattered lanes from GenPositionArray lose the skip but produce the same values.
master.continuity: Value and Index discontinuous at borders by design. Mask and Blend C0: weights are compactly supported in energy and reach zero before a source drops out, so a skipped source was contributing exactly nothing. Margin C0.
master.params: Axis A, B, C, D (hybrid, 2 to 4 used), Axis Distribution enum, Axis Std, Biome Count, per biome: Point, Share, Weight, Value and hybrid Source, Output enum (Value, Index, Margin, Mask, Blend), Selected, Blend Width
master.risks: Share is exact only for independent axes with the assumed marginal. Perlin FBm is near Gaussian, so expect about a point of bias, and ExactGaussianNoise axes remove it. One world at low axis frequency still has per seed swings, which only QuotaCells removes. Correlated axes such as altitude and temperature break the share. Blend width is in climate units, so world width varies; the DistFade discovery is the fix, at more evals. Solve cost at member set is why weights are members; needs a NodeEditor solve button.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE from the entry, not measured: 2 to 3 ns for K=8 over the axis cost, plus Phi. Axes here would be about 9 ns (8 Perlin at 1.1 ns). Blend pays only for the sources with an active lane.

climate-diagram.changed_from_entry: Added a second solve against samples of the real axes (solved=2, now the default), which removes the 1.8 point bias with no change at Gen time. The entry expected this bias and offered ExactGaussianNoise axes as the remedy; calibration gives the same accuracy on plain FBm. Map samples are at 1/8 linear resolution of the entry's 2048^2 to respect the machine load rule, with the same world size. Only 2 axes built.
climate-diagram.proto_note: Eval has only constant weights, so it stays pure.

extra_measured.c0_notes: The default Value output jumps at every biome border, by design, step 1.35. The continuous outputs have no jump: Margin c0ratio 7.899, straddle 7.898, steps 0.04679 / 0.00468 / 0.00047. Mask 7.943 / 7.955, steps 0.05456 / 0.00543 / 0.00059. Blend 7.468 / 7.494, steps 0.02427 / 0.00243 / 0.00025.
extra_measured.shares_measured: Target 40 / 20 / 15 / 10 / 10 / 5 percent, 100 seeds, map 64 x 64 units (about 19 axis features across), at 256 x 256 samples, which is the entry's 2048^2 at 1/8 the resolution in each direction to keep the run short. Plain nearest point on Perlin FBm: 20.4 / 15.9 / 19.4 / 20.0 / 16.3 / 7.9. Solved on a uniform square, Perlin FBm: 38.2 / 20.3 / 15.3 / 10.5 / 10.4 / 5.3, a bias up to 1.8 points as the entry predicted, per-seed std 0.4 to 0.8 points. Solved on a uniform square with Exact Gaussian axes: 39.8 / 20.0 / 14.8 / 10.2 / 10.0 / 5.1, std 0.7 to 1.4 points (its single octave has fewer features). Calibrated, solved on 40000 samples of the real FBm axes: 40.3 / 20.1 / 14.8 / 10.1 / 9.9 / 4.9, std 0.4 to 0.8 points. 3D with uniform-square weights over 20 seeds,: 38.0 / 20.2 / 15.5 / 10.5 / 10.4 / 5.4 on FBm, 39.8 / 20.3 / 15.0 / 9.9 / 10.0 / 5.0 on Exact Gaussian.
extra_measured.solve_measured: Simple gradient ascent, 1024 R2 points, 400 iterations, step 0.08 with linear decay: max share residual 0.0027 at iteration 50, 0.0016 at the end, about 1.6 points of 1024. Calibrated solve: residual 0.0000 at 40000 samples. Both run in well under a second, which makes a Node Editor solve button realistic.
extra_measured.adjacency_measured: Diagram facets from a 2048^2 climate grid: 8 of 15 pairs (0-1 0-2 0-3 0-4 1-3 1-4 1-5 2-4). Map adjacency over 40 seeds with bisection between neighbouring samples, final step 0.004 / 0.0005 / 0.00006 units: exactly those 8 pairs at all three steps, 0 pairs outside the diagram. 7 pairs never touch, including desert-ice 2-5, desert-tundra 2-3, jungle-tundra 3-4. With the earlier uniform-square weights at step 0.004, one false pair 3-5 did show up: the triple point of forest, tundra and ice lands at u = (-0.0004, 0.492), just outside the square, so a razor-thin forest sliver separates them there. It went away at steps of 0.0005 and finer. So the rule holds, but a sliver can be sub-pixel, and a designer should expect near-touches when a triple point is close to the square's edge.
extra_measured.skip_measured: 6 biomes, blend 0.04. Active sources per lane 1.315. Per 8-lane row batch at 512 px over 8 units: 1.450; at 4x finer: 1.338. So the entry's Fade-skip claim holds for coherent batches in this measure, in a row of 8. A real port's gain depends on branch costs. GenPositionArray with scattered lanes was not measured.
extra_measured.scalar_vs_perlin_notes: 510.8 ns Value, nearly all axes: 8 Perlin in two 4-octave axes, plus Phi with libm exp. Blend 750.4 ns, ratio 13.66, including biome sources, with skip. Exact Gaussian axes 376.8 ns (their cost is a 3x3 search per axis, single octave).

seed-route.look: Hard with mortar: stones or slabs, each holding its own take of the same ridged terrain, reading in relief as tilted blocks of different mountains between deep mortar cuts. Terrazzo (cracks subgraph, no mortar): big polygons where the fine crack pattern visibly restarts at each border; the seams are hard cuts and read as a deliberate inlay. Morph: the image and the image show the same stationary texture becoming another, with no sliding. On crisp cracks you see a double exposure for frames near t=0.5, so it is a dissolve and not motion, as the entry warned. Blend over a gradient or a coarse Perlin looks like plain stationary noise in a still, which is the point and also dull to look at. Volume is noisy broken chunks with flat mortar cuts, and not a strong image.
seed-route.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D range -1.000 to 0.974, z step 0.0260 at dz 1e-3). Any dimension in a node, no window, since it only forwards positions.
seed-route.range: Hard: -1.000 to 0.984 over 8 seeds and offsets. Blend on Ridged with Mean=0: -0.612 to 1.310, past 1, because of the wrong Mean above. No NaN.
seed-route.artifacts: Hard jumps on cell borders by design, unmasked. At crossfade midpoints crisp structures lose contrast and overlap. On structured sources, the blend over a gradient shows contrast banding with period 1/grad, faint vertical bands on Ridged, because variance really does oscillate there (see std_measured). Mortar from F2-F1 is thicker where cells meet at shallow angles, a stock limit; EdgeDistance would fix it. Near-parallel walls show fat wedges.
seed-route.node_shape: SeedRoute: Source, Seed Source (hybrid), Quantise, Mode {Hard, Blend}, Salt (int), Mean. Seed Source is read at the real position.
seed-route.port_notes: Convert Floor(s) to int and hash with Primes::X and Salt, per lane. Hard: one Source call with int32v seed2, already legal in FastNoise. Blend: k and k+1 hashes, two Source calls, PolyMath SinCos. Keep k below 2^24. Mean could be measured when the graph is built. No state.

master.one_liner: Reseed any subgraph from a FIELD: hard per-region reseeding keyed by a quantised source (terrazzo, per-shard re-rolls), or a continuous seed axis that morphs any graph in place with variance preserved.
master.look: Hard over CellularValue: every Voronoi cell runs its own re-rolled copy of the whole subgraph (same graph, different take), the CellDomain/ShatterLookup seed's per-shard re-randomisation and NestedVoronoi's terrazzo without dedicated nodes, hard seams at cell borders that a CellularEdge mortar hides. Blend with a swept Constant: any graph, including ones with no 4D (TileDomain, Textile, Cellular 2D), morphs in place with no sliding and no lattice drift. Blend with Gradient 0.002 per unit: a world-sized material that never repeats while every window is a stationary standard texture. Blend with a coarse Perlin: patches of alternative takes dissolving into one another at unchanged statistics.
master.algorithm:
s = SeedSource(p) * Quantise   (hybrid: CellularValue with a 0..1e4 range for per-cell keys, Gradient for a drift, Constant swept for animation, a coarse Perlin for patches)
k = Floor(s); t = s - k
Hard: seed2 = seed ^ HashPrimes( Convert<int>(k) * Primes::X, int32v(Salt) ); return Source( seed2, p )
Blend: a = Source( seed ^ H(k), p ); b = Source( seed ^ H(k+1), p ); tt = smoothstep(t) * pi/2; return Mean + (a - Mean) cos(tt) + (b - Mean) sin(tt)   (exact variance preservation for uncorrelated equal-variance fields)
SeedSource is read at the real position before any scaling; k is kept below 2^24.
master.why_new: SeedOffset is an int member, so no graph can reseed by region or by time; ExchangeFoam uses K seeds for an argmax and StochasticPatch for tiling, neither keys the seed to a field or sweeps it continuously; FlowNoise phases only its three built-ins. Nearest: seed-offset, exchange-foam, stochastic-patch, flow-noise, domain-tile.
master.simd_plan: Hard: 1 hash + 1 source. Blend: 2 sources + one PolyMath::SinCos. Any dimension, no window.
master.continuity: Hard: discontinuous at quantisation borders by design. Blend: C0 (C1 with smoothstep) in position and in t; the variance is constant but individual features dissolve rather than move.
master.params: Seed Source (hybrid), Quantise, Mode (Hard, Blend), Salt (int), Mean, Source.
master.risks: Blend at t = 0.5 is a superposition of two fields, so single structures lose contrast even though variance holds (a dissolve, not motion); Hard seams are the point but need masking; float keys must stay under 2^24.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE: 1 hash (under 1 ns) plus the seed source plus one Source (Hard), or plus two Sources and a SinCos (Blend). The cost is the user's graph.

extra_measured.c0_notes: Hard with mortar: the mortar hides the seams, so it is continuous. Hard without mortar (mort=0): REAL JUMPS by design, c0ratio 1.029, straddle 1.024, steps 1.135 / 1.090 / 1.090, all on cell borders. Blend constant t=0.5: c0ratio 8.185, straddle 8.118, steps 0.00667 / 0.00067 / 0.00007. Blend gradient: 8.120 / 8.127, 0.00623 / 0.00062 / 0.00017. extra_measured.std_measured: 200000 samples over a 2000 unit square per t. FBm Perlin: std 0.2719 to 0.2728, spread 0.30 percent, well inside the 2 percent target. Same with a plain lerp: 0.1925 to 0.2728, spread 29.43 percent. Structured subgraphs are not so clean: Ridged 0.2300 to 0.2435 (5.54 percent), Cellular cracks 0.6881 to 0.7110 (3.22 percent). The variance rises at t = 0.5, which means two different seeds of those sources are positively correlated, because Perlin's zeros and the cell lattice do not move with the seed. Mean does not affect the std, as the algebra says, but a wrong Mean shifts the output's mean by a factor of up to 1.41 (from the formula, not measured).

seed-value.look: Plain wall: every brick has a different hash, yet all look like one brushed texture running one way. With SeedValue: each brick has its own brushing angle, roughness, tone, aspect and bevel, like a wall of reclaimed planks and metal plates. Borders are identical. Quilt: stripes, checks and dots at different widths, angles and tones per tile against a uniform stripe field: a real patchwork from a Choice output. Stamps: craters of different sizes, floors and rims against identical copies, reading in relief as a real crater field. Grains: rough, broken patches next to smooth ones, with soft borders, same look as RegionSpectrumFractal but at a finer region scale in these defaults. Recipe: seeds 7 and 8 differ in octaves, gain and ridged balance. Volume: 3D running bond blocks, most of them solid with clean orange cut faces, and a few eaten away into loose fibres, since per-brick tone and depth move each brick relative to the isosurface. That per-block erosion was not asked for and is a good effect.

seed-value.range: Wall -1.000 to 0.963, Grains -1.145 to 1.178, Stamps -0.729 to 0.911, Quilt -1.000 to 0.878, each over 8 seeds and offsets. No NaN. The node's own output is in Output Min/Max by construction.
seed-value.artifacts: None in the kernels' continuity. The Gauss output is approximate (three 8-bit fields) by design. Per-brick angle needs Cos/Sin per lane in the child, which is the child's cost. Grains uses a fixed 4 child evals, so it costs 4x the child, and RegionSpectrumFractal is cheaper if all you want is per-region gain, since it reweights one set of octaves. Decode is not shown: it needs parents to adopt an Encode convention.
seed-value.node_shape: SeedValue: Salt (int), Output {Uniform, Gauss, Choice, Decode}, Choices N, Decode Shift, Decode Bits, Output Min, Output Max. No position, no sources.
seed-value.port_notes: One hash and about six ops, identical in every dimension, tiles trivially. Fully per lane since seed is int32v. Any parent that mixes its child seed per lane already works: TileDomain, StampScatter, CellFrame, ExchangeFoam stride. Node editor needs a dial or similar, since it renders flat. A plain hybrid member read in a child makes this work with no other change: hybrid members are sampled per lane, and the seed passed down is what the leaf hashes.

master.one_liner: A leaf node whose output is a random number of the SEED alone, constant in space, so every parent that reseeds its children per tile, stamp, grain or phase can hand them their own random parameters, not just their own hash.
master.look: No look of its own (a flat value per seed). The payoff shows wherever a parent already routes a per-element seed, which the library does today in CellFrame (CellMix(grain.hash,3)), TileDomain (sourceSeed ^ tile hash), StampScatter (MixHash(stamp.hash,6)), FlowShingle's interior seed, StampLayers, and ExchangeFoam's seed stride: a brick wall where each brick has its own bevel depth, roughness gain and brushing angle (TileDomain -> SteerablePerlin(Angle = SeedValue * pi), continuous angles instead of the Quarter-rotation enum of the Brushed metal plates discovery); stamps whose crater depth/rim ratio differ per stamp through a Stamp subgraph; CellFrame grains with their own fractal gain, which is RegionSpectrumFractal as a two-node graph; Choice picking weave A/B/C per tile through a Fade chain (Patchwork quilt without a special node). Outside a reseeding parent: a graph whose recipe re-rolls with the seed (seed 7 is a 5-octave gain-0.5 world, seed 8 a gain-0.62 one).
master.algorithm:
h = HashPrimes( seed, int32v( Salt * Primes::Y ) )
Uniform: rnd11(h) = (h & 0xFFFFFF) * 2^-23 - 1
Gauss: ( field(h,0) + field(h,1) + field(h,2) ) / sqrt(3) from three 8-bit fields (approximately normal)
Choice: Floor( ((h >> 8) & 0xFFFF) * N / 65536 ) as float 0..N-1 (an enum pick per element)
Decode: ( (seed >> Shift) & ((1<<Bits)-1) ) / (2^Bits - 1) * 2 - 1 reads a payload a parent wrote into the child seed (convention: parents get an Encode enum, e.g. TileDomain writes the tile's size rank, StampScatter the stamp's radius fraction or a guide value sampled at the stamp centre, into 8 bits).
Output scaled by Output Min/Max. No position term at all; GenT is the same in every dimension.
master.why_new: Nothing reads the seed as a value: White varies with position, Constant ignores the seed. Per-lane seed routing is not a wall in FastNoise (any node may pass any int32v seed to a child, and the stamp/tile/grain nodes already do), but no leaf can turn that routing into a parameter, so per-element variation stops at 'a different hash'. Nearest: region-spectrum-fractal (merged), nested-voronoi aniso grains, the Brushed metal plates and Patchwork quilt discoveries.
master.simd_plan: One hash and about six ops; identical in 2D/3D/4D; tiles trivially.
master.continuity: Constant within an element; the jumps at element borders belong to the parent, which already blends or grouts them for any reseeded child.
master.params: Salt (int), Output enum (Uniform, Gauss, Choice, Decode), Choices N (int), Decode Shift (int), Decode Bits (int), Output Min, Output Max.
master.risks: Decode needs an Encode convention adopted parent by parent (small, not core); the node renders flat in the editor preview, so it needs a 'dial' presentation; parents that mix their child seed from a per-batch constant would give one value per batch (none of the listed ones do).

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE: one hash and about six ops, well under 1 ns per SeedValue.

simplex-plates.look: Hardness 8 with warp and log gains: irregular flat plates, close to warped CellularValue, plates vary in size and have slightly curved walls. Without warp and with small gains it is a plain hex lattice. The comparison shows the same layout going from overlapping translucent leaf shapes at 0.1, through rounded soft hills at 0.25 to 0.5, to bevelled pebbles at 1, to hard plates at 8, which no Fade of two nodes can do. Order 1 cuts each plate into a harlequin pair of opposite tones, strong on plates with a large value and mild on the rest, and reads as an angular mosaic of slate shards, which plain cellular does not give. Order 3 gives triangle fans around each vertex, like stained glass, with the hex lattice visible as it is the point of the pattern. Volume at iso 0 is smooth rounded stones with flat facets at plate tops, like a cut pebble bed.
simplex-plates.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D range -0.964 to 0.793 std 0.332 at the default seed, z step 0.1243 at dz 1e-3). 4D not built; it needs only the simplex corner selection from Simplex.inl.
simplex-plates.range: Gaussian output f/3: -1.326 to 1.435 over 8 seeds, so it exceeds [-1,1] in the tails like any Gaussian. Uniform output is in [-1,1]. No NaN.
simplex-plates.artifacts: Plates cannot exceed the vertex's star, so there are no large plates, and the size range is narrow. Lattice regularity needs warp, whose cost is on the user. Log gains above about 2 make plate edges sharply angular at star boundaries, since the gain cannot move a wall past the star. Very high hardness has a steep wall, at sampling scale a jump. Facet sign flip inside a plate is a real C0 slope but very steep at facet=4. Gaussian output is outside [-1,1] in its tails.

simplex-plates.port_notes: Simplex corner selection as in Simplex.inl, D+1 hashes. Integer Hardness by squarings is far cheaper than hybrid Exp(H*Log(w)); offer both. Divide by the largest c before squaring to avoid underflow, and keep a Gaussian table or byte-field sum for G. Use complex power rather than atan for Order. No window.

master.one_liner: Plate mosaics with no cell search: D+1 simplex corners under a hardened L2 partition, morphing per lane from soft noise to crisp plates with an unchanged exact histogram, irregular via hashed weights.
master.look: Hardness 1: soft clouds. Hardness 8 or more: flat hexagon-dual plates, irregular with Size Jitter, with raised or sunken joints from the L2 sum. A slow hybrid Hardness makes soft hills visibly condense into tile plates in the same layout. Order 3 gives a random hexagonal pinwheel tile, shard-like in 3D (planes through an axis). Regular lattice structure stays visible unless warped upstream.
master.algorithm:
WHY THE ACCIDENT LOOKS LIKE IT DOES. Exact Gaussian hex mosaic came from (0.5 - r^2)^4 weights: L2-normalised weights over a sharply peaked kernel behave as a soft argmax, so the nearest corner's value fills a flat hexagon. Multipole order 3 pinwheels, sparse octaves stencil floor and facet grout are relatives: steep weights make a partition. The exact marginal holds for any weights, as the prototype's comment notes, which is the actually useful property.

Simplex lattice corners i = 0..D, offset d_i, hash h_i.
w_i = Max(0, r2 - dot(d_i, d_i))^4      // vanishes on the opposite face, as in Simplex with r2 = .5, so no seams
w_i *= lerp(1, gain(h_i), SizeJitter)   // hashed multiplicative gains move walls: curved irregular plates, still no window, and they cannot leave the vertex's star
c_i = Pow(w_i, Hardness)                // hybrid
v = Sum(c_i*G_i) * InvSqrt(Sum(c_i*c_i) + 1e-30)   // G_i iid N(0,1) from h_i, or sign-symmetric
The variance of v is 1 at every point for every Hardness, so the histogram is N(0,1) throughout a morph.
Output: Gaussian v/3, Uniform via erf polynomial (the prototype's mode 1), Id = hash of largest c_i.
Facets: G_i becomes G_i*Sharpen(cos(Order*(angle(d_i) - phi(h_i)))), computed by complex power with no atan. Order 1 cuts each plate into a harlequin half pair, order 3 gives 6 wedges meeting at the vertex (the Multipole pinwheel in plate form). Marginal stays exact if the factor is sign symmetric and independent of G_i's sign.
Denominator exponent q as an option (Sum c^q)^(1/q): q = 2 exact, with slightly raised or sunken seams at (v1+v2)/sqrt2; q = 1 plain partition with no seam overshoot and a narrower histogram.
master.why_new: Hard made easy: CellularValue costs 3.9 / 12 / 41 ns, this about 2 / 3 / 6 ns, with soft walls, and histogram is exact and independent of Hardness. Fade between CellularValue and a noise has two unrelated layouts and a changing histogram. SimplexFacet is the triangle dual, with slopes instead of plates. exact-gaussian-noise has only a fixed kernel, no hardness, gains or facets. multipole-noise has no plate structure.
master.simd_plan: Simplex corner selection as in Simplex.inl, D+1 hashes, Pow per corner for hybrid Hardness via Exp(H*Log(w)), or squarings if int. Branch free, all dimensions, no window. Estimates AVX2 with Pow: 3 / 5 / 8 ns.
master.continuity: C0 for all finite Hardness: each w_i vanishes on the face where corner i leaves the set, and the normalised c_i is continuous provided the corners cannot all vanish, which the simplex kernel guarantees for r2 = .5. Very high Hardness approaches jumps at sampling scale. Near underflow: this is exactly the facet grout accident, so use log-space or clamp Hardness.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max, Output enum, Size Jitter, int Order, Facet Sharp, Norm enum. Hybrid: Hardness, Lookup (Source sampled at each corner, for D+1 extra evals).
master.risks: Looks like a hex lattice unless warped, and Size Jitter only reshuffles it so far. Sharing the D+1 star bound means no large plates. Near-duplicate of warped cellular value for most users; speed in 3D and 4D plus the hybrid morph are the case for it.

Relief is the strongest view; raising height with Level makes the highlands stand as a plateau. Stones preset: boulders where Level is high grading to fine gravel, a sorted bed, clearly sorted but the stones are plain domes. Pits in 3D at iso: a pumice block with pore sizes changing across the cube, which reads more as cratered sponge than as a clean gradient at this window. FFT is near isotropic, a few faint streaks from the row lattice.

master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: craters, vesicles or stones whose size follows a map: big craters on highlands, crater density varying as between maria and highlands, pumice that gets finer towards a rim, riverbeds and scree sorted from boulders to sand.
master.algorithm:
FORM GradedStamp (maintainer lens): Sample Level L(p) once at the lane position. For k = 0..Levels-1 (fixed int loop): scale s_k = ratio^k; cell c_k = Floor(p * s_k); h = hash(seed + k, c_k); centre = (c_k + 0.5 + jitter(h) * 0.5 * (1 - 2 r_k)) / s_k with radius r_k = rmin + bits(h) * (rmax - rmin) so the stamp never leaves its own cell (one hash per level, no window). Profile f = Shape(|p - centre| * s_k / r_k) from {Crater, Dome, Disc, Source sampled in the stamp frame}. Level weight a_k = SmoothStep(L(p) - (k - Levels/2) * Spacing, Width) * density gate from spare bits. Compose with the cascade fade from stamp-scatter: out = Lerp(out, f, inside_k * a_k) in youngest-last order (Erase) or Max or Sum via a 3-value enum. Because a_k depends on L(p) at the sample and not at the cell, a stamp fades in as a whole across its own footprint: no pop. Cost about 1 hash + 1 profile per level + 1 Level eval, dimension agnostic (estimate).

FORM GradedCraters (graphics-researcher lens): 1) lev = Level hybrid source at p (0..MaxLevels float). 2) For L = 0..MaxLevels-1 (fixed int loop, coarsest first): cell size s_L = Base * Ratio^-L; own-cell crater stamp exactly as crater-field (one hash per cell, occupancy bit, radius, bowl, rim, peak, confined to the cell). 3) Level weight w_L = smoothstep(lev - L + 1) * (1 - smoothstep(lev - L - Fade)) is NOT used to fade height (that would show as soft ghost craters); instead it scales the occupancy threshold per lane: a crater at level L exists if hashOcc < Occupancy * w_L, and to keep C0 the crater depth is multiplied by smoothstep((Occupancy * w_L - hashOcc) / Soft) so craters shrink to nothing as the local level passes them. 4) Erasure: young floors overwrite older ones by the same priority rule as crater-field (later level inside an earlier floor replaces height within the floor radius). 5) Output height in [-1,1] by the measured table. 3D: same with 3x3x3 own cells (crater cavities volume with graded pore size). Cost: same as crater-field plus one Level eval.

FORM SortedSediment (artist-material lens): Level is a hybrid source in [0,1], with 0 for boulders and 1 for sand. Constant loop over layers i=0..L-1: s_i = s0*g^i in a per-layer rotated and offset frame q. ix = floor(q/s_i); h = hash(ix, seed+i); centre c = (ix + 0.5 + jit*bits(h))*s_i; radius r = s_i*lerp(rmin, rmax, bits(h)), with jit and rmax bounded so a stone fits its own cell and no neighbour window is needed. Evaluate Level once per layer at the stone centre rotated back to world, so the map never slices a stone. keep = bump(|i/L - Level(c)|, width); r = r*keep, so stones shrink out instead of popping, and hash bits < keep decide presence. dome = sqrt(Max(0, r^2 - |p-c|^2)) or a parabola. Height = Max over layers. Output enum Height, StoneValue (Select of the winner's hash), LayerIndex. Same rim slope issue as PebblePile with sqrt; the parabola profile is smoother. Any dimension. Cost ESTIMATE from PebblePile's 1.5-2 ns per layer plus 1.1 ns for a Perlin Level: about 20-25 ns at 8 layers in 2D.
master.why_new:
GradedStamp: graded-voronoi proved that grading feature size by a hybrid Level across space works without seams; crater-field and bubble-pack are own-cell multi-level stamps with a fixed size spectrum. Breeding them gives craters, vesicles or texture islands whose size follows a map (big craters on highlands, pumice that gets finer towards a rim) in one node.
GradedCraters: The crater field's one honest flaw is that the top level is one size class evenly spaced, and crater density on real bodies varies (maria versus highlands). Graded-voronoi's idea of a per-lane Level that fades whole lattice levels in and out transfers directly, because crater-field already loops over fixed levels with erasure ordering.
SortedSediment: Riverbeds and scree are sorted by size, and every ground material needs that. PebblePile has size layers but no spatial sorting; GradedVoronoi has seam-free size control but makes cells rather than stones. Not built, look unverified.
Seed gap: density and size that follow a map: planets, riverbeds.
master.simd_plan:
GradedStamp: Cost about 1 hash + 1 profile per level + 1 Level eval, dimension agnostic (estimate).
GradedCraters: Cost: same as crater-field plus one Level eval.
SortedSediment: Cost ESTIMATE from PebblePile's 1.5-2 ns per layer plus 1.1 ns for a Perlin Level: about 20-25 ns at 8 layers in 2D.
master.continuity:
GradedStamp: Because a_k depends on L(p) at the sample and not at the cell, a stamp fades in as a whole across its own footprint: no pop.
GradedCraters: 3) Level weight w_L = smoothstep(lev - L + 1) * (1 - smoothstep(lev - L - Fade)) is NOT used to fade height (that would show as soft ghost craters); instead it scales the occupancy threshold per lane: a crater at level L exists if hashOcc < Occupancy * w_L, and to keep C0 the crater depth is multiplied by smoothstep((Occupancy * w_L - hashOcc) / Soft) so craters shrink to nothing as the local level passes them.
SortedSediment: Not stated by the panel.
master.params: Level (hybrid: 0..MaxLevels in GradedCraters, 0 boulders to 1 sand in SortedSediment), Levels or Layers (int), Ratio, Radius Min, Radius Max, Jitter, Shape enum {Crater, Dome, Disc, Source sampled in the stamp frame}, Spacing, Width, Compose enum {Erase, Max, Sum}, Occupancy, Soft, Fade, crater members as crater-field (bowl, rim, peak), Keep Width (SortedSediment), Output enum {Height, StoneValue, LayerIndex}.
master.risks:
Seed risk 0.25: own-cell cap on top size stays.
The three forms read Level in different places and that matters: GradedStamp and GradedCraters read it at the lane, SortedSediment at the stone centre 'so the map never slices a stone'. GradedStamp's claim that a stamp 'fades in as a whole' does not follow from reading Level at the lane, since Level varies across the footprint. Compare the two on the ramp test.
