nested-craters.look: Relief reads as a lunar landscape with real hierarchy: big flat floored craters with terraced walls and central peaks, small craters sitting on the floors that scale with their floor and stop short of the wall, then craters on those. The base lattice between parents is a dense carpet of small craters and rims with star shaped ejecta fringes. A clean ring between floor children and the wall is visible, width set by Rim. Vol: cavities with nested pits, the crater-field 3D form with more interest.
nested-craters.dims: 2D and 3D rendered and measured. Vol shows spherical caverns with small dimples on their walls. 4D not written, the code is dimension agnostic apart from the frame rotation.
nested-craters.range: measured -1.0 (clips) to 0.523 over 8 seeds and offsets, default window -0.712 to 0.427; far coords -1.0 to 0.464, no NaN. The -1 clip is the deepest floors on some seeds; 3D -0.441 to 0.398.
nested-craters.artifacts: No jumps after the fix. Nothing of the lattice reads in the FFT. The fade means a child straddling the rim is flattened rather than kept whole; at default Rim it reads as a slightly softened small crater near the rim. Rim ring is visually regular on the largest craters. Inverted route (route=1, DomainInvert comparison, the entry's smallest test): also clean, c0ratio 7.40, straddle 7.45, steps 0.0105, 0.00105, 0.00013, needs no fade and is conformal, but the children cross the rim as mirrored pairs and break it, so crater rims look mottled and the bowl is less legible; the owner frame wins on looks and keeps its rim whole.
nested-craters.node_shape: Levels (int passes), Base Frequency, Lacunarity, Child Scale, Rim, Child Depth, Density, Child Density, Radius Min/Max, Ejecta, Depth, Rim Height, Peak, Flat, Terrace, Rays, Row Shuffle (bool), Output Min/Max
nested-craters.port_notes: Lane state is q[D], world scale, F, fade, amp, seed, all Selected per lane at each pass, one own cell per pass with one hash. Everything is a fixed loop, so it is a plain mask port. Additive stamps only: erase multiplies the height of the parent floor, and in a coarse to fine fold that lifts a pillar (first attempt measured a 0.46 step shrinking only 7x over 2 decades); crater-field folds fine to coarse, which is why erase worked there. Crater-field's terrace and ray terms jump as written (terrace at t = 0.6, rays at t = 1), measured 0.17 at h=1e-3 here; this prototype ramps them in, and crater-field needs the same fix if its terr or ray ever ship. New owner's rotation is from a 16 entry table of unit vectors, no trig at Gen time.

master.one_liner: Child craters in the owner crater's local frame: they sit on its floor, scale with it, and fade at its rim.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: small craters on a big floor that scale with that floor, ejecta rays in the owner frame, terraced walls.
master.algorithm: 1) Level 0: 3x3 own-cell crater search as crater-field; keep the owning crater's centre c0, radius r0, hash h0 (or no owner). 2) Transform p into owner frame: q = (p - c0) / r0 rotated by an angle from h0; seed1 = h0. 3) Level 1: run the own-cell crater stamp on q with cell size ChildScale (0.2..0.4) and seed1; child depth multiplied by a fade smoothstep((1 - |q|) / Rim) so children vanish at the parent rim, which keeps continuity across owner switches exactly as NestedCaps does. Lanes with no owner evaluate level 1 on the base lattice instead (Select). 4) Repeat for Levels (fixed int), each child becoming the owner for the next. 5) Combine: parent height + child height * ChildDepth^L; rays: optional term in the owner frame, Abs(sin(k * atan-approx(q))) * falloff(|q|), continuous because it is a function of q only. 6) Output range by measured table. 3D: own-cell in 3x3x3, child frame = scaled translation only. Cost about Levels x crater-field.
master.why_new:
NestedCaps was the strongest surprise in lobes: children living in the owner's frame never cross a parent boundary and scale with it. Applied to craters it gives small craters that sit on a big floor and scale with that floor, ejecta rays in the owner frame, and terraced walls, none of which the absolute-lattice crater field can do.
Seed cluster InvertedStamp / NestedCraters: InvertedStamp is in dropped (duplicate of bubble-invert / DomainInvert). Different mechanisms, so they do not share an entry.
master.simd_plan: Cost about Levels x crater-field.
master.continuity: 3) Level 1: run the own-cell crater stamp on q with cell size ChildScale (0.2..0.4) and seed1; child depth multiplied by a fade smoothstep((1 - |q|) / Rim) so children vanish at the parent rim, which keeps continuity across owner switches exactly as NestedCaps does. 5) Combine: parent height + child height * ChildDepth^L; rays: optional term in the owner frame, Abs(sin(k * atan-approx(q))) * falloff(|q|), continuous because it is a function of q only.
master.params: Levels (int), Child Scale (0.2 to 0.4), Rim, Child Depth, Rays k, crater members as crater-field.

Noticed in merge: lanes with no owner evaluate level 1 on the base lattice, and nothing fades those children at the parent's rim from outside, so a base-lattice child crossing a parent rim may jump there. Check with the jump scan.

No owner lanes continue in the current frame (the entry evaluates them on the base lattice); that is the same at level 1 and generalises to any level, and the frame stays continuous across cells. flagged_jump.fix: fade *= smoothstep(0, rim, t - 1) on lanes outside an alive crater, so every later pass reaches zero at the rim from outside too, as it does from inside. Rim <= ejecta keeps this ramp inside the own cell, so it is finished before the cell border and the no owner frame stays continuous across cells. fixout=0 keeps the entry's form for comparison.

crater-gullies.look: Crater walls are dissected by fine radial gullies running from rim to floor, spoked out over the ejecta: craters look old and weathered, or like ink splats in the threshold view. Floors and plains stay clean, so small craters survive. Mid sized craters get a few spokes, large ones many. The graph route has the same gullies on big walls but dissects every small crater and every plain as well, giving a crumpled look everywhere, because a gradient cannot tell a small crater from a big wall. At hscale 80 rims looked like a jagged crown with str 0.055, so str came down to 0.042.
crater-gullies.dims: 2D only as a true shape. Eval3 is the heightfield form: h(x, z), and with ydens > 0 a density h - ydens * (y - y0); y does not enter the craters. That is the erosion filter's own 3D form and its stripe kernel has no sensible volumetric meaning. z-continuity mean 0.0012, max 0.0052 at dz 1e-3. 4D not written.
crater-gullies.range: measured -0.867 to 0.641 over 8 seeds and offsets, far coords -0.881 to 0.563, no NaN
crater-gullies.artifacts: No jump in the default route. Where walls of two overlapping craters oppose, the vector field cancels and gullies stop there, a small blank patch rather than a seam. Gully scale is one world scale per octave: it does not follow crater size, only amplitude does, so a mid crater gets a few wide spokes. FFT is isotropic.
crater-gullies.node_shape: Best as members of the crater node: Gully Octaves, Gully Scale, Gully Strength, Gully Frequency, Wall Start, Gully Min Radius, Gully Full Radius. A standalone node would duplicate the crater members.
crater-gullies.port_notes: Steering field is the whole trick: S = S (1 - m) + wall(t) smoothstep(rlo, rhi, Rw) radial, composited by the fold's own erase mask, then M = easeOut(|S| / sloperef) and direction S / |S|. wall(t) is smooth and zero on the floor and at the ejecta edge, so no finite differences and no kink. Cost is about 6 ops per stamp. No line field needed: doubling the angle looked the same, and needs a branch cut that breaks stripe feedback (measured 0.011 at h=1e-5). The tile trick from the erosion family would apply but was not tested here.
crater-gullies.params_text: (defaults: gmode=2,line=0,oct=3,s0=0.2,str=0.042,sf=0.6,branch=0.3,sloperef=0.6,tf=0.55,rlo=0.22,rhi=0.9,lev=10,lacc=1.45,f0=0.2,dens=1,slope=2.2,replay=2,repf=0.6,ogain=2.6). gmode=1 is the graph route with finite differences, gmode=0 the entry's analytic gradient with a slope mask.

master.one_liner: Radial gullies cut into crater walls: the erosion filter's stripe kernel steered by the crater field's closed-form gradient, with no finite differences.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: crater relief whose rims are dissected by radial gullies that fade on flats: planet surfaces, an old eroded moon, Mars.
master.algorithm: Per lane: evaluate CraterField levels as today but accumulate (h, dh/dx, dh/dy) analytically per level (bowl, rim and peak are polynomials of r, so grad = f'(r) * (p - c)/r, masked by the same erase rule). Slope mask m = smoothstep(s0, s1, |grad|). Then run 2 octaves of the erosion filter's 3x3 triangular stripe kernel with direction = grad/|grad| and amplitude a*m, exactly as erosion-filter does on its Perlin base, and return h - stripes. Fixed loop counts (levels, 2 octaves), one hash per lattice point, 3x3 window per octave. Cost estimate: crater (~16 ns 2D est.) + 2 x ~8 ns = ~32 ns 2D; 3D/4D by the same window rule. Tiles via the torus-angle trick the erosion family already built.
master.why_new:
Crater walls in the relief are smooth; real crater rims are dissected by radial gullies. The erosion filter already proves the steer-by-gradient kernel; the crater profile is closed form so its gradient is free, no finite differences.
Seed gap: planet surfaces; Old Eroded Planet and Mars presets want the same thing.
master.simd_plan: Cost estimate: crater (~16 ns 2D est.) + 2 x ~8 ns = ~32 ns 2D; 3D/4D by the same window rule.
master.continuity: Not stated by the panel.
master.params: Crater levels and members as crater-field, Slope Mask s0 and s1, Stripe Octaves (2), Stripe Amplitude a, stripe kernel members as ErosionFilter, torus-angle tiling.

Reachable with real nodes as ErosionFilter(Source=StampLayers crater), which uses finite differences at the rims; the presets Old Eroded Planet and Mars propose exactly that graph. Only the closed-form gradient through the erase rule is new, so look at the graph first.

moon-base.look: From above: dozens of bright boulders ringed round big and medium craters, thinning out onto the plain, and rather few on plains between them. The rim mask itself (grid out=1 during tuning) is a clean set of halos, removed inside young floors. Vol: chiselled rocks sitting on a cratered ground, denser around the rims, half buried, which reads as a boulder field. Stones are a small part of the picture at thumb scale, so without close views they read as bright speckle. The ring is not strongly legible on medium craters, as each has only a few stones.
moon-base.dims: 2D (top view: height with stone tops, what the sheet, thumb and relief show) and 3D (density with chiselled stones, y up) both rendered and measured. The sheet's 3D slice panel is black because it cuts the empty air above the ground, ignore it. 4D not written.
moon-base.range: 2D measured -0.776 to 0.738 over 8 seeds and offsets, far coords -0.804 to 0.621, no NaN. 3D density -1 to 1 by construction, z-continuity mean 0.0001, max 0.0093 at dz 1e-3.
moon-base.artifacts: No jump. A stone on a steep inner wall leans into it by height, since it rests on its centre's height with no tilt. The own-cell cap applies to the ejecta: rings can never exceed 1 + ej radii. Some boulders sit out on the wide ejecta of adjacent craters, which is correct. In relief at hscale 60 the stones read as small cones rather than rocks; the vol is the honest view of them.
moon-base.node_shape: As members on the two parents: Crater Field gets Output = Rim Mask with Inner Width, Outer Width, Thinning Power, Min Radius, Full Radius. Grounded Scatter gets Density (hybrid sampled at candidate) and Soft.
moon-base.port_notes: The rim mask is worth having on the crater node regardless: 2 ops per stamp, composited by m exactly like height, so a young floor removes old boulders with no extra logic. Reading density at the candidate, radius scaled by on, means density thins continuously and a stone is a pure function of its column, as grounded-scatter already does for height. No extra window.

master.algorithm: Per lane in 3D: Height = CraterField(p.xz) (the Height source). For each of the 9 (27 with tilt) stone candidates, evaluate the crater rim mask once at the candidate's cell centre c (rimMask = clamp(1 - |r - R_rim| / ejectaWidth) summed over levels, available from the same crater evaluation at c); stone exists where hash < density0 * rimMask(c) using stamp-scatter's cascade fade so appearance is continuous as the mask varies in space. Stone SDF, sink and smooth-min union exactly as grounded-scatter; output density = min(terrain SDF, stones). Fixed candidate count, no extra window. Cost estimate: grounded-scatter cost + 9 crater evals at ~16 ns each (so ~150-200 ns 3D, a bake node like its parents).
master.why_new:
Crater relief has no ejecta; real craters are ringed by boulder fields that thin with distance from the rim. Grounded-scatter already attaches stones to a Height source; the only new part is a density that depends on the rim mask, which stamp-scatter's cascade fade keeps pop-free.

halftone-spots.look: An even stipple whose density follows the source: clean dots, no clumps and no bald patches, and it visibly beats ThinSpots beside it (the random row clusters and tears, the IGN row does not). jit=0 gives a graphic halftone with a diamond textured dot screen, and jit=0.7 reads as a mezzotint or sand stipple. Pits on white read as a leather or pitted surface whose pores thin evenly. Ramps: Random is clumpy, IGN and R2 are well dispersed with visible diagonals, LocalRank is between them and a little blocky. 3D is a stippled sphere cloud, not striking on its own. Plain AM growth with soft=1 at a flat order is a normal screen and no better than a graph, so the new thing is the dispersed order.

halftone-spots.range: -1 to 1 by construction, measured over 8 seeds and far coords, no NaN. Mean -0.34 with the default coverage.
halftone-spots.artifacts: IGN at jit=0 shows diagonal rows at some coverages, as the entry predicted; R2 at jit=0 shows lattice lines more strongly and looks less natural. Shuffle does not change block counts here but its block seams let live cells touch (0.272 against 0.001 at 6 percent), so it trades local dispersion for long range structure, and it stays off in defaults. At jit 0.7 the structure is not visible by eye. Dots merge at high coverage, as a halftone should. No jump.

master.one_liner: ThinSpots' whole-spot thresholding with LowDiscrepancyDither's ordering: each spot switches on at an IGN, R2 or local-rank value of its cell instead of a random one, so coverage ramps as a halftone screen or a dispersed stipple with no clumps and no bald patches.
master.look: A halftone of any source: round dots that grow from pinpricks to merging blobs as the source brightens (AM), or an even stipple whose density follows the source with dots of one size (FM), in both cases visibly free of the clumps and voids ThinSpots shows. Grid Jitter 0 with IGN is a true screen; jitter 0.8 is a mezzotint or engraving stipple; Pit profile gives leather pores or rust pitting that thins evenly; LocalRank at low coverage is a Matern hard-core scatter with guaranteed spacing. 3D: a sphere stipple whose density follows a volume.
master.algorithm: As t_thin_spots: lattice at Feature Scale, one spot per cell, jittered site, coverage C from a hybrid read once at the sample, ramp = C*(1+Soft). Per cell the order value o in [0,1): Order enum Random: rnd01(hash) (ThinSpots); IGN: frac(52.9829189*frac(0.06711056*(ix+so) + 0.00583715*iy)) with the LDD seed offset so and its 3D frame term; R2: frac(0.5 + 0.7548776662*ix + 0.5698402910*iy) (R3 constants in 3D); LocalRank: rank of the cell's hash among its 3^D neighbours divided by 3^D (HardCoreCellular's exactly uniform rank; 2D only at full cost, 3D uses the 7-cell axis cross). on = smoothstep(o, o + Soft, ramp); radius r = s*(1 - Size Jitter*rnd)*on^Gain; height profile as ThinSpots (Lens, Dome, Pit, Ring, Cone), value scaled by on, max over the 3^D window (Min for Pit). Soft small gives FM: dots pop in at their ordered thresholds at full size; Soft near 1 gives AM: every dot grows across the whole coverage range after it switches on. Output: Height, Mask (hard at r), Value (per-spot flat), and Inverse (holes in a sheet). LDD's block shuffle (xs) is offered as Shuffle to break IGN's long diagonals.
master.why_new: ThinSpots (keeper) orders spots at random, so its density ramps are clumpy; LowDiscrepancyDither (keeper) thresholds per pixel and has no dots, sizes or profiles; BlueNoiseScatter (keeper) and StencilFilter's blue-noise dots need a neighbourhood test per candidate. Here the ordering is a free function of the cell index evaluated inside the spot loop, which no graph can inject into StampScatter's or ThinSpots' per-spot decision.
master.simd_plan: ThinSpots' 3^D loop with masks; IGN and R2 are two fracs on converted ints; LocalRank adds 8 hashes per candidate (72 in 2D, cheap integer ops). Estimated AVX2: 2D 5-8 ns (LocalRank 9-12), 3D 15-25 ns, 4D 60-80 ns plus the coverage hybrid.
master.continuity: C0 for continuous Coverage: as ThinSpots, radius and height both scale with on, so a spot reaches zero before it vanishes; Mask output is discontinuous by design. The order value is per cell and never changes with the sample position.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Coverage (hybrid), Order enum {Random, IGN, R2, LocalRank}, Soft, Gain, Size, Size Jitter, Profile enum, Shuffle (int, 0 off), Output enum, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: IGN shows a diagonal texture at low jitter and R2 shows lattice lines at some coverages; Shuffle fixes the long range structure at the cost of local dispersion. Spots overlap above about 50 percent coverage unless Size is kept under half a cell, which is correct for a halftone but not for a non-overlapping scatter.

quota-cells.look: Mask: round stamps spread evenly with no bald patches and no clumps, beside the coin version that clearly bunches and leaves holes. Hi from fbm thins by losing whole stamps, as asked. It looks like scattered dots: it is a utility and not a picture, and its point is the guarantee. The dyadic question: at t = 1/4 the FFT has no dots or cross, but the 4x wide view shows a faint woven regularity. At t = 1/16 the wide view shows no blocks by eye, and the FFT has no peaks, only a faint low contrast diagonal ripple. Rank and Class are flat pixel confetti, Smooth is lattice looking value noise, F1 is plain cell blobs; those three are useful only for what the counts give.

The Mask's 4D form on an oblique plane: c0 7.53, straddle 7.59. 3D plane: c0 8.04, straddle 8.07, steps 0.0741, 0.00743, 0.00075. Tiling via 4D not tested. The harness's check 3D line reads flat -1 at default fine=4 because its plane z=0.5 sits on a lattice plane where own cell stamps never reach; at fine=3.7 it reads -1 to 0.488, z-continuity max 0.0555.

quota-cells.artifacts: Selected cells can touch across a block border, so pairs appear: spacing is even but not hard-core, as the entry warned. Own cell Mask with rad 0.4 keeps centres near lattice points, so a dense layer shows the lattice, and small stamps wander more. A 2D slice of the 3D form is not stratified, and rows of aligned dots and voids show in the sheet's slice. The guarantee holds only for aligned blocks where Lo and Hi are constant, and a warp breaks it.

quota-cells.port_notes: Hash per level, one bijection per level from a 2 bit xor and a small table lookup of parity masks. Fixed loop over L. 4 bit parity is 2 shifts and xors, or use popcnt. Tables: 6 matrices is all of GL(2,2), 3D and 4D have 8 hand checked invertible matrices, so fewer than all, which only reduces scramble quality and not the guarantee. 2D L=12 and 3D L=8 and 4D L=6 fit the float mantissa. Sites use the free room (1-2R) as jitter, so jitter needs no separate limit. Exact proof holds for the top digits, so a port must keep finest digit on top.

master.one_liner: Per-cell rank from a hash-scrambled Morton descent: threshold it and every aligned block holds its exact quota of cells, at every scale, so N villages per region, exact ore counts and non-overlapping placement layers come from one pointwise value.
master.look: Mask: round stamps spread evenly with no bald patches and no clumps, thinning by losing whole stamps as density falls. Class: confetti with exact budgets. Smooth: even blobs whose thresholded coverage barely changes from block to block, less natural at large scale than FBm, which is what a designer asking for 'every region has some' wants. Good for trees, rocks, ore, spawn points, structure slots.
master.algorithm:
c = floor(p / Feature Scale) as ints. L = Levels (block side 2^L cells). D = dimension.
rank = 0
for l = L-1 down to 0:
  node = c >> (l+1)                 // arithmetic shift, one id per parent block, fine for negative cells
  h = Hash(seed + l*K, node)        // one hash per level, same scheme as FastNoise
  b = (c >> l) & 1                  // D bits: which child of this parent holds the cell
  d = T(h, b)                       // random affine bijection on D bits. 2D: bit0 = parity(m0 & b) ^ h.bit0, bit1 = parity(m1 & b) ^ h.bit1, (m0,m1) from a 6 entry table of invertible GF(2) matrices indexed by hash bits (AGL(2,2) is all of S4). 3D, 4D: xor mask plus a short fixed table of invertible matrices
  rank |= d << (D*(L-1-l))          // the FINEST level goes to the TOP of rank
u = (rank + rnd(h_last)) / 2^(D*L)
Proof of the quota: in a block of side 2^m (cells share c >> m) the path to each cell is a chain of bijections, so the top D*m bits of rank are a permutation of all 2^(D*m) values. So #{u < t} in that block is floor(t*n) or floor(t*n)+1 with n = 2^(D*m), for every aligned block and every t.
Outputs:
  Rank: 2u-1, flat per cell.
  Mask: own cell only, no window. Site s = c + 0.5 + J*(rnd-0.5), radius r <= (1-J)/2. Active = Lo(s) <= u < Hi(s), with Lo and Hi hybrids read once at the site. out = dome(|p-s|/r) if active, else floor. Whole objects only.
  Class: shares f_1..f_n, cumulative F_k in a small table, out = value of first k with u < F_k.
  Smooth: quintic tensor interpolation of the 2^D corner ranks: value noise with a stratified lattice.
  F1: 3^D window of sites with the same active test, for Voronoi biome regions.
Exclusive layers: two instances with the same seed and disjoint [Lo,Hi) can never use the same cell. Raising Hi only adds cells, it never moves or removes one.
master.why_new: Hard made easy, and a guarantee nothing here has. Nearest: CellularDensity (independent Bernoulli per site: for 64 cells at t=0.1 the count is 6.4 +- 2.4; here it is 6 or 7, always), HardCoreCellular (rank among 3^D neighbours: exact spacing at one density, no block counts, no free threshold), LowDiscrepancyDither (quasi-periodic grid, no block guarantee, no scramble), ExactGaussianNoise (exact expected area; its entry admits small windows fluctuate). Evidence read: Horizon Zero Dawn's shipped placement uses a precomputed pattern whose thresholds are spread evenly and ordered for distance, and gives each same-footprint layer a density range so a point can fall in one layer only, which avoids readback and overlap; artists stack more than 20 such layers. This is the same contract on an infinite lattice, with no tile. A Godot Voxel Tools user on FastNoiseLite cellular asks for 1 capital, 2 villages and 3 dungeons per biome from a generator that sees a small window. The Riverheim mod for Valheim lists budgeted biomes, a guaranteed amount of each, as a feature. Minecraft's rarity_filter is an independent per position coin. Red Blob recommends jittered grids or Poisson disc over noise maxima but neither has a count guarantee.
master.simd_plan: Integer only, fixed L, no search for Rank, Mask and Class: L hashes plus bit ops, cost nearly independent of dimension. Estimate at L=6: 1-2 ns per sample in 2D, 3D and 4D, plus Lo/Hi evals at the site. Smooth: 2^D descents, about 5 / 10 / 20 ns. F1: 3^D descents, about 13 / 40 / 120 ns, so offer it but steer people to Mask. 4D is the same code with 4 bit digits and L <= 6 so rank fits a float mantissa; tiling comes from the 4D form. Estimates only.
master.continuity: Rank and Class discontinuous per cell by design. Mask C0: the stamp reaches zero at its rim inside its own cell and activity is a per site constant, so nothing pops inside a stamp. Smooth C2 from quintic weights.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Levels (int), Grid Jitter, Radius, Lo (hybrid), Hi (hybrid), Shares (table up to 8), Output enum (Rank, Mask, Class, Smooth, F1), Output Min/Max
master.risks: The count is a proof, the look is not: dyadic structure may read at densities near powers of 1/4, and selected cells can touch across a block border, so spacing is even but not hard-core. Exact only in aligned blocks and only where Lo/Hi are constant across the block. A warp moves area across blocks; an area preserving DomainWarpShear keeps the global share only. No adjacency control for Class, that is ClimateDiagram's job.

grain-packing.look: Exact non overlapping ellipses of many sizes that follow a slow angle field, packed tightly with small grains in the corners: pebbles laid by a current, almonds, seeds, fish scales, or a river bed in relief, which is the strongest view. The flow is clear in the threshold panel. Mode 1 (Fit) has no large black voids and shows the triangulation as a web, more like cells in tissue. Blot (shape=1) makes spiky flakes or shards, which reads as a different material. No visible lattice in the wide view; FFT is isotropic with no dots.

grain-packing.artifacts: No jump. Coverage drops with aspect, as the entry warned (0.724 to 0.589 from aspect 1 to 3), which leaves dark gaps that show where triangles meet at high aspect; Blend reduces this. Vertices of the triangulation give small dark star shapes between grains. 3D: flat lattice planes between grains. Alignment is per triangle, so two neighbours can differ by the hash jitter and the noise slope, and a sharp change of angle reads as a slip, which looks natural here.

World minor semi-axis needs the 2x2 largest singular value, closed form, 2 sqrts, or for mode 0 is just 1/a. Steiner frame needs one divide by the triangle's det. Blend falls back to Fit per triangle if the blended matrix's det gets near zero, which is constant per triangle and so seamless. Blot uses complex powers of the unit vector instead of trig: the harmonics are 3rd and 5th.

master.one_liner: CellularCirclePacking run inside an affine frame per triangle: the incircle becomes an inscribed ellipse with its own orientation and aspect, still tangent to the three sides, so the plane fills with rice grains, almonds, scales and pebbles of many sizes that never overlap.
master.look: A bed of elongated grains tightly packed without overlap: rice, almonds, coffee beans, fish scales, river pebbles, each at its own angle and size, large grains hugged by small ones in the corners (the Apollonian levels). With Angle driven by a slow noise the grains align into flows: a shoal of fish, wheat laid by wind, brushed grain. Mask output is a crisp non-overlapping ellipse packing. Relief reads as a pebble beach of flattened stones; 3D volume is a packing of ellipsoids like a gravel core sample.
master.algorithm: Reuse t_cellular_circle_packing unchanged except for one wrapper. Locate the triangle T of the jittered triangulation that contains the sample (the proto's oneTri path: 4 quads, 8 triangles, max of min barycentric). For T choose an orientation theta_T and aspect a_T >= 1: from the triangle id hash, or theta from a hybrid Angle read once at T's centroid plus hashed jitter. Build S = diag(1, a_T) * R(-theta_T). Map the three vertices and the sample: v' = S v, x' = S x. Run the incircle, corner-circle homothety (q = (D-r)/(D+r)) and gap-circle code on the mapped triangle and mapped sample, exactly as the proto does, obtaining the best circle (centre c', radius r', normalised distance t = |x'-c'|/r'). Because affine maps preserve tangency and containment, every mapped circle is an ellipse inside T in world space, tangent to the same sides, with semi-axes r' along theta and r'/a along the perpendicular; adjacent triangles each keep their ellipses inside themselves, so ellipses never overlap whatever theta and a they chose. Shade with the proto's Dome/Lens/Mask/Id outputs using t; Dome height uses the world minor semi-axis r'/a so flat grains stay low. Shape enum adds Blot: inside the ellipse, scale t by 1/(1 - b*|S_dir(u)|) where S_dir is a direction-sampled source as SplatBurst does, clamped so the blot stays inside its ellipse. SDF output (needs all 8 triangles) also maps each triangle separately. 3D: insphere of the located tet mapped by S = diag(1, a, b) R^T, giving packed ellipsoids; the proto already has the tet insphere and corner spheres.
master.why_new: CellularCirclePacking (keeper) is circles only; FlowShingle (ship) gives oriented stamps but they overlap with a stacking order; CellularMetricField (keeper) gives elongated cells, not discs with gaps; BubblePack and PebblePile are round or stacked. Exact non-overlapping oriented ellipses of widely varying size are not reachable by a graph because the orientation has to be applied before the incircle is solved, inside the kernel.
master.simd_plan: Same window and branch structure as CellularCirclePacking (4 quads, point location by Select, one triangle's circles), plus a 2x2 matrix multiply of 4 points and one hybrid eval at the centroid. Estimated AVX2: 2D 8-12 ns, 3D 40-60 ns (48 Kuhn tets located, one insphere), 4D not planned beyond dropping w (a 4D simplex packing is possible but the located-simplex search is large).
master.continuity: Dome and Lens are C0 (each ellipse's dome reaches zero at its rim, background flat); Mask and Id are discontinuous by design; SDF is C0 with the proto's clamp outside. Hybrid Angle read at the centroid keeps one frame per triangle, so no in-triangle shear; a per-lane Angle would break the guarantee and is not offered.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Aspect Min/Max (per triangle hash range), Angle (hybrid, read at the triangle centroid), Angle Jitter, Depth (corner levels), Gaps (bool), Gap (shrink factor), Shape enum {Ellipse, Blot}, Blot Amount, Output enum {Dome, Lens, Mask, Id, SDF}, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Fill fraction drops with aspect (an in-ellipse of a nearly equilateral triangle at aspect 3 is small), so high aspects give sparse grains in a visible triangle lattice unless Depth and Gaps are on; the look may want Grid Jitter near 1 plus a CellularRelaxed-style step to even the triangles. Blot shapes must be clamped inside the ellipse or the guarantee is lost.

master.one_liner: CellularCluster's explicit children joined in their shape order by BondGraph's capsule segments: dotted rings become necklaces, trails become polylines, clumps become molecules, so constellations, circuit traces, beaded chains and ring hedges draw themselves with one parent hash.
master.look: Black ground with thin bright line figures: beaded rings and ovals, zigzag polylines with knots at the joints, star bursts, short wandering chains, mixed across the field, each a single connected object and well separated. Reads as constellation charts, molecule diagrams, circuit traces with solder pads, bead necklaces, fairy-ring hedges from the air, or sewing stitches. Height output in relief is wire sculpture on a plain; 3D volume is a scatter of molecules and wire rings. ClusterValue colours each figure.
master.algorithm: Parent lattice at Feature Scale, 3^D window. Per parent cell (hash H, alive with probability Density read at the parent centre): centre cp = cell + 0.5 + Parent Jitter; Count children M (fixed int, default 8); shape from Shape enum or hashed when Mixed. Child k position c_k as an explicit function of (H, k): Ring: cp + S*(cos(2*pi*k/M + phi0 + Spin*w), sin(..)) + Child Jitter*rnd(H,k); Arc: the same for k < M*Arc Fraction; Trail: cp + dir*(2*k/(M-1) - 1)*L + bow*(1 - (2k/(M-1)-1)^2)*perp(dir); Walk: c_0 = cp, c_k = c_{k-1} + step*rndDir(H,k) folded back into radius S (a squiggle); Star: all children at radius S, segments to cp instead of to the next child. Segments join (c_k, c_{k+1}) for k < M-1 plus (c_{M-1}, c_0) when Closed. For each segment the capsule distance (segDist as in t_cellular_dual_mesh) with half width Width*(1 - Width Jitter*rnd(H,k)); bead discs of radius Bead at every c_k. d = min over the window's parents, segments and beads; radii bounded so S + L + Width stays under the window reach (Feature Scale/2 minus jitter), as ClusterCellular bounds its macro shapes. Outputs: Distance (clamped), Mask, Height (ribbon profile 1 - (d/W)^2 with beads raised), ClusterValue (per parent hash, flat inside the strokes, background -1), SegmentIndex (k/M along the chain for gradients along necklaces). Spin uses w in 4D or a Phase hybrid: rings rotate, trails wag, walks writhe, each child position being an exact periodic function of the phase, so loops are seamless. 3D: Ring lies in a hashed plane, Walk in 3D, Star to the centre; segments are 3D capsules; molecules and ball-and-stick clusters in volume.
master.why_new: ClusterCellular (promising) draws only dots arranged in macro shapes; BondGraph (keeper) wires neighbouring lattice points locally and can make no closed ring, star or long polyline; CoralNoise branches hierarchically but never closes. The child order k is the mechanism BondGraph lacks and the segment distance is the mechanism ClusterCellular lacks; joining them is a one-kernel job because the segment endpoints are the children of the same parent hash.
master.simd_plan: 3^D parents times (M segments + M beads) capsule tests, all fixed loops with masks; each child position is a few FMAs and one sin/cos (Ring) or a table of hashed directions. Estimated AVX2: 2D with M=8: 15-25 ns; 3D with M=8: 60-90 ns, honestly heavy, M=5 for volumes; 4D by dropping w into Spin only (the shape lattice stays 3D), which keeps tiling via Spin periodic.
master.continuity: Distance and Height are C0 (min of capsule distances, clamped at the window reach); Mask, ClusterValue and SegmentIndex are discontinuous by design. Spin is C0 in the phase because every child position is continuous in it.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Density (hybrid at the parent), Count (int), Shape enum {Ring, Arc, Trail, Walk, Star, Mixed}, Closed (enum), Size, Size Jitter, Child Jitter, Width, Width Jitter, Bead, Spin (hybrid phase), Output enum, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Polylines with few children look polygonal; Width Jitter and bow help but true arcs would need per-segment arc distances. 3D cost is high. Dense settings tangle neighbouring figures (they are not hard-core); a HardCoreCellular rank gate on parents would space them at 9 extra hashes per parent.

master.one_liner: Stamps rooted on any 3D isosurface and oriented by its normal: each own-cell site Newton-projects onto a guide density, so crystals, barnacles, shelf fungi and spikes sit on walls, ceilings and overhangs with no placement pass.
master.look: Geode and vug interiors lined with hexagonal quartz pointing out of every surface; barnacle crust on a sea cave; urchin rock; bracket fungi stacked on a cliff; ice needles under overhangs. Crystals keep rigid facets at any angle, which no warp or threshold can give. Judge from stills: vol of a sponge or Perlin cave with the cut face through a wall. Stamps must point away from rock on floor, wall and ceiling alike, and none may float.
master.algorithm:
Guide G is smooth and cheap; S is the full density. Lattice 3D, cell C, own cell only.
cell = floor(p/C); h = hash(cell); s = C*(cell + 0.5 + J*(rnd3(h) - 0.5))
4 tetrahedral taps of G around s give g0 and gradient gv; n = gv/|gv|
s2 = s - g0*gv/|gv|^2    // one Newton step; a second step costs 4 more taps
fit = Min over axes of (cell border distance of s2)   // how much room the stamp has
ri = Min(Rmax*(0.5 + rnd(h,2)), fit)
gate = rnd(h) < Density, and ri *= smoothstep(Keep range, n.y)   // n.y band selects floors, walls or ceilings, shrinking to zero rather than popping
t1, t2 = orthonormal frame from n (Frisvad, sign Select instead of a branch)
q = (dot(p - s2, t1), dot(p - s2, n), dot(p - s2, t2))/ri
d(q) by Stamp enum:
  Crystal: Max(hexdist(q.xz) - w, q.y - L + TipSlope*hexdist(q.xz)), lean by a hashed shear of q.xz with q.y
  Spike: Max(|q.xz| - w*(1 - q.y/L), q.y - L)
  Barnacle: truncated cone with a crater in its top
  Shelf: world up replaces n as the disc axis, half disc on the wall side
d = Max(d, -q.y - Sink)   // root inside rock
out = Max(S(p), -d*ri*Scale)
Clusters: Layers (int) repeats the pass with a lattice offset and a new seed.
master.why_new: GroundedScatter and GroundedCrystals (crossbreed 29) need a heightfield, so they cannot reach a ceiling or the far side of an overhang. FlutedCave (crossbreed 4) adds surface detail, not bodies. Dripstone is vertical only and needs no normal; this needs one but is limited to about a cell in size. StampScatter has no notion of a surface.
master.simd_plan: Per lane: 4 G evals at the site, 1 S at p, a frame and an SDF; no window since each stamp is confined to its cell. G = 2 octave Perlin: about 18 + 3 ns plus S (estimate). 2D is a side view with a tangent frame. 4D uses a 4D gradient (5 taps) and a stamp in the n, t1, t2 subspace with w as extra radius.
master.continuity: C0: ri falls to 0 at the cell border via fit, and site data does not depend on the lane. Hexdist and Max make creases, intended for facets.
master.params: Source S, Guide, Feature Scale, Density, Stamp enum, Rmax, L, Lean, Normal Range, Newton Steps, Layers. Hybrid: Density is read at the site in a Guide-like eval (1 more).
master.risks: Coverage. Rough S against smooth G leaves stamps floating over dimples or buried. Size is bound to cell size. Cost scales with the Guide.

Second Newton step replaced by a chord step (1 tap, stale gradient) and a check tap that kills sites further than 0.1 from the guide and doubles as a last chord step: 6 taps instead of 8, fewer floaters. Added the cell border ramp so Max( S, stamp ) is C0 in the value, which the entry's plain Max is not.

master.one_liner: Imbricated talus: flow-shingle stamps aligned downhill by the terrain gradient, using the chisel-rubble silhouette.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: angular stones overlapping down a slope, with flats left bare. Hard edges, so a material or mask rather than a smooth heightfield.
master.algorithm: Per lane: terrain height H(p) and gradient from 3 taps (2D) give downhill direction u and slope m. Run flow-shingle's 3x3 (3x3x3) candidate search with per-candidate frame aligned to u sampled at the candidate's cell centre (one extra H tap per candidate, 9 in 2D, or reuse the lane's u for a cheaper approximation), stamp = chisel-rubble polygon from fixed icosahedral cut axes in the candidate's hashed rotation, priority = position along u so downhill stones overlap uphill ones. Density hybrid = smoothstep of slope m so flats stay bare. Output H + stoneHeight * mask. Hard edges like flow-shingle (c0 ~1), so a material/mask, not a smooth heightfield. Cost estimate: 3 + 9 H taps + ~8 ns.
master.why_new:
Flow-shingle stacks oriented overlapping stamps along a field; scree and talus are exactly that: angular stones imbricated down a slope. The field is the terrain gradient and the stamp is the chisel-rubble silhouette, both already prototyped.
Seed gap: imbricated talus.

scree-shingle.changed_from_entry: Stones are height stamps with Max of tilted plates instead of flow-shingle's priority winner. Each plate rises toward its downhill lip, so the plate from the uphill cell lies over the next plate's tail without any sort, and an edge ramp takes each stone to 0 at its outline: height is C0, not the c0 ~1 the entry expected. Top is a Min of 3 planes for facets. Polygon uses 3 fixed 2D axes with a small hashed rotation. Default order is lip over tail (uphill stone on top, like roof tiles), which I chose after comparing it to the entry's order: the flipped order shows the same pattern with dark steps facing uphill, and less of a stepped read from downhill. Density is a per stone slope threshold instead of a uniform fade, so field edges dissolve into single stones. Per candidate gradient kept as cand=1 only: 27 taps, and its isolated rigid stones did not justify the price.

peak-scatter.look: Relief with Horn next to plain fBm: 6 to 8 sharp, textured mountain horns rise from existing summits, while the slopes and valleys between them are the same terrain as plain fBm. The horns carry the terrain's fine detail, so they do not read as smooth pasted cones, but they have a similar shape to each other and at hslope 0.8 some look like small volcano cones. No aretes form: the entry's promise of aretes is not met. Mask is soft discs centred on anchors. Anchors view: live dots sit on bright spots of the field. Pits mode is subdued in relief; it carves narrow holes and they are hard to spot in the blue basins. 3D nodules are plain spheres at maxima of a 3D fbm: correct but dull.
peak-scatter.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured two ways: heightfield density of the Horn, and true 3D anchors at maxima of a 3D fbm (2x2x2 cells, 7 tap stencils). 4D not written.
peak-scatter.range: Horn over 8 seeds -0.81..1.47 at famp=1.3 (not rescaled); apex can exceed 1, a port should normalise by Rise. Mask -1..1.
peak-scatter.artifacts: No jump measured. Smallest test on seed 1337, 2 octave climb field, C=1, ff=0.5: the entry's normalised ascent puts 6.1%, 12.7%, 20.4% of anchors within 0.1 C of a local max at polish 1, 2, 3, and after a convergence gate only 28.7% of the live ones at polish 2 are within 0.15 C of a prominent max. Newton on a 6 tap stencil: 7.8%, 16.1%, 26.3%. The cell owned search (default) at 2 stages: 31.2% of anchors within 0.1 C, but what matters is the live set: 112 live of 676 cells, 78.6% within 0.15 C of a prominent max, and 43.9% of prominent maxima have a live anchor; 3 stages: 85.1% and 66.2%. So the search still misses a third to half of the summits, and about 1 live anchor in 5 sits on a lesser bump. At the default C=2 (metric scales with C), 221 of 676 cells are live. A summit near a cell border can get no owner or, rarely, two near each other: seen as a few close pairs in the anchors view when the gate is off. Range exceeds 1.
peak-scatter.node_shape: PeakScatter: Field (source), Route (hybrid, cheap Field for the climb), Stamp Source, Feature Scale C, Mode {Peaks, Pits}, Stages (int), Stencil (5 or 9), Cells K {4, 9}, Size, Horn Rise, Horn Slope, Spire, Smooth, Keep Detail, Density or snowline on anchor height, Output {Horn, Mask, AnchorHeight, Stamp}.
peak-scatter.port_notes: Every per cell quantity depends only on the cell hash and the source, so lanes agree. Fixed taps: K x Stages x 9. Quadratic fit by fixed weights, hard gate per cell is fine since each stamp reaches zero at its reach. Horn is Max of cones with a term that forces each below any terrain at reach (-6 * smoothstep( 0.8, 1, d / R )), so a horn cannot make a seam. A core GenJet would not cut this much, because the wide stencil is the point: it is what ignores small bumps. The practical port would restrict Route to 1 or 2 octaves and accept the price, or use a low resolution mask pass.

master.one_liner: Measure-then-act: candidates per lattice cell climb the user's own field for a fixed number of steps, so stamps land exactly on its summits or in its hollows, and a Horn output caps every rounded fBm summit with a real peak.
master.look: Stamps that sit where the user's terrain actually peaks or pools: snow caps, cairns and towers exactly on summits, tarns and boulders exactly in the lowest hollows, which GroundedScatter cannot do because it places anywhere on the surface. Horn turns rounded fBm summits into horns and aretes while leaving slopes and valleys untouched, a long-standing complaint about fractal terrain. In 3D, ore nodules exactly at the richest points of a density field.
master.algorithm:
Lattice of cells of size c (Feature Scale); per cell a jittered candidate a from the cell hash.
For each of the K nearest cells in the 3^D window:
   x = a; repeat Polish times (1-2, fixed): (v, g) = jet of Field at x (GenJet or D+1 taps); x += dir * Step * c * g / (|g| + eps), dir = +1 Peaks / -1 Pits  (normalised ascent; total move <= Polish * Step * c <= 0.5 c keeps the anchor near its cell)
   anchor A = x; height h = Field(A) (one more tap or the last jet). A and h depend only on the cell hash, so every lane agrees on them.
   mask m = profile( |p - A| / r ), r = Size * c * (1 + SizeJitter * hash)
   priority = h (Peaks: higher wins; Pits: lower wins); overlaps resolved by StampScatter's cascade fade on priority-ranked masks, so two cells converging on one summit give one stamp.
Outputs: Stamp (Source drawn at A in local coords with the cell's seed), Mask, AnchorHeight (flat h inside the stamp), Horn: max( Field(p), h + PeakRise - HornSlope * |p - A| ) (a cone with its apex just above the summit that meets the terrain tangentially where it falls below it; 0 effect in valleys).
Density (hybrid, read at A): thins by the anchor's own height so only summits above a snowline keep stamps.
3D: same with a 3D Field, anchors at density maxima.
master.why_new: GroundedScatter places on terrain anywhere, ContourSnapLandforms snaps to a contour, CellularDensity and ThinSpots thin by a density read at the point, IsolatedExtremaNoise makes its own extrema: none locates the user's extrema. The trick is a per-cell deterministic polish (measure, then act) so a fixed loop replaces a search and all lanes agree on the anchor. Nearest: grounded-scatter, contour-snap-landforms, isolated-extrema-noise, blue-noise-scatter (hash priority becomes field priority).
master.simd_plan: Heavy: K x (Polish x (D+1) + 1) Field evaluations + 1 Source. K = 4, Polish = 2: 28 Field evaluations in 2D (36 in 3D) with FD, 12 with jets. Keep Field cheap (Perlin, 2-3 octaves) or wrap it in BatchGate above a height threshold. 4D as 3D with 81 cells: offline only.
master.continuity: C0 (cascade fade; anchors are per-cell constants); Horn is C0 by the max.
master.params: Feature Scale, Field (source), Source (stamp), Mode (Peaks, Pits), Polish (int), Step, Size, Size Jitter, K (int), Output enum, Horn Slope, Peak Rise, Density (hybrid).
master.risks: Cost; cells whose features are much smaller than c miss peaks; Horn slope versus terrain slope needs tuning or the caps read as stamped cones; duplicates on one summit rely on the fade.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 72 Route taps at 2 octaves (about 160 ns) + 4 Field taps at 5 octaves (about 22 ns) + F(p) and Route(p) (about 8 ns) = about 190 ns. The entry's 28 taps would be about 90 ns, but its climb does not find summits: see artifacts.

peak-scatter.changed_from_entry: Replaced the climb. The entry's gradient polish failed the smallest test, as above, so a candidate now starts at its cell centre, fits a quadratic to a wide 9 tap stencil (rho 0.33 C), steps to the fitted summit, repeats with a tighter stencil, and counts only if the fit is a summit, the last step is under rho, and the result is inside its own cell. One owner per summit replaces the cascade and dedupe (pair dedupe code kept for climb 0 to 2). Reach becomes R <= 0.5 C at K=4 with no drift term. Also added: horn keeps fine detail by adding Field - Route to the cone, a spire term, and a smooth max. Tap count is 76 instead of 28. Route is a true prefix of Field (same normaliser), so Field - Route holds only the fine octaves.

pinned-noise.look: Relief: ordinary fBm terrain with extra rounded peaks at chosen sites. At the same radius, side by side on a zoom, the pinned peak keeps rough rock texture up to the summit and the Fade peak is a smooth dome, which is the real difference. Peaks at many sites with one target read as a repeated row of similar hills; the default hashes the target to avoid this. Coast proof: at target 0 each white dot sits on the land and sea border. Cave vol at target -0.9: the difference from the plain source is small, a few enlarged openings, so judged from a still it is modest, as the entry warned.
pinned-noise.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D measured: the value assert ran through the real eval in all three (4D with a copy of the code and a 4D value noise source). No harness images in 4D.
pinned-noise.range: -0.93..1.08 over 8 seeds at the default targets (output follows the source and the targets; the node does not rescale). 3D slice -0.56..0.55.
pinned-noise.artifacts: No jump measured. Smallest test, seed 1337, 1000 active sites through the real eval: max |value - target| 2.38e-7 in 2D (also 1.79e-7 with flatten and with hashed targets), 1.79e-7 in 3D and 4D, passing the 1e-5 assert. Fade with k=1 at the site is exact at that one point too, so exactness alone is not the advantage: texture is. Measured roughness (mean |Laplacian| at step 0.02, r from 0.15 to 0.6 R, 22864 points): source 32.87, pinned 35.49 (108%), Fade 25.91 (79%). Slope pin: source slope at sites mean 0.95. flatten=1 with ge=0.03 leaves mean 0.28 max 0.79, because the 5 octave source has detail below the step; ge=0.002 gives mean 0.020 max 0.053. So level at the point needs a small step, and the wobble around it is unchanged. Discs: with a large residual and a low octave source the bump reads as a hill, not a disc. The bump can be a visible rounded dome with target far above the source, since the kernel shape is fixed.

master.one_liner: Conditioned noise: any source is made to pass exactly through chosen values (and slopes) at jittered sites by Matheron's pathwise update, keeping its texture right up to the site, because disjoint compact kernels make the matrix inverse trivial.
master.look: Looks like the source. The difference is a guarantee: summits at exact heights, all sites on one coastline, a cave density forced open at chosen points with walls that keep their noise, a surface passing level through a point. In a strip of sites along a route, a walkable thread. Visually modest by itself. With Target = high constant and small R it makes individual sharp peaks on rough ground without a pasted cone look.
master.algorithm:
Wilson et al. 2021, Corollary 4: (f|y)(x) = f(x) + k(x,X)*K_nn^-1*(y - f_n). Xu et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2025, use this kind of pathwise update for Gaussian process implicit surfaces with sparse convolution noise, which eliminates linear solves; I read only their landing page. TRICK: if each site owns a compact kernel that lies inside its own cell, K_nn is the identity and the update needs one site.
c = floor(p*scale); site = c + 0.5 + (0.5 - R)*rnd11D(hash(c)); active = rnd(hash) < Density
r = |p*scale - site|/R; k = active*(1 - r)^4*(4*r + 1) when r < 1   // Wendland C2
sw = site/scale
e = Target(sw) - S(sw)   // Target is hybrid: constant, a coarse graph, or a hash
out = S(p) + k*e
Slope pin: g = forward difference of S at sw (D more evals); out -= Flatten*k*dot(g - TargetSlope, p - sw)
This matches value and slope at the site exactly, and only there; the surface elsewhere keeps its own detail.
Note on what it is not: conditioning is exact only if k equals the source's covariance. Here it is an approximation chosen by R, close to one feature length. Variance dips near a site rather than matching the true posterior.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Fade flattens the noise inside the mask. Add of a bump shifts by a fixed amount, so the final value is unknown. BuildSites cuts flat pads and rejects rough ones. PeakScatter moves stamps to summits instead of moving the terrain. Here the value at a known coordinate is exact and texture survives. CellularLookup gives S at a site but hard edges and no way to subtract it smoothly. A graph needs a per-cell site offset in a Source input, which no node exposes.
master.simd_plan: Own-cell site, no window. 2 evals per lane for value (one at p, one at the site), D more for the slope pin, one more if Target is a node. Lanes cannot share site evals because lanes are unrelated. 2D, 3D, 4D identical code. Tiling works if the hash is periodic. Estimate overhead 2 ns plus evals.
master.continuity: C1 from the Wendland kernel if Source and Target are C1. Inactive cells give exactly S.
master.params: Source, Target (hybrid), Target Slope X/Y/Z (hybrid), Flatten, Radius, Density (hybrid), Feature Scale, Output (Value, SiteMask, Residual).
master.risks: Discs can appear on a smooth source when e is large versus S's local range, as a bump. Radius bound limits how wide the effect can be per cell. Rough octaves near the site still make the point itself noisy; a person standing there sees exact height only at one point. The value of the idea is practical, not visual, and a judge looking at thumbnails will see nothing.

build-sites.look: Relief: rolling fBm with a few crisp flat rotated rectangles. On hillsides a pad has a straight cut wall on the uphill side and a slope below; none sit in water or on the roughest ground. Beside it, the stock Fade graph at a similar pad count gives large round smooth blobs, with a pit-like crater on a steep site and a tall mesa on a peak, since it cannot reject sites and has a fixed blend. The pads are sparse: about 4 in a default relief view. vol shows flats let into the terrain. FFT has radial streaks from the straight edges.

build-sites.artifacts: No value jump in Height. Slope test over a 40 x 40 window, seed 1337: 87 pads of 169 cells; 7.32% of area changed, 2.62% exactly level. Points above max( batter, terrain slope ) * 1.1 + 0.05: 0.53% of the changed area, near the band's end, where max slope reaches 23.6 vs batter 0.9 and terrain 2.58. Those are short steep steps where the fine octaves stand further from the pad than the cone reaches at Reach. Without the ring taps 97 pads and 0.67%; with Max Relief also off 107 pads and 0.72%. So the entry's bound holds except in that narrow ring, and it does not hold exactly. Five and ring taps can miss a narrow gully. Own cell makes pads sparse and on a jittered lattice, though at this sparsity the lattice does not show in the relief.

Pad radius is shrunk to fit: radius + Reach <= ( 1 - J ) / 2 * C. Value at the cell border is exactly T. Route must be a true prefix of Source: a Route normalised by its own octave count puts pads about 10% off terrain height (found here and fixed).

master.one_liner: Sparse level building pads on any terrain: a site is rejected if its footprint is too rough or too low, and accepted pads are cut and filled at a constant batter slope, with one terrain eval away from pads.
master.look: A rolling terrain with sparse crisp terraces: flat rectangles with a cut wall on the uphill side and a fill slope below, none on cliffs or under water. Reads as farms, camps, castle mounds, and in rough terrain as quarries. With rounded pads and large Toe, burial mounds or threshing floors.
master.algorithm:
Own cell only, no window. c = floor(p/C). Site s = (c + 0.5 + J*(rnd-0.5))*C. Pad half sizes (Rx, Ry) and yaw hashed, yaw optionally quarter turns. d = rounded box distance from p to the pad in its frame, 0 on the pad. Constraint: max pad radius + Reach <= (1-J)/2 * C, so a pad never leaves its cell.
T = Source(p). If all lanes have d > Reach return T, whole batch skip.
Footprint: h0 = Route(s), h1..h4 = Route(s +- Rx*ex), Route(s +- Ry*ey). m = mean, rho = max - min.
accept = rnd(h) < Density(s) && rho < Max Relief && m > Min Height. Per site constants, so nothing pops within a pad.
b = Batter*d + Big*smoothstep(0.8*Reach, Reach, d)
out = accept ? Max(Min(T, m+b), m-b) : T, rounded by Toe.
The pad height is the footprint mean, so cut and fill roughly balance. Height where the batter meets T needs no parameter, it follows from the terrain. Output Site Value returns the same hash the game can use to choose what to build, so placement and terrain cannot disagree.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Stock graph: Fade( Source, CellularLookup(Source), F1 ramp ) is 5 nodes and 2 cellular searches, reads height at one point, cannot reject sites, and a fixed blend width turns into a cliff on a slope. Nearest idea GroundedScatter sits objects on the ground rather than changing the ground. CellLens flattens every cell. This is one of the most repeated forum requests I found: Roblox reports harsh corners, holes and a slowdown from generating terrain twice to get heights; the Unreal, World Machine, Terragen and Cashgen threads all arrive at a radial blend toward a constant. None of those threads reach slope limited transitions or footprint rejection. From memory, Minecraft's jigsaw structures have a terrain_adaptation setting that does this at engine level (the wiki pages I read do not cover it), so shipped games do need it; an MCreator thread asks how to make structures spawn on flat land.
master.simd_plan: One hash, a box distance and a Select: under 1 ns away from pads plus T. Inside reach of any lane: 5 Route evals. Estimated 1 Source plus 2 ns on average at 5 percent pad area. No window, same cost in 3D with Up Axis. 4D drops w, no tiling.
master.continuity: C0 with crease at the toe, C1 with Toe > 0. Accept and pad height are per site constants; the band is wide open before the cell edge, so lanes either side of a cell border see plain T.
master.params: Source (required), Route (hybrid, cheap version), Feature Scale, Density (hybrid), Radius Min, Radius Max, Grid Jitter, Yaw enum (Free, Quarter), Max Relief, Min Height, Batter, Reach, Toe, Up Axis, Output enum (Height, Density, Pad Mask, Pad Height, Site Value)
master.risks: Own cell constraint makes pads sparse and on a jittered lattice; 3^2 window is possible at 9x the footprint work. Big relief with a small Reach means a steep wall at the edge of the band, so Max Relief must stay under Batter*Reach, which the node can enforce. Five tap footprint misses a narrow gully. A cut can expose a wall that needs game side dressing.

graded-network.look: Road relief: pale level strips run across the terrain, cut into hillsides with a sharp face uphill, carried on an embankment across dips, joining at soft junctions. Where a crossing is too deep the road stops at a wall and the terrain is left alone, which reads as a gap for a bridge; there is a visible case in the front valley. Plan at a wide view reads as an irregular country road map with loops and dead ends rather than a clean grid, though a lattice is still felt in the long roughly axis aligned runs. Cut and fill output is a clean map along the roads. The single bond test shows one benched straight road across a hill. River mode is weak: the plan is star shaped drains around pits, with no long rivers, and in relief the ribbons are hard to read.
graded-network.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured as heightfield density (y up) in vol. 4D would drop w; not written.
graded-network.range: -0.74..0.76 over 8 seeds at hamp=1.2 (follows the terrain)
graded-network.artifacts: No value jump in Height. Steep, not C0 broken: max slope about 80 at gap walls and band ends, which is why c0 reads about 3.4. Slope test, window 40, seed 1337: 16.26% of area changed; 2.42% of changed points exceed max( batter, terrain slope ) * 1.1 + 0.05, near open bands and gap walls; max slope 35 at the 0.01 step vs batter 0.9, terrain 2.31. Single bond: 1.78%. So the entry's bound holds outside open bands only. A lattice remains in the plan. Bonds dropped for grade leave dead ends. River: 17.83% of changed points over the limit, because the bed profile is steeper than batter by design, and pits end rivers in stars. Along output has jumps between bonds, by design. Width and Reach are tied to C: Reach <= margin - bulge - warp.
graded-network.node_shape: GradedNetwork: Terrain (required), Route (hybrid), Feature Scale, Keep (hybrid), Width (hybrid), Batter, Max Cut, Max Grade, Drop Grade, Reach, Toe, Grid Jitter, Bulge, Bend (Off, 3 tap), Warp, Up Axis, Output {Height, Density, Mask, Along, Grade, Fill}. River is not worth including as it stands.
graded-network.port_notes: No sort. 4 axis bonds at this cell's site are the complete set when Reach + bulge + warp <= ( 1 - J ) / 2 * C, proved in the code comment. Each bond is built from its lower index end so neighbouring cells get the same arc. Node height is Route( site ), so junctions agree. Route must be a true prefix of Terrain: same octaves and the same normaliser, or the road floats off the terrain by a scale; this prototype's Fb does that. MaxCut is capped by batter * ( 0.8 Reach - Width ), so a cut too deep for the cone opens rather than ending in a wall at the band's end.

master.one_liner: Roads or rivers as a pointwise bond network whose node heights come from your terrain, cut and filled into it with a constant batter slope in world units, so a road benches across a hillside instead of being a mask painted over it.
master.look: In relief: pale benches winding over hills, a cut face on the uphill side, an embankment on the downhill side, flat crowns, soft junctions. Valleys crossed get causeways up to Max Cut and then the road goes untouched for a bridge. River mode: a level water ribbon with banks of constant slope. Fill output tells the game where to place bridges and tunnels, and Along gives lane markings.
master.algorithm:
Sites s_c = (c + 0.5 + J*rnd2(h_c)) * C. Road mode: each cell owns one bond to its -x or -y neighbour by hash, degree at most 3, arc bulge from the hash (BondGraph arc mode). River mode: each site drains to its lowest of 8 neighbours by Route; a pit owns no bond and gets a level pad.
1. Plan search, no source evals: distance d and arc parameter t to the bonds owned by the 3^2 cells. Complete if Reach + bulge <= (1-J)/2 * C, the usual reach rule. Keep the K=3 nearest by sorting network, 3 because degree is at most 3.
2. T = Terrain(p). If no lane has d_1 < Reach, return T: whole batch skip, common because roads are sparse.
3. For each kept bond: ha = Route(a), hb = Route(b). Optional bend: 3 bulge candidates, pick the one whose midpoint Route height is closest to (ha+hb)/2, a per bond constant, so the road prefers contours. Road height: h = Hermite(ha, hb, t) with flat ends, or through the capped midpoint hm = clamp(Route(m), mean +- MaxGrade*len/2). A node's height is Route(site), so all bonds at a junction agree.
4. Batter band, in world units: b_k = Batter*max(0, d_k - Width) + Open(d_k) + OpenCut(|T - h_k|). Open and OpenCut are 0 inside Reach and Max Cut and rise steeply past them, so a bond has no influence at the distance where it could swap out of the K nearest, and a deep crossing leaves the terrain alone for the game to bridge or tunnel.
5. out = Max( Min(T, min_k (h_k + b_k)), max_k (h_k - b_k) ), rounded by MinSmooth radius Toe.
Inside Width the result is exactly h: flat across, following grade along. Outside it follows T unless T is further than the cone allows, so the surface slope never exceeds max(Batter, slope(T), grade).
River mode: heights descend along a bond because a site drains to a lower one. Bed = h - Depth*(1-(d/Width)^2), Water Level = h.
master.why_new: Clearly different output. Nearest: BondGraph has network distance and no height, SpanningMaze and TubeNoise contour lines have no connection to a terrain, DendryNoise Carve is rivers only, 110x Perlin by its own description, and has V, U and Box profiles of fixed shape rather than a batter. Terrace, contour scarp and iso distance shape along a level, not along a route. Evidence read: Ghost Recon Wildlands used a custom pathfinding road builder and Future Soldier's tools carved roads; Galin et al. 2010 use anisotropic shortest paths then carve, with tunnels and bridges; the WorldGen UE5 plugin uses slope weighted A* and graded roadbeds with a queryable graded height; all of these need a global step. Mawhorter's slides explain why rivers defeat chunk independence, since flow depends on the whole watershed. The arXiv plate-local river paper traces descending rivers on a low resolution grid and blends by distance at full resolution, which is this carve with a cache. A Roblox thread reports harsh corners from reshaping and a 4x slowdown from generating terrain twice. This node gives up optimal routing to stay pointwise, and the batter clamp is a new, simple way to meet terrain.
master.simd_plan: Plan search about CellularDistance 2D cost, 4 ns. Road straight: 6 Route plus 1 Terrain; Bend: 15 Route plus 1 Terrain; River: 25 Route for the drain choice, like Dendry level 0. At 1 octave Route that is about 10 / 20 / 30 ns over Terrain inside reach and nothing outside it (estimates). Heightfield node: the 3D form uses two horizontal axes with an Up Axis and can output density as height minus up. 4D drops w and does not tile, stated plainly.
master.continuity: C0: min, max and clamp of continuous functions, and bonds entering or leaving the kept set have an open band there. Crease at the toe unless Toe > 0. Node heights are shared, so junctions agree. Where two roads at different heights fall within reach of each other the fill side wins, still continuous. Mask and Fill are C0, Along is discontinuous between bonds.
master.params: Terrain (required), Route (hybrid, a cheap 1 to 2 octave version of Terrain), Feature Scale, Mode enum (Road, River), Density (hybrid), Width (hybrid), Batter, Max Cut, Max Grade, Reach, Toe, Grid Jitter, Bend (Off, 3 tap), Up Axis, Output enum (Height, Density, Mask, Along, Grade, Fill, Water Level)
master.risks: No pathfinding, so a road will happily cross a ridge at Max Grade rather than go around it, and the network may read as a warped lattice at wide views. Bond removal for grade leaves dead ends. Width and Reach are limited by the cell window, so highways need a large Feature Scale. River mode has no discharge, so width is a stand in, and pits end rivers in pads rather than the sea. The K=3 argument needs checking near nodes.

graded-network.changed_from_entry: Plan search reduced to 4 candidate bonds with no K=3 sort (the entry's own reach rule implies it). Plan is hash kept axis bonds rather than one owned bond per cell: the owned form is available as net=1 and shows a diagonal bias from always pointing to -x or -y. landform-mask.look: Tinted class map: reads as a GIS landform map, red ridge ribbons along the high ground, white peak blobs, blue valley ribbons, dark blue pits, cyan hollows heading up from valleys, olive slopes between. It follows the terrain's form at the search scale rather than each bump. Shoulder, footslope and flat classes are almost absent on this fBm (0.2%, 0.2%, 0.0%), since it has few level benches. Mask for ridge + spur + peak is clean contiguous regions with some wide blobs rather than thin lines. Wetness: gray with black dry patches on summits and a banded look from the 2 rings. It tracks low convex ground; measured correlation with Convexity -0.885 and with height -0.761, so it adds little beyond Convexity at M=2.
landform-mask.dims: 2D measured. 3D: Eval3 uses a 3D fbm source with offsets in the XZ plane and y selecting the slice, works by check (z continuity max 0.0231 for dz = 1e-3); no vol since the output is a mask, not a surface. 4D not written.

landform-mask.artifacts: Smallest test, IoU of a mask between 3 and 7 octaves, seed 1337, window 16. Entry's squared spacing M=3: 0.601 ridge group, 0.595 hollow group, noisy outlines in the first render. With inner skip radius 0.5 and M=2: 0.857 and 0.860. Laplacian at step 0.05 at the same coverage: 0.314 and 0.316. An important caveat: an 8 tap ring Laplacian at the same radius at the same coverage gets 0.909 and 0.906, better than the mask, with 9 evals. So for a simple high versus low split the stability claim does not favour this node, and that wide Laplacian beats it; what this node adds is the classes (spur vs ridge, hollow vs valley, slope, peak). Convexity has terraced steps because counts change quickly over small soft, visible in its hillshade. Class output has jumps by design. Table from the entry, from memory, not checked against the paper. Small angle form differs from the published angle test on steep terrain.

master.one_liner: Geomorphons as a pointwise soft mask: 8 lines of sight from any height tree give ridge, spur, shoulder, slope, hollow, footslope, valley, pit, peak and flat, stable on rough terrain where curvature falls apart, plus a wetness estimate from the same taps.
master.look: A landform map from GIS: long ridge and valley ribbons, hollows heading up each valley, flat shoulders along benches. Reads the terrain's shape at the search scale instead of each bump. Good as trees in hollows and on north slopes, ruins on spurs, villages on shoulders, scree at footslopes, moss by Wetness.
master.algorithm:
h0 = Source(p). For each of 8 directions e_k, optional hybrid rotation; for j in 1..M with r_j = L*(j/M)^2:
  s = (Source(p + r_j*e_k) - h0)/r_j
  up_k = Max(up_k, s); dn_k = Min(dn_k, s)
Ternary, soft: x = up_k + dn_k (small angle form of zenith minus nadir). plus_k = smoothstep(t-soft, t+soft, x); minus_k = smoothstep(t-soft, t+soft, -x).
Counts: np = sum plus_k, nm = sum minus_k, in [0,8], continuous.
Outputs:
  Convexity: (nm - np)/8, a continuous peak to pit value.
  Mask: bilinear lookup in a 9x9 table on (nm, np), filled when Class Set changes with 1 for selected classes, using Jasiewicz and Stepinski's published table: row nm 0: FL FL FL FS FS VL VL VL PT; 1: FL FL FS FS FS VL VL VL; 2: FL SH SL SL HL HL VL; 3: SH SH SL SL SL HL; 4: SH SH SP SL SL; 5: RI RI SP SP; 6: RI RI RI; 7: RI RI; 8: PK. Table written from memory, verify against the paper.
  Class: nearest entry, a hard label.
  Wetness: walking outward per direction, alive = alive * smoothstep(0, eps, s_j rising), area += alive*(r_j^2 - r_(j-1)^2); wet = log(area/(|mean slope| + eps)). A star shaped stand in for upslope area in the GIS wetness index, with no drainage solve.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Nearest SurfaceProbe: Slope and Laplacian are local, and its Crest output needs 1 to 2 octaves or breaks into dashes by its own description; on a 5 octave tree a Laplacian is noise. StencilFilter Range and PeakMargin give single numbers with no shape classes. HorizonShadow and RayMarch march one direction. Geomorphons compare horizons, so adding a small bump does not flip the class. Evidence read: Horizon Zero Dawn feeds baked Terrain_Cavity and erosion maps into placement; Wildlands drove scatter rules from cliff and road detection; Far Cry 5 placed species by growing conditions and had forests thicken on the north side of mountains; Red Blob's polygon maps derive moisture from distance to water and note the limits of that. All baked or authored. This is the pointwise form. Esri and GRASS ship the same method on rasters.
master.simd_plan: 8*M + 1 Source evals with fixed loops, 25 at M=3. Give it a 2 or 3 octave tree: about 60-80 ns per sample (estimate), for masks often computed at lower resolution. Smooth counts and bilinear lookup branch free. Heightfield node: in 3D the plane is chosen by Up Axis and Source is treated as height. 4D offsets x and y, leaves z and w, so GenTileable2D stays continuous but the plane is curved in the torus, which distorts directions.
master.continuity: C0: max and min over fixed taps, smooth signs, bilinear table. Class is discontinuous by design. Wetness C0 with eps > 0.
master.params: Source, Search Radius L (hybrid), Steps M (int, 2 to 4), Flat Slope t, Softness, Class Set (bitmask), Rotation (hybrid), Output enum (Convexity, Mask, Class, Wetness), Output Min/Max
master.risks: 25 evals. 8 directions with squared spacing can alias on sharp ridges, and a soft count near a border can be noisy on white-like detail. Small angle form differs from the published angle test on steep terrain. Table from memory. Wetness is rough: a valley that bends out of a ray's line loses upslope area, so treat it as a look, not hydrology.

contour-engrave.look: At the sheet's close view: fine even contour lines of a smooth field, thin hairlines on lit slopes and heavy black lines on shaded slopes, so the terrain's light and shadow reads through line weight alone. In shadow the lines nearly close into black masses, nibbled by a straight diagonal hatch, which gives a real engraved or woodcut feel. Without hatch at 9 levels (it1) it is a bolder woodcut topo map. The 3D XZ slice shows the same lines with heavier blobs where the 3D light grazes. Vol with invert=0 shows thin wavy shells; the orange cut faces carry the contour lines, and the outer surface is a lumpy shell set rather than a clean onion.
contour-engrave.dims: 2D and 3D measured (check, sheet XZ slice, vol). 4D not measured: the harness has no Eval4; the formula is dimension agnostic with 5 taps.
contour-engrave.range: -1..1 over 8 seeds, binary by design with a soft edge; no NaN; far coords (4e4) fine
contour-engrave.artifacts: Wide 4x view aliases to black and white speckle: the lines are thinner than a pixel at that scale, so this needs a sensible scale, like any line art. Small dots appear at some extrema when a level lands near the critical value (specks the entry predicted, a few per panel, and they look like map spot heights). Threshold panel on the sheet is blank because p50 is the paper value of a binary output. Stair-stepped look in the hillshade panel is just the binary field being treated as a height. No value jumps.

master.algorithm: Tap Source at pos and pos + h*e_i (D+1 taps): H, g = forward difference gradient. m = Sqrt(dot(g,g) + k*k), k a floor for flats. t = H * Levels + Offset. tri = Abs(t - Round(t)), a continuous triangle wave. d = tri / (Levels * m), the first-order world distance to the nearest contour. tone = sat(0.5 + 0.5 * dot(normalize(-g, 1), Light)) from the same taps. w = WidthMin + (WidthMax - WidthMin) * (1 - tone). out = 1 - 2 * smoothstep(w, w + Soft, d). Works unchanged in 2D, 3D (onion shells) and 4D (5 taps, tiles if Source does). Estimated cost: (D+1) * Source + about 1 ns, so about 19 ns AVX2 2D on a 5 octave FBm (estimate).
master.why_new:
strata-bands has crowded contours and iso-distance has constant width only at one level. This gives constant world-width lines at every level, with width driven by hillshade: banknote engraving of any field. Cheap, no window, no hash. Not built; the look is a prediction.
Seed gap: banknote engraving of any field; constant world-width contours.
master.simd_plan: Estimated cost: (D+1) * Source + about 1 ns, so about 19 ns AVX2 2D on a 5 octave FBm (estimate).
master.continuity: tri = Abs(t - Round(t)), a continuous triangle wave.
master.params: Source, Step h, Floor k, Levels, Offset, Light, Width Min, Width Max, Soft.

Seed risk 0.25: specks at critical points.
The panel says iso-distance has constant width only at one level, but the catalogue entry has a Period member that already gives the whole contour family at constant world width. What is new here is the width driven by hillshade, read from the same taps.

forking-contours.look: Zebra or fingerprint: even-width black and white stripes following the contours of the field, whorls around extrema, and Y forks where contours spread, all the same handedness. The FFT shows a tight ring, so the stripe frequency is held nearly constant. Near a few saddles and shallow extrema there are small busy knots with tiny stripes. In 1D test (it1) the binary tree of pitchforks is exact, and stagger scatters the fork heights. The curtain mode gives a real hanging-curtain fan: many fine pleats at the top doubling up into fewer wide ones downward, with scattered fork heights. In 3D the cut faces show thick agate-like laminae and sheets that split. The 4x wide view on the sheet aliases to a fine labyrinth.

forking-contours.artifacts: No value jumps. Small knots at saddles and shallow extrema, where level rises to Max Level. Soft mode duty=0 has gray patches in the fork zones (it2), since the blend passes through intermediate contrast; duty=0.45 makes that crisper but the fork tips still have a slightly blurred taper. Stripe widths are not fully constant: a factor 2 spread between one level and the next is inherent to a doubling scheme.
