master.one_liner: Even-width contour stripes of any field: where contours spread apart each stripe forks into two along a hierarchical binary tree, the way wrinkles double towards a curtain's free edge, with real Y junctions and no phase vortices.
master.look: From a plain Perlin: fingerprint whorls around each extremum with constant ridge width everywhere, and Y forks wherever contours spread, every fork opening the same way. From Gradient plus a frequency law: hanging curtains, mushroom gills, scallop ribs, palm fronds, parallel leaf venation, feather barbs. In 3D: sheets that split into thinner sheets, like gill fungus or laminated bracket. On a terrain source it gives engraved contour hachure with an even tone.
master.algorithm:
Published fact: Vandeparre et al. 2011 show wrinkle wavelength changing by doubling through localised Y-shaped transitions (wrinklons), with lambda proportional to x^(2/3) for light sheets and x^(1/2) under tension. That paper is a physics scaling law, not an algorithm. The pointwise form below is mine.
u = Source(p)*UScale
g = gradient of u by finite differences, stencil h about 0.5/F (the wide stencil discovery), exact-step divisor
lv = log2(F / max(|g|, tiny)) + LevelBias(p)   // F is the wanted stripes per world unit
n = clamp(floor(lv), Nmin, Nmax - 1); t = sat(lv - n)
w = 2^n * u; k = floor(w); x = w - k
h = hash(int(k), n, seed)
delta = Stagger*rnd01(h); width = 1 - Stagger
b = smoothstep(delta, delta + width, t)
A = -cos(2*pi*x); B = 1 - 2*A*A   // B = -cos(4*pi*x), the next level, no second cos
return A + b*(B - A)
Why it is seamless, and this is the point of the idea. Level n has a crest at x = 1/2 and troughs at x = 0. Level n+1 has troughs at x = 0 and x = 1/2 and crests at 1/4 and 3/4. So the crest splits in two straddling crests by a pitchfork, a proper Y. At a stripe boundary (x = 0) A = B = -1 with zero slope, so b may jump from one stripe to its neighbour with no visible seam: that is what lets each stripe fork at its own hashed moment. At n rollover the window [delta, delta+width] is inside [0,1], so b = 1 before t reaches 1 and level n ends exactly as level n+1 begins. Stagger is what makes the forks scattered rather than a synchronised line.
Curtain mode: Source = Gradient along x, F(y) = F0*|y|^(-2/3), gives the published fan.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Oscillator on a noise packs tight rings on steep ground and bare blobs on flat ground. LocalPhase needs a narrowband input and gives vortex dots. EikonalStripes projects onto one zero set and has seams at the medial axis. PhasorNoise, LatticePhasor and VortexPhase need an orientation field and produce paired defects of both signs at random. Here the stripes are the exact contours of the user's field, with hierarchical same-handed forks, which those mechanisms cannot give. BarrancoCones has analytic period doubling but only in log-polar around a cone; this is the same idea driven by any field and with per-stripe timing.
master.simd_plan: No lattice, no window. D+1 source evals for the forward difference. n from the float exponent, t from a small mantissa polynomial, 2^n by exponent bits. One cos, one hash. Same code in 2D, 3D, 4D; tiling is inherited from the source. Estimate AVX2: 3 to 4 ns overhead plus (D+1) x source.
master.continuity: C1 in the stripes as shown above, except where |g| goes to 0, where it clamps at Max Level and the last ring has a plain centre. Discontinuous only in the Stripe ID output.
master.params: Source (required), Frequency (hybrid), Stagger (0 to 0.7), Level Bias (hybrid), U Scale, Sample Distance, Min Level, Max Level, Duty (optional hard edge via Oscillator's PWM). Output: Stripes, Level, Stripe ID.
master.risks: Contours of a rough source wiggle, so the stencil and a 2 to 3 octave source probably matter. At saddles, where |g| goes small on a contour that also goes wild, levels may rise fast and make a busy knot. Stripe count near a shallow extremum could rise to Max Level and look like a dense bull's eye; a cap on level gives a blank spot instead. It may read as engineered rather than natural if Stagger is too low.
sources: https://github.com/runevision/Dither3D (level doubling that keeps a screen density; idea only, MPL 2.0, no code used)

ripple-overlay.look: Relief: fine wind-blown sand ripples on smooth rolling dunes, as short sinuous dark crests with broken dislocations, bending around each hill and thinning towards the steep side. In the close 3 unit hillshade they read as real desert ripples that curve across the hill, whorling loosely at the crown. The gray panel on the sheet is dominated by the base, the ripples are a faint texture at this amplitude. FFT: a clean thin ring for the ripple wavelength. At w=0, parallel stripes with dislocations; at w=.5 to 1 tight fingerprint whorls around hills (it1). Coarse settings (it1) read as rock shingles or fish scales on the hills. Vol: rippled patches on the iso surface, rough at this resolution but the waves run across the surface.

Direction shrinks where wind and slope cancel, so stripes stretch to large ones or smooth out in a small spot near that point (seen as a loose whorl). In vol the ripples look torn at cut faces and at the highest curvature, partly due to the ray march step. Stock Fade cannot steer stripes, so nothing comparable was rendered.

master.one_liner: Stripes steered by a graph's own terrain: a hex phasor whose direction mixes wind and the base gradient, with an asymmetric dune profile.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: sand ripples and wind-blown snow running across the local slope-and-wind direction. Walled domains above about F2.5.
master.algorithm: Per lane: base B(p) from Source; gradient from D+1 taps (exact-step divisor); direction u = normalize(mix(windDir, grad B, slopeWeight)) with a fallback to windDir when |grad| < eps (Select, no branch). Evaluate the SuperSimplex-vertex phasor (4 kernels in 2D, 8 in 3D) with direction u and spread s to get phase phi via re*InvSqrt(re^2+im^2+eps^2); profile = dune(phi, stoss, round) from transverse-dunes. Output B + rippleAmp * mask(slope) * profile. Fixed window, hash per vertex, 2D/3D; 4D via the torus-angle trick. Cost estimate: D+1 Source taps + ~4.3 ns (measured hex kernel) + profile.
master.why_new:
Sand ripples and wind-blown snow run perpendicular to the local slope-and-wind direction; the phasor family showed steered stripes are clean on the hex kernel at 4.3 ns, and the dune profile gives the stoss/slip asymmetry. Nothing lets a graph steer stripes by its own terrain today.
Seed gap: stripes steered by your own terrain.
master.simd_plan: Cost estimate: D+1 Source taps + ~4.3 ns (measured hex kernel) + profile.

normal-lookup.look: Default: hammered or cast silver: soft pools of bright and dark metal, bounded by thin ropes of fine detail along curves where the Gauss map folds, a clearly non-noise look. Mercury settings: bold white on black liquid blobs with sharp thin rims. Cast silver with Drift 0 shows repeating flower-like patterns because every hill reads the same disc. F1 cones with small Flat and Displace (relief, as viewed in it1): radial parasol or palm-fan petals on each cone, with steep walls at the Voronoi borders. Vol: clusters of bumpy balls, like mulberries or asteroids, rather than the ribbed gourds the entry hoped for; every ball has similar bumps. 3D XZ slice has the same silver look. The wide 4x view on the sheet reads as gray grain: the fine fold ropes alias there.

master.one_liner: Read a source at a field's surface normal instead of its position, the matcap trick as a node: liquid chrome and mother of pearl from any smooth field, radial pleats and gourd ribs from any cone.
master.look: On a smooth one or two octave Height: enamel or chrome swirls, a flower of equal petal count on each hill and pit, reversed fans on saddles, mirror seams along inflection curves. On F1 with small Flat and Displace: parasols, palm crowns, ribbed gourds in 3D, spiky asteroids. Rough Height will just give grain, since the normals decorrelate.
master.algorithm:
SHARED CAUSE. Radial parasols came from displacement depending only on direction from the parent centre, and for a cone that direction is exactly the gradient. Barranco ribbed gourds, fluted cone flanks, satin petal fans from closest-point-transport and steered sunbursts are all detail tied to the gradient, so they all make a fan round every critical point. The clean form of that is the Gauss map: sample detail as a function of the normal alone. Around an extremum the normal sweeps every direction once, so a whole circle of the lookup appears; around a saddle it sweeps the same circle in reverse. On parabolic curves (det H = 0) the Gauss map folds, so the pattern mirrors there, which is why real chrome looks the way it does.

g = FD gradient of Height at p (D+1 taps, or 2D with Central), step hybrid Sample Distance
n = Slope*g
b = n * InvSqrt(Flat*Flat + dot(n,n))      // Flat 1: true normal, bounded by the unit ball. Flat small: direction only, pure pleats
q = Drift*p + Radius*b                      // Drift 0: pure Gauss map, all peaks see the same pattern. Drift 1: refraction, Facet shatter on an F1 Height
v = Lookup(q)                                // one eval
Output Lookup = v. Output Displace = Height(p) + Amount*v*sat(|n|/N0), which fades where direction is undefined.
Petal count on every extremum is about tau*Radius*(Lookup features per unit), so Radius is the petal knob, and it is the same on every hill regardless of hill size.
master.why_new: Different output. SurfaceProbe Hillshade is the linear special case with no lookup. closest-point-transport and anchored-frame-detail make fans but with petal counts that follow local topology, and cost more. SplatBurst is the F1-only special case. It is reachable as a graph today: DomainAxisScale(0, 0, DomainOffset(X=K*SurfaceProbe(Normal X), Y=K*SurfaceProbe(Normal Y), Lookup)). That is why the node has to justify itself: one shared gradient instead of two probes, so half the Height evals, plus Flat, Drift and Displace, which the graph cannot do cleanly. If the graph shows no look worth having, drop the idea.
master.simd_plan: Branch free, D+1 or 2D Height evals plus one Lookup, no loops of its own, generic GenT. Works on the 4D torus because b is a function of 4D position. Estimate: 3 Height + 1 Lookup, so 2D Perlin Height with Perlin Lookup is about 5 ns.
master.continuity: C0 for any C0 Height at fixed Sample Distance, since a finite difference of a continuous function is continuous, so F1 is fine. C1 where Height is C2.
master.params: Height source, Lookup source, Output enum, Stencil enum, Slope, Flat, Radius, N0. Hybrid: Sample Distance, Drift, Amount.
master.risks: All pure Gauss map hills look alike since they read the same disc; Drift above about .05 is needed. Output may read as fancy hillshade if Radius is low. Too much Radius aliases on steep flanks.

shell-coordinates.look: Rings: even black and white bands of nearly constant thickness following one level set, crossing at crisp thin seams along the medial axis like a distance field, with soft gray patches where Newton does not settle. The bands look clearly more regular than first order f/|grad f| in it1, which crowds around flats. FFT shows a ring at the band frequency, plus straight streaks from the seams. Vol rind: sculptural constant-thickness shells hugging a smooth blob, with an onion on the cut faces, the best image of the set. Vol foot: a smooth blob pierced by clean round bores running along the surface normal, like porous bone or Swiss cheese; cut faces show the cells stretching inward. Lift fbm: soft noise crossed by thin crack lines along the medial axis, with a petal-like cell look; different from plain noise, and nothing like strata.

shell-coordinates.artifacts: Steep lines along the medial axis everywhere in Rings, Foot and Lift: inherent, as in the entry. They read as thin crisp creases. In 3D the foot mode shows slivers and thin spikes at cut faces near the medial surface. Gray patches where the convergence fade works. Without the trust region and a large eps there are noisy lace zones in the middle of shapes (it1): Newton is chaotic there, so eps=0.2 and maxs=0.8 are load bearing. Larger eps reduces landing accuracy where |g| is small, so band thickness there is a bit wider. Stripe width measure at 512 px (hard threshold): rings CV 0.592, mean 15.6 px, p5..p95 7..32; first order with same Rings CV 0.721, mean 8.65, p5..p95 1..20, which includes its thin crowded bands.

master.one_liner: Iso-solve with a fixed Newton loop to a (foot point, signed depth) chart of any field, then feed the Source one extra dimension: rinds and strata of constant NORMAL thickness around any implicit shape, and surface patterns carried straight inward along the normal.
master.look: Lift with Source = SineWave or Oscillator on the depth axis: shells of constant normal thickness hugging any implicit shape: geode bands around a blob field, bark rings around a knotty trunk field, weathering rind on boulders, strata draped over a buried dome at even thickness, all as 3D volumes. Foot with Source = Cellular: scales or plates painted on the iso-surface and carried inward as prisms, so a cut face shows the surface pattern undistorted instead of a smeared slice. Depth: constant-width bands where IsoDistance's first-order f/|grad f| frays on strong curvature.
master.algorithm:
C = Control (source), L = Level
x = p
for k in 0..Steps-1 (Steps 2 or 3, fixed):
   (v, g) = jet of C at x  (GenJet, or Probe::Jet D+1 taps)
   x -= Damping * (v - L) / max( |g|^2, eps ) * g        (Newton onto the level set along the gradient)
   clamp |x - p| <= MaxDepth
foot f = x; depth = sign( C(p) - L ) * |f - p|
Lift mode:  out = Source( f..., depth * DepthScale )   (the Source's (D+1)-dim Gen: a 2D control feeds a 3D source, a 3D control a 4D source)
Foot mode:  out = Source( f... )                         (surface texture extruded along normals)
Depth mode: out = depth / Width                          (second-order iso distance, clamped to +-1)
In 4D (tileable) Lift falls back to Foot since no 5th dimension exists.
master.why_new: ClosestPointTransport reads detail at the foot only; TubeNoise and IsoDistance give first-order distance; StrataBands and the GeodeField seed make rinds for their own shapes. None gives a (foot, depth) chart for an arbitrary field so that a D-dim texture becomes a (D+1)-dim 'surface plus normal' texture. Nearest: closest-point-transport, iso-distance, tube-noise, GeodeField (seed 14), SurfaceFlutes (seed 4).
master.simd_plan: Steps x (D+1) Control taps (or Steps jets) + one Source call in D+1 dims: 2D ~10 evaluations with FD, 4 with jets; 3D ~13 / 4. Control should be smooth (few octaves) for Newton to land; Damping 0.7 for rough ones. No window.
master.continuity: C0 away from the medial axis of the level set; across the medial axis the foot jumps (an inherent seam, the thin crisp lines ClosestPointTransport shows); depth itself stays continuous.
master.params: Control (source), Level (hybrid), Steps (int), Damping, Max Depth, Depth Scale, Width, Mode (Lift, Foot, Depth), Source.
master.risks:
Newton divergence on rough controls (MaxDepth clamp and Damping mitigate); medial-axis seams in Foot mode; cost without jets.
Overlap to know about: Foot mode is closest-point-transport (keeper prototype). Lift and Depth are what is new here; judge those first.

kuwahara-brush.port_notes: 4 extra source taps for the central difference frame on top of KuwaharaField's 17 (2D) or 25 (3D). Aniso blends to 1 where |g| < g0, so critical points degrade to the isotropic stencil.

master.one_liner: KuwaharaField's sector-variance selection run in GradientSmear's local frame with CellularFacet's plane fit: elongated sectors follow the source's own structure and the winning sector returns a fitted plane, giving painterly strokes, tilted slab facets that follow the landform, and a free ink-outline channel.
master.look: Value: oil-paint dabs stretched along the source's contours, like a painterly or watercolour filter on terrain and noise, much more directional than KuwaharaField's round dabs. Facet in relief: tilted slabs whose borders run along the landform's ridges and valleys rather than Voronoi walls, like weathered flagstone following a hillside or low-poly terrain whose triangles follow the structure. Outline: a clean comic ink line map of the patch borders, usable as cracks between the slabs. Stroke: hatched engraving that follows the field.
master.algorithm: Step 1 (frame): 4 taps at +-h on the axes (GradientSmear's single gradient) give g = grad S at p; theta from (gx, gy) normalised, strength |g| (3D: the gradient and one hashed perpendicular give the frame). Step 2 (stencil): KuwaharaField's taps (centre, N outer on a ring, N inner on a half-step rotated ring) placed on an ellipse in the frame: long axis along the contour direction perp(g) with semi-axis r*Aniso, short along g with r/Aniso, Aniso blended toward 1 where |g| is small (so flats stay isotropic). Step 3 (sector fit): sector s uses taps {centre, outer_{s-1}, outer_s, outer_{s+1}, inner_s} as the proto. Fit enum Mean: mean and variance as the proto. Plane: least squares plane v = a + b.u over the five tap offsets u_k (offsets are fixed in the ellipse frame, so the 3x3 normal matrix inverse is a constant table per sector, precomputed when params are set; the fit is 5 FMAs per coefficient), residual variance = var - explained. Weights w_s = ((vmin + e)/(v_s + e))^(2^qp) as the proto, output value = sum w_s * a_s / sum w_s (the plane value at the sample itself). Outputs: Value (the filtered field), Facet (Plane fit with a hard knee qp, so each patch is a tilted plane with crisp borders), Outline: 1 - w_max/sum w (near 0 inside a patch, rising where two sectors tie: an ink line along every patch border), Stroke: Value with the frame's theta quantised to Bins (LocalFrame's trick) for a hatched impasto. 3D: icosahedral sectors as the proto, ellipsoid stencil prolate along the contour plane (short axis along g).
master.why_new: KuwaharaField (keeper) is isotropic and flat-topped; CellularFacet (keeper) fits planes on Voronoi cells, so its facets ignore the source's structure; GradientSmear (keeper) supplies one gradient but only smears along it. The oriented stencil, the plane fit and the border channel all need the same tap set inside one kernel. Published lineage: anisotropic Kuwahara (Kyprianidis, Kang, Dollner 2009); the plane-fit facets and the pointwise noise-space form are the variation.
master.simd_plan: 4 + 1 + 2N source evals (21 at N=8) in fixed loops, then N sector fits of 5 taps with constant tables, N weight powers by repeated squaring, Selects only. Cost is dominated by source evals: about 21 x source in 2D, 29 x source in 3D (centre + 12 + 12 + 4 gradient taps), 4D via the 3D stencil in the first three axes (a 4D ellipsoid stencil is possible but 4D sources are expensive anyway).
master.continuity: Value is C0 with a soft knee and effectively discontinuous at qp >= 4 (borders are the point); Facet is designed to be near-discontinuous at borders; Outline is C0. The frame theta is continuous away from critical points of S; at critical points Aniso blends to 1 so the stencil degenerates gracefully to the isotropic one.
master.params: Radius (hybrid), Aniso, Taps (int 4..8), Fit enum {Mean, Plane}, Sharpness (qp int), Epsilon, Output enum {Value, Facet, Outline, Stroke}, Bins (int, Stroke only), Source.
master.risks: At high Aniso the stencil's long axis crosses the source's own features when the gradient is noisy, which produces streaks across edges; the gradient should come from the smoothed ring mean rather than from 4 tight taps if that shows (one more pass). Plane fits on 5 taps are noisy on rough sources; the inner ring helps. 21 source evals is expensive on fractal sources.
sources: Kyprianidis, Kang, Dollner, Image and Video Abstraction by Anisotropic Kuwahara Filtering, Computer Graphics Forum 2009 (from memory, not fetched)

master.one_liner: Fingerprint ridges inside every watershed basin, by iterating an over-large descent step on purpose and reading where the step map folds: ring spacing, ring count and onset each get their own control.
master.look: A rounded cell network from the watersheds of the noise with no Voronoi anywhere, each cell filled with nested ridges, whorls and chevrons; the threshold is zebra thumbprints. Good for fingerprints, agate cells, coral polyps, tortoise shell, alien skin. Parity should read as a crisp two-colour version of the existing accident image; that part is a prediction.
master.algorithm:
WHY THE ACCIDENT LOOKS LIKE IT DOES. FTLE fingerprint cells came from a fixed descent step q -= Eta*g*m with m = 1/sqrt(1+|g|^2), Eta = .2, N = 8. Far from a sink the step has length about Eta. Near a sink the step map F has Jacobian A = I - Eta*(mH - m^3 g (Hg)^T); where Eta*lambda(H) > 1 there is a closed fold curve around the sink on which det A = 0. Every sample whose k-th iterate lands on that curve has a singular factor in its Jacobian product, so the k-th preimage of the fold curve is a dark line, at arc distance about r_fold + k*Eta up the flow line. That predicts spacing about Eta (the image shows about .19 units at Eta .2, read by eye from the 8 unit panel), at most N rings, and rings only in basins steep enough. The chain-rule contour accident in the caustic family is the same thing for a Picard map (M = 3 gives the parallel groups of black worms), slope blur shell plates is the same for a unit speed walk, and t_stretch_ftle's own comment notes unit speed descent makes rings. I have not explained why some rings join into spirals; Alpha below is my attempt at a handle on it.

NODE. Potential h = 1..3 octave analytic Perlin via GradientNoise::ValueGradHessian<D> (CausticWeb already has it).
q = p; S = 1; T = 0; J = I
for k in 0..Steps-1:
  (g, H) = kernel(q)
  n2 = dot(g,g)/(G0*G0); m = InvSqrt(1 + n2); v = m*g/G0
  M = (m/G0)*H - (m*m*m/(G0*G0*G0))*outer(g, H*g)
  A = I - Eta*Rot(Alpha)*M
  d = det(A)
  S *= d*InvSqrt(d*d + Line*Line)   // soft sign: flips across each preimage, no 1/0
  J = A*J                            // Stretch output only
  T += Eta*sqrt(dot(v,v) + 1e-4)     // Isochrone output only, needs ValueGrad only
  q -= Eta*Rot(Alpha)*v
Outputs: Parity = S (zebra, with the flip count the 2-colouring). Stretch = Contrast*log(sigma_max^2(J)) - Offset (the accident itself, the safe fallback). Isochrone = wave(T/Wavelength): smooth rings of arc length to the sink, spacing free of Eta. Whorl = cos(tau*T/Wavelength + n*arg g(p)) by complex power with no atan, faded by |g(p)|: winding +n at extrema and -n at saddles, so real whorls and deltas. Steps = 1 with Parity gives the bare fold curves (parabolic-like worm lines).
master.why_new: Different output. Nearest is stretch-ftle, whose keeper settings stop below the overshoot regime and show only the bright net; LyapunovStretch cannot do it because shear chains never fold. Oscillator over CellularDistance gives circles in polygons, eikonal-stripes gives bands parallel to a coast with no basin walls. Nothing else on the sheets gives one ridge system per natural basin with the ridges stopping at the divides. The Parity output has no precedent at all.
master.simd_plan: Fully branch free, Steps is an int member, no window beyond the Perlin lattice. Generic over D: 2x2, 3x3, 4x4 closed form det. Estimates, AVX2, Steps 8, one octave: Stretch/Parity 35 / 90 / 200 ns; Isochrone 15 / 30 / 55 ns. Steps sets the bill directly.
master.continuity: C0 by construction on all but Whorl's singular points (faded): a finite-step map of a C1 gradient is continuous, including across divides, where the stretch just becomes very large. Quintic Perlin has a continuous Hessian. In practice the rings crowd near divides: the accident measured c0ratio 1.7, max slope 2069 at the sheet's sampling, so expect the lab's probe to read low.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Octaves, int Steps (8), Output enum, G0 (ring onset: small means unit speed, rings in every basin; large means plain descent, rings only in steep basins), Line, Contrast, Offset, int Arms. Hybrid: Eta (ring spacing), Alpha (spiral), Wavelength.
master.risks: Aliasing where rings crowd near divides; needs Line and possibly a stretch-driven fade. Parity may look harsher than the soft log. Rings exist only with Eta*lambda above about 1, so sparse ring coverage with low octave or low frequency potentials. 4D is expensive. Isochrone may look like plain contour rings and lose the charm.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate from the entry, scaled to these steps: Stretch or Parity at 8 steps 35 / 90 / 200 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D, so about 22 ns for 2D at steps=5. Isochrone at 8 steps 15 / 30 / 55 ns, so about 22 ns for 2D at steps=12.

Parity at sharp 1e-4: c0 1.00 / 1.00, 2.00000, 2.00000, 1.99995: a real jump at this probe, binary by design (it is a sign). Isochrone: c0 1.00 / 1.00, 1.99928, 1.99255, 0.79973: acts as a jump at watershed divides, since flow lines separate sharply. Whorl was not measured, it shares Isochrone's T.

fold-print.changed_from_entry: Stretch gets a soft clamp to +-1 and a small floor added inside the log, in place of a max floor, so its range is known. Parity adds a final sharpen, S / sqrt( S^2 + sharp^2 ), because the plain soft sign product decays to gray near sinks. Defaults use alpha .4, eta .3 and steps 5 rather than the entry's 8 and alpha 0, because that had the best look and is cheaper. Isochrone and Whorl work with G0=1, not the small G0 the entry suggested for unit speed. 3D Stretch uses the Frobenius norm.

origin.smallest_test: t_stretch_ftle with hess=1,field=1: sweep eta .15,.2,.25,.3 and N 4,8,12. If ring pitch does not scale with eta and ring count does not follow N, the theory is wrong. Then add the one-line S product to analytic2 and look. Also try the 3D form at eta .3 to .5: the log says the 3D slice at eta .2 had no rings, and the theory says that is only because Eta*lambda stays below 1 there.

jet-fractal.look: Default relief: a field of eroded volcanoes: dark pointed summit spires, flanks with radial ribs and gullies, and smooth pale aprons meeting blue plains cut by thin ravines at the Voronoi walls. Beside it plain fBm over the same cones (it1) is a chaotic rough scatter with no such structure, so the payoff is visible. Slope erosion without Perturb gives only very smooth cones with a spike on top (it1): no gullies, no terraces, against the entry's prediction; Perturb is what makes the ribs. The FD default render (fd=1) looks nearly the same, slightly more rugged, so the look survives FD. Warped Simplex by FD: flowing folded terrain with streaks along the folds; with ridged sharpness, long sinuous mountain ranges with streaked flanks; these are the cases FractalDerivative cannot do. F2-F1 crests: angular slabs with rough valleys. Ridged cones and heavy ridged warp at full height are too spiky (it2). Vol: separate rounded balls with scaly bumpy skins and a few sharp slivers. SimplexFacet with Perturb was not tried: no such kernel in the harness.

jet-fractal.artifacts: Jet discontinuity is the real issue for a core interface. Where a source's gradient jumps (F1 walls, F1 apex), the slope weights of later octaves jump, so the height gets real seams (see no fade in c0_step_by_h). A faded analytic F1 jet removes them; this means a jet's gradient must deliberately differ from the true derivative near walls. The entry's claim of an exact gradient output holds only without feedback. Measured | G - FD of Height | against mean | FD |, in world units: plain Perlin fBm 0.008 against 0.72 (1 percent, FD noise); slope erosion only on cones 0.297 against 0.721 (41 percent); default with Perturb 2.413 against 2.513 (96 percent, G is not the slope of the output at all). So GradX, GradY, Slope and Hillshade outputs are only right with Slope Erosion, Altitude Erosion and Perturb all off, or the node must also propagate derivatives of the weights. Sheet axis stat 44.08, from the first panel's bright radial wall lines; the FFT shows radial streaks, no plain lattice cross at the viewed size.
jet-fractal.node_shape: JetFractal: Source, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Gain (hybrid), Sharpness (hybrid), Slope Erosion (hybrid), Altitude Erosion (hybrid), Perturb, Output {Height, Carved; GradX, GradY, GradZ, Slope, Hillshade only as exact outputs when feedback is off}. In core: GenJet virtual with an FD default, plus CellularDistance F1 override with Wall Fade and Apex Fade members.
jet-fractal.port_notes: Fixed octave loop, no branch. The FD default is D+1 Gen calls per octave; it needs no core change for this node to ship as a slower first version. The analytic F1 jet is one winning-site vector, F1 and F2 are already computed. The smooth substitute 2 v for sign( v ) keeps G continuous under Sharpness, as in fractal-derivative. Jets on a Source with internal discontinuities (Checkerboard, CellularValue, F1 edges) should be documented, and the FD stencil's step needs the far-coordinate law from the entry.
jet-fractal.params_text: default = eroded volcano field on F1 cones (src=1,slope=0.5,perturb=0.2,oct=6,gain=0.55,lac=2,scale=0.5,sharp=0,alt=0,wall=0.12,apex=0.05,jit=0.9). Plain fBm over the same cones: slope=0,perturb=0. FD default: fd=1. Warped Simplex by FD: src=2,slope=0.5,perturb=0.15,oct=6,scale=0.4. Sinuous ranges: src=2,slope=0.5,sharp=-1,perturb=0.1,alt=0.6,oct=5,scale=0.3,gain=0.5 with relief --hscale 55. F2-F1 crests: src=3,slope=0.5,perturb=0.15,oct=5,scale=0.35,gain=0.5. Vol: --window 4 --iso 0.1 --set scale=0.7,oct=4

master.one_liner: Forward-mode derivatives as a node interface (GenJet: value + gradient from one evaluation, finite differences only where no node overrides it), shown by a derivative-feedback fractal that erodes ANY source, not just a built-in basis.
master.look: Derivative-weighted fBm over sources that have no derivative basis today: F1 Voronoi cones under slope erosion grow gullied, terraced flanks and keep crisp crests (an eroded volcano field from CellularDistance); a Simplex warped first by DomainWarpSimplex and then eroded gives de Carpentier's 'swiss' turbulence with the warp's folds kept, which FractalDerivative cannot do because its basis is internal; SimplexFacet with Perturb drifts facets into stepped scree. GradX/GradY make the node an exact, one-evaluation SurfaceProbe for any jet-capable graph (hillshade with no step artefacts, no Sample Distance).
master.algorithm:
CORE CHANGE (GenJet): DispatchClass<Generator> gains virtual GenJet( int32v seed, float32v x, float32v y, float32v& gx, float32v& gy ) -> value (and 3D/4D forms). Default = Probe::Jet finite differences (D+1 Gen calls, small step with the probe's far-coordinate law), so every existing node works unchanged. Overrides, in order of value: Perlin/Simplex/Value/SuperSimplex via GradientNoise kernels times frequency; Constant/Gradient/SineWave/DistanceToPoint analytic; Add/Subtract/Multiply/Divide/Min/Max/Abs/Fade/Remap/PowFloat/PowInt/SignedSquareRoot chain and product rule (hybrid inputs are jets too, or documented as locally constant); DomainScale/Offset/AxisScale/Rotate/RotatePlane/AddDimension/RemoveDimension linear maps; SeedOffset passthrough; FractalFBm/Ridged/PingPong octave sums; DomainWarp family: g_p = J^T g_q using WarpJet (idea WarpStrain); CellularDistance F1 Euclidean: grad = (p - site1)/F1 for free; Terrace/CellularValue/Checkerboard stay on the FD default.
JetFractal GenT (fixed Octaves loop):
  sum = 0; G = 0 (D comps); amp = 1; freq = 1
  for k in 0..Octaves-1:
    (v, g) = Source.GenJet( seed + k, pos * freq ); g *= freq
    sharp: v = lerp( v, Sharpness < 0 ? 1 - 2|v| : 2|v| - 1, |Sharpness| ); g scaled by the same derivative (sign(v) factor)
    w = amp / ( 1 + SlopeErosion * |G|^2 )          (Uber-noise slope erosion from the accumulated gradient)
    w *= 1 - AltitudeErosion * saturate( sum )
    sum += w v; G += w g
    pos += Perturb * G / freq (de Carpentier swiss/jordan drift, optional)
    amp *= Gain; freq *= Lacunarity
  Output: Height (sum), GradX/Y/Z (G), Slope (|G|), Hillshade (dot(G, sun)), Carved (sum minus the plain weighted sum).
master.why_new: FractalDerivative (judged 5.91) carries derivatives only through its own Perlin/Simplex basis; SurfaceProbe and every gradient user in the catalogue pays 2D+1 or D+1 taps per use. GenJet is one incremental core interface with a safe default that makes the basis any graph and turns 3 extra taps into 0 wherever a kernel is analytic. Nearest: fractal-derivative, surface-probe, fractal-slope-aligned.
master.simd_plan: Jets return D extra float32v by reference. Analytic jets cost 1.3-1.8x a plain Gen (GradientNoise's Perlin grad reuses the lerp tree); the FD default costs (D+1)x. GenT packs for 2D/3D/4D. The 4D jet serves GenTileable2D exactly: the gradient lives in the torus embedding, so a 2D slope output projects it onto the tangent plane (note in the port).
master.continuity: C1 where the source is C1 (slope erosion is smooth in G); Sharpness toward ridged is C0; Perturb keeps C1.
master.params: Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Gain (hybrid), Sharpness (hybrid, -1 ridged .. +1 billow), Slope Erosion (hybrid), Altitude Erosion (hybrid), Perturb, Output enum, Source (any node; analytic where it overrides GenJet).
master.risks:
The core change touches every node, though the default makes it incremental; spatially varying hybrids need product-rule jets or are treated as locally constant; the GradientNoise Simplex kernel is r^2 = 0.5 and differs slightly from the stock 0.6 node in 3D/4D; FD default bias on rough sources far from the origin.
Overlap to know about: the octave loop (sharpness, slope erosion, altitude erosion, perturb) is fractal-derivative's, and that entry's FractalGradientFeedback variant already mentions finite differences on a Source. What is new here is running it on sources with no derivative basis (F1 cones, warped Simplex, SimplexFacet), so judge those and do not re-judge Perlin or Simplex.

measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: JetFractal over F1 at 6 octaves with a 3x3 window port, 6 x about 5 ns = 30 ns analytic (no FD taps), 90 ns with FD. Perlin at 5 octaves: about 8 ns analytic, per the entry's 1.3 to 1.8x plain cost, about 16 ns FD. No core interface was built, so these are not measured.
measured.c0_step_text: Default: h=1e-3 0.10154, h=1e-4 0.05138, h=1e-5 0.01532. On a small window (--window 1): 0.07586, 0.04583, 0.01792, h=1e-6 0.00243, h=1e-7 0.00043, so it does shrink: very steep folds from Perturb, not a jump. Perturb off: c0 6.05 / 6.49, 0.00544, 0.00055, 0.00006, clean. Unfaded F1 jet (wall=0.0001,apex=0.0001, perturb on): c0 0.89 / 0.97, 0.29916, 0.25382, 0.09757; small window 0.15703, 0.21058, 0.07025, 0.03011, 0.01752, so it does not settle: real seams at every wall. FD default on cones (fd=1): c0 1.77 / 2.15, 0.14559, 0.09831, 0.05813; small window 0.13903, 0.10816, 0.03796, 0.01334, 0.01699: it reads as a jump of about 0.015 at the smallest steps. FD at a fixed step is continuous in principle, so float rounding amplified by the feedback is a likely cause, but that is not confirmed. Warped Simplex by FD: c0 2.05 / 1.67, 0.16762, 0.05880, 0.03746.

jet-fractal.status_note: Keeper for the fractal node and its look. The GenJet core interface was NOT built or tested: this prototype uses hand written kernels and finite differences only. The look survives the finite difference default, so the node does not depend on GenJet; GenJet is a speed and continuity gain.
jet-fractal.changed_from_entry: No core change: hand written kernels and FD taps only. Added a fade to the F1 jet's gradient at walls and at the apex, because without it the height has real seams. Sharpness uses a smooth substitute for sign( v ). Added a warp in src 2 and an F2-F1 source in src 3. Perturb is on by default since slope erosion alone does not give the entry's gullies. out 6 and 7 report gradient exactness.

extra_measured.scalar_vs_perlin_notes: Measured against perlin2. Default, analytic F1 jet, 6 octaves of a 5x5 cell search: 17.42x (881 ns). Same with the FD default: 42.81x (2183 ns), so the analytic jet is 2.48x faster here. Plain Perlin fBm at 5 octaves: analytic jet 621 ns, FD 949 ns, 1.53x faster. Warped Simplex by FD at 6 octaves: 65.01x (3339 ns). Map lookups of params are part of all of these, and they shrink the apparent gain.

warp-strain.look: LogStretch: a dense net of thin white nerve or vein filaments that bundle, part and swirl around dark calm pools. The sheet's threshold reads as torn white strands. With warp=2 and the Lyapunov chain settings it matches the LyapunovStretch parent's thumb in shape and contrast, side by side, confirming the same filament character from a generic Jacobian. The wide panel is an even white web. Det is black and white crumple with dense fine stars at the compression centres, busier than LogStretch. Fold is a harsh caustic net with dust at the simplex warp's third octave; I find it noisier than the LogStretch. Rotation gives smooth gray marble bands with visible hard wrap edges. The striking result is the line correction: the uncorrected zebra and uncorrected cell walls go from fat blobs to hairlines and dust, while the corrected ones keep one world width everywhere. StrainLines through 3 shears reads as long even contour lines with cell junctions, close to a topographic map or stretched hide. At twice the warp amplitude the corrected zebra stays even but becomes busy white scribble because the stripes crowd; the uncorrected one is dust. The 3D corrected Perlin lines render as thin corrugated sheets of even thickness.
warp-strain.dims: 2D measured: all outputs. 3D measured: check gives 3D range and z continuity (mean 0.0022, max 0.0295 for dz=1e-3), the volume renders the corrected Perlin lines, XZ slice on the sheet. 3D Rotation is not implemented and returns 0. 4D not built.
warp-strain.range: default LogStretch -1.000..0.442 over 8 seeds, mean -0.406, 0 nans. All other outputs are clamped to -1..1 and reach both ends in the grid, except Rotation which spans the full range by construction. 3D LogStretch -1.000..0.057 on the slice checked by the check command.
warp-strain.artifacts: Rotation has a real jump of 2.0 at the plus or minus pi wrap, as the entry predicted; offer a sin/cos pair. Dotted beads run along some filaments, from the third octave stretched, visible in LogStretch at this scale. Fold, Det and CorrectedSource are very steep at this warp strength (max slope about 1400 to 1950 per unit, c0ratio 1.0 to 1.4) but their step table keeps shrinking, so these are slopes, not jumps. Cell wall lines with a 3x3 wall pass have a real seam, measured as 1.116 at h=1e-3, because the nearest site can change between two sites that are not in each other's window; a 5x5 wall pass removes it (0.081), so wallw=2 is the default in 2D and costs 25 hashes. The 3D wall pass is still 3x3x3 and has not been scanned for that seam. The FD Jacobian adds a 0.01 flutter at small steps in the wall output (h=1e-5 stays at 0.0103), caused by float rounding in the differences; analytic jac=1 removes it (0.0012). Corrected lines are first order: where the warp bends within a line width, width wobbles. Stripes crowd above the spacing the width allows, which turns to white scribble.
warp-strain.node_shape: Warp (GeneratorSourceT<DomainWarp>), Source (hybrid, CorrectedSource only), Output enum {LogStretch, Det, Fold, Anisotropy, Rotation, CorrectedSource, CellLines}, Contrast, Line Softness, Gamma, Width (hybrid), Floor, Sample Distance.
warp-strain.port_notes: Needs WarpJet to be cheap. The FD default is 2D+1 warps, measured 3.6x the analytic scalar cost, and the rounding flutter above favours analytic. Step law used: h = max(2e-3, 5e-7 * largest coordinate), dividing by the real step after rounding; far coordinates at 4e4 stayed clean (std 0.35, 0 nans). 2D post processing is 2 sqrt and 1 atan, as the entry says. 3D uses a trigonometric eigen solve here; a port wants polynomial acos and cos.
warp-strain.params_text: plain default: out=0,warp=0,jac=0,oct=3,amp=0.55,fq=0.5,contrast=0.2. Even width zebra: out=5,width=0.05. StrainLines: out=6,warp=2,steps=3,samp=1.1,sfq=0.4,jac=1,wallw=2. Analytic Jacobian: add jac=1.

master.one_liner: The Jacobian of ANY DomainWarp subgraph as a node: log-stretch filaments, fold caustics, compression shading and rotation of the user's own warp, plus a Source whose line width is corrected back to world units through the warp.
master.look: LogStretch of a DomainWarpFractalProgressive: the hidden vein structure of the marbling, thin bright filaments where neighbouring points were torn apart, for the user's own warp rather than LyapunovStretch's internal shear chain. Fold of a strong Simplex warp: a caustic net with cusps and bowties (FoldCaustic for any warp). Det as squash shading: a crumpled sheet darkens where the warp compressed it, which is how real folded cloth and skin wrinkles shade. CorrectedSource: craquelure, veins or zebra stripes that keep the same width through a violent warp instead of going fat in stretched zones and hairline in compressed ones. StrainLines form, predicted by the panel and not built: craquelure, stretched hide and even marble veins whose line width stays constant in world units.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: Warp (GeneratorSourceT<DomainWarp>, held the way DomainWarpFractal holds its warp), Source (hybrid, only for CorrectedSource), Output enum.
CORE CHANGE (WarpJet): add to DispatchClass<DomainWarp> a virtual WarpJet( seed, amp, pos..., out..., J[D][D] ) that returns the displacement AND its Jacobian dW/dp. Default implementation = central finite differences: for each axis d call Warp at pos +- h e_d (2D extra Warp calls, h from Probe::Step/Snap), J[:,d] = (out+ - out-) / 2h. Overrides: DomainWarpGradient (differentiate the Hermite blend weights, same fold as GradientNoise::PerlinFold carries grad), DomainWarpSimplex/SuperSimplex (per-vertex falloff derivative as GradientNoise::SimplexVertex), DomainWarpShear (ShearChain::Run<true> applied to the D basis tangents, or carry a DxD matrix since the tangent update is linear), DomainWarpFractalProgressive (J = J_n ... J_1, each octave's jet taken at the running point), DomainWarpFractalIndependent (J = I + sum_k A_k DW_k), DomainWarpFlow (per step J <- (I + eta A H) J with H from the potential's jet, else fallback).
Node: q = p + W(p); J = I + dW.
2D closed form: m = (J00+J11)/2, n = (J00-J11)/2, a = (J01+J10)/2, b = (J01-J10)/2; P = sqrt(m^2+b^2), Q = sqrt(n^2+a^2); s1 = P + Q, s2 = |P - Q| (singular values); rotation theta = atan2(b, m) (PolyMath::ATan2); det = J00 J11 - J01 J10.
3D: det by cofactors; s1^2 = largest eigenvalue of J^T J via the closed-form symmetric 3x3 solve already in SurfaceProbe::CrestLines; rotation omitted. 4D: det + Frobenius proxy s1 ~ sqrt(trace(J^T J)/D).
Outputs: LogStretch = 1 - 2 * s1^(-2 Contrast) (LyapunovStretch's shrink form); Det = clamp(log2(det), -4, 4)/4 (compression negative); Fold = (soft^2 / (det^2 + soft^2))^(gamma/2) (CausticWeb's line form, bright where det -> 0); Anisotropy = 1 - 2 s2/s1; Rotation = theta/pi (2D).
CorrectedSource: v = Source(q); g_q = gradient of Source at q (GenJet if available, else Probe::Jet D+1 taps around q); g_p = J^T g_q; d = v / (|g_p| + eps) is a first-order WORLD distance to the Source's zero set; out = 1 - 2 saturate(|d| / Width) (constant world-width lines through the warp).

MERGED FORM StrainLines (artist-material lens, crossbreed seed #22), same mechanism, kept in full: M = identity. Constant loop i=1..S of shears: s = dot(n_i,p) + phi_i; p += A_i*f(s)*t_i with t_i perpendicular to n_i; M = (I + A_i*f'(s)*t_i*n_i^T)*M. This is the ShearFlow kernel, and Lyapunov already carries a tangent. Then the exact edge pass at warped p. For each neighbour k in the fixed window: n_k = unit(s_k - s_1); e_k = dot(m_k - p, n_k); D_k = e_k / Max(|M^T*n_k|, floor). D = Min over k of D_k. Output line = profile(D/W), or bevel from D. Each term is zero on its own bisector and continuous, so Min stays C0 where the unwarped edge distance is. 3D uses a 3x3 M and 3D shears; 4D only if the window budget allows. Cost ESTIMATE: shear kernel about 2-3 ns, edge pass 5.5 / 16 ns, about 6 FMAs per neighbour, so about 10 / 25 ns in 2D / 3D. Risk: first order breaks down at very high strain, so the floor needs tuning.

Merge note: StrainLines is the shear-chain special case of CorrectedSource: carry the Jacobian through the warp, then divide a level-set distance by |M^T n|. It needs no Source taps because each wall's normal is known, and it corrects per wall where CorrectedSource uses one gradient. Build it as a second corrected output (per-wall edge lines) and render both.
master.why_new:
LyapunovStretch only knows its own shear chain and FoldCaustic only its own field; the StrainLines seed (22) asks for exactly the width correction but as a bespoke build. A graph can in fact reach the warped position today (DomainWarp with Source = Gradient(Multiplier X=1) returns q_x) and finite-difference it with SurfaceProbe, but that is (2D+1) x D warp evaluations, about ten nodes, and gives no singular values or rotation. IsoDistance on the warped composite already gives constant-width lines at (2D+1) x (warp + source) cost; this node does it at one warp jet plus D+1 cheap source taps and exposes the strain itself. Nearest: lyapunov-stretch, fold-caustic, stretch-ftle, StrainLines (seed 22).
StrainLines: Warped line work goes fat and thin with stretch, and that is how warped cells give themselves away. Carrying the Jacobian through the warp keeps line width constant in world units: craquelure, stretched hide, even marble veins. A graph cannot do this because nodes cannot pass a Jacobian. Not built, look unverified.
Seed gap: even line width through warps.
master.simd_plan:
A DxD float32v matrix per lane. Analytic WarpJet costs about 1.5x the plain Warp (the grad falls out of the same lerp tree); the FD default costs (2D+1)x the warp. 2D post-processing is 2 sqrt + 1 atan polynomial; 3D eigen solve ~40 ops; 4D uses det + Frobenius proxy. GenTileable2D goes through the 4D path and gets Det/Fold exactly, LogStretch approximately. Estimate 2D: ~2x a DomainWarpSimplex fractal of the same octaves.
StrainLines: Cost ESTIMATE: shear kernel about 2-3 ns, edge pass 5.5 / 16 ns, about 6 FMAs per neighbour, so about 10 / 25 ns in 2D / 3D.
master.continuity:
C0 wherever the warp is C1 (Gradient, Simplex, Shear-noise warps are; Shear-parabola is C1 too). Fold has a sharp line core bounded by Line Softness. Rotation wraps at +-pi: offer sin/cos pair or 2*theta for line-field use.
StrainLines: Each term is zero on its own bisector and continuous, so Min stays C0 where the unwarped edge distance is.
master.params: Warp (source, DomainWarp family), Source (hybrid, CorrectedSource only), Output enum (LogStretch, Det, Fold, Anisotropy, Rotation, CorrectedSource), Contrast, Line Softness, Gamma, Width (hybrid), Sample Distance (FD fallback step). From StrainLines: Steps S, per-step n_i, t_i, A_i, phi_i (the ShearFlow kernel), Line Width W, floor, Output adds a per-wall corrected edge line or bevel.
master.risks:
FD fallback at far coordinates (use the probe step law); first-order width correction breaks where the warp curves within one line width; 3D rotation omitted; the full value needs the WarpJet core change, otherwise every output costs 2D+1 warp evaluations.
StrainLines, seed risk 0.5: first order breaks at high strain. Risk: first order breaks down at very high strain, so the floor needs tuning.

warp-component.look: Steered grain over the warp's displacement reads as combed fur or hair, with sweeping parted tracts, swirls around a few centres and a clean even contrast, and looks good. The grain-beside-stripes test does NOT match the entry's prediction. In the comparison the left panel mixes displacement-steered grain with the same warp's stripes, and the grain plainly crosses the stripes at all angles. Measured agreement |cos| between the displacement direction and the true stripe tangent: mean 0.587 to 0.669 over 4 seeds and 0.569 to 0.677 over 3 stripe directions, against 0.637 for no relation at all. So displacement direction is unrelated to where the warped stripes go. With steer=1, using the perpendicular of J^T n from a finite-difference Jacobian, the right panel's grain runs along the stripes everywhere. X and Y were not rendered to an image, only measured. Length is soft clouds with dark creases where the displacement passes through zero. Angle has hard wrap edges. Divergence and Curl give soft gray fields with bright streaks and a few spots at vortex-like points, and read better than Length. The 3D vol shows rough elongated slabs, messy rather than clean fibres.
warp-component.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: check gives range -0.888..0.931 and z continuity mean 0.0027, the volume exists with 3D fibres along the displacement, XZ slice on the sheet. Each 3D axis is its own warp evaluation. 4D not built.
warp-component.range: grain -1.000..0.991 over 8 seeds, mean 0.000, 0 nans. With Normalise = amplitude, measured over 8 seeds: X -1.000..1.000, Y -1.000..1.000, Length -0.998..1.000, all clamped, mean near 0 for X and Y and -0.119 for Length.
warp-component.artifacts: Angle has a real jump of 2.0 at the wrap, as the entry said: steer with the X/Y pair. Displacement steering has cores where the displacement vanishes (grain goes isotropic by the eps fade) and thin kinks where the third octave's direction turns fast, seen as scars in the top right of the first steer panel. Tangent steering by FD has a 0.0086 flutter at small steps (h=1e-5), and Divergence and Curl 0.0016 and 0.0025, from float rounding in the differences, not a seam.
warp-component.node_shape: As an output set on warp-strain's node: Output adds X, Y, Z, W, Length, Angle, Divergence, Curl, StripeTangentX, StripeTangentY. Normalise, Stripe Direction (for the tangent), Sample Distance.
warp-component.port_notes: Why merged: same input (a typed DomainWarp source), same shape (one enum of outputs), and the output that delivers the entry's promise needs the Jacobian. X, Y, Length and Angle need only the existing Warp virtual, so they could ship before WarpJet. Also the warp-strain entry notes a graph can already reach q_x through DomainWarp over Gradient(Multiplier X=1), so plain X/Y are about three nodes today. A direction pair costs two warps without a memo. Fractal warps need their octave loop shared, as the entry says.

master.one_liner: Export the vector a DomainWarp computes (component, length, angle, divergence, curl) as a scalar, using the Warp virtual that already exists, so any warp becomes a direction field for SteerablePerlin, FlowShingle, LineIntegral and friends.

master.algorithm:
warp = GetSourceSIMD( mWarp )   (GeneratorSourceT<DomainWarp>, as DomainWarpFractal holds)
amp = warp amplitude hybrid read at p; v = 0; warp->Warp( seed, amp, (p * warpFreq)..., v... )  -> displacement v in world units
Output: X/Y/Z/W -> v[d] / Normalise; Length -> |v| / Normalise; Angle (2D) -> PolyMath::ATan2( v1, v0 ) / pi; Divergence, Curl2D, CurlZ3D -> from WarpJet when present, else central FD of Warp (2D extra Warp calls)
Fractal warps: accept DomainWarpFractalProgressive/Independent by running their octave loop here (small refactor to share the loop), so a whole fractal warp exports its vector.
master.why_new: FastNoise's only vector outputs live in the DomainWarp family and nothing exports them; DomainWarpSource goes scalar to warp, this is warp to scalar. No core change: the Warp virtual and the typed source are already there. Nearest: domain-warp-source, lyapunov-stretch, seed 20.
master.simd_plan: One Warp per component (two nodes for a 2D direction: two warp evaluations, or shared through the CellularMulti memo pattern). Any dimension; every warp node has a 4D Warp so tiling works. Cost = the warp, about 1-3 ns per octave.

advected-scatter.look: Default: an andamento mosaic or cobbled street. Rows of near rectangular setts curve in fans and waves, with even dark mortar of one width, per-brick tone, and bricks that grow and shrink with the local strain. The threshold panel reads as curved paving. A thin dark cusp shows at one spot in the top left where rows pinch. Pebbles: round white dots crowded into bands and sparse elsewhere, like gravel bars, next to the plain warp control whose stamps are streaked ellipses. Measured blob aspect ratio (second moment), dense pebbles: median 1.08, p90 2.08 with some of that from merged overlaps, against median 2.18, p90 4.03 for the plain warp. Sparse pebbles: median 1.055 against 1.632. Block correlation of stamp area with log det J: 0.855. 3D: vol shows a heap of round balls, cut circles and ellipses in orange from the cube faces. vol_boxes shows long beams that bend along the warp and keep a rectangular cross section, like warped timber. The entry's polar rotation frame tears bricks badly, seen, and the constant size bricks leave wavy black gaps and overlaps where the row spacing changes. Those constant size rows do bend, and the bricks do stay rectangular away from strain peaks. Density output is a soft cloud.
advected-scatter.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: check gives range and z continuity, the volume shows spheres, the volume shows boxes in the course frame, both with Perlin warp and FD Jacobian. The one hash course lookup is 2D only here; 3D uses the 3x3x3 window. 4D not built.
advected-scatter.range: default -1.000..1.000 over 8 seeds, mean 0.268, 0 nans. Pebbles -1.000..0.997, mean -0.591 (mostly background).
advected-scatter.artifacts: No jump found with analytic J: all steps shrink. With FD the default keeps a small flutter (0.031 at h=1e-5) from float rounding in the differences; it was 0.133 at FD step 2e-3 and raising the step to 0.01 reduced it, analytic gives 0.002. Pebble edges use a sqrt dome, so the step shrinks about as sqrt(h), a steep edge rather than a jump. First order only: where the warp curves within a stamp, edges bow, as the 3D beams show. Courses at higher strain (samp=0.6, the image top right) gain thin leaf-shaped slivers and very thin rows where they pinch; samp=0.8 is steep (1.99 at h=1e-3) but shrinks to 0.041. In the windowed forms a stamp shrinks per lane when strain would overflow the window, reading as thinning. Dense pebbles overlap and merge with no collisions. The 3D windows were not scanned for jumps by the harness, since jumps only probes Eval2.

advected-scatter.port_notes: Courses is the cheap and strain-proof form: row = floor(Qy); along a row o.t = tl ( dqx + K dqy ), so the column is the floor of Qx + K dqy. One hash, no window, no Select chain. Bond is an integer test on the row. Scatter uses the 3^D window with per-row x offset, and clamps the stamp by allow / (bound * sigma_max * cell), allow = 1.5 - jitter/2. Max of stamps is C0 since each reaches 0 at its edge. Needs WarpJet for its real cost, and FD rounding favours analytic too. Shares Jacobian plumbing with warp-strain.

master.one_liner: Stamps or cells arranged by a DomainWarp but measured through its inverse Jacobian, so pebbles crowd into compression bands and brick courses bend along a river while every pebble stays round and every brick a rectangle.
master.look: Pebbles sorted by a flow: dense where a shear or gradient warp compresses, sparse where it stretches, every pebble round (sediment sorting, gravel bars). Jitter 0 with a rectangular stamp in Flow orientation: brick courses that curve along a river warp, bricks evenly sized and rectangular inside. Fish scales or roof tiles following the warped grid lines of a swirl. The Density output alone is a crowd map of the warp.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: Warp (GeneratorSourceT<DomainWarp>), Source (stamp or lookup), window pattern (jittered lattice, or a regular grid / TileDomain bond for courses).
q = p + W(p); J = I + dW(p) from WarpJet (idea WarpStrain; FD fallback). Ji = J^-1 (2x2 closed form; 3x3 cofactors / det; det clamped at eps).
Sites s_i live in q-space (jittered cell points, 3^D window as StampScatter).
World offset o_i = Ji ( q - s_i )          (first-order vector from the site to p in WORLD units)
Distance d_i = |o_i|; or exact G-metric edge distance with G = Ji^T Ji constant per lane: the bisector of s_1, s_i stays a plane in q-space, edge = min_i dot( 0.5(s_i + s_1) - q, G (s_i - s_1) ) / |Ji (s_i - s_1)|.
Orientation enum: World (local = o_i / r, content axes = world axes) or Flow (local = R^T o_i with R the rotation part of J: 2D angle = atan2( J10 - J01, J00 + J11 ); 3D: Gram-Schmidt of J's columns).
Source evaluated once for the winning site (StampScatter's K candidates and cascade fade, priority by hash or by 1/det) at local coords with the site's seed.
Window safety: a site within world radius R must be inside the 3^D q-window, so clamp the per-lane stamp radius r <= min( R, (1 - jitter) / sigma_max(J) ) (sigma_max from the 2D closed form, Frobenius bound in 3D/4D): stamps shrink smoothly where strain is extreme instead of popping.
Outputs: Stamp, F1 (world distance), EdgeDistance, Density (1/det J), CellValue.
master.why_new: The AndamentoMosaic seed (3) wants flow-aligned tiles of constant size and says coursed rows need a stream function a pointwise node cannot integrate: a DomainWarp IS an integrated displacement, the image of a regular grid under it gives the courses, and the inverse Jacobian keeps the content undistorted. GradedVoronoi, GradientMetricCellular and FlowCellular stretch cells on purpose; a plain DomainWarp around StampScatter stretches the pebbles. Nearest: AndamentoMosaic (seed 3), stamp-scatter, graded-voronoi, gradient-metric-cellular, cellular-metric-field.
master.simd_plan: One warp jet + the StampScatter 3^D window + a DxD inverse (2D 6 ops, 3D ~30) + a D^2-FMA matrix-vector per site (9 / 27 sites). About 1.3x StampScatter plus the warp. 4D: 81 sites as StampScatter; Flow orientation in 2D/3D only, World in 4D.
master.continuity: C0 with the cascade fade; J is continuous where the warp is C1; the per-lane radius clamp is continuous; EdgeDistance C0 as iq's method.
master.params: Warp (source), Source (source), Feature Scale, Size, Jitter, Orientation (World, Flow), K (int), Combine, Output enum, Density (hybrid).
master.risks: First-order metric breaks where the warp curves within one stamp (large stamps or sharp warps: brick edges bow); window overflow above strain ~2 is handled by shrinking, which reads as thinning; needs WarpJet or 2D+1 warp evaluations per sample.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: courses with analytic WarpJet through 6 shears about 6 to 8 ns, since it needs one hash and no window. FD default about 15 to 20 ns. Pebbles with a 3 octave Perlin warp and 3x3 window: about 15 ns analytic, about 40 ns FD.

advected-scatter.changed_from_entry: Three changes. 1. The entry says Flow orientation is local = R^T o with R the rotation part of J. Polar rotation does not follow the rows under shear and tears bricks, seen. Replaced by a Course frame: t = J^-1 e_x normalised, n = normalised J^T e_y. Polar is still orient=1. 2. Added Conform and the one hash Courses lookup, which the entry did not have, because the constant size rectangles leave gaps where row spacing changes. Courses gives bricks that exactly tile in the first order and removes the window limit. It gives up constant brick size. 3. The entry says density goes as 1/det J. With sites in q space and q = p + W(p), world density is det J, confirmed by the positive 0.855 correlation with log det, so the Density output is det J. Window clamp uses allow = 1.5 - jitter/2 from the actual window geometry, not (1 - jitter).

metric-waves.look: Default still: curving bands of one width that follow the warp's flow, like a fingerprint or combed putty, broken into shorter dashes and dots in calm regions. The threshold panel looks most like a fingerprint. The wide panel is a combed swirl with a directional FFT. The frames row shows the mechanism directly: at A = 0 both rows are the same ring labyrinth noise. As A grows the plain control's bands get finer and tighter with moire-like packing at A = 2, while the metric row's bands keep their width and only gain direction. In the first image the plain row has fat blobs next to tight patches at A = 1 and 2, the metric row does not. Isotropy 1 with Const 16 gives even round grain close to plain ring noise, as the entry predicted, and some finer patches remain where strain peaks. Measured local spectrum, smallest test, 7 radii default, sin warp A = 2: radial mean 2.60 for metric against 3.75 for plain, local centroid CV 0.142 against 0.179. With the 32 x 11 table, sin warp A = 2: radial mean 2.36 against 3.62, CV 0.074 against 0.224. Fractal warp A = 1.4, default table: radial mean 2.54 against 3.88, CV 0.114 against 0.302. A = 2: 2.95 against 6.41, CV 0.233 against 0.444. At that strain the metric's relative radial width (0.726) is no better than plain's (0.693). Under the simplex warp with 3 octaves the bands come apart into broken noisy filaments with some wide black and white bands left over, as the entry's risk says. The 3D vol is soft blobs with no clear filament character at F = 1.2; unremarkable.
metric-waves.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: check gives range -1..1 and z continuity mean 0.0032, the volume exists, using 48 sphere rays x 7 radii (336 waves), and it has no isotropy gate. 4D not built; tiling would need integer wave vectors, as the entry says.
metric-waves.range: -1.000..1.000 over 8 seeds, clamped, mean 0.000, std about 0.43, 0 nans. Clamp touches about 1 percent of samples; the sheet's p1 is -1.000 and p99 0.984.
metric-waves.artifacts: No jump: with analytic J every step shrinks cleanly and c0ratio is 8. With FD on a simplex warp it is steep (1.37 at h=1e-3) and keeps shrinking (0.094 at h=1e-5). Band breakup at high strain: the table's radii cover k up to F b^3, and past that the normaliser amplifies whichever wave is left, giving wide wrong-wavelength bands. Fine warp detail makes packets break into noise. Normaliser needs eps because a lane can have nearly all windows closed. Isotropy depends on Const: at the entry-suggested small value only 2 rays stayed open and the result was a plain crosshatch, seen. The local look alternates between clean bands and dashes, so it reads less clean than the entry's 'even filaments' at this table size. The payoff in motion is not shown except as a row of stills.

metric-waves.port_notes: No lattice; a fixed wave loop with every wave costing on every lane. nv2 once per ray, q per radius by multiplying by b^2. Phases from a table computed when a param is set. The prototype rebuilds that table per sample in non-speed runs to keep Eval pure, so only the speed command's number is meaningful. Far coordinates: range held at 4e4 in check, but phase precision is the usual weakness of wave nodes. Cost scales with rays x radii, and it is a sum of 112 waves at default, so 4D would be expensive.

master.one_liner: A wave sum phase-locked to any domain warp whose per-wave amplitude is set by the local Jacobian, after SIGGRAPH 2026's wave-based textures for extreme deformation: features move with the warp but stay at one world wavelength, so strong warps give even filaments instead of smears and pinched grain.
master.look: With no warp, ring-spectrum labyrinth noise. With a strong warp and Isotropy 0: constant-width bands that follow the warp's stretch direction and bend with it, like combed filaments in lava or putty, with no thick blobs where the warp stretches and no moire where it compresses. With Isotropy 1: even grain everywhere, so a still looks close to plain ring noise; the gain is that animating Warp Amplitude advects the features with no smearing. Good for lava, flowing sludge, marble that keeps its vein width.
master.algorithm:
Source: Kalinov, Ly, Hafner, Wojtan, TOG 2026. HONESTY: their main PDF is over my fetch limit. I read the abstract, the press text and the two page supplement. From those: texture is waves, not pixels; stretched regions lose fine detail to lower frequency detail and compressed regions lose low to high, with a restoring force in frequency space; two algorithms, spectrum rescaling and isotropy preserving; wave vectors lie on rays with exponentially distributed magnitudes (base 1.5 to 3); rays have refinement levels with theta(r,j) = 2^-r*pi*(1+2j); a ray at level r is active when target level l(v,I) > r - 1/2, with l = log2(omega*const) and omega = sqrt(det I^-1)/<v, I^-1 v>. The band window below is my reconstruction of the first algorithm, not their formula.
Table at param set: Nr base rays plus refinement rays, radii k0*b^m, phases from seed: about 48 to 96 waves.
u = p + Warp(p)   // any DomainWarp node through Warp()
J = du/dp by differences, D+1 Warp calls; C = J*J^T; dj = |det J|
out = 0; E = 0
for each ray (unit v, level r):
  nv2 = v^T C v   // |J^T v|^2
  gate = Isotropy > 0 and r > 0 ? sat(log2(dj/nv2*Const) - r + 1) : 1
  s = dot(v, u)
  for each radius k on this ray:
    q = k*k*nv2/(F*F); a = gate*pow(4*q/((1+q)*(1+q)), P)   // peak at q = 1, no log, smooth
    out += a*wave(2*pi*k*s + phi); E += a*a
return out*InvSqrt(E/2 + eps)
Per wave, the world wave vector is J^T k, so a wave only sounds where its world wavelength is close to 1/F. CoatField's explanation of its accident (a warp turns the ring of wave vectors into an ellipse) applies here, but here the ring is held at one radius by swapping which waves are on.
master.why_new: Hard made easy: warping any amount with a stable spectrum and no aliasing. Nearest: any Source under DomainWarp (features stretch and alias). CoatField (hybrid angular spread with no warp and no phase lock). LyapunovStretch and WarpStrain (draw or report strain but do not rebalance the spectrum). AdvectedScatter does a related thing for stamps. The per-wave window needs J and a loop over waves, so no graph reaches it.
master.simd_plan: No lattice, fixed wave count; every wave costs on every lane. Compute nv2 once per ray, q per radius by multiplying by b*b. With the parabola kernel, estimate 25 to 40 ns plus (D+1) warps in 2D; 3D needs 3x3 J, more rays, about 60 ns; 4D about 100 ns, and 4D lets it tile only if table wave vectors are integer. Use the WarpJet path from the WarpStrain proposal where it exists to drop the extra warp calls.
master.continuity: C0 and smooth wherever J is continuous. Warps with creases give kinks in amplitude, not jumps, because phase depends only on u.
master.params: Warp (DomainWarp source), Frequency (hybrid), Rays, Radii, Base b, Band Sharpness P, Isotropy (0 gives flow-aligned filaments, 1 keeps the grain round), Wave Kernel (Sine, Parabola).
master.risks: The window changes on the scale of the warp, and if the warp has fine detail amplitude changes faster than a wavelength and the packets break into noise. A still may look unremarkable, since the real payoff is in motion and the lab tools show stills. My reconstruction may lose whatever makes their result look good. Far-coordinate phase precision is the same weakness as all wave nodes.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: about 25 to 40 ns for 112 waves with a parabola kernel, as the entry guessed, plus (D+1) warps if no WarpJet exists.

metric-waves.changed_from_entry: The source paper's main PDF was not available to me; this follows the entry's reconstruction and is not their formula. Table moved from 48-96 waves to 16 rays x 7 radii at base 3 (112 waves) with P = 2, chosen by measuring centroid CV (0.114) against a 32 x 11 base 2 table (0.126), so the wider base costs nothing here. Const fixed at 16 so at least levels 0 to 3 stay open when there is no strain. Added an optional early-out in the proto when the sine kernel is used; it is not in the default and a port cannot use it. The control mode uses one ring of the same rays with fixed amplitudes.

shear-frame-ink-strokes.look: Layered ink or impasto strokes: tapered bands with bristle lines along them, overlapping with a dark rim, all following one field that bends and folds but has no whorl and no centre. A single large swell dominates this seed's window. The threshold reads as a woodcut. Hillshade shows ridged brush marks. The line field cos(2 theta) is smooth white and gray marble with thin bright bands and no point-like cores, in the panel I viewed. The entry's J v0 frame shredded strokes into jagged chevrons at higher strain (amp 0.55, 8 steps). At the gentler default it is acceptable, but still choppier than the J^-1 frame. Hard priority (comp=1) looks about the same but with crisper white edges, and it has real jumps. 3D vol: separate tapered rods with a coherent lean through the cube, no strokes merge; it reads as straws or pine needles. Wide panel is a busy horizontal hatch with wavy bands.
shear-frame-ink-strokes.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: check gives range and z continuity mean 0.0025, the volume shows capsules, XZ slice on the sheet. Reverse pass works in both. 4D not built; the entry proposes Angle only there.
shear-frame-ink-strokes.range: strokes -0.950..0.937 over 8 seeds, mean -0.153, 0 nans. Background is -0.95. 3D -1.000..0.912 on the checked slice.
shear-frame-ink-strokes.artifacts: comp=1 has real jumps by design, 1.29 at h=1e-5. The default composite is C0: its step table shrinks. My first composite, m * exp(14 pr), was also formally C0 but behaved as a jump (0.89 at h=1e-5); changing to m^3 weights and K=8 fixed that. The slope is still steep, c0ratio 2.29, max slope 652 per unit. Where the field turns within a stroke the stroke bends unevenly, since each lane uses its own tangent: a few mangled shapes show at the lower right of the sheet. Bends only, no whorls, as the entry warned, so it cannot draw eddies. log2 |J v0| / 4 over 8 seeds at the default stays in -0.483..0.490, so |J v0| is at least 0.26 there; at amp 0.8, 12 steps it clamps at -1, so that minimum is below 1/16 and unmeasured. Singular-point freedom holds by construction (det J = 1), not by that measure. Angle did not wrap in this window at this strain but it can at higher strain, jumping 2.0; take sin and cos or cos(2 theta).
shear-frame-ink-strokes.node_shape: Direction part: Steps, Amplitude, Frequency, Lacunarity, Gain, V0 angle, Frame enum {PushForward, WorldTangent}, Output {Angle, Cos2Theta, Strokes}. Stroke part: Stroke Scale, Length, Width, Jitter, Bristle, Bristle Frequency, Softness, Priority Sharpness K, Tone, Background. 4D Angle only.
shear-frame-ink-strokes.port_notes: Reverse pass: store g_k from the forward loop, then v -= g_k (t_k . v) u_k from k = N-1 down to 0; 3 FMAs per step, no matrix, any dimension. The forward tangent is a q space vector; the reverse one is the world tangent of the chain's warped lines, so strokes run with the chain's own stripes, unlike a displacement vector (see warp-component's 0.6 agreement). exp(K pr) per candidate can come from the hash as a table or pow. m^3 is two multiplies. Reach: 4x4 window gives 2 - jit/2 = 1.7 lattice units at jit 0.6, matching L = 1.7. Strokes could be a mode of FlowShingle with this as its direction source.

master.one_liner: A direction field with no singular points, from a tangent pushed through a shear chain, output as an Angle for every steered node or as painterly strokes.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: ink strokes and streaks that bend along a field with no cores: bends only, no whorls.
master.algorithm: p = pos; v = v0 (fixed per seed). For k in 0..N-1 (int member, same for all lanes): s = dot(p, d[k]) * f[k] + off[k]; n, dn = 1D noise and derivative at s; p += a[k] * n * perp[k]; v += a[k] * f[k] * dn * dot(v, d[k]) * perp[k]; v *= InvSqrt(dot(v, v)). perp[k] must be orthogonal to d[k], using the perpendicular pairs table. Output A: Angle, from fastAtan2 of v; the wrap is harmless to consumers that take sin and cos. Output B: strokes at the original pos in the flow-shingle window (16 candidates in 2D, 27 in 3D). For each candidate r = pos - site; u = dot(r, v); w2 = dot(r, r) - u*u; capsule mask from u and w2, so 3D needs no full frame; bristles from sin of w * B; keep the highest hashed priority with Select. 4D: Angle output only, since 81 candidates is too much. Estimated AVX2 2D: 17-19 ns (critic estimates: about 10 for 8 chain steps, 7-9 for the stroke window).
master.why_new:
Lyapunov streaks and the flow-strokes curl are the two best 2D images, and every steered node needs a direction field. Gradient fields have cores. Each shear has det J = 1, so J*v0 can never vanish: this direction field has no singular points in any dimension. Limit: it cannot make whorls, only bends. Not built; the look is a prediction.
Seed gap: a direction field with no singular points, usable by every steered node.
master.simd_plan: Estimated AVX2 2D: 17-19 ns (critic estimates: about 10 for 8 chain steps, 7-9 for the stroke window).
master.continuity: Not stated by the panel.
master.params: Steps N (int), v0 (per seed), per-step d, f, off, a from the perpendicular pairs table, Output enum {Angle, Strokes}, Bristle B, stroke window as flow-shingle.
master.risks: Seed risk 0.5: bends only, no whorls.

curl-steered-grain.look: 2D: grain that follows closed streamlines. Whorls, eddies and swept tracts with no seam and even contrast, like Van Gogh skies, Jupiter's bands or smoke. Threshold panel shows bold flame or wood-eye shapes. Wide panel is an even mat of curls with no visible grid; the FFT has the same faint octave rings as the steerable parent. Two potential octaves give many small eddies, one gives a few big bends. Added psi gives dark swirling hollows and bright ridges. Steps=3 becomes folded smoke with some thin dark crack lines. 3D: at iso 0 both vol renders are a torn sponge with some directional streaking, with no clear strands or eddies. The XZ slice is blotchy with one recognisable swirl. The 3D is the weak part, matching what the parent reported about its 3D fibres.
curl-steered-grain.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: curl of three Perlin potentials, check gives range -0.990..0.963, z continuity mean 0.0027, the volume and the volume exist. The 4x4 window has no 3D form, so 3D uses 2x2x2. 4D not built.
curl-steered-grain.range: -1.000..1.000 over 8 seeds after a clamp, mean -0.001, std about 0.25, Gaussian histogram, p1 -0.565 and p99 0.550, so a real node could scale it up. 0 nans.
curl-steered-grain.artifacts: No jump: all default steps shrink, c0ratio 8. eps controls the fallback at critical points of the potential: grain goes isotropic and slightly lumpy at eye centres and saddles. eps=0.02 is steeper (c0ratio 5.81) with no jump. Steps=3 is steep along separatrices (c0ratio 1.84, 0.83 at h=1e-3, shrinking to 0.012) and shows them as thin cracks. FFT rings are the lacunarity 2 banding known from the parent.
curl-steered-grain.node_shape: As a direction mode inside SteerablePerlin: Direction Source enum {Hybrid, CurlOfPerlin}, Potential Scale, Potential Octaves, Potential Gain, eps, optional Steps. Existing Aspect, Octaves, Lacunarity, Envelope Normalise, Window 2x2/4x4.
curl-steered-grain.port_notes: Why merged: in 2D this is steerable-perlin's existing dir=2 contour mode, d = (-g.y, g.x), which the parent's proto already has, with a second potential octave added, seen side by side. The new ideas are the second octave, 3D curl and Steps, and they all belong as members of that node. It is still worth building: a hybrid direction cannot provide a gradient without D+1 extra evaluations (the parent's notes say this), and this is the best-looking default for that node so far. Normalise uses one sqrt. The anisotropy weight is l2 / (l2 + eps^2 F^2) and needs no extra branch.

master.one_liner: Steerable grain whose direction is the curl of an analytic Perlin potential: closed streamlines with no Euler stepping.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: grain following eddies, whorls and smoke, with even contrast because the kernel stays undistorted.
master.algorithm: 1) psi, g = perlin gradient at p * PotentialScale (analytic derivative, as perlin2h provides). 2) direction d = (-g.y, g.x) normalised with a floor: d = (-g.y, g.x) * InvSqrt(|g|^2 + eps^2); where |g| is tiny the kernel falls back to the isotropic case automatically because the steerable kernel's anisotropy matrix is G = I + (Aspect-1) d d^T weighted by |g|/sqrt(|g|^2+eps^2). 3) Evaluate the steerable lattice kernel (2x2 corners in 2D, 2^D generally) with per-lane G exactly as steerable-perlin does, Octaves times with lacunarity; direction field shared across octaves. 4) Optional Steps int: before step 1, advance p by Steps small curl steps (the DomainWarpCurl loop) so the grain also folds; Steps=0 default. 5) Envelope normalise per octave (envn=1 discovery). 3D: d = curl of a 3-component Perlin potential, kernel anisotropy about the unit curl vector. Cost estimate: one perlin gradient (about 1.5x Perlin) plus steerable octaves; not measured.
master.why_new:
Steerable's per-lane angle is its whole value, and the downslope-flutes discovery already showed a gradient-of-Perlin direction works. Taking the direction from the curl of an analytic Perlin potential gives grain that follows closed streamlines (eddies, whorls, smoke) without any Euler stepping, at the price of one perlin-with-gradient evaluation. Different from warping steerable: the kernel stays undistorted so contrast stays even.
Seed gap: whorled grain without Euler steps.
master.simd_plan: Cost estimate: one perlin gradient (about 1.5x Perlin) plus steerable octaves; not measured.
master.continuity: Not stated by the panel.
master.params: Potential Scale, eps, Aspect, Octaves, Lacunarity, Steps (int, default 0), Envelope Normalise.
master.risks: Seed risk 0.25: singular points need the fallback.
