domain-warp-knot-flow.look: Default checker through the warp: the textbook flow past cylinders. Squares crowd and curve around each knot, with concentric bullseye rings inside, a strong technical drawing look. Stretched white or black patches sit at the stagnation points, where the map's scale goes to zero. Twill through the warp: threads bend around oval buttons with over-under still readable everywhere, next to the simplex control where the same twill is shredded into blobs and scrawl. Bricks: courses part and rejoin around knots with mortar lines staying connected, though with a tear-drop lens shape in the knot and a messy black tear at the lower left where two knots overlap. Stripes with a slow pre-warp reproduce KnotFlow's grain lines hugging ringed knots, smooth as flowing lines. 3D strata: flat layers that bulge and open around concretions, with holes; a bit flat since few spheres hit the view. Measured local anisotropy s1/s2 of the map by central differences: default median 1.18, p75 2.36, 49 percent of the plane under 1.15. The entry's window (band=0): median 1.41, 25 percent under 1.15. Simplex warp at amplitude 0.25: median 3.0, p75 6.1, 1.3 percent under 1.15. Weaker simplex warp at 0.12: median 1.7, p75 2.2, 4.1 percent. Rings interior is singular by design and is the top decile of the default.
domain-warp-knot-flow.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: Stokes flow past a sphere, check gives z continuity mean 0.0004 with stripes, the volume shows strata. 4D measured on an oblique plane by slice4=1: runs and C0 (c0ratio 7.92), 3^4 window. 4D uses the same doublet rule with exponent 4 and is a heuristic, not derived. Only a few knots cross the plane at this density.
domain-warp-knot-flow.range: the source's range, -1..1 over 8 seeds, 0 nans. Default checker std 0.92. A warp does not itself normalise.
domain-warp-knot-flow.artifacts: Entry's Flat mode has a real jump of 2.0 at the rim, and Polar a real jump of 2.0 (0.88 at h=1e-5 on a sample path), from the rim mismatch and the angle wrap. Both are kept as modes 2 and 3 for the record, not as defaults. Rings and Lens are C0. Fade band still shears a little, seen as gently skewed squares around each knot; band=0.7 cuts it. Sum of doublets is only approximate where influence discs overlap, which gives torn patches at close pairs. Scale goes to zero at the two stagnation points on each rim. A 3D rim slope is infinite by the sqrt, so z continuity for the default checker reads max 0.55 for dz=1e-3 and mean 0.001, a slope. My first 3D interior had a rim phi mismatch found by that same check, now fixed.
domain-warp-knot-flow.node_shape: DomainWarp family: Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Direction (angle, or X/Y/Z), Density (hybrid), Radius Min/Max, Fade, Hold Band, Jitter, Along, Knot Mode {Rings, Lens}, Ring Spacing. Source. Optional sibling generator outputs Speed and Knot mask.
domain-warp-knot-flow.port_notes: Standard Warp node: 3^D hashes, one sqrt and one reciprocal per knot, a few FMAs, two Selects for inside and outside. Density test is a mask, so cost is the worst case. Reach is 1.5 - jitter/2 = 1.1 at jitter 0.8, so fade 1.05 fits. Rings and Lens need no blend band, so there is no extra cost at the rim. In the frame t = -ny x + nx y, n = nx x + ny y; rotate the displacement back to world axes in Warp().

master.one_liner: KnotFlow's potential-flow doublets as a DomainWarp: the displacement is the exact (phi, psi) deflection of flow past scattered obstacles, so any source (Textile, TileDomain courses, stripes, checker) bends around the knots conformally, and the knot interiors get their own ring, polar or flat frame.
master.look: Whatever the source draws, flowing around round inclusions as water flows past posts. Textile twill as source: cloth or wire mesh bending around buttons and rivets, with threads crowding at the sides of each knot and opening at the stagnation points, over-under intact because the map is locally a similarity. TileDomain courses: brickwork or parquet parting around pillars. Checkerboard: the textbook conformal grid of flow past cylinders, a strong technical-drawing look. Oscillator stripes reproduce KnotFlow. In 3D with sheets of noise: strata draped around concretions.
master.algorithm: Grain frame as in t_knot_flow: rotate by Dir so t runs along the grain and n across; optional pre-warp of n by a slow source (KnotFlow's warp member). Scatter knots on the 3^D window of the (t,n[,b]) lattice with Density, Jitter, radius R in [Rmin,Rmax], fade radius Fade, w(r) = 1 - smoothstep(R, Fade, r), q = R/r. Outside a knot (r > R) in 2D the complex potential of uniform flow past a cylinder gives phi = t + dt*q^2, psi = n - dn*q^2 (KnotFlow already computes the psi part as outside = pn + dn*(1-q^2)); accumulate dphi += w*dt*q^2, dpsi += w*(-dn*q^2) over knots, exactly the sum KnotFlow does for psi plus one FMA for phi. 3D (sphere): dphi += w*dt*q^3/2 and the cross-stream pair (dn, db) scaled by sqrt(1-q^3) - 1 (Stokes stream function psi = rho^2 (1 - q^3)/2 gives the upstream radius rho_inf = rho*sqrt(1-q^3), azimuth conserved). Inside a knot (r < R), Knot Mode: Rings: phi = pt, psi = pn + K*(R - r) (KnotFlow's rings); Polar: phi = pt + R*ang(u)/pi with ang from fastAtan2 or the octant-free approximation, psi as Rings; Flat: (phi, psi) = (pt, pn) + (dt, dn) (the source shows an undeflected disc, a button or rivet). The inside branch is a Select, blended by w which is 1 inside. Warp() adds (dphi, dpsi[, db]) rotated back into world axes to the position, then the Source is evaluated once. Extra scalar outputs for a sibling generator form if wanted: Speed = |grad phi| from the analytic derivative (stagnation points dark), Knot mask.
master.why_new: KnotFlow (keeper) outputs only its own stripes of psi; it has no phi coordinate and no Source, so nothing but stripes can bend around its knots. The existing warps cannot make a doublet: DomainWarpSimplex/Gradient smear, DomainWarpCurl and VortexCells give vortices, ScatterWarp (ship-as-mode) lists sources, sinks, vortices and pushes but not the doublet with an interior remap, and a general warp is not conformal, which is why the discoveries list says an upstream warp 'shreds the knit' and distorts thread width on Textile. Nearest: ScatterWarp, DomainMobius (conformal but global, no scattered obstacles), KnotFlow.
master.simd_plan: Standard Warp-family node. 3^D window of hashes with a density mask, per active knot one sqrt, one reciprocal, a few FMAs, two Selects for inside/outside; then one Source eval. Estimated AVX2 for the warp alone: 2D 4-6 ns, 3D 12-18 ns, 4D 40-50 ns (the 4D form repeats the 3D rule in the (t, n, b, c) frame with a 3^4 window; KnotFlow's prototype already has EvalC4).
master.continuity: C0 and C1 away from the fade band and knot rims; w fades each term to zero at Fade so knots entering the window cause no jump; the inside/outside switch at r=R is continuous because outside at r=R equals pn (psi) and pt + dt (phi) matches the Flat mode exactly, the Rings and Polar modes match psi but not phi, so those two modes are C0 in psi and jump in phi at the rim unless a thin blend band (R..1.1R) is used; recommend the blend.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Warp Amplitude (hybrid, scales the deflection so 1 is the physical flow), Direction (float angle, 2D) or Direction X/Y/Z, Density (hybrid, read at the knot cell), Radius Min/Max, Fade, Jitter, Along (anisotropy of the lattice along the grain), Knot Mode enum {Rings, Polar, Flat}, Ring Spacing, Source.
master.risks: The window w(r) breaks analyticity in the band R..Fade, so threads are slightly sheared there; with Fade close to R the shear is strong and with Fade near the window limit the band is wide but gentle. Overlapping influence discs of two knots are not an exact two-body flow (sum of doublets is only approximate), which is cosmetic. Polar inside mode needs an angle approximation.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: the entry's 4 to 6 ns in 2D, 12 to 18 ns in 3D, 40 to 50 ns in 4D for the warp alone, plus one source evaluation. Scalar ratio near 1.8x Perlin is consistent with the low end, but the proto skips empty knots with a branch, which a port cannot.

domain-warp-knot-flow.changed_from_entry: 1. The entry says outside at r = R equals pt + dt in phi and pn in psi, matching Flat exactly. It does not: phi = pt + 2 dt and psi = pn at the rim, so Flat jumps by 2.0 in the checker. Replaced with Lens: phi = t + dt (r/R)^2, psi = n - dn (r/R)^2, C0 by construction, the outside map mirrored. 2. Rings gets a phi that reaches the rim value (pt + 2 dt (r/R)^4), so no blend band is needed. 3. Added Hold Band: w = 1 - smoothstep( R + band (fade - R), fade, r ), default 0.7, because the entry's window starting at R shears over a wide band. Entry's form is band=0. 4. 3D interior mirrors the outside in the same way. Polar still has the angle seam the entry warned of.

flow-beads.look: On one still it is just scattered round domes of mixed size, some in short chains, close to StampScatter. A few beads are slightly pear shaped or pointed at the steepest parts of the flow. The rest of the case needs frames. In the image the top row's discs stay round from frame to frame, with new ones growing and old ones shrinking, while the warp control's discs flatten into ellipses and streaks. An overlay of 28 frames of one cohort, shows beads following long smooth curved paths and closing around two eddies, each path an even width dash of connected discs. The warp control's overlay has the same paths but with flaring, fan shaped and uneven streaks, and one sheared flare at the bottom. Measured blob aspect, isolated beads at R=0.08: median 1.045, p90 1.135 at U=3; median 1.046, p90 1.198 at U=6. Warp control: median 2.199, p90 4.055 at U=3; median 3.699, p90 9.638 at U=6. Exact loop: frame t=0.37 against t=1.37 has max gray difference 0 at 512 px. With loop=0 it has mean gray difference 44.7. Ring kernel looks like soap bubbles, slightly deformed in places. Source kernel gives lumpy rounded plates, blobby rather than ice-like. 3D vol: separate round balls, with a few teardrop or cone shapes where J varies strongly within a ball. FFT is broad and shows no lattice.
flow-beads.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: same mechanism with analytic 3x3 J, check gives z continuity mean 0.0011 max 0.163 for dz=1e-3, the volume shows the solids. 4D not built.
flow-beads.range: -1.000..1.000 over 8 seeds, mean -0.629 (mostly background at -1), 0 nans. 3D -1.000..0.998.
flow-beads.artifacts: The entry's exact carry has real jumps: at U=3 the step stays 1.18 down to h=1e-5, from beads clipped where the owning site changes in material space. Its requirement (bead footprint inside the Voronoi cell) holds only near U=1 with small beads. The first order window carry has no jump up to U=6: all steps shrink, roughly as sqrt(h) from the sqrt dome edge. Price of first order: where the flow curves within a bead, a bead turns pear shaped or pointed; visible in the sheet and vol. Window shrink reduces a bead per lane where strain would overflow the window, so radius varies a little across such a bead. Beads pass through each other with no collisions; Max merges overlaps, and the dome sqrt gives a steep edge (max slope 563 per unit). Cohort rhythm: I saw no pulse in the six frames, but six stills cannot prove that. 3D was probed only by z continuity, since jumps scans Eval2.
flow-beads.node_shape: Time (hybrid), Period T, Loop bool, Cohorts M (int), Flow Cycles K (int), Flow Amplitude U, Flow Frequency F, Feature Scale, Radius R, Radius Variation, Jitter, Birth Offset, Kernel enum {Dome, Ring, Source}, Source. Flow is internal; a real node could take a DomainWarpShear chain.
flow-beads.port_notes: Each shear is one 1D noise with an analytic derivative, so J is 4 FMAs per step in 2D and needs no matrix store beyond the 2x2. Inverse is the same steps reversed with opposite sign; det J = 1, so sigma_max(J^-1) = sigma_max(J) and the window shrink needs only the 2D closed form. Age, tau and dt are per cohort and depend only on t and T when those are constants; a hybrid Time makes them per lane with no change. Envelope reaches 0 at both ends of a life, so the age wrap cannot pop. With loop=1 the hash has no generation term, so the period is exact. Relies on the same first order idea as advected-scatter, with a chain whose Jacobian is free.

master.one_liner: Features carried by a flow that stay rigid: map the sample back along an invertible steady flow to find a site, carry the site forward, and measure a true distance from where it now is. Discs stay discs along curved paths, individually born and dying, with an exact time loop.
master.look: River foam, ash, snow, plankton, leaves, embers: round things moving together along curved paths, swirling round eddies, staying round. Each grows from nothing and shrinks to nothing on its own schedule. With dense plate shapes as Source, it could give drifting ice floes. In 3D: spheres drifting in a shared current, no streaks. Judge from stills: a strip of 6 frames. Bead aspect ratio must stay 1 and centres must move consistently with neighbours; compare to the same discs under DomainWarpFlow, which become streaks by the third frame. Frame 0 equals frame T in loop mode.
master.algorithm:
Flow: a steady Strang split of shear steps, as in DomainWarpShear: V is the sum over j of u_j*n_j(dot(x,t_j)*F); Phi(x, tau) applies K cycles with step tau/K, exact inverse by reversing the order and sign.
M cohorts (default 3). Per cohort m:
  age = fract(t/T + m/M)      // t is a hybrid
  tau = age*T
  q = Phi^-1(p, tau)          // material position of the sample at birth
  site search in the 3^D window around q on a seed per m: nearest site c, hash h; or hard-core thinning for a guaranteed spacing
  gen = Loop ? 0 : floor(t/T + m/M)   // mix gen into h for endless variety
  x = Phi(c, tau)             // where that particle is now
  e = Env(age - dh*rnd(h))    // radius envelope, sin^0.5 of age, per particle offset dh so cohorts do not pulse
  r = R*(0.6 + 0.8*rnd(h,2))*e
  d = |p - x|/Max(r, eps)
  out = Combine(out, Kernel(d))   // Max dome, or Source eval in the local frame (p - x)/r rotated by hash spin
Requirement: R*stretch(T) < half the minimum material spacing, so at the point where the nearest site changes, the kernel is already 0. stretch(T) is a measured constant for the flow.
Exact loop: with Loop on, age and h are periodic in t with period T for every lane, so frame 0 and frame T match exactly.
master.why_new: Warps move the domain, so features stretch without limit, and flow maps hide this with a global cross-fade pulse. LavaColumns and OrbitBlobs move rigid features, but on integer scroll or private Lissajous paths with no shared flow. StampScatter does not move. Here the shape is rigid and the path comes from a real shared field.
master.simd_plan: Per cohort: K*D shear evals back (1D noise, about 0.3 to 0.5 ns each), a 3^D window, and K*D forward from one site. 2D, M=3, K=3: 54 shear evals plus 3 windows, about 30 to 35 ns (estimate). 3D about 60 to 80 ns. Cost is independent of Time. 4D possible but 3^4 is poor; use a 2 site simplex window if needed.
master.continuity: C0 under the spacing requirement, since each kernel reaches 0 before the owner changes. C1 in time with a sin^0.5 envelope replaced by a smooth one, except at birth. Violations show as clipped discs in high strain, a measurable failure.
master.params: Feature Scale (site spacing), R, Cohorts M, Flow Steps K, Flow Amplitude, Flow Frequency, T, Loop, Kernel enum (Dome, Ring, Source). Hybrid: Time; Source member in Source kernel mode.
master.risks: Cost. Strain limits flow strength against bead size. Cohort rhythm may be visible despite offsets. Overlaps between beads have no collisions, so dense fields read as passing through each other.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: per cohort 6 shears back, 6 forward with J, 9 window sites: about 10 ns, so about 30 ns at 3 cohorts in 2D, as the entry's 30 to 35. 3D about 100 ns with 16 Perlin shears and 27 sites per cohort, above the entry's 60 to 80 because the 3D shears use a 2D Perlin slice.

flow-beads.changed_from_entry: Added carry=1 and made it the default, since the entry's exact nearest-site carry clips beads from about U=2. It measures all 9 window sites through a first order map x - p = J ( c - q ) rather than running the chain forward from one, costing about 1.9x the exact form but removing the entry's strain limit. Beads are rigid to first order rather than exactly. Exact carry is kept as carry=0. J = 3 shear directions per cycle at K = 2, 6 evaluations each way, instead of K*D. Radius clamp per lane added for window safety. 3D shears use a 2D Perlin slice so the flow is not sheets.

At the entry's sy=0.4 the same channels stand up into mostly vertical columns and arches, so the entry's value gives shafts, not galleries. Rock view zoomed to window 1.6, seeds 1337 and 7: lens and teardrop holes on the cut faces, a few long gashes where a tunnel runs close to the face. The floor is hard to see in these views: side by side at thumb size, the vertical slice with the floor (F=0.55) and without it (F=1.5) look almost the same. The effect is real in the measure below but it is not a striking look.

walkable-worms.range: Measured over 8 seeds: -0.712 to 1.000. Rock positive, 0 at the wall, clamped at +1 in the rock. The floor keeps it from reaching -1 in the air.
walkable-worms.artifacts: Steep slopes at near parallel gradients: maxSlope 922 per unit (straddled 1465), which is why c0ratio reads 1.7 and 1.05 while jumps shrinks 10x per step. No jump found. Slope scales about as 1/L (L=0.4 gives c0ratio 6.3) but L=0.3 fills the tangle with webs and hairline dust (seen), so L stays low. sy>1 makes the two gradients more parallel and so makes lens flakes more common: flat flakes remain visible. The entry's Select on min |r| has a real theoretical jump at junctions because r.y differs between pairs: at L=0.02, h=1e-4 it read 0.28074 against 0.20557 for per pair Min, h=1e-5 0.02735 against 0.02045, both shrinking with h, so this probe did not catch a jump in either form.

walkable-worms.port_notes: No window, no per lane control flow beyond Min. Network adds nothing beyond TubeNoise's three 2x2 solves, except that r needs its y component kept and each pair has one extra Max with smoothing. r.y = J[0][1] * l0 + J[1][1] * l1, and |r|^2 = n^T lambda - L lambda^T lambda, so the length can reuse the solve.

master.algorithm: One Perlin lattice visit as in TubeNoise: channels n0,n1,n2 with gradients g0,g1,g2 and the per-vertex value term. Apply a fixed Y squash sy (about 0.4) to the input, and multiply g.y by sy by chain rule so results are in world units. For each of the 3 fixed channel pairs: A = J J^T + Damping*I (2x2), lambda = A^-1 n, r = J^T lambda, the first-order vector from curve to sample. Keep the r with min |r| using Select. sd = SmoothMax( |r| - R, -r.y - F*R, k ), giving a round roof and a flat floor F*R below the axis. Steep axes have r perpendicular to the axis, so r.y stays near 0 and the floor does not cut: shafts stay round. Output Clamp( sd / R ). No window, no per-lane control flow. 4D uses the same algebra with a 4 component r. Cost estimate: network 5-7.5 ns 3D (tournament estimate) plus about 0.3 ns. Inherits the flat lens flakes.
master.why_new:
Tube-noise has the best cave section here and strata-caverns has the only floors you can walk on. A round worm tangle is a fall-through hazard in a voxel game. TubeNoise already computes the offset vector to the axis, so a flat floor costs almost nothing. Not built or rendered: untested idea.

master.one_liner: Tube-noise tunnels confined to bedding planes by using a sawtooth of a warped depth coordinate as one channel: limestone galleries along layers, linked by short cross-cuts.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: karst-style galleries that run laterally along layers and connect through short cross-cuts.
master.algorithm: Two channels as in tube-noise Network mode: n0 = Perlin(seed, x, y, z) and n1 = Saw(y' / Thickness) - 0.5 where y' = y + Dip.x * x + Dip.y * z + Fold * Perlin(seed+1, x * ff, z * ff) (the bedding warp) and Saw is a sawtooth with hashed per-layer thickness from Floor(y'/Thickness). Tube distance d = sqrt(n0^2 + n1^2) / sqrt(|grad n0|^2 |grad n1|^2 - (grad n0 . grad n1)^2)^(1/2) exactly as tube-noise estimates distance to the intersection curve, with the gradients from the derivative Perlin kernel and the analytic saw gradient. Output 1 - d / Radius. Add a third channel n2 = Perlin(seed+2) and take the Min over pairs (tube-noise Network rule) for cross-cuts between layers. Cost about tube-noise Network plus one cheap analytic channel (estimate 5-8 ns 3D).
master.why_new:
tube-noise gives round worm tunnels but no stratigraphy; strata-caverns gives flat-floored galleries but is a graph recipe. Tubes constrained to bedding planes give limestone-style galleries that run laterally along layers and connect through short cross-cuts, which is the actual look of karst.
Seed gap: walkable floors on round tunnels.
Split from seed cluster WalkableWorms / BeddingTubes: see walkable-worms.

master.risks:
Seed risk 0.25: inherits lens flakes; floor cut may clip junctions.
Noticed in merge: with hashed per-layer thickness |grad n1| changes across a layer boundary, so d can jump there unless Radius is small enough for the output to be clamped at the boundary. n1 itself is safe, since n1^2 is equal on both sides of the sawtooth. The denominator goes to zero where grad n0 is parallel to the bedding normal, the usual lens flakes.

layer_jump_check.question: Flagged by the merge: hashed layer thickness may make d jump at layer boundaries.
layer_jump_check.answer: The jump is real in the entry's saw form, and the fix removes it. It is also wider than flagged: the true Gauss-Newton d on a saw jumps even at uniform thickness.
layer_jump_check.why_jumps_alone_is_not_enough: `jumps` straddles lattice lines at integers, halves and quarters, and hashed boundaries lie anywhere. So t_bedding_tubes_meas also finds each boundary along 6000 random columns by bisection and reads the output on both sides, at T=1.3, f=0.45, J=0.7 or 0, third=0.
layer_jump_check.bisection_entry_form_1_J0.7: 37744 crossings. R=0.13: none over 0.01, all clamped. R=0.2: none. R=0.3: 1798 over 0.01, 1216 over 0.1, worst 0.5708. R=0.45: 16890 over 0.01, 11589 over 0.1, worst 0.5715.
layer_jump_check.bisection_entry_form_1_J0: 37397 crossings: no jump over 0.01 at any R tested, so the merge note is right that this form is safe at uniform thickness.
layer_jump_check.bisection_gauss_newton_saw_form_2_J0: R=0.3: 1 over 0.01, worst 0.0115. R=0.45: 24453 over 0.01, 19781 over 0.1, worst 0.6705. Cause: the cross term 2 b n0 n1 flips sign when n1 goes from +0.5 to -0.5.
layer_jump_check.bisection_fix_form_0: R=0.13, 0.2, 0.3, 0.45, each at old layer boundaries (37733) and at its own window lines (37397), plus third and riser form at window lines: zero over 0.01, worst prints 0.0000. At R=0.45, 24196 of the crossings were unclamped, so the clamp is not what hides it.
layer_jump_check.fix: Stop using a saw. n1 = y' - m_c in world units, one candidate per gallery plane, Min over the 4 planes around the sample. grad n1 is the same for every candidate, so a, b, e, det are shared and a candidate costs 3 multiplies plus a sqrt. Each candidate is continuous, so the Min is C0 except where a plane leaving the window would still be the nearest and inside the clamp. That needs near parallel gradients and no such crossing was found in the counts above; it is not proved impossible.

master.one_liner: Tube-noise channels evaluated with steerable-perlin's per-lane elliptical kernel, so tunnels follow a field.

master.algorithm: Per lane: direction unit vector u from a hybrid Direction input (constant, source, or gradient of a source via 3 taps). Build the per-lane metric G = I + (aniso - 1) u u^T. Evaluate the two (Network: three) tube channels n_i as steerable-perlin octaves: at each of the 2^D corners the kernel offset is G (p - corner), with the per-vertex value term from tube-noise so channels do not share zeros. Distance d = sqrt(sum n_i^2) / max(|grad n|, eps) using the analytic corner gradients steerable-perlin already carries, then tube-noise's radius/network logic unchanged. Single lattice visit per channel, no window, 2D/3D/4D by the GenT path. Cost estimate: tube-noise cost x ~1.3 for the metric multiply, plus the Direction eval.
master.why_new:
Tube-noise worms are isotropic; lava tubes, roots and burrows follow a field (down-slope, down gravity, along bedding). Steerable-perlin proves an elliptical per-lane kernel costs little and needs no window.

master.one_liner: A bundle of never-crossing uniform wires in 3D from any two noises: a jittered lattice in (A,B) value space, pulled back to world units by Gauss-Newton, so hair, rope, roots and muscle cost a 3x3 window in every dimension.
master.look: Dense combed wires that flow with the fields, partings where channels go flat, clumps where they steepen, hairpin turns at folds of the map. Reads as hair, wire brush, root mats, muscle fibre, kelp. The prototype's fixed Milnor map already shows this quality of wire; I have not seen it on noise channels.
master.algorithm:
SHARED CAUSE. Knot fibre bundle, Hopf-link and cinquefoil bundles, TubeRope and TubePipe are all fibres of a map f: R^n -> R^2. The knot family only looked special because f was a Milnor map. Fibres of any map are disjoint by definition, so wires cannot cross. TubeNoise renders only the one fibre f = 0. Worley on the f plane renders a whole family.

f = K*(n0(p), n1(p)) + offset, with n0, n1 two channels of one Perlin visit including the value term, or two Sources by finite differences.
A = g0.g0, B = g0.g1, C = g1.g1    // J J^T
det = A*C - B*B + 1e-3*(A+C)^2     // the prototype's scale-free floor
sigmaMax2 = 0.5*(A + C + sqrt((A-C)^2 + 4*B*B))
Reff = min(Radius, KeepApart/(K*sqrt(sigmaMax2)))   // wires thin where they crowd; also what keeps the chart window sufficient
for each of the 9 lattice cells c around floor(f):
  site = c + 0.5 + Jitter*(hashvec(c) - 0.5); e = (site - f)/K
  d2 = (C*e0^2 - 2*B*e0*e1 + A*e1^2)/det
  keep min d2 with its c and e (Select), drop by hash against hybrid Coverage
d = sqrt(d2)
Outputs: Wire = 1 - d/(Reff*radiusJitter(hash)); Distance; Pipe = 1 - |d - Reff|/Wall; Rope = Wire with Reff*(1 + Rib*cos(n*theta + Twist*tau)), cos(n theta) by complex power of normalised (e0,e1), tau = position along Axis. Cable = run the same 9 cell search again on (f - site)*SubK, so each wire is made of wires that wind round its axis as the chart rotates. Strand Id.
Generalises by Codim: 1 channel, 3 candidates: parallel sheets of constant world thickness (contour lines in 2D). 2 channels, 9 candidates: wires. 3 channels, 27 candidates: beads. In 2D with 2 channels the result is round dots of constant size whose layout follows a warp, which is the fix for warped dots smearing.
master.why_new: Different output and hard made easy. TubeNoise gives one curve family at one level. root-strands needs a lattice of bonds and looks vertical. FiberNoise and StreakScatter are short window-limited capsules; these wires are unbounded in length and the window is in value space, so it stays 3x3 in 3D and 4D where a cubic window would be 27 and 81. RootStrands' critic found no real graph rival in this territory.
master.simd_plan: One multi-channel ValueGrad visit, then 9 candidates of hash + 3 multiplies in fixed loops with Select. Sqrt once. Estimates AVX2: 2D 9 ns, 3D 14 ns, 4D 22 ns; Cable adds about 6 ns. 2D/3D/4D are the same code via the parameter pack, since only J's height changes.
master.continuity: C0: min of continuous functions over the window, as the prototype's comment argues, given Keep Apart so the nearest site stays inside the 3x3 chart window. Without Keep Apart a seam can appear only where wires already overlap.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, int Codim (2), Output enum, K (strands per unit channel value), Jitter, Keep Apart, Rib, int Ribs, Twist, Sub K, Axis enum. Hybrid: Radius, Coverage. Optional hybrid Sources A, B; built-in Perlin when unset.
master.risks: Wire density varies by maybe 5 to 10 times with |J|, and that may read as blotchy rather than as clumps. Wires are hidden in a 2D slice, so the 2D sheet will undersell it. Flat flakes near rank-deficient J, as TubeNoise warns. Hybrid Radius near zero leaves hairlines.

master.one_liner: Canyons and vadose passages whose overhang is placed by geomorphology: the channel centre shifts toward the outer bank with depth, in proportion to plan curvature, so outer bends are undercut, inner bends get slip-off slopes, and the asymmetry flips at each inflection.
master.look: 3D: Goosenecks or Horseshoe Bend. Cut faces show the section lean one way on one bend and flip on the next, cliffs hanging over the river on outer banks, stepped gentle spurs on inner banks. Straight reaches have vertical walls. With Roof: keyhole cave passages that swing from side to side with depth, which in caves is called meander niching; Flute makes horizontal ledges running along the walls. Judge from stills: vol at a bend and at an inflection, with cut faces; plot wall lean against the measured curvature.
master.algorithm:
Plan source g(x,z), smooth 2D. Stencil radius h near the channel width.
g0, gx, gz, lap from 5 taps at (x +- h, z), (x, z +- h), centre. G = sqrt(gx^2 + gz^2 + e^2)
d = g0/G   // signed plan distance to the zero contour
kappa = lap/G   // level set curvature, normal second derivative ignored; a 9 tap option uses the exact form (gxx*gz^2 - 2*gx*gz*gxz + gzz*gx^2)/G^3
ks = kappa/(1 + Rmin*|kappa|)   // soft clamp
zd = sat((Rim(x,z) - y)/D)   // 0 at the rim, 1 at the floor. Rim is hybrid
delta = Lean*ks*D*zd^p + Flute*n1(y*fy)*w0   // move the channel along +normal with depth: on a circle g = |x| - R, kappa = 1/R > 0 and +normal is outward
w = w0*(1 - zd)^q + w1   // V, U or slot width profile
a = |d - delta| - w
v = SmoothMax(a, (Rim - D) - y, k)   // floor
Closed passage (Roof > 0): b = sqrt(d^2 + (y - Rim)^2) - Rt; v = SmoothMin(SmoothMax(v, y - Rim, k), b, k), so a round phreatic tube sits on the slot: a keyhole section.
Output is rock positive; a terrain graph uses Min(terrain, v), or passes it as Rock.
master.why_new: TubeNoise Canyons is symmetric with vertical walls everywhere. FiskMeanders handles plan only. BeddingTubes and WalkableWorms (crossbreed 6) have a round section with a flat floor. Random overhangs are easy; overhangs whose place follows from the plan shape are not, and no node here uses curvature to move material. A y-only warp over a TubeNoise canyon gives a slot canyon, which is a nice recipe, but every wall leans the same way, so it cannot flip at inflections.
master.simd_plan: 5 or 9 Plan evals in x,z (the plan does not depend on y, so no extra cost for the 3D form), plus 1 Rim, plus a few ops. 2 octave plan, 5 taps: about 12 ns (estimate, 2D Perlin 1.1 ns). 2D form is a heightfield with the lean term applied as an asymmetric section (no overhang). 4D passes w to the plan.
master.continuity: C0. |d| is exact only near the zero contour, and d is bounded by the e term at critical points, where the channel is not. Gradient bound: |grad(d - delta)| is 1 + Lean*D*|grad ks| near the channel, and is a reason to keep Plan smooth.
master.params: Plan Source, Sample Distance h, Rim (hybrid), Depth D, Lean, p, Width w0, Slot w1, q, Rmin, Flute, fy, Roof, Rt, Curvature Stencil (5 or 9).
master.risks: Curvature estimate is noisy on rough plans. Sharp bends where Rmin clamps look kinked. Loops of contour: oxbow moats. Junctions are absent, it is a single contour channel, and a saddle crossing gives a messy pinch.

surface-flutes.look: Cave density with flutes: the smooth Perlin walls become hung with long parallel vertical flutes that run down the wall and turn with it, like flowstone or curtain limestone, on walls that overhang and on walls that slope. Flat cut tops of holes stay smooth. This was the entry's unbuilt claim and it holds. Compared with the bare surface in a side by side, the surface reads as geological. In the first attempt at ff=5 and sf=3, flutes were lumps, and read as bark or shredded texture; the fix was long stripes per lattice cell. Ridged at ff=16 is sharper and more torn. Two octaves with branching were busier and more shredded, so one octave is the default. Form 0 (steerable sheets) at low strength: subtle soft vertical grain, clean and gentle. Terrain solid (dy=0.9): gullies radiate down every slope, reads as badlands. 2D sheet: star bursts of radial gullies around each peak and pit, reads a bit like palm fronds in the hillshade and feathered edges at the threshold, with a stronger star pattern than a real drainage network.
surface-flutes.dims: 2D: heightfield, flutes run down S's slope, c0ratio 1.985. 3D: real, flutes on caves and overhangs, z-continuity mean 0.0008, max 0.0112 for dz=1e-3. 4D: not built. The prototype has no 4D form; the algebra needs a cross product, so a 4D form would fix w and drop out of tiling, as the entry already says.
surface-flutes.range: Not normalised: it is a density plus a displacement. Measured over 8 seeds in 2D: -1.917 to 1.984, 3D slice -1.314 to 0.904, with built-in gs=2.2. A node's range is its Density's plus or minus Strength.
surface-flutes.artifacts: Steep slope, c0ratio about 2, where |Z| is small at phasor dislocations: raising eps to 0.3 moves c0ratio on the slice to 4.0 but softens stripes. Saw teeth where flutes meet a flat cut, as on the ring at the top of vol; some of the staircase on vol is the renderer's march step. Near the flat parts where L fades, direction changes fast and flutes break up. Rough source lowers c0ratio, the entry's listed risk; rough source not viewed. The 2D star bursts are a signature that can look unnatural over a wide area. No per lane early out, so it should run only near a surface in an engine.

surface-flutes.port_notes: 4 Source taps by the tetrahedron stencil give S and g together. Per lane: one rsqrt for n, cross product and rsqrt for b. Then 8 corners of hash, jitter free phase, sin and cos, with a fixed loop. One sqrt for |Z|. Branch free. Phase is f (p - c) . b, so b must stay continuous, which the L mask guarantees for the output though not for b itself: Strength goes to 0 where L is below slo.

master.algorithm:
FORM SurfaceFlutes (3D erosion) (voxel-engineer lens): Density S, solid above 0. Tetra jet: 4 Source taps at stencil h near the flute wavelength, exact-step divisor. g = grad S, n = g*InvSqrt(g.g), t = down - n*dot(n,down), L = |t|, surface distance s = S*InvSqrt(g.g). Thin direction b = normalize(cross(n,t)). Fixed loop over O octaves (default 2): run one steerable-perlin octave in Sheets topology with d = b, using G v = e1 v + (e0-e1)(d.v)d per corner; sign of d does not matter because d appears twice. Take a ridged value and analytic gradient from the same corner sum. Add that gradient to g scaled by the octave amplitude, then recompute t and b for the next octave: that is the erosion filter's branching rule. Output S + Strength * smoothstep(Band,0,|s|) * smoothstep(0.1,0.4,L) * sum(gain^i * v_i). The L term fades flat tops and ceilings, where t is undefined, so it stays C0 there. Cost estimate: 4*Source + 2*2.89 ns (hand kernel, 3D) + about 1 ns; about 30 ns on a 3-octave Perlin density. No per-lane early out, so the engine should run it only in surface-band chunks. 4D steerable has a timing kernel only. Risk: 3D sheet aspect is about 3.3, so flutes may read short.

FORM FlutedCave (artist-material lens): s0 = Density(p), plus D forward differences for g (4 evals in 3D). n = g*InvSqrt(dot(g,g) + eps). With gravity axis a: t = a - dot(a,n)*n; tl = |t|; b = cross(t,n)/Max(tl,eps), the across-slope axis. Constant octave loop (2): 3x3x3 cell window; for each cell, hash gives jittered point c_j; w_j = Max(0, 1 - |p-c_j|^2/R^2)^3, with R inside the window reach; psi_j = f*dot(p-c_j, b); Z += w_j*(cos psi_j, sin psi_j). stripe = Re(Z)/sqrt(|Z|^2 + eps). out = s0 + A*saturate(tl/0.3)*saturate(|g|*k)*stripe. The tl mask removes flutes on floors and ceilings, where direction is undefined. 2D reduces to the ordinary ErosionFilter path. 4D's 81 cells are not affordable, so 4D drops w and does not tile. Cost ESTIMATE from the reported stripe kernel of about 8.1 ns per octave on 9 cells: about 24 ns per octave on 27 cells, so about 50 ns plus 4 Density evals. Risk: gradient noise on rough density shreds b, so it needs a smooth input.
master.why_new:
SurfaceFlutes (3D erosion): The biggest hole for a voxel world: every terrain winner is a heightfield, and raw erosion in 3D is vertical extrusion. This puts downhill flutes on any isosurface, including overhangs and cave walls. Not built or rendered: untested idea.
FlutedCave: The erosion filter transforms terrain but nobody ran it on a volume in my images. Flutes running down cave walls and flowstone would make noise caves look geological. Not built, look unverified.
Seed gap: voxel lens hole B: every terrain winner is a heightfield.

FlutedCave: Cost ESTIMATE from the reported stripe kernel of about 8.1 ns per octave on 9 cells: about 24 ns per octave on 27 cells, so about 50 ns plus 4 Density evals.

SurfaceFlutes (3D erosion): The L term fades flat tops and ceilings, where t is undefined, so it stays C0 there.
FlutedCave: Not stated by the panel.

director-disclination.look: Stripes, m=1, corners: a zebra or fingerprint of long even stripes that flow with the field, meeting at three-way deltas and turning round defect points in loops, and it reads as a fingerprint or a tiger. Side by side on the same A, B, m=2 gives a different picture: spirals, whirls and fans converging on one point, which is the integer charge family that the other nodes make. The difference is clear at a glance. Schlieren, m=1: dark curving lines, two meeting per point. m=2: cross shapes with four lines per point: the textbook signature. Faint straight seams at lattice cells show in 2D stripes at corners. Simplex layout removes those but the stripes break into short dashes like scales, so it is worse in 2D. Lines output: thin broken wandering lines, less attractive than stripes. Grain: soft blobby flow, lower contrast; the m=2 row shows a straight horizontal seam. 3D stripes: lamellae that bend through the volume in coherent stacked sheets, turning across the cube, like a smectic liquid crystal or a marbled layered block, striking on cut faces. 3D grain with fibres: random blobs with no readable fibre direction, dull. 3D Core: thin threads and a few thicker curved ones, with some flattened parts, because the gap is not a distance.

Hard to see all the time, but they are lattice aligned. A smudge at some defect cores, where the fade to 0 happens over a small area. Core output's radius is not uniform. 3D eigen solve uses acos in the prototype; a port needs a polynomial.

Sources A, B or built-in; Charge Numerator m (default 1); Stripe Frequency; Lattice Frequency; Eps (core size).
director-disclination.port_notes: Unsigned wave kernel: the phase per corner is F (p - c - r_c) . n with a hashed corner offset r_c in place of a hashed phase. Under n -> -n, Z conjugates, so Re Z and |Z| do not change and no sign logic exists downstream. n needs Select between two half angle forms in 2D. r_c needs 2 or 3 hash bit fields per corner. 2D needs no atan2. Schlieren is a two node recipe, as the entry says.

master.one_liner: Steer stripes or grain by a nematic director (a line field, the Z/2 double cover of a vector field) built from two noises without atan2, so the defects are half-integer: fingerprint loop cores and deltas, which no scalar phase can make; in 3D the principal axis of a random Q-tensor gives disclination lines.
master.look: Stripes that flow and, at +1/2 defects, make a tight U-turn (the loop core of a fingerprint); at -1/2 defects three stripe families meet in a triradius (the delta). Between defects the texture is the usual steered zebra or combed grain. Schlieren alone is the dark-brush texture of a nematic drop under crossed polarisers, soft lobes meeting at two-brush points. In 3D, grain that wraps around disclination loops like the texture of a liquid crystal droplet or twisted wood.
master.algorithm:
2D: A, B sources (or two built-in Perlins). r = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 + eps^2); c2 = A/r; s2 = B/r. These are (cos 2theta, sin 2theta) of the director theta = arg(A+iB)/2, which is never computed: the director tensor N = n n^T = [[1+c2, s2],[s2, 1-c2]]/2 is single valued although n is not.
Steer: evaluate a lattice noise with the anisotropic metric G = I + k(2N - I) = [[1 + k c2, k s2],[k s2, 1 - k c2]], i.e. SteerablePerlin's anisotropy built from (c2, s2) directly rather than from a direction vector's own double angle. Around a zero of (A,B) the pair (c2,s2) winds once, so the director winds half a turn: charge +-1/2.
Charge m/2 in general: apply de Moivre power m to (c2, s2) first (m = 2 gives the integer-charge behaviour of the existing nodes).
Schlieren output (crossed polarisers): I = s2^2 = B^2/(A^2+B^2): dark brushes on B = 0, two brushes per defect, the photographic signature of charge 1/2 (four brushes = charge 1 = (2AB)^2/(A^2+B^2)^2).
Angle output: fastAtan2(B, A)/2 in [-pi/2, pi/2], with a cut, only for feeding nodes that use an angle modulo pi.
Stripes output: the LatticePhasor/steerable stripe kernel driven by N (its per-corner orientation is a line, so it takes N as is).
3D: Q = symmetric traceless 3x3 from five noises (q11, q22, q12, q13, q23; q33 = -q11-q22). l1 = largest eigenvalue (trig form as in EigenStrata); n = normalised cross product of the two longest rows of (Q - l1 I); use only N = n n^T. Disclination lines are where l1 = l2, codimension 2: closed loops and threads of charge 1/2. Steer a 3D lattice noise with G = I + k(3N - I)/2; Schlieren I = 4 (n_x n_y)^2 on the view plane.
4D: a 4x4 Q has no closed-form eigenvector; use the 2D A,B form, which is dimension agnostic because A and B are.
master.why_new: vortex-phase, phasor-noise, lattice-phasor and dislocation-stripes all build stripes from a scalar phase, so their defects are dislocations of integer charge: forks, terminations, spirals, targets. A fingerprint core and a delta are disclinations of the direction field with charge +-1/2, which a scalar phase cannot have at all. steerable-perlin takes an orientation input but derives its line from a vector, so its defects are charge 1 (four brushes). The whole change is to feed (cos 2theta, sin 2theta) = (A,B)/|(A,B)| instead of doubling a vector's angle, plus the 3D Q-tensor eigenvector where the vector trick does not exist. The schlieren texture itself is a two-node graph (Divide(B*B, A*A+B*B)) and should be listed as a recipe.
master.simd_plan: 2D: two source evals + one rsqrt + the steered kernel (SteerablePerlin cost), so ~1.5x SteerablePerlin. 3D: five noises + eigenvalue trig form + a cross product and rsqrt (~5 ns) + the 3D steered kernel. No window beyond the host kernel; branch free; tiles if A and B tile.
master.continuity: The director tensor is continuous except at the defect cores (r -> 0), where eps makes it fade to isotropic, so the steered field is C0 everywhere and C1 away from the cores, like steerable-perlin at a vortex of its direction field. Schlieren is C-infinity with eps.
master.params: sources A, B (2D form) or built-in Feature Scale + Seed; Charge Numerator m (int, default 1, so charge m/2); Anisotropy k (hybrid); Output enum {Grain, Stripes, Schlieren, Angle}; Stripe Frequency; Eps (defect core size); Dimension form enum {Pair, QTensor3D}. Probably best shipped as a Direction Mode 'HalfCharge' on SteerablePerlin/LatticePhasor plus a Schlieren output, rather than as a new node.
master.risks: At the cores the stripes must do something, and a steered lattice kernel may show a smudge rather than a clean loop; the stripe output needs the phasor-style kernel with per-corner orientation to make real loops. May be judged a mode, not a node.

clumped-strands.look: 2D: a pelt of tapered tufts, each a rounded clump that narrows to a sharp tip with visible strands running together inside it, overlapping like fur or shaggy feathers and bending with the warp. Threshold gives claw and flame shapes. The wide view reads as an even pelt or feather coat, with no visible grid. Dark partings show ground between clumps. Straight, unwarped, with brick bond columns it read as regular scales, so hashed stagger and the warp matter. Level 2 adds some finer tufting in each clump, and it is a mild effect. Entry's crossfade (scratch): gray flat mass with faint strand marks and little sense of clumps, weak. 3D: a forest of tapered spikes with vertical grooves from the strand read, wide at the base and pointed at the top, many cut by the cube's faces. It reads as hoodoos or coarse bristles at this size. Relief (scratch): rows of rounded ridges pinching to points.

clumped-strands.port_notes: No lattice window beyond 2 columns x 2 along in 2D, 4 x 2 in 3D, all fixed. Each candidate: hash, sigma, remap, Max. Window rule: root half width wid C / 2 + jit C / 2 must stay below 1 C minus half a column for the side rule, which is what wid=1.3 and jit=0.3 give.

master.one_liner: Hair and fur clumping as a domain remap: strands converge into pointed clumps toward their tips, clumps of clumps across levels, with partings that show skin, applied to any strand source.
master.look: Fur or wet hair: strands run together into tapered spikes with pointed tips, grouped again into larger locks, partings between clumps exposing the ground, tips darker or thinner. In relief the clumps are rounded ridges that pinch to points. Useful for fur, wet hair, grass tufts, feathers down, brush bristles, and frost spikes.
master.algorithm: Frame: direction d (param angle, or a hybrid angle quantised into bins with a two-frame crossfade as LocalFrame does), s = p . d along the strands, t = p . n across. Clump level l (Levels L, lacunarity between levels): clump width C_l across, clump length Lam_l along, columns staggered by Lam_l / 2 in alternate columns (brick bond, so clump tips do not line up). Column index c = floor(t / C_l), clump centre t_c = (c + 0.5 + 0.3 (hash(c) - 0.5)) C_l; along index m = floor((s + stagger(c)) / Lam_l), fraction g = frac(.) in [0,1) (0 at the root, 1 at the tip). Narrowing factor sigma(g) = 1 - Q g^2 (the bundle is (1 - Q) of its width at the tip). Remap: t' = t_c + (t - t_c) / sigma(g): strands, which are lines of constant t' in the source, converge in world space toward the tip. Clump mask: inside if |t - t_c| < 0.5 C_l sigma(g); outside is the parting. Seamlessness: across column edges t' would jump, so evaluate the two nearest columns (c and the one on the side of t) and crossfade with weight smoothstep over the outer 20 percent of each clump; the blend zone lies in the parting where the mask is already low. Along s, the next clump's root overlaps this clump's tip: evaluate m and m+1 and crossfade over the last 15 percent of g. Levels compose: apply level 0 remap, then level 1 remap to the result coordinates (clumps of clumps), before the final source reads; the crossfades then need 4 source reads per level pair (2 across x 2 along), kept at 4 by composing the maps per branch rather than nesting the blends. Source reads: S(s, t') for a strand texture (FiberNoise, a stretched Perlin, LyapunovStretch fur) given by the user. Outputs: Strands (the source in the remapped frame times the mask), Height (clump ridge sqrt(max(0, (0.5 C sigma)^2 - (t - t_c)^2)) plus Strands * amplitude, so clumps read as rounded spikes in relief), Mask, TipFade (1 - g^4, to darken or thin strands toward the tip).
master.why_new: LyapunovStretch Stretch fur gives dense directional hair with statistical clumps and partings but strands never converge to tips; FiberNoise and FlowStrokes give individual strokes; SteerablePerlin follows a direction. Real clumping is a geometric convergence of strands toward a common tip in a hierarchy, which no warp of a stationary noise produces because warps have no notion of a clump tip. This is the pointwise form of the clump modifier every hair tool has.
master.simd_plan: No window: lattice index math plus 4 source evaluations per level pair (4 total for Levels 1 and 2 if maps compose per branch, 8 for Levels 3), so cost is about 4x Source plus 60 ops. 3D: two across axes (t1, t2), clumps are cones: 4 nearest columns x 2 along = 8 source reads; 4D: the same with w as a third across axis or as time.
master.continuity: C1 with smoothstep crossfades; C0 if linear. The remap itself is continuous within a clump (sigma > 0 as long as Q < 1).
master.params: Direction (hybrid angle), Levels (int 1-3), Clump Width, Clump Length, Lacunarity, Convergence Q (hybrid), Jitter, Tip Fade, Blend Width, Source (GeneratorSource), Output (enum).
master.risks: The partings may look like a regular comb at low jitter; a direction field (hybrid angle) needs the bin crossfade and doubles the reads; strands crossing the along crossfade zone can ghost (two tips visible) if the stagger is small.

thin-cut.look: Viewed, which was at T=.08 with the threshold at the full 2T. Thin sheets open into windows and lace with ribs left between them, and thick lobes keep their surface. Beside it Erode at the same T visibly shrinks everything. The cave roof source gains skylights where the roof is thin. Hole rims are ragged rather than clean, and at T=.12 and above the first chord version left a scatter of detached fragments. Fill closes only small slits and is a modest effect on the test source. So their look is inferred from the numbers below, not seen.

thin-cut.artifacts: No jumps. Measured on a 96^3 voxel grid, window 3, seed 1337. Thick rock is the opening of the source by a ball of 1.5 T. Share of thick rock lost: Cut T=.08 0.11 percent, T=.12 0.46, T=.16 0.59. Erode measured before the margin fix, which does not touch Erode: T=.08 48 percent, T=.12 62, T=.16 63. Volume kept by Cut: T=.05 0.998, .08 0.917, .12 0.646, .16 0.415. Unsolved: floaters and flakes. Connected components go 2 at T=0, 3 at .05, 16 at .08, 96 at .12, 277 at .16, mostly under 30 voxels. One-voxel-thick cells go 110 at T=0, 112 at .03, 177 at .05, 1372 at .08, 3020 at .12. So the claim that T about one voxel is a mesher guard is not supported: at T=.016 and .03 (half and one voxel) it changes almost nothing, and at larger T it adds thin cells at hole rims. This is the reason for promising rather than keeper.

thin-cut.port_notes: Fixed taps and masks only. The early return in air is a Select in a port. fastest route is a Guide for the taps, not tried here. T must stay above the source's own noise step or the secant sees nothing.

master.one_liner: Removes solid thinner than 2T and leaves flat walls exactly where they were: a point survives only if for every direction at least one of p+Td, p-Td is still rock. Windows and skylights open at the thinnest spots first; at T about one voxel it is a mesher guard.
master.look: On a foam, sponge or thin-roofed cave: holes open in the thinnest walls, widen, and leave ribs and lace, while thick rock keeps its exact surface. Roof over a cave near the ground gets skylights exactly where a geologist expects them; thin fins get windows, which become arches. T about one voxel: no flakes, no one-voxel slits, and the large shape is unchanged. In motion, with T rising: walls perforate then dissolve like bone resorption, with no surface receding and no dust, and with Fill rising: crevices silt up narrowest first. Judge from stills: vol at T = 0, .02, .04, .08 with the difference image, which must be empty on flat walls; and a count of connected components and of one-voxel-thick cells at each T.
master.algorithm:
Mode Cut:
v = S(p)
for each direction d_k in a table (3D: 3 axes + 4 body diagonals, 14 taps; 2D: 4 directions, 8 taps; 4D: 6 direction subset, 12 taps):
  a = S(p + T*d_k); b = S(p - T*d_k)
  if Substeps == 2: a = SoftMin(a, S(p + 0.5*T*d_k)); b = SoftMin(b, S(p - 0.5*T*d_k))   // stops a neighbouring wall at distance T keeping p alive
  v = SoftMin(v, SoftMax(a, b, kt), kt)
out = v
Mode Fill is the dual: v = SoftMax(v, SoftMin(a, b, kt), kt), which closes pinholes and slits narrower than 2T.
Why flat walls do not move: for a locally linear S, one of a, b equals S(p) + T*|d.grad S|, so SoftMax(a,b) >= S(p) and v = S(p). v only falls where both ends leave the rock: sheets, flakes, thin bridges, convex edges (which get a chamfer of about T).
T is hybrid; T(t) is a decay front. Optional Guide: taps use a cheap G and only the first term uses full S.
master.why_new: Nearest is StencilFilter Erode: it moves every surface by T, so the shape shrinks. Real opening is Dilate of Erode, which costs K*K evals and rounds everything. ThinCut is one pass, 2D taps, and keeps flat walls. Compared with SurfaceProbe or TubeNoise, which normalise slope, this removes the features that break a mesher, instead of rescaling them.
master.simd_plan: Fixed taps of the source and only Min, Max and soft variants. 3D with 7 directions: 14 evals, plus 14 for Substeps 2. On a 2 octave Perlin that is about 62 ns (estimate). 4D subset works, and it tiles since it only offsets the source's own 4D position.
master.continuity: C0, as a min-max of continuous functions. Lipschitz constant no larger than the source's for fixed T: min, max and translation are non-expansive, and polynomial soft variants are convex combinations. This is the actual property meshers want. With hybrid T it gains G*|grad T|.
master.params: Source, T (hybrid), Mode (Cut, Fill), Direction Count (4, 7, 13), Substeps (1, 2), Softness kt, optional Guide.
master.risks: Orientation dependence from the direction table. Non-monotone with T at Substeps 1. Removal is local: a floater bigger than 2T stays. Cost scales with the source, so Guide will be needed in practice, and Guide cannot see fine crumbs.

thin-cut.changed_from_entry: The algorithm changed. The entry's test (rock if either p+Td or p-Td is rock, with the half tap) leaves a central slit and two skins for any sheet of thickness 2h with h < T < 2h, which the render showed as shredded double walls at T=.16, and Substeps 2 does not fix it. Replaced by a chord length: first crossing each way by secant over taps at T and 2T, capped at 2T, cut where the shortest counted chord is below 0.85 * 2T, so a sheet goes whole or not at all. Same tap count as Substeps 2. A direction counts only if S drops along it at least about as fast as along the steepest direction, which stops grooves where a table direction is tangent to a curved wall, though the panel without this weight looked similar. Output is the source times (1 - 2c) rather than a min of taps. The Lipschitz claim in the entry therefore no longer holds: max slope rises from 2.6 to 29 per unit. algo=0 keeps the entry's form, c0ratio 8.0. The test source is th - |fbm| since the entry's |P| - 0.1 is the air sheets, not the rock sheets, under solid = value > 0.

origin.smallest_test: Source = Subtract(Abs(Perlin3), 0.1), whose wall thickness varies with slope: vol at the four T values against StencilFilter Erode at the T that removes the same sheets. Measure volume loss on the thick parts. A uniform TPMS sheet is the wrong test since all of it goes at once.
origin.confidence: high for the mechanics (flat walls stay, thin parts go). medium for beauty: 7 directions give a threshold that varies about 15 percent with wall orientation, so hole outlines may look faceted.

extra_measured.jump_scan: Own bisecting scan, which also finds jumps off the lattice lines. Cut, 2D 32 scanlines x 2000 steps, seeds 1337 and 7: 0 true jumps, worst 0.0006. Cut 3D, 24 scanlines: 0. Fill 2D: 0. Scanlines trigger at a step difference of 0.03, so smaller jumps are not examined.

bed-undercut.look: From the comparison, whose towers panels had guard=1. Default towers at seed 7: pillars and spires with stepped flanks and overhanging flat caps, reading as hoodoos. Sphere erode rival: the same silhouettes at this scale, a little rounder, so on towers the rival is close and the difference shows in the numbers rather than at a glance. Fin field: horizontal ledges wrap the fins and small rectangular windows open under hard beds, seen on the cut face. With rmax well above the fin thickness every soft bed breaches, and the hard beds are left as floating slabs: striking but wrong, in the first render. Heightfield with fold: strata ledges wrapped around a dissected hill, with visible bedding lines. Retreat: towers thin to spires, then at .24 stacks of discs, at .36 crumbs and floating pieces. 2D section: mostly flat black and white, with notched columns at the top; it does not sell the idea.
bed-undercut.dims: 2D (vertical section x, y with a 2 tap ring) and 3D measured. 4D not run; the ring stays in x, z and w passes through, so tiling would have to come from the source alone, with the bed coordinate a plain y.
bed-undercut.range: Eval2 clamps to [-1, 1] after a gain of 3 (a density section). Eval3 is raw density, -2.89 to 2.22 on the check slice, no NaN. The far coordinate check sits inside solid rock (y about -3e4), so it shows only that nothing breaks.
bed-undercut.artifacts: No jumps. Ledge depth, measured on a plane of slope m in soft beds, horizontal depth divided by Rc: ring 1.13 at m=.5, 1.04 at m=1, 1.02 at m=2, 1.01 at m=5. Sphere rival 2.13, 1.33, 1.06, 1.00. So the constant ledge claim holds to about 12 percent, and the sphere's depth doubles on gentle slopes. Tunnels (first Betti number on a 96^3 grid, window 6): fin params, b1 2 without undercut and 15 with it. Those include crumbs: 17 solid parts, 12 not touching the box, 15 under 30 voxels. Towers at seed 7: 1 part to 17, 14 not touching the box, 15 under 30 voxels, b1 0 to 29. Unsolved flaw: floaters. The stem guard from the entry did not help: 19 parts with it against 17, and it raised the max slope about 12 times, so it is off by default. Plain 2D thumb is weak since it is a section. Polygon imprint was not visible in the renders at K=8 with the turning ring.

master.one_liner: Strata that act on rock in world units: a horizontal ring erode whose radius depends on the hardness of the bed the sample lies in, so ledges have constant depth on any slope, caprocks overhang, and fins too thin for the recess open real windows under a hard lintel.
master.look: 3D: mesas with ledges that keep one depth around the whole outcrop, including on steep faces where StrataTerrace's ledges thin out. Hoodoos with mushroom caps and balanced rocks. Fins of a Perlin wall field develop rectangular-topped windows and natural bridges under hard beds, since recesses from both sides meet. Notch at sea level gives wave-cut notches, sea caves and stacks. Dip gives flatirons. In motion, Retreat rising: cliffs walk backwards at constant rate, mesa to butte to spire, nothing fades. Judge from stills: vol with a vertical cut, measure ledge depth at several slopes (should be nearly constant), and count windows on a fin field.
master.algorithm:
c = y/BedH + Dip.x*x + Dip.z*z + Fold(x,z)
j = floor(c), with boundaries jittered by a 1D piecewise linear warp so thickness varies per bed
Hj = hardness from hash(j), biased by Hard Fraction; Hn = hardness of the nearer neighbouring bed
H = lerp(Hj, Hn, smoothstep across a band of width Band at the bed boundary)   // continuous in c
Rc = Rmax*(1 - H)^2 + Notch*exp(-((y - Sea)/NotchW)^2) + Retreat
v = S(p)
for k in 0..K-1 (K = 6 to 10, fixed ring with a golden offset):
  v = SoftMin(v, S(x + Rc*cos(ak), y, z + Rc*sin(ak)), sk)
out = v
Only horizontal taps: tops stay at their height, and undersides of hard beds come out flat because Rc changes over a thin band in y.
Optional stem guard: a second ring at 2*Rc; if all of it is air the sample is in a narrow stem, and v = SoftMax(v, S(p) - Keep), so caps stay attached.
master.why_new: Nearest is StrataTerrace density mode. I looked at its vol: good stacked ledges, but it adds a sawtooth to density, so ledge depth follows slope and thin walls never get breached. The Overhanging caprock hoodoos discovery had the right idea with the same limit. StencilFilter Erode with a banded hybrid Radius is the closest graph and should be rendered as the rival; its taps are on a sphere, so it also eats tops and rounds undersides. A first order distance (S/|grad S|) cannot do this, because the estimate blows up at a fin's medial axis and the recess never breaks through.
master.simd_plan: K + 1 source evals plus one bed hash pair, no window. S should be the macro shape, 2 to 3 octaves, with fine detail added after. On 2 octaves at K=8: about 40 ns (estimate). 2D (x,y) is a vertical section with a two tap ring. 4D: ring stays in x,z, w passes through, so tiling comes from S but the bed coordinate is a plain y.
master.continuity: C0. Lipschitz constant G*(1 + |grad Rc|), and |grad Rc| is at most about Rmax/Band: an explicit number to tell a mesher, and the trade between flat undersides and gradient bound.
master.params: Source, BedH, Bed Jitter, Hard Fraction, Rmax, Band, Dip X/Z, K, Softness sk, Notch, Sea, NotchW. Hybrid: Fold, Retreat. Stem Guard on or off.
master.risks: Caps float when the stem is thinner than the recess, and the stem guard is only a heuristic. Polygon imprint. Cost if S is detailed. Windows may read as aqueduct arches if beds are too even.

bed-undercut.changed_from_entry: The ring rotates continuously with height (angle 2.4 * y / BedH) rather than a fixed golden offset, so the polygon does not stack. Hardness is either in a hard range or 0.3 * random, rather than one biased draw. Added src=2, a tower field, since the entry's hoodoos come from a heightfield with flat ground and spikes. Stem guard was built as a blend, then measured as no help and turned off.

dripstone.look: From the comparison: in the room, carrot stalactites of varied size hang from the ceiling, stalagmites stand under them on the same axis, and thick columns appear, with a lump where the two parts meet. It reads as dripstone. Small ones are slim and few big ones dominate, as the heavy tail intends. Some small stalagmites looked like detached ovals on the floor, likely where the rough source floor is below the smooth guide floor; rootBand was raised for this and that was not re-viewed. The rival has soft scallops along the ceiling with no spikes, no pairing and nothing on the floor, so the difference is clear. Curtain makes rough drapery hanging from the ceiling with a stepped lower edge. On a Perlin cave source spikes do appear in the openings, but the view shows little of the inside: only small parts of cave are visible through the clip plane. The 2D section is a dark room between white rock, with a few columns; it is a plain image. Text section after the fix: paired spikes meet at about mid room with a thin gap or waist, wide at ceiling and floor, as the entry asks.
dripstone.dims: 2D (side section with a 1D column lattice) and 3D measured. 4D not run; w would pass through to the source and guide.
dripstone.range: [-1, 1], clamped after a gain of 3. No NaN. The far coordinate check sits in solid rock, so it shows only that nothing breaks.
dripstone.artifacts: First version needed three fixes for true jumps or wrong shapes, all found by the probes: a collar that did not match the ceiling side, fused switching on at the reach, and the roof*ground factor that made columns fattest mid room. Remaining: a thin rock layer seen by some taps gives real jumps on rough guides (see jump_scan). Most spikes are short at the default heavy tail. Tap count is 13 in every lane. Coverage of the look is modest, since one spike per cell at C=1.2 is few per room. Why promising and not keeper: no render of the final fix was viewed, and the guide-source mismatch at the root is unresolved.

A surface band restriction would save most of the cost and is not possible inside a node, but a graph could mask with a cheap source.

master.one_liner: Stalactites, stalagmites and fused columns on any 3D density: fixed taps up and down a jittered site column find the nearest ceiling and floor by secant, and carrot profiles hang from them, so upper and lower spikes line up and merge when the room is low.
master.look: Cave rooms with carrot stalactites of heavy-tailed size, each with its stalagmite below it, and hourglass columns in the low parts of the room. Nothing appears on open ground. This is what the tube, strata cavern and hopf-lax volumes lack: they are all bare. Works on any density, so also icicles under overhangs and hanging lips on mesas. Judge from stills: vol of a room with the cut face through a column, and a side slice; tips must taper to points and pairs must share an axis.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: Density S (solid > 0), optional Guide G, a cheap version of S used for all taps (default S). Axis y. Own column, no window.
cell = floor(xz/C); h = hash(cell); site = C*(cell + 0.5 + J*(rnd2(h) - 0.5))
ri = C*(0.5 - J/2)*(Rmin + (1 - Rmin)*rnd(h,2)^3)   // always fits inside the cell, heavy tail of sizes
Reach = K*hy; Lu = Reach*rnd(h,3); Ld = Reach*rnd(h,4)
g0 = G(site.x, y, site.z)
up = INF; prev = g0
for k in 1..K: g = G(site.x, y + k*hy, site.z); up = Select(prev <= 0 & g > 0 & up == INF, (k - 1 + prev/(prev - g))*hy, up); prev = g
dn: the same loop downward; keep gd1, the first downward tap
roof = sat((Reach - up)/(0.25*Reach))   // stalagmites only under a roof within reach, so open ground stays clean
a = sat(1 - up/Lu); b = sat(1 - dn/Ld)*roof
rad = ri*Max(Prof(a), Prof(b))   // Prof(q) = sqrt(q)*(1 + Bead*sin(y*fb + ph)), a carrot with optional beading
fused = smoothstep(Lu + Ld, 0.7*(Lu + Ld), up + dn); rad = Max(rad, ri*Neck*fused)   // when they would meet: a column with a waist
collar = ri*sat(1 - g0/RootBand)*Max(sat(-gd1*Gain), roof)   // inside rock, keeps rad continuous at the rock surface
rad = Select(g0 > 0, collar, rad)
d = |xz - site| - rad
out = Max(S(p), -d*Scale)
Curtain mode: taps at the sample's own column, no site. Hem length Lu comes from a hybrid 2D source, and solid = up < Lu, so any 2D node can hang from any ceiling: a line field gives flowstone draperies, constant gives a sagging lining.
master.why_new: Nearest is GroundedScatter: stamps on a heightfield, one ground per column, no ceilings. It cannot see a floor under an overhang. RootStrands gives hanging fibres on a lattice with no relation to any ceiling. The closest graph is StreakSmear Mode=Max along y over the density plus a bump field; it should be rendered as the rival. It will show tap banding and has no floor and ceiling pairing, no fusing and no taper control.
master.simd_plan: Masks only, 2K + 1 Guide evals per lane at the site column plus 1 S. K = 6, 2 octave Guide: about 13 * 4.4 = 57 ns plus S and about 2 ns (estimate). Worst case applies to every lane, so the engine should restrict it to a surface band. No window because each disc is confined to its cell. 2D is a side view with a 1D column lattice; 4D passes w through to S.
master.continuity: C0 in the normal case: the crossing distance is constant under a given ceiling, rad reaches 0 at Lu, and discs vanish before the cell border. Small jumps remain where a rock layer thinner than hy is seen by some taps and missed by others, so Guide must be smooth at scale hy.
master.params: Source S, Guide, Feature Scale (C), K, Step hy, Rmin, Bead, Neck, RootBand, Density, Mode (Spikes, Curtain). Hybrid: Hem Length in Curtain mode. Up Axis enum.
master.risks: Cost. Tips thinner than a voxel alias in a mesher. Only vertical spikes, no helictites. Lane cost is K-driven even where nothing hangs. The collar rule is the part I am least sure of.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured. 2K + 1 = 13 guide evals plus 1 source. A 1 octave Perlin3 guide: about 13 * 2.2 = 29 ns, source 2 octaves 4.4 ns, arithmetic 2 ns: about 35 ns in 3D. Every lane pays this even where nothing hangs.
measured.c0_step_text: default room: h=1e-3 0.02139, h=1e-4 0.00214, h=1e-5 0.00021, a slope. Perlin cave: 0.04122, 0.00416, 0.00040, c0ratio 5.0, straddled 2.9, a steep slope on the lattice lines. Curtain: 0.09903, 0.04010, 0.00100, c0ratio 7.97, very steep near the ceiling rather than a jump

dripstone.changed_from_entry: Spike length is tied to size, so small spikes are also short. Prof is q^0.75, not sqrt(q), since sqrt reads as blunt. The fused term ends before the gap reaches 0.75 Reach, so a crossing first seen at the reach cannot switch it on; the entry's form jumps there. The collar's factor is -gd1 / g0 rather than -gd1 * Gain, so it matches the air side at the surface on any slope, and the floor case uses Prof(roof). The spike term falls to -1.5 at the cell border so the max cannot jump there. Curtain gets a root term inside the ceiling only, since without one it jumped by 1. Added a slab room source (src=1) and a view-only clip plane, because a closed cube shows no inside.

arbor-fold.look: From the comparison and earlier renders. Bare trees standing on a ground: a trunk, branching 1 to 2 to 4 to 8 to 16 with filleted crotches, fat limbs and thin twigs, branch directions differing from tree to tree. Reads as winter trees at once, and the first render already looked this way. Inverted: root systems hanging from a stump. L=3 with a wide flare: candelabra or antlers. master.one_liner: Trees, roots and coral from a height-ramped mirror fold: a disc in the plane across the axis splits into 2, 4, 8 discs as height rises, giving smooth Y-junction branches with no segment list and no window, and a moving slice is literal cell division.
master.look: 3D: bare trees, fan coral, antlers, candelabra cactus; roots when inverted. Radius follows the area law, so trunks read heavy and twigs light, and crotches are filleted rather than capsule-on-capsule. Slice at fixed y: discs in hierarchical pairs, a clustered dot pattern. Slice moving up through y, in motion: each disc stretches, necks and divides, 1 to 2 to 4 to 8, nothing fades. That is a mitosis animation from a volume. Judge from stills: vol at window 4 for the forest, and a strip of 8 XZ slices where the blob count per cell must go 1, 2, 4, 8 with no blob arriving from nothing.
master.algorithm:
Axis y, plane (x,z). Own column only, no window.
cell = floor(xz/C); h = hash(cell); alive = rnd(h) < Density
site = C*(cell + 0.5 + J*(rnd2(h) - 0.5)); l = xz - site
base = Ground(site) (hybrid, 1 eval at the site so trunks do not shear with the hill); H = Height*(0.7 + 0.6*rnd(h,3))
t = (y - base)/H (Invert member: t = (base - y)/H gives roots or hanging growth)
l -= Wander*(sin(2.1*t + ph1), sin(1.7*t + ph2))
r = R0; id = h
for i in 0..L-1:   // L is an int member, same for all lanes
  ti = T0 + i*Dt + TJit*rnd11(id,0)
  q = sat((t - ti)/Spread); s = q*q*(3 - 2*q)
  a = A*Ratio^i*(s + Flare*Max(0, t - ti - Spread))   // half separation of the two children at this height
  (c,sn) = 16 entry unit vector table, index from hash bits of id
  u = c*l.x + sn*l.y; v = -sn*l.x + c*l.y
  side = v >= 0
  e = Soft*r*s
  v = sqrt(v*v + e*e) - e - a   // smooth mirror fold (the post-fold crease softening discovery); an isometry when a = e = 0
  l = (u, v)
  id = mix(id + side*prime + i)   // Identity = Symmetric skips the side term
  r *= lerp(1, Rr, s)             // Rr = 2^(-1/3) = 0.794, the pipe model area law
d = |l| - r*(1 - Taper*sat(t))
d = SmoothMax(d, y - (base + H*TopT), k); d = SmoothMax(d, base - Sink - y, k)
out = Clamp(-d/Band, -1, 1), and -1 when not alive
Extent rule: Wander + R0 + Band + sum over i of A*Ratio^i*(1 + Flare) <= C*(0.5 - J/2), so output is exactly -1 at the column border.
Growth: TopT = Age (hybrid or w) gives a tree that rises tip first, with r multiplied by sat((TopT - t)/TipLen) so tips taper as they advance.
master.why_new: Nearest is CoralNoise: it enumerates sum M^l capsules over 27 cells, 7 segments for about 45 ns by its own entry. ArborFold reaches 16 to 32 tips for L folds because the descent visits only the branch the sample is on. FernFold is the 2D ancestor, but its own notes say 3D slices show only dots. WanderingColumns has the bundled look and never branches. Column-free dendrite nodes (DendryNoise) are lines in a plane, not limbs in a volume. A graph cannot do this: each fold needs the branch identity from the previous one.
master.simd_plan: No window. Fixed loop of L: one hash, table lookup by bit selects, one sqrt, a few FMAs; one final sqrt. Estimate 1 to 1.5 ns per level on AVX2, so L=5 is about 6 to 8 ns in 3D. 2D (x,y) form: l is 1D, v = |v| - a, a side view tree. 4D: w drives Age; no tiling story, a torus mapping would not mean anything for a tree, so it is documented as not tileable.
master.continuity: C0, and C1 at crotches when Soft > 0. Rotations and folds are isometries, so d is a true distance to the branch at that height. With Identity = Symmetric there is no jump at all. With Hashed, id changes across v = 0, but this only matters below the next split, and is hidden when A*Ratio^i*(1 - Ratio) >= r + Band at the deepest level, since the jump then lies in clamped air.
master.params: Feature Scale (C), Levels L, Height, R0, A, Ratio, Rr, T0, Dt, TJit, Spread, Flare, Soft, Taper, Wander, Density, Identity (Symmetric, Hashed), Invert, Band. Hybrid: Ground (sampled at the site), Age, Density.
master.risks: Everything is binary. Levels above 5 force thin limbs or big cells because of the budget rule. Limbs diverge only sideways, so no horizontal boughs or weeping forms without a domain warp upstream. One tree per cell can look planted; use Density and a low frequency warp.

arbor-fold.changed_from_entry: Identity changed. The entry's Hashed form jumps at the fold plane unless a budget holds at every level, and the scan found those jumps. Replaced with a smooth identity: sg = clamp( v / ( asymW * a ), -1, 1 ), 0 on the fold plane and +-1 on the children, accumulated as code = 0.5 * code + sg * rnd( level ), and code then varies the next level's rotation, split height and spread. Both sides agree at the plane, so no jump is possible at any budget, and this is what lets the tree be asymmetric. The budget rule became a limit on A rather than a stated condition. The rest is as written. Rotation by real sincos rather than the 16 entry table, in this mode.

master.look: In volume: caves with flat water tables that differ from gallery to gallery, thin rock dams where two bodies meet, and dry passages above. In 2D relief: terraced mountain lakes held by small natural lips, which SpillLevel could not hold cheaply.
master.algorithm:
Anisotropic jittered sites at spacing (Cell XZ, Cell Y, Cell XZ). Window 3^D search for F1 and all candidate distances.
Per site: L = level. Default hashed: floor((c.y + rnd)*Cell Y). Or hybrid Level Source read at the site for the 2 nearest. Dry by hash against Flood: L = -inf.
Fluid kind: hash of the coarser cell c >> 2, so water and lava come in regions.
Outputs:
  Level: L_1 of the nearest site, piecewise constant.
  Fluid: L_1 - y, positive under water.
  Barrier: B = max over j != 1 of [ max(0, 1 - (d_j - d_1)/Wall) * clamp((max(L_1,L_j) - y)/Fade,0,1) * clamp(|L_1-L_j|/Fade,0,1) ].
     So walls form only near a cell border, only where levels differ, and only below the higher level. Equal levels merge freely into one big lake.
  Density: Max(Source(p), B*Strength - Bias), walls cut into caves only where needed.
2D form, for surface lakes: Source is terrain. L_i = Source(site) + Depth for a lake site. Output Height: terrain raised to a lip by B at borders where the water would otherwise escape, so a lake holds at any altitude on any terrain. Output Water: L_1 where terrain < L_1.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Stock graph: CellularValue index 0, index 1 and F2-F1, plus masks, about 8 nodes and 3 full searches (36 ns in 3D), and no multi candidate barrier; so this is partly a 3x speed case, and it adds Y logic and the 2D lip mode. Nearest idea SpillLevel (dropped at 2.44): computes where water would stay from rays; this inverts the problem and builds the rim. Nothing else in the catalogue has water at all. Evidence read: the Minecraft Wiki describes per cell local fluid levels (16x40x16), water or lava per 64x40x64, flooded, empty and local states, and barriers separating liquids with a noise for height. A 1.18 overview calls aquifer water in spaghetti caves the contentious change, so players do notice it. A Mojang tracker result, seen only as a search summary, says merging is meant to read as one big aquifer, which the equal level rule gives.
master.simd_plan: CellularDistance window, 9 / 27 / 81 sites, with a per candidate term in the max: about 5 / 15 / 45 ns, plus Source and up to 2 Level evals (estimates). Bit fields from one hash. 4D form exists but is expensive; 4D use: time on w gives rising water if levels are driven by w. Tiles if the hashes wrap under the torus form as other cellular nodes do.
master.continuity: Level and Fluid discontinuous at borders by design, hidden by walls in practice. Barrier C0 at F1 swaps when levels differ, since the pair term dominates; when F1 swaps between equal levels the other terms are equal. A small jump is possible at some triple junctions where a third site's term changes reference; expect to find them with seams and judge if they matter once thresholded.

master.risks: Walls can look like straight cell faces, so warp the input and use high jitter. Water surfaces are flat by construction, with no rivers feeding them. Game side still needs voxel material logic; one float at a time means two instances. 2D lips may read as artificial dams on rough terrain. It is partly graph expressible, so the panel may call this a preset.

gated-bond-graph.look: From panels. A wiry street or crack network of curved strokes that exists only on land and stops at the shoreline in dead-end stubs and loose fragments, with a ragged edge that follows the coast at a distance. Cost patches open bare areas inside the land where bonds thin and vanish while the nodes on both sides stay, and both ends of every stroke remain nodes. Smallest test: a density step across x gives a ragged front with stubs, where the mask rival gives a straight soft cut through bonds. A cost ridge gives a straight bare gap, with stubs up to it on both sides. Height relief: islands of tent-like peaks and sharp ridges, thinned to where density allows. It is BondGraph's look, so it still reads as lattice-derived. 3D: a tube scaffold confined to a rock volume with stubs at its edge; dense where density is high, and at seed 7 nearly all alive, so it is not always visibly confined at window 6.

Density is hash against field per site, so its front is statistically soft, with a width set by dcon.
