master.one_liner: BondGraph's network thinned the CellularDensity way: a node lives only if a hybrid Density read at its own site passes its hash, and a bond only if a Cost read at its midpoint is low enough, so roads stay in lowlands, caves stay inside one rock volume, and the network frays into dead ends at the boundary instead of being cut by a mask.
master.look: A wiry road, crack or vein network that exists only where the density map allows and whose links avoid high-cost ground: a town plan that stops at the shoreline with streets ending in stubs, a cave network confined to a limestone volume with passages that stop short of the contact, roots that avoid stones. The boundary of the network is ragged with dead ends, not a straight cut. Degree output shows junction dots on a path map.
master.algorithm: As t_bond_graph: jittered lattice points in the 3^D window, candidate bonds to the forward neighbours (axis and diagonal), each bond present by a symmetric pair hash. Add two gates. Node gate: for every window site i, alive_i = rnd01(h_i) < Density(q_i), where Density is a HybridSource evaluated at the site position q_i (9 evals in 2D, 27 in 3D; CellularDensity's trick, so the decision is per feature and cannot pop with the sample). Bond gate: for each present bond (i, j), cost = Cost(m_ij) at the midpoint (one eval per bond, about 12 in 2D) and keep = alive_i & alive_j & (rnd01(pair hash) < 1 - Cost soft-compared with Threshold). A soft form: width factor wf = smoothstep(Threshold + Soft, Threshold - Soft, cost) scales the bond's half width so bonds thin out before vanishing (C0 in the cost field). Distance = min over kept bonds of segDist minus width, node beads as BondGraph. Outputs: Distance, Mask, Height (BondGraph's per-edge width, height and beads), Degree: number of kept bonds at the nearest alive node divided by the maximum (1 bond = dead end, 2 = path, 3+ = junction), which lets a graph colour junctions and cul-de-sacs. Arc mode (BondGraph's bulge) unchanged. 3D: same with 27 sites and 3D bonds.
master.why_new: BondGraph (keeper) is uniform; multiplying it by a mask cuts bonds mid-span and leaves half-bonds, and cannot remove a bond because its far end lies in forbidden ground. CellularDensity (keeper) has the per-feature gate but no network. DendryNoise follows a control downhill but is a tree, not a mesh with loops. The gate must be applied per node and per bond inside the bond loop. Modest novelty, high usefulness: it is what makes BondGraph usable for terrain and caves.
master.simd_plan: BondGraph's loops plus 3^D Density evals and one Cost eval per candidate bond, all fixed counts with masks; with cheap hybrids (constants or Perlin) the added cost is about 9 + 12 evals in 2D and 27 + 40 in 3D. Estimated AVX2 with Perlin gates: 2D 25-35 ns, 3D 150-250 ns (heavy; the Cost gate can be disabled per enum to drop the midpoint evals).
master.continuity: Distance and Height are C0 in position (min of capsules, clamped) and C0 in the Density and Cost fields with the soft width form; Mask and Degree are discontinuous by design. A node switching alive with the sample is impossible because Density is read at the site, not at the sample.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Bond Probability, Diagonals (enum), Density (hybrid at the site), Cost (hybrid at the bond midpoint), Threshold, Soft, Width, Width Jitter, Bead, Bulge, Output enum {Distance, Mask, Height, Degree}, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Expensive with fractal hybrids, and the per-bond midpoint eval doubles the source count; a per-site-only variant (both ends must be cheap) covers most uses. Connectivity is not guaranteed: thinning a percolating network can leave isolated fragments, which is fine for roads and poor for caves.

drainage-frame.look: Relief at seed 7: a dissected mountain range. Thin dark trunks branch and join, with long fine herringbone gullies running into them from both sides at an acute angle, and smooth narrow divides where frames meet. In the sheet the trunks are the dominant dark lines and the FFT is a soft star. Vol of the terrain: same, as faceted ribs running down into narrow trenches. Cellular, read at the first seed: scree-like tongues. Stripes, read at the first seed: bold black and white chevrons, the most graphic. Small window: narrow feathered valleys in otherwise plain smooth land, a different and cleaner look at 60 percent of the cost. 3D source: a block of slab-like fractured pieces, of little use. master.one_liner: Make any source follow drainage: each steepest-descent trunk segment rotates its neighbourhood rigidly so a stretched source runs down into the trunk. It was endorsed twice and dropped only because a node cannot output a vector, and it does not need to.
master.look: Very convincing: thin dark trunks with fine streaks running into them from both sides, herringbone along each trunk, ridges where frames meet. Relief reads as a dissected mountain range. Any Source works: Ridged gives gullies, Cellular gives scree tongues, Stripes gives strata wrapping into valleys. Star hubs at sinks are a known weakness, which stochastic descent reduces.
master.algorithm:
THE ACCIDENT. rivers_drainage_frame: a plain stretched Perlin fractal sampled at (along trunk, distance from trunk) gave hillslope streaks draining into every trunk, reading as eroded terrain close to catchment-rivers. Two entries found it; both notes stopped because vector output exists only in the DomainWarp family. A meta-node with a Source input solves that the normal way.

Frame: exactly rv::trunkFrame in t_rivers_common. 7x7 jittered nodes with control heights from a cheap hash-only valley noise, 25 links each to its lowest neighbour (with stochastic descent, the rivers discovery that dissolves star hubs), nearest segment owner by m = d + lam*overshoot, fade = ownership margin * window limit * axis-side guard.
THE TRICK for one Source eval and C0: instead of local coordinates (near zero, which a lerp would sweep across huge distances), rotate rigidly about the segment start a: t = trunk direction, n = its normal.
  u = dot(p-a, t); v = dot(p-a, n)
  p' = a + (u + Slant*|v|)*X + v*Y             // Slant makes streaks meet the trunk at an acute downstream angle, a pinnate pattern. |v| crease is hidden on the trunk
  P = lerp(p, p', fade*Strength)               // bounded move: |p' - p| is at most a few cells
  Out = Source(P.x*AlongScale, P.y*AcrossScale, ...)
Output enum: Framed (just that); Carved = Framed*(1 - TrunkDepth*trunkMask) with width growing downhill, as the prototype's out=3; Trunk Mask; Elevation e (interpolated control height along the segment).
In 3D the frame lives in the plane normal to Up and other axes pass through. In 4D, tile via the torus-angle-wrapped lattice discovery: recover two angles, run the same 2D lattice with an integer Period.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. ErosionFilter adds gullies from a height's own gradient, with no real trunks. DendryNoise and LocalFrameDrainage draw networks but cannot host an arbitrary source. catchment-rivers needs walkers. anchored-frame-detail aligns to a gradient but has no shared trunk or confluences. This is the only one where any user subgraph drains along an explicit network.
master.simd_plan: Fixed 49 control hashes and value evals, 25 x 9 neighbour Selects, min tracking with masks, one Source eval. Measured scalar 2166 ns at the prototype stage. My AVX2 estimate is 150 to 250 ns plus Source, roughly 150 times Perlin, justified only for bake or terrain, not as a building block. Small window (25 control, 9 links) is about a third of that but leaves more plain area. Cost is the same in 3D as 2D. 4D only via the torus trick.
master.continuity: C0: P is continuous because fade reaches 0 at each ownership change, at the window limit and across the side flip, and the Source is C0. The prototype's frame measured c0ratio 7.9 with 0 true jumps in the rivers family.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Up Axis, Jitter, Fade Width, Slant, Along Scale (high), Across Scale (low), Stochastic Descent enum, int Window (Full 7x7 or Small 5x5), int Period, Output enum, Trunk Depth, Trunk Width. Hybrid: Strength. Source required.
master.risks: Cost. Fade bands at ownership changes show as patches of plain Source if Fade Width is large. Rigid rotation about a differs from the prototype's (u,v) by offsets per segment; a Source with visible long features will show that. The 25 link pass does not reduce further without losing connectivity.

meander-delta.look: Mask, seed 7 and seed 42: a tree of rivers whose thick trunks wander in tight sinuous bends and whose thin twigs stay near straight, with tributaries joining the bends rather than stopping short of them. Beside the straight baseline it is a clear change: straight spokes become wandering rivers. At this amplitude the bends are tight and fairly regular, so some stretches read as lightning or a crack more than a slow meander, and the fattest rivers read as a wiggly band. Earlier at k=11, tighter still, it looked like squiggles. Relief carve, read at a lower amplitude: valleys a little more irregular, otherwise close to the straight version, so the payoff is in plan view and at the mask. 3D: worm-like corkscrew tubes against the straight rods of the parent, playful and of less use. Function graph limit holds as the entry says: no omega loops, no oxbows.

So width is preserved well for thin lines, and Proximity and wide Carve are rough on the inside of bends. Rivers go straight for a moment at each joint, since the taper returns to 0 there. Single wavelength per level. Amplitude is capped by the window at 0.6 rk.

master.one_liner: Width-preserving Kinoshita offsets per Dendry segment: a sinuous river tree where big rivers wander and twigs stay straight.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: sinuous river trees, with no omega loops or oxbows, since a function graph cannot double back. A bake node.
master.algorithm: Inside Dendry's fixed-window segment loop, per level and candidate segment (a,b): t = clamp(dot(pos-a, b-a) / L2); n = signed perpendicular distance; s = t * L. y = A[level] * (sin(k*s + ph) + J * sin(3*k*s + ph3)) * Sqrt(sin(pi*t)), taking phases from the segment hash. The taper is 0 at both ends, so joints stay connected. dy = derivative of y with respect to s. d = Abs(n - y) * InvSqrt(1 + dy*dy), first-order width correction. Feed d into the existing min and width logic in place of the segment distance. A[level] grows with river order. Adds one or two sincos per candidate. Critic estimate for Dendry is 60-100 ns AVX2 2D at 4 levels; expect 10-30 ns more (estimate).
master.why_new:
Dendry trees are straight-limbed and Fisk has meanders but no tributaries. Width-preserving Kinoshita offsets per segment give a sinuous tree where big rivers wander and twigs stay straight. Honest limit: a function graph cannot double back, so no omega loops or oxbows; only Fisk gets those. Not built; the look is a prediction. Bake node.
Seed gap: sinuous river trees.
master.simd_plan: Critic estimate for Dendry is 60-100 ns AVX2 2D at 4 levels; expect 10-30 ns more (estimate).
master.continuity: Not stated by the panel.
master.params: Dendry members, A per level, k, J, phases from the segment hash.
master.risks:
Seed risk 0.75: bake only; no omega loops possible.
Noticed in merge: if n is the perpendicular distance to the segment's infinite line, then past the segment ends (t clamped, y = 0) d is |n| rather than the distance to the end point, so a segment draws as an infinite strip. The end-cap distance has to be kept when feeding d into Dendry's min.

strip_problem.how: t_meander_delta_strip.cpp, one segment from (0,0) to (2,0) against brute force distance to a 2000 point polyline of the curve, at the default A, k, J. strip=1 is the entry's formula as written.
strip_problem.before: d at (3,0), (6,0), (20,0): 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, against a true 1, 4, 18. In a 12 x 4 box, samples within width: 13764, against 2841 on the true curve. Whole field: a mesh of infinite lines, 102 true jumps in the scan, c0ratio 1.0.
strip_problem.after: d at the same points: 1.000, 4.000, 18.000, equal to the true values. Samples within width: 2842, with 84 outside the true curve's band. Whole field: 0 true jumps on seeds 1337, 7, 42. Fixed: yes.
strip_problem.fix: d = sqrt( d_in^2 + over^2 ), with over the overshoot past the end along the axis, d_in the first order distance. Fixing the strip alone was not enough, because the entry's taper sqrt( sin( pi t ) ) has infinite slope at both ends, so y' blows up and d_in collapses along a line through each end point, and d_in disagrees with the end cap there. Measured: a step of 0.038 in d across a segment start, and with this taper 111 true jumps in the field even with the end cap. So the taper changed to smooth shoulders with value and slope both 0 at the ends: step 0.00002, no jump. d_in is also floored at |n| - A(1+J), since no curve lies further out than that, which keeps first order lobes inside the window.

master.one_liner: A cheap cauliflower or cumulus: each lobe has 12 child lobes on icosahedron vertices, the nearest is found in closed form, and descent visits only that child, so 4 levels take no window at all; each lobe has a birth time, so a time input makes clouds erupt rather than fade.
master.look: Vol: lobes on lobes with clean soft creases, like the CumulusNoise still, which is the best solid in my 12 stills, and with flat-based towers if Base is set: cumulus congestus, romanesco, brain coral, cave popcorn, moss. In motion, Age rising: small lobes rise out of the surface and swell, then carry their own children, so billows bulge without any fading. A view of time-lapse cloud, which threshold-animated fBm never gives. Judge from stills: vol at L = 1, 2, 3, 4 and vol at four Age values on a fixed view; a lobe once born only grows, and surface points move only outward.
master.algorithm:
Axes A[0..5] = normalised (0,1,phi), (0,-1,phi), (1,phi,0), (-1,phi,0), (phi,0,1), (phi,0,-1).
Top: own cell (3D lattice or XZ column), site s0, radius R0 confined to the cell by R0*(1 + sum of child reach) <= margin.
q = (p - s0)/R0; scale = R0; dist = (|q| - 1)*scale; liftAcc = 0; id = h0
for i in 0..L-1:
  u = q*InvSqrt(Max(q.q, 1e-8))
  find m1, m2 = two largest |dot(u, A[a])| with Max/Min and Select, a1 = argmax, sg = sign of that dot
  h = hash(id, a1*2 + sg)
  present = rnd(h) < Keep
  g = sat((Age - Birth*(i + rnd(h,2)))/Rise); rc = Ratio*(0.75 + 0.5*rnd(h,1))*g*g*(3 - 2*g)*(1 + UpBias*(sg*A[a1].y))   // rc = 0 until the lobe is born
  c = sg*A[a1]*(1 - Sink*rc)
  qc = q - c
  dc = |qc| - rc
  liftAcc += (1 - smoothstep(0, W, m1 - m2))*Lift*scale*rc   // the whole subtree lifts off near a bisector, so the owner change is invisible
  dist = SmoothMin(dist, dc*scale + liftAcc, Kt*scale*rc)
  q = Householder(unit vector from h)*(qc/Max(rc, 1e-3)); scale *= Max(rc, 1e-3); id = h
Flat base: dist = SmoothMax(dist, Base - y, k). Out = Clamp(-dist/Band, -1, 1)
master.why_new: CumulusNoise needs three cellular searches with a two-parent blend, and its own risk note says three-way corners kink: about 36 ns or more in 3D. PuffyCaps and SphereFractal are graphs or lattices with window searches at each level. IcoBillow's descent is one closed form choice per level. KIFSFractal is the same family of map but gives foam by orbit traps and has no lobes with radii or birth times. Answers the clouds hole in the seeds file.
master.simd_plan: Per level: 6 dot products, Min/Max/Select to get the top two, one hash, one Householder, two InvSqrt. Estimate 1.5 ns per level on AVX2, 6 to 8 ns at L=4, about a fifth of CumulusNoise. 2D: 6 directions on a circle for cloud sprites. 4D: w = Age, not tiling; a true 4D form would use the 24-cell vertices.
master.continuity: C0 proved by lift: at any owner change the subtree is lifted by a growing liftAcc, so it does not contribute, and SmoothMin returns the parent's value. Continuous in Age. Creases at low Kt are C0 by intent.
master.params: Feature Scale, Levels L, Ratio (about .5), Keep, Sink, W, Lift, Kt, UpBias, Base, Band. Hybrid: Age (constant = fully grown), Density at the top.
master.risks: Soccer-ball regularity at level 1. Lift bands make visible valleys if W is large. Own-cell puffs read as separate balls; grouping needs a density and possibly a top level window. Thin smooth creases can alias in a mesher.

measured.scalar_note: Measured with the harness. Each Eval reads about 26 params through a string-keyed map; I did not separate that cost from the kernel.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 8 to 10 ns at L=4 (entry's 1.5 ns per level, plus two Perlin evals for the wall warp). Not measured.

ico-billow.changed_from_entry: Own-cell free balls came out small and separate (first render), so the top level changed. Lobes now sit in XZ columns with a flat base, and the whole tree lifts off near a warped cell wall, the same trick as a sub-level owner change, so a lobe may fill its cell with still no window. Added Hover (dome centre above Base), a floor on the lift when rc is small, position jitter on the sphere, and Band2 for 2D. Top lobes also grow with Age. W is much wider than the entry implies, since narrow W gave facets.

motion.statement: I did not see this move. The judgement comes from the six still frames and from text measurements.
motion.time_param: There is no param called Time. The time param is Age.
motion.best_range: Age 0.25 to 2.0 reads best and does not loop. Most of the visible change is before Age 1.0, and Age 1.3 to 2.0 only adds small lobes. Age 2 and Age 10 are identical (max abs diff 0 in 2D and in a 3D slice).
motion.frames_show: Age 0.25 has only two small flat patches, Age 0.6 has small separate lumps, Age 0.95 has nearly full towers, and later frames add small lobes.
motion.outward_only_measured: 3D slices through z=1 and z=3, Age steps from 0.3 to 2.0: at most 0.023% of samples decreased, worst decrease -0.17 of output range, so growth is almost but not strictly outward. Lift rising with rc is the likely cause; I did not confirm it.

origin.smallest_test: L = 3, Keep = 0.85, own cell: vol at window 2 on one cell, then jumps. If L = 1 looks like a virus particle and L = 3 still does, raise radius jitter and add position jitter on the sphere.
origin.confidence: medium: lobes on lobes are certain, but the icosahedral regularity may show through; I do not know how much jitter that needs.

domain-plume.look: Gray panels show a smoke plume with soft bright billows split by thin dark creases, fine at the apex at the bottom of the picture and large at the top, inside a wandering cone. Vol at window 8 is a conical tower of lumps, fine at the base and large at the top, breaking into separate fragments at the top. An earlier 3 by 5 grid (older defaults) showed Exponent 0 with round lumps, and Exponent 1 with lumps flattened into wide horizontal streaks at the top.
domain-plume.dims: 2D (side view with one lateral axis) and 3D measured. 4D is not written; the entry says w would pass through and tiling means nothing for an axis-symmetric form.
domain-plume.range: about [-0.79, 0.89] over frames; far field flat at about -0.58. tanh keeps it inside [-1, 1]. No NaN or Inf over 8 seeds.
domain-plume.artifacts: No jumps: the jumps table shrinks with the step, and straddled c0 is 8.05. Detail gets very fine near the apex, where slopes peak at 15 per unit (they scale as 1/(Spread*Y0), as the entry says). The top of the vol breaks into separate fragments at Detail 2. At Slots 3, lumps partly cross-fade rather than keep identity.
domain-plume.node_shape: DomainPlume: Source, Y0, Spread, Exponent, Ref Height, Rise, Cycle, Slots, Scale, Detail, Bias, Meander, Meander Frequency, Contrast, Wind X/Z, Axis X/Z. Hybrid: Time. Source shape billow is here a built-in for the test; a real node takes any source.
domain-plume.port_notes: One Pow or Log, one sqrt, one Sin per slot, Modulus for fract. Exponent switch is a per-node branch, not per-lane. The small-e form (h^e - 1)/(Spread*e) is continuous through 0 but needs a constant-time switch near e = 0. Meander is 1 extra source eval in 2D and 2 in 3D per slot.

master.one_liner: A similarity coordinate for rising smoke: sample any source at (radius/height, power of height minus time), so eddies move up and grow in proportion to the plume's own width and stay recognisable, from a flame-like stretch to an explosive billow by one exponent.
master.look: Vol at iso 0: a conical tower of lumps, fine at the base and big at the top, which is how eruption columns and chimney plumes are actually built, not a cylinder of constant noise. In motion: lumps move up and swell, keeping identity; never a stretch, never a fade. Exponent 0 gives an accelerating explosion, Exponent 0.5 flames that lick upward, Exponent 1 a mushrooming top. With IcoBillow or CumulusNoise as Source: a billow tower. Judge from stills: lump size against height in a side slice must be linear; between two frames, a best-shift correlation with a local scale factor should be high.
master.algorithm:
Axis y. Optional wind path xc(y) = WindX*(y + Y0)^1.5, zc similarly.
h = Max(y + Y0, eps)
rho = Spread*h
qx = (x - xc)/rho; qz = (z - zc)/rho
qy = Exponent == 0 ? Log(h)/Spread : h^Exponent/(Spread*Exponent)
E = 1 - sqrt(qx^2 + qz^2)   // 1 on the axis, 0 at the cone wall
v = Source(seed, (qx, qy - Rise*t, qz)*Scale)
out = v*Detail + E*Bias
Exact loop: Slots = 2 or 3; s_i = fract(Rise*t + i/N), slot i samples at qy - s_i*Cycle with amplitude Sin(Pi*s_i), and with a seed per slot; as in ZoomLoop, sum of squares is constant. Slots = 1 is a plain scroll with no loop.
At Exponent 0 the map in (r,h) has equal scales on all axes near the axis, so features stay round. Above 0 features get taller with height, and a Exponent near 0.5 reads as flame tongues. Inverted axis gives falling water or a hanging plume.
master.why_new: DomainMap's log polar is radial about a point, with a fixed seam-free embedding; DomainScale is not hybrid and has no height dependence; a warp with time grows shear. There is no node dividing coordinates by a position function, so no graph gives it today. Nearest in spirit is LogPolarVortex, which zooms each Voronoi cell into its centre.
master.simd_plan: Single source eval, one Pow or Log, one sqrt. About source + 1 ns (estimate). 2D is a side view with one lateral coordinate. 4D passes w through and tiling is not meaningful for an axis-symmetric form.
master.continuity: C-infinity above the y = -Y0 plane except at E's axis (sqrt, handled by adding e). Gradient of the source shrinks as 1/rho, so it is bounded by the source's bound divided by Spread*Y0, a stated limit for meshing.
master.params: Source, Y0, Spread, Exponent, Rise, Scale, Detail, Bias, Wind X/Z, Slots, Cycle. Hybrid: Time.
master.risks: A single-eval domain map is a modest node, and could be a mode of DomainMap. Cone looks too clean at the wall without warp. Accelerating rise at Exponent 0 runs away near the top. Y0 too small gives frantic detail at the base.

measured.scalar_note: Measured at the defaults: Slots 3 times Octaves 3 is 9 source evals, plus 3 Perlin evals for meander. With Slots=1 it measures 9.73x. Params go through a string-keyed map per Eval, and I did not separate that cost.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 3 slots x 3 octave Perlin 2D is about 10 ns plus 3 ns of meander and 1 ns of map, so about 14 ns in 2D. It is about source cost x slots + 1 ns. Not measured.

domain-plume.changed_from_entry: Added Meander: a slow noise in q space, applied per slot, so the wall wanders in proportion to width. The clean cone needed it, as the entry's risk note feared. Added tanh Contrast. The cone term E adds by amp^2 and noise by amp, so mean and variance both stay constant over the loop. The source fades outside the cone so the far field is flat. Added RefH: vertical over lateral feature size is (h/RefH)^-e, so the entry's 'taller with height' is true only below RefH when e>0, and above RefH lumps flatten. Exponent now uses (h^e - 1)/(Spread*e), continuous through 0. 2D flips y so the plume rises up the picture.

motion.statement: I did not see this move. The judgement comes from the six still frames and from text measurements.
motion.best_range: Time 0 to 1 is one exact loop at Rise=1 and Slots>=2 (period is 1/Rise). Time 0 vs 1 max abs diff is 3.9e-06 in 2D and 8.9e-07 in a 3D slice, which is float rounding. A row at steps of about 0.17 reads well: lumps are still traceable between neighbouring frames (frame correlation about 0.75 to 0.79). Slots=1 does not loop but keeps lump identity for good.
motion.frames_show: Lumps sit at different heights and sizes across the row, and some can be followed upward. Some also fade out between frames, which is the slot cross-fade, so this is not the entry's 'never a fade' at Slots 3.
motion.identity_measured: Correlation of frame(t) with frame(t+dt) after the exact similarity scale about the cone apex: Slots=1 gives 1.000 (dt 1 and dt 0.2), Slots=3 gives 0.941 (dt 0.2). Plain correlation without the scale is 0.72 to 0.77.
motion.contrast_measured: Per-frame std 0.3735 to 0.3827 over the loop, a spread of about 2.4%.

origin.smallest_test: Source = Simplex FBm 3 octaves, Exponent 0, Spread 0.3: side XZ slice and a vol. Then a 6 frame strip for Exponent 0, 0.5 and 1 side by side.
origin.confidence: medium: lump scaling and coherent motion are guaranteed by the map. Whether it reads as smoke, not lumpy cone, depends on source and bias.

boil-pot.look: frames_vol (Sync=1, all columns on one phase) shows the stages clearly: round voids in the cut face at 0.45, swollen domes at 0.6, real holes in the surface at 0.64, craters at 0.7, ringed craters at 0.8, a nearly calm surface at 0.95. It reads as a mud pot or a thick soup. The image (free running, plan) shows white domes, dark craters with concentric rings, and a soft mottled base. In gray 2D it reads somewhat as stamps on noise, more than as liquid. Panels are normalised one by one, so overall brightness differences between them are not real.
boil-pot.dims: 2D (plan view of the surface) and 3D (density with voids) measured. 4D is not written; the entry would use w as Time.
boil-pot.range: 2D about [-0.87, 1.0] with clamp, mean near 0.01, std 0.09 to 0.14; 3D clamp to [-1, 1]. No NaN or Inf over 8 seeds.
boil-pot.artifacts: No spatial jumps: the jumps table shrinks with the step. No time jumps either. Overlapping events simply add, and the 3 by 3 window limit keeps ring waves small. Between events in gray 2D the surface is only the calm base. Sync=1 shows how regular the staged shape is, and should not be the default look.
boil-pot.node_shape: BoilPot: Feature Scale (Cell), Level, Bubble Radius, Burst Age b, Depth, Ring Amp, Wave Speed, Wave Frequency, Ring Width, Sway, Jitter, Density, Max Rate, Loop. Hybrid: Time, Base (calm surface; here a built-in two-slot Perlin).
boil-pot.port_notes: 9 hashes in 2D and 18 evaluations of column data in 3D in this scalar form, though a port reuses one set. No sqrt beyond r and one per sphere. Phase selection by masks: all stage terms are compact and multiply by smoothstep gates, so nothing needs a lane branch. Exp and Pow per column can be replaced by polynomials. Generation hashing with Loop=0 needs per-lane Floor of t*rate.

panel_over.maintainer: boil-pot: frames read as staged events, a scene and not a building block, and the per-frame low end swings from -0.26 to -0.87

master.one_liner: Real boiling as staged events: each column runs a bubble timeline, rising void, dome on the surface, pop, crater, ring wave, on its own phase with an exact time loop, and in 3D the isosurface truly opens when a bubble breaks through.
master.look: Mud pot, lava lake, thick soup. Bubbles rise as voids, the surface swells in a dome over each, the film opens, a crater collapses and a ring runs off. In 3D, a cut face shows round voids at many heights. Not the shimmer of 4D noise, since features have a beginning, a middle and an end. Judge from stills: strip of 8 frames on one column and a vol frame caught at the pop, where the surface has a real hole; frame 0 equals frame 1/rate with Loop on.
master.algorithm:
Column lattice in XZ, window 3x3. Per column: h = hash(col); site (cx,cz); rate = integer from a small table; age = fract(t*rate + rnd(h)); gen = Loop ? 0 : floor(t*rate + rnd(h)), mixed into h.
Burst at age b (about .7). R = R0*(0.5 + rnd(h,2)).
Rise phase (age < b): a = age/b; cy = y0 + (Ys - y0)*a^1.4; rB = R*(0.5 + 0.5*a); sway = S*(sin(5*a + ph), cos(4*a + ph))
Surface term:
  depth = Max(Ys - cy - rB, 0)
  dome(r) = 0.6*rB*exp(-depth/rB)*k(r/(1.6*rB))   // k(x) = Max(1 - x^2, 0)^3
  after burst, A = (age - b)/(1 - b): crater(r) = -0.8*R*(1 - A)^2*k(r/(R*(1 + A)))
  ring(r) = Amp*(1 - A)^2*k((r - c*A)/w)*cos(f*(r - c*A)), with c*A + w below 1 cell of window reach
Hs = Level + Base(x,z,t)*B + sum over 9 columns of those terms
3D density: D = Hs - y; for each column in rise phase, D = SmoothMin(D, |p - (cx + sway.x, cy, cz + sway.y)| - rB, k)
2D (x,y as plan): output Hs.
All terms fall to 0 at age 0 and 1, so the event cycles without a pop.
master.why_new: FlowNoise's Boil preset swirls in place with no events, by its own entry. RippleNoise's Rain mode has only rings that expand. LavaColumns has moving blobs with no surface and no burst. Nothing ties a rising 3D body to a surface response, and nothing in the graph can, because the phase must match per column.
master.simd_plan: 9 hashes, 9 sets of about 3 compact kernels, no sqrt except r and one per sphere. Estimate 6 to 8 ns in 2D and 10 to 14 ns in 3D, plus Base. Same in 4D with w as Time. Mask based phase selection, no lane branching.
master.continuity: C1 in space (compact cubic kernels inside the window) and continuous in time. SmoothMin of a void through the surface is smooth, topology changes on the isosurface are the intended event.
master.params: Feature Scale (column), Level, R0, b, Ys, y0, Amp, Wave Speed c, Wave Frequency f, Sway, Rate Table, Loop, Density. Hybrid: Time, Base (a calm surface noise, e.g. FlowNoise).
master.risks: Too few events reads as isolated stamps, too many as noise. The ring limit in window reach keeps waves small. Without a calm Base the surface looks dead between events.

measured.scalar_note: Measured on Eval2 (plan). Eval3 adds 9 more column hashes and spheres and was not timed. Params go through a string-keyed map per Eval, and I did not separate that cost.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: the entry's 6 to 8 ns in 2D and 10 to 14 ns in 3D, plus 2 Perlin evals for the calm base (about 2 ns). Not measured.

boil-pot.changed_from_entry: Dome to crater has a Blend crossover around b (0.05), and the void radius grows from zero at birth and closes at the pop. As written the entry's terms jump in time at age b and age 0, so the claim 'continuous in time' needed this. Rate comes from 1 + hash * MaxRate rather than a table. Calm base is two cross-faded Perlin slots, so it also loops. DomeK is 0.7 rather than 0.6 and hole width depends on it. Added Sync for the staged test and Cell for framing.

motion.statement: I did not see this move. The judgement comes from the still rows and from text measurements.
motion.best_range: Time 0 to 1 is one exact loop with Loop=1, since rates are integers. Time 0 vs 1 max abs diff is 1.5e-06 in 2D and 7.2e-07 in a 3D slice; 0.3 vs 1.3 is 2.6e-06 and 1.1e-06. Those are float rounding. Each column's event lasts 1 or 0.5 Time (rate 1 or 2). Pops take 0.05 to 0.1 Time, so steps of 0.02 or finer are needed to follow one: frame correlation at 0.02 steps is 0.93 to 0.96 away from a large pop and 0.65 to 0.77 across one, and at 0.167 steps it is only 0.08 to 0.30.
motion.time_continuity_measured: Largest change for dTime 0.001 vs 0.0001 at eight times, including across a wrap: about 0.05 vs 0.005, so it scales with the step and there is no jump in time.

origin.smallest_test: 2D Hs, one column made active, age sweep strip of 8 frames, then a 3D vol at b - 0.02 and b + 0.02.
origin.confidence: medium: each stage is simple, and I am fairly sure about event legibility, less sure it reads as liquid and not as stamped animations.

vortex-pair-billows.look: Read (2D, final defaults). Age row: soft puffs with stems at 0.2, caps with curled edges at 0.5 to 1.1, then clear spiral rims with several turns at 1.5 and 2.2. It reads as ink drops, jellyfish or small mushroom clouds, each a cap with two spiral tips and a tapering stem. Read at Cell 0.8 and at older settings (contact sheets): at high density the same shapes turn into a field of small icons, and an earlier sweep with no stem and a thin blob gave a clean arch with two line spirals, like a stylised cloud motif, at Age 1 to 2. 3D was seen only at older defaults (Cell 0.8 and 1.2): floating smooth bean or cap shapes. The rolled rim shows only on cut faces, so from outside it reads as pebbles, not smoke rings.
vortex-pair-billows.dims: 2D measured and good. 3D measured (ring form via the axial and radial half plane). 4D not written.
vortex-pair-billows.range: [-1, 1] exactly, mostly background: mean -0.78, std 0.51. No NaN or Inf over 8 seeds.
vortex-pair-billows.artifacts: No jumps: at defaults the jumps table shrinks with the step. Slopes get very steep as Age grows, because the flow folds the blob into filaments: Age 2 gives 1.19 at h=1e-3, 0.052 at 1e-4, and 0.0053 at 1e-5, and Age 4 gives 1.13, 0.31 and 0.034. These still shrink but are not usable for hillshade at high Age. Age 4 and above tears visibly at Steps 12 (seen on an early sweep). The field is mostly flat background (mean -0.78). Sparse fields read as clipart, as the entry feared.
vortex-pair-billows.node_shape: VortexPairBillows: Feature Scale, Separation b, Core Radius, Circulation, Age, Age Jitter, Size Jitter, Steps, Blob Aspect, Softness, Trail, Density, Up Bias, Texture amount and scale, Life Cycle (bool), Rise. Hybrid: Age, Time. Optional Source for interior texture; built-in sine of a Perlin here.
vortex-pair-billows.port_notes: Fixed loop: cells x Steps x 2 velocity evals, one Reciprocal per vortex. Union is a screen product, so no Max crease and no K-nearest switch. Comoving form means puffs stay at their cells and nothing leaves the window unless Rise is large: Rmax = 2.5 b stays under 1 cell, Trail + jitter must stay under the 3 by 3 reach. 3D needs one sqrt per cell and costs 27 cells unless b is small enough for Rmax < 0.5 and a 2x2x2 window.

master.one_liner: Smoke billows with rolled-up edges: scattered vortex dipoles each carrying a blob of smoke, so every puff is a mushroom cap with spiral tips (the Kelvin oval), in 2D and as vortex rings in 3D.
master.look: A field of mushroom-shaped puffs: each a smooth convex cap whose two edges curl inward into spirals, with a thinner stem behind; overlapping caps at different ages, young ones rounder, old ones with several spiral turns. In 3D, smoke rings and cauliflower cap tops with rolled rims. Reads as smoke, cumulus turrets, ink drops in water, nuclear mushroom clouds, and volcanic plumes; a Swirl output with an fbm Source gives marbled puff interiors.
master.algorithm: 3x3 window of jittered dipole centres C with hashed travel direction u (unit), half separation b, core radius rc, circulation G, age T (hashed in [0.5,1] * Age hybrid). The two vortices sit at C +- b uperp with opposite signs chosen so the pair propagates along u. Velocity of one vortex at offset d: v = (G / 2pi) * d / (|d|^2 + rc^2) rotated 90 degrees (Lamb-Oseen-like, finite at the core). In the frame moving with the pair (subtract the self-induced speed U = G / (4 pi b)) the streamlines inside the Kelvin oval (radius about 2.1 b) are closed, so a tracer blob that starts inside stays inside: this is why the influence region is compact and fits the cell. Multiply the pair velocity by a cutoff w(r) = (1 - (r / Rmax)^2)^2 with Rmax = 2.5 b so it vanishes before the cell edge. Per dipole: back-advect the sample q = p - C for N fixed steps (N int, 8-16) of RK2 with dt = -T / N in the comoving frame; read the initial blob: an ellipse centred on C, semi-axes (0.6 b along u, 1.2 b across), soft edge, value m = saturate((1 - ellipse)/soft). Optional Source read at q (any node) gives swirled interior texture, blended by m. Combine dipoles by Max over the 9 cells (each contributes 0 outside its cutoff, so no K-nearest switching). Trail output: capsule from C back along -u of length U T, radius shrinking, Max with the caps: a plume stem. 3D: each dipole becomes a vortex ring of radius b around axis u: for the sample, compute the axial coordinate a = (p - C) . u and the radial coordinate rho = |(p - C) - a u|; advect in the (a, rho) half plane with the ring's meridional field approximated by the same two 2D vortices at (0, +-b) plus the self-induced ring speed; the blob is a disc in that half plane, i.e. a torus-shaped puff that rolls into the classic smoke ring cap. 4D: w scales Age (puffs mature with w), exact looping not available.
master.why_new: DomainWarpShear Curling smoke and FlowNoise Stirred smoke give continuous swirly haze with no discrete billows; VortexCells is single vortices (no dipole, so no mushroom), ScatterWarp sums vortex stamps as a warp over whatever source lies there, which cannot give the Kelvin oval roll-up because the blob and the dipole are not co-located and co-aged. Co-locating a blob with its own dipole and integrating for a per-puff age is what produces the rolled rim, the universal visual signature of a smoke billow.
master.simd_plan: Fixed loop over 9 cells x N RK2 steps x 2 vortex evaluations (each ~10 ops with one reciprocal), then an ellipse test: 9 * 12 * 2 * 10 = ~2200 ops worst case, about 10-15x Perlin 2D at N=12; a Density mask skips nothing (worst case always paid) so Density only sets the look. Cheaper variant: only the nearest 2 dipoles by centre distance with a rank-subtract fade (StampScatter's trick), about 4x cheaper. 3D costs 27 cells unless the ring is restricted to the nearest 4 by a 2x2x2 window around the cell, fine because Rmax < 0.5 cell.
master.continuity: C1: smooth flow map, smooth cutoff, smooth blob; Max between puffs is C0.
master.params: Feature Scale, Separation b, Core Radius, Circulation (hybrid), Age (hybrid), Steps N (int), Blob Aspect, Softness, Trail (float), Density (hybrid, fraction of cells with a dipole), Source (optional, swirled interior), Output (enum Density, Swirl, Age).
master.risks: The classic mushroom needs enough steps (tearing at low N); a field of identical mushrooms looks like clipart unless ages, sizes and orientations vary and the Trail joins them into plumes; the 3D ring approximation is thin-ring theory and may look wrong for fat rings.
sources: Saffman, Vortex Dynamics (Kelvin oval of a vortex pair; thin vortex ring self-induced velocity), background only

measured.scalar_note: Measured, no early-out, Steps 12, on Eval2. Steps 8 measures 37.10x. Velocity evals dominate the cost. Eval3 uses a 27 cell window and was not timed.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 9 cells x 12 RK2 steps x 2 velocity evals x 2 vortices at about 10 ops per vortex is about 4000 ops, so 15 to 25 ns in 2D. Not measured. The entry's 10 to 15x Perlin looks low for the same count. The 2-nearest variant in the entry was not tried.

vortex-pair-billows.changed_from_entry: Union is a screen product (1 - (1-a)(1-b)) rather than Max, smooth and no extra cost. master.one_liner: An endless zoom on any source with an exact time loop: octave slots slide up the frequency axis under a constant-variance window, so features expand past the camera forever at N source evals, and every frame looks like every other.
master.look: A fly-in or fly-out through clouds, foam, cells or caves which never runs out of detail and never hits a fractal limit. In 3D isosurface frames, blobs grow outward from the anchor and pass the camera while new fine ones come up between them. With a cave density and an anchor at the view centre, an endless descent. For loading screens, portals, drug-trip sequences, screen transitions. Judge from stills: frames at t and t + 1/(N*Rate), zoomed by L: correlation should be high; std per frame is constant. Frame diff at t = 0 and 1/Rate is exactly 0.
master.algorithm:
N slots (int, 3 to 8), lacunarity L (2). Anchor a (float per axis). t is hybrid.
out = 0; norm = 0
for i in 0..N-1:
  s = fract(t*Rate + i/N)
  scale = L^(N*(s - 0.5))
  env = Sin(Pi*s)*scale^(-Slope)   // with Slope = 0, sum of env^2 = N/2 at every t for N >= 2, so contrast is constant
  out += env*Source(seed + i*Stride, (p - a)*scale + a)
  norm += env*env
out /= sqrt(norm)
Exact loop: s and scale depend only on fract(t*Rate + i/N), and each slot keeps its own seed, so t and t+1/Rate give the identical field. Axis Mask zeroes the scale on chosen axes, e.g. zoom only in x,z for an endless tunnel of a column field.
master.why_new: FractalFBm with an animated DomainScale runs out of octaves and DomainScale is not hybrid. FractalSpectrum gives a static equaliser of octaves. ZoomLoop's slots travel. It is a known shader trick for a single texture; as a meta-node on any source it is not available and cannot be made in a graph because scale has to depend on t.
master.simd_plan: N source evals, plus per lane Pow via Exp of s (constant t means a per-call constant, hybrid t means per lane). About N*source + 1 ns (estimate). Works in any dimension by parameter pack. Tiling is not preserved except when Period-based sources line up, so it is documented as not tileable.
master.continuity: C-infinity in t and C1 in space for C1 sources: a slot's amplitude is 0 at the moment it wraps. Spatial jumps of the source pass through.
master.params: Source, Slots, Lacunarity, Slope (0 flat, about 1 fBm-like), Rate (signed, zoom in or out), Anchor X/Y/Z/W, Axis Mask. Hybrid: Time.
master.risks: Far from the anchor the high slots move very quickly, aliasing unless Slope damps them. Slots are unrelated patterns, so a feature fades slowly while growing instead of keeping identity forever. Near-identical to a cross-fade if N is too low.

measured.scalar_note: Measured at 5 simplex slots with two Pow per slot and a string-keyed map read per Eval. I did not separate those costs.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: N x source + about 1 ns, so about 7 ns for 5 Simplex in 2D. Constant Time means the Pow values can be per-call constants. Not measured.

zoom-loop.changed_from_entry: Output is tanh limited, since the normalised slot sum reached about 1.8. Default Slope is 0.8 rather than 0, because a clean cloud look needs a falling spectrum. Default Rate is -1 so features grow. Added a Stride param (Seed Stride): Stride=0 gives a loop shorter by a factor of N. Axis Mask not implemented.

Use steps of about 0.04 or smaller to keep identity. Rate negative zooms in (features grow), positive zooms out.

phase-morph.look: Read (Mode 0 top row, plain value Fade bottom row, same sources). Top row stays black and white at every t, with bands intact. Bands in the top row shift across sharp thin slip curves that move through the picture, and these end at points. Bottom row shows grey double images with crossed moire at the middle frames. Vol is nested agate-like sheets with breaks where the bands reconnect. An earlier row with Vary=0 at t=0.5 had whole closed slip curves all at once, a cut-and-offset look.
phase-morph.dims: 2D and 3D measured. 4D not written; the code is the same in any dimension, and it would tile when its sources do.
phase-morph.range: [-1, 1] in Mode 0. Mode 1 reaches 1.002, because |z| can pass 1 when all weights are on and the sqrt(1+eps^2) correction overshoots slightly. No NaN or Inf over 8 seeds.
phase-morph.artifacts: No true jumps while Eps>0: the jumps table shrinks with the step. But slip curves are very steep, with max slope 150 per unit at Eps 0.08, and at Eps 0.02 c0 falls to 3.4 (jumps 0.454, 0.047, 0.0047), so a slip reads as a hard line at any normal resolution. Bands do not all glide evenly: most of the change happens in a thin moving front, which is a sharper look than the entry's 'bands glide'. Hillshading a slip gives a crease.
phase-morph.node_shape: PhaseMorph: Source A, B, optional C, D; Frequency, Mode (Pair, Loop), Epsilon, Output (Wave, Triangle, Duty, DefectMask), Phase Offsets, Sharp. Hybrid: Time. Vary works as a hybrid Time fed with a slow noise, and could be left to a graph if Time is hybrid.
phase-morph.port_notes: One Sin and one Cos per source, one InvSqrt. Triangle uses the polynomial atan2. Loop weights are one Cos per source, and are per-call when Time is constant. With Vary or hybrid Time they are per lane.

master.one_liner: A cross-fade for stripes, rings and bands that never greys out: blend unit phasors rather than values, so bands slide from A's position to B's and reconnect through dislocations, at constant contrast; with several sources on a circle it loops with no breathing and no extra dimension.
master.look: Wood rings, agate, contour bands, zebra and phasor patterns that morph: bands glide, pinch and reconnect, dislocation pairs nucleate, travel and annihilate, and the image stays full contrast all the way. Fade between the same inputs at t = 0.5 gives grey double images. In 3D, nested sheets slide, open holes and fuse, so an agate volume morphs like layers moving, not fading. Judge from stills: a 5 frame strip beside Fade; per-frame std must stay within a few percent, and no double bands may show. Loop mode: frame 0 equals frame 1 exactly.
master.algorithm:
For each of N = 2 to 4 sources: phi_k = Pi*Freq*Source_k(p) + Offset_k; (Cos phi_k, Sin phi_k)
Weights: N = 2: (1 - t, t). Loop mode: w_k = Max(0, Cos(2*Pi*(t - k/N)))^2 for N >= 3
z = sum w_k*(Cos phi_k, Sin phi_k)
out = Re(z)/sqrt(|z|^2 + eps^2)   // Wave output
Other outputs: Triangle from a polynomial atan2 of z, Duty via the Oscillator pulse shape on the same phase, DefectMask = 1 - |z|/(|z| + eps) which marks where bands reconnect.
At t = 0 this is Cos(Pi*Freq*A), at t = 1 Cos(Pi*Freq*B). At t = 0.5, it is the mean phase with sign flips on lines where phi_A - phi_B = Pi mod 2 Pi, and those lines are the dislocations.
master.why_new: Fade and ContrastFade work on values; even a variance-preserving fade shows both patterns at once. VortexPhase takes arg(A + iB) as a pattern, not a morph between two. Oscillator of a blended source moves bands too, but its wavelength depends on the blend's slope, and it cannot reconnect pattern to pattern because the blend's level sets are not those of either input. Graphing this takes about 10 nodes and 4 evals per source, against 1 here.
master.simd_plan: N source evals, one Sin and Cos per source, one InvSqrt. About N*source + 2 ns (estimate). Works for any dimension the sources do; 4D is the same code, so it tiles when the sources do.
master.continuity: C1 away from defects where |z| falls to zero, softened to a smooth dip by eps. A source with jumps gives bands with jumps. Discontinuous only if eps = 0.
master.params: Source A, B, optional C, D; Frequency, Time t (hybrid), Mode (Pair, Loop), Epsilon, Output enum, Phase offsets.
master.risks: Only meaningful for band-like output, it is not a general terrain morph. Low Freq gives cosine of a blend, which is nothing special. Near-identical A and B produce no defects, and the morph is uninteresting.

measured.scalar_note: Measured in Mode 0, two Perlin sources, plus one Perlin for Vary. Vary=0 measures 5.20x. Params go through a string-keyed map per Eval, and I did not separate that cost.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: N x source + about 2 ns, so about 4 to 5 ns for two Perlin sources in 2D. Not measured.

phase-morph.changed_from_entry: Two changes. With 2 sources z = 0 needs equal weights, so with a constant t every defect appears at t = 0.5 at once on whole curves, not as point pairs that travel. So I added Vary: a spatial spread of t by a slow noise, zero at t = 0 and t = 1, which is what a hybrid Time would do, and slip lines then end at points. Second, Loop weights are (0.5 + 0.5 cos)^Sharp, with all N on. The entry's Max(0, cos)^2 leaves only two nonzero weights at any time, which has the same whole-curve problem. Frame 0 in Loop mode is thus not pure source 0. Default Vary is 0.8. Offsets not wired.

Mode 0 (Pair): Time 0 to 1 is a one-way morph from pure A to pure B, and does not loop; with Vary 0.8 the middle (0.25 to 0.75) has the most going on. flame-licks.look: Gray: white-hot base fading to gray tongues that taper, lean and curl, with a few detached slivers above the tips. Threshold panel shows a clean flame silhouette. Through a fire ramp (bottom row of the image) it reads at once as stylised, slightly cartoon fire. It is not soft, photographic fire. Hillshade reads as leaves or grass, since this is not terrain. The wide view shows a straight bright ground line with flames along it. The spectrum shows diagonal streaks from the leaning tongues. An early Layers=1 test with strong swelling gave chains of teardrops, like beads; that was fixed by weakening swell at the root.
flame-licks.dims: 2D good. 3D measured and works, but through iso rendering it read as a field of spikes (seen small, at window 8, on an earlier contact sheet); fire in 3D needs a volume renderer, so this view is not fair to it. 4D not written.
flame-licks.range: [-1, 0.995] on the default frame. Mostly background: mean -0.66. Far from the ground it is flat at -1. No NaN or Inf over 8 seeds.
flame-licks.artifacts: No jumps: the jumps table shrinks with the step, and straddled c0 is 7.98. `jumps --window 1` is flat here and says nothing, since that window is above the flames. The smooth max gives soft joins but tongues still show faint darker seams where they cross. Lean plus warp could push a tongue past the window at extreme settings; lean is clamped, warp is not. There is no ground beyond a rounded root, so below the ground line the field falls to -1.
flame-licks.node_shape: FlameLicks: Height, Radius, Feature Scale (Cell), Layers, Lacunarity, Lean, Pinch Wavelength, Pinch, Taper, Swell, Swell Base, Rise Beats (int), Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Warp Scale, Warp Period (int), Softness, Smooth K, Output (Mask, Heat, Core, Signed). Hybrid: Time.
flame-licks.port_notes: Warp needs a Perlin with a wrapped axis for the exact loop; one int Modulus per lattice line. Heat does not use the tongue's u, so it has no index jump where tongues meet. Pow on (1 - u) can be replaced with a cheap polynomial. 3D window is 3x3 tongues per layer. A 2-channel warp could come from one eval with bit fields.

master.one_liner: A stationary wall of flame: tapered tongues that lean, wave more with height and pinch off into rising blobs, with detail that scrolls upward with a Time parameter.
master.look: Static: a row of flame tongues, fat and bright at the base, narrowing and leaning as they rise, with detached teardrop blobs above the tips; the threshold panel shows the classic flame silhouette with pinched tips. Animated by Time the swellings and warp travel upward, which is what makes it read as fire rather than tentacles. For fire walls, torches (single tongue, Count 1), burning edges (use any source as y via DomainMap), and in 3D for volumetric fire.
master.algorithm: Coordinates: x across (and z across in 3D), y up, Time t from a hybrid or w. Layers L (int, 1-3), each a 1D lattice of tongues along x with cell width C_l (lacunarity between layers) and a time offset. Tongue k of a layer: root (x_k, 0) with x_k = cell centre + jitter; height h_k = H * (0.6 + 0.8 hash); lean lambda_k in [-0.3,0.3] clamped so the tip stays inside +-1 cell; tongue axis from root to tip (x_k + lambda_k h_k, h_k). Radius along the axis r(u) = R * (1-u)^0.7 * (0.6 + 0.4 cos(2pi (u h_k - v t)/Lambda_k + phi_k)), u in [0,1]: the cosine makes swellings travel up the tongue at rise speed v; near the tip where (1-u)^0.7 is small the swelling minima pinch the tongue to zero so the tip separates into a rising blob (the pinch-off signature). Before the tongue test, warp the sample: p' = p + A(y) * (n1, n2) where n1, n2 are two channels of a noise sampled at (x / Sx, (y - v t) / Sy) with Sy = 3 Sx (vertically stretched, scrolling upward with t) and A(y) = A0 (0.3 + y / H) so bases are steady and tips wave (the flicker signature). Field f = max over layers and the 3 nearest tongues of (r(u) - d) where d is the distance from p' to the tongue axis (capsule distance, u from the projection). Outputs: Mask = saturate(f / soft); Heat = Mask * exp(-y / H) * (1 - 0.5 u) (bright base, cooling tips: users map it through a black-body ramp); Core = saturate((f - R*0.4)/soft) (inner tongue); Signed (raw f, for compositing).
master.why_new: No flame on any sheet. The usual graph (vertically stretched ridged noise times a height falloff) gives a glowing haze with no tongues, no taper, no pinch-off; Hook wisps (a FiberNoise extreme) gives curled wisps without rise or pinch. The signature here is the tapered capsule with travelling swellings whose minima break the tip, and height-growing warp amplitude; a graph cannot modulate a capsule radius along its own axis.
master.simd_plan: Per layer 3 tongues (the lean clamp bounds the window to 3 cells in x, 3x3 in 3D), one 2-channel noise for the warp (two Perlin evals or one Simplex with a seed offset), a capsule distance and a cos per tongue. 2D: about 3-5x Perlin. 3D: tongues root on the xz plane, 9 tongues per layer, about 8x Perlin 3D; Time from a hybrid; 4D: w as Time, so GenTileable2D loops the flicker exactly if v t wraps with Period (make Lambda_k = h_k / integer).
master.continuity: C0 at the max between tongues, C1 inside a tongue; the pinch makes the mask topology change (blobs detach) but the field itself is continuous.
master.params: Height H, Radius R, Layers (int), Lacunarity, Lean, Pinch Wavelength Lambda, Rise Speed v, Time (hybrid), Warp Amplitude A0 (hybrid), Warp Scale Sx, Softness, Output (enum Mask/Heat/Core/Signed).
master.risks: The static gray image may read as tentacles or stalactites; fire is largely motion and colour. Overlapping tongues under max give hard creases that need a smooth max. Lean plus warp can push tongues out of the 3-cell window at extreme settings (clamp).

measured.scalar_note: Measured on Eval2 at Layers 3. Layers 1 measures 8.61x. Params go through a string-keyed map per Eval, and I did not separate that cost. Eval3 costs 3 times the tongues and was not timed.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 3 Perlin evals for warp, plus 9 capsule tests with one Cos and one Pow each at Layers 3: about 8 to 10 ns in 2D. Not measured.

flame-licks.changed_from_entry: Radius: swelling grows with u (SwellBase), and pinch is a subtractive term in u^2 on the troughs. As written, r(u) stays positive so tips never separate, and strong swell at the root gives bead chains. Union is a smooth max at all times, as the entry's risk note asked. Heat drops the (1 - 0.5u) factor to avoid an index jump, using a core term from f instead. Exact loop: Beats and a wrapped warp lattice instead of Lambda = h/integer. R and height fall per layer, as finer layers with the same R swamped the shape. Warp also moves y a little.

motion.statement: I did not see this move. The judgement comes from the six still frames and from text measurements.

Steps of 0.04 read well: neighbouring frames correlate at 0.974 to 0.979 and tongues can be followed. At 0.1 steps it is 0.90 to 0.925.
motion.frames_show: Across Time 0 to 0.2, tongue tips rise and bend, tall tongues change shape, and at 0.16 to 0.2 a teardrop has separated above a tip. Tips appear to move more than bases; I did not measure that.

Then add A0 = 0.15 and render a grid over Time to see whether the blobs rise and the tongues flicker; if the static look reads as stalagmites, view it through a black-body ramp before judging.
origin.confidence: medium

aurora-curtains.look: Gray: many thin near-vertical rays over a dark sky, leaning toward a point above the picture, brightest just above a wavy lower edge and fading upward, with bright knots where the ribbon folds. Through a green to violet ramp on Height (bottom row of the image) it reads at once as an aurora. The dark region below the edge reads a bit like a mountain silhouette, because the undulating base is a hard limit. In the sheet, the XZ slice (x against the z time axis) is a separate striking image of flowing silk-like strands. The wide view shows fine dotted texture in rays at that scale.
aurora-curtains.dims: 2D is the picture. 3D measured, with z as a second time axis as the entry says: no real 3D curtain, no the volume, top-down views are not supported. 4D not written.
aurora-curtains.range: [-1, about 0.77] over the loop, and up to 0.61 over 8 seeds on the plain frame. Mostly dark: mean -0.88. std 0.126 to 0.214 over the loop. No NaN or Inf.
aurora-curtains.artifacts: No jumps: the jumps table falls about 8 to 9x per decade of step, a steep slope (max 78 per unit). Tap dependence is real and not solved: K=24 against K=96 differs by up to 0.345 (mean 0.027) and K=48 against K=96 by up to 0.217 (mean 0.012). Before the Newton read K=24 differed by up to 0.615, since fine rays were sampled at the taps and showed as evenly spaced ghosts, the entry's stated risk. Hillshade showed a dotted moire before that fix. The dotted texture in the wide view shows some undersampling remains. Rays are 1D in the ribbon, and only Tilt bends them, so they stay straight.
aurora-curtains.node_shape: AuroraCurtains: Fold Amplitude, Fold Scale, Curl Amplitude, Curl Density, Curl Turns, Ray Scale, Ray Contrast, Bundle Scale, Base Height (hybrid), Base Amp, Base Scale, Edge Sharpness, Fade Height, Taps K (int), Sigma, W, Tilt, Zenith X, Gain, Time Rate, Output (Intensity, Height above base, Fold density). Hybrid: Time.
aurora-curtains.port_notes: Fixed K taps, no window. 5 control samples each for fold, base and bundle, then Catmull-Rom per tap, so slow noises cost 15 evals rather than 3K. Ray noise is 1D with 2 hashes per tap, with gradients that turn at integer rates. Newton read needs a small local array of tap values per lane, which is allowed; it needs no search. The curl cell index differs per tap, so 2 hashes per tap. Exp and Pow per tap could become polynomials.

master.one_liner: Aurora as a folded luminous sheet: vertical rays indexed by a material coordinate along the curtain, a sharp bright lower border fading upward, and fold brightening that falls out of projecting the folded curtain, a 1D caustic.
master.look: A luminous band across the field made of many thin vertical rays, sharp and bright along a wavy lower edge, fading to nothing above; where the curtain folds the rays pile up into bright vertical knots and curls; between folds the rays thin out. Through a green-to-red ramp on the Height output it is unmistakably an aurora. Also usable as a stage-light curtain, drapery of light, or a sci-fi energy field.
master.algorithm: Coordinates: x across the sky, y altitude; 3D adds time z, 4D w. The curtain is a ribbon parametrised by s (position along the curtain in the ground plane). Its apparent screen position is X(s) = s + F * g(s) + sum over curl centres k of A_k * win((s - s_k)/rho_k) * cos(omega (s - s_k)/rho_k), where g is a slow 1D noise (gentle folds), the curl terms are local oscillations (a spiral in the ground plane seen edge on projects to a few back-and-forth folds, which is what the bright knots of auroral curls are), and win is a bump. Where X'(s) < 0 the sheet folds over itself and several s project to the same x. Rather than inverting X, splat the ribbon: for the sample (x, y) take K fixed taps s_i = x + (i/K - 0.5) * 2 W, i = 0..K-1 (W = max fold excursion, K = 24-32), and accumulate B = sum_i R(s_i) * E(y - base(s_i)) * bump((X(s_i) - x) / sigma) / K. R(s) = ray texture: a fine 1D ridged noise (spacing 0.01-0.03 of the field) times a slower 1D bundle envelope; E(h) = smoothstep(-e, 0, h) * exp(-h / Hfade) (sharp lower edge, long fade up); base(s) = slow 1D noise giving an undulating bottom edge; bump = Gaussian of width sigma (a fraction of W/K). Fold brightening is automatic: near a fold X' is small so many taps land inside the bump at the same x, which is exactly the caustic 1/|X'| density. Perspective: rays converge on the magnetic zenith; implement by sampling s at x + (y - y0) * Tilt * (x - x_zenith) / Width before the tap loop, so rays lean outward from the zenith. All 1D noises take time (z) as a second coordinate, so the curtain drifts and rays flicker; Period on the 1D lattices makes x tile.
master.why_new: No sheet has it. A graph would need rays in a material coordinate along a curve and a density that doubles where the curve folds: StreakSmear gives streaks in screen space, CausticWeb gives fold brightening of 2D maps but not along a ribbon with a vertical profile. The novel piece is treating the aurora as a projected folded ribbon and splatting it with fixed taps, so fold knots, rays and the sharp lower edge come from one cheap kernel.
master.simd_plan: Fixed loop of K taps, each: 3 cheap 1D lattice noises (ray, base, fold; 1D Perlin is 2 hashes and a lerp), one exp, one Gaussian; about K * 30 ops: K=24 is roughly 3-4x Perlin 2D. Dimension story: 2D is the picture; 3D is time; 4D w is a second time axis so GenTileable2D loops; no window search, no atan2.
master.continuity: C1: sum of smooth bumps times smooth profiles.
master.params: Fold Amplitude F, Fold Scale, Curl Amplitude, Curl Density, Curl Turns omega, Ray Scale, Ray Contrast, Bundle Scale, Base Height (hybrid), Edge Sharpness e, Fade Height, Taps K (int), Tilt, Zenith X, Time (z or hybrid), Output (enum Intensity, Height above base for colour ramps, Fold density only).
master.risks: Without colour it may read as a generic ray texture; the K taps band if sigma is too small relative to W/K (visible discrete rays that are tap artefacts rather than ray texture); the 1D model has no real 3D curtain so top-down views are not supported.

measured.scalar_note: Measured at K=24 with Output 0. Output 2 (fold density, no rays) measures 38.77x. Before the Newton read, K=16 measured 44.57x and K=24 57.33x. The first form with 4 noise evals per tap measured 133.75x.
measured.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 15 slow noise evals at control points, plus K x (2 hashes, 3 Cos and one Exp and Pow, curl) at K=24: about 25 to 40 ns in 2D. Not measured. The entry's 3 to 4x Perlin is far too low.

aurora-curtains.changed_from_entry: Four changes. (1) Slow noises come from 5 control points with Catmull-Rom instead of evals per tap: 133x down to about 55x Perlin. (2) Ray noise is 1D gradient noise whose gradients turn with Time at integer rates, instead of a 2D noise in (s, t): flicker is in place and loops exactly. (3) New: the ray is read at the true crossing of the ribbon via one damped Newton step from the tap (s - dX*X'/(X'^2 + 0.05), clamped to one tap gap), which reduces tap ghosts. (4) Fold, base and bundle wrap on a time lattice of TimeCells for an exact loop. Fold brightening is automatic as the entry says: fold density std goes from 0.26 at F=0 to 0.40 at F=1.5.

motion.statement: I did not see this move. The judgement comes from the six still frames and from text measurements.
motion.best_range: Time 0 to 1 is one exact loop at TimeRate 1 (0 vs 1 max abs diff 2.0e-06 in 2D and 3.2e-05 in a 3D slice; 0.13 vs 1.13 is 4.2e-05 and 2.1e-05; consistent with float rounding magnified by steep rays, which I did not separately confirm). The default is fast. Fine rays lose identity quickly: frame correlation is 0.57 to 0.67 at 0.03 steps and 0.29 to 0.50 at 0.1. The slow part, base edge and bright knots, reads well at 0.03 steps. Following one ray likely needs steps of about 0.005, or a lower TimeRate; that is an estimate from the correlation.
motion.frames_show: Across Time 0 to 0.15, the lower edge rises into a wider hump right of centre, bright knots shift and spread, and individual rays change.
motion.time_continuity_measured: Largest change for dTime 0.001 vs 0.0001 at Time 0.37: 0.185 vs 0.0195, so it scales with the step and shows no jump there, but rays change very quickly. I checked that one time only.
motion.brightness_over_loop: Per-frame max ranges from 0.006 to 0.77 and std from 0.126 to 0.214 over the loop, so the curtain brightens and dims. This is not constant.

origin.smallest_test: F = 0.3, no curls, K = 24: the gray panel should show vertical rays with a sharp wavy bottom, brighter where the bottom edge is sloping steeply (folds). Then add two curls and look for bright knots; if the rays look like a plain 1D noise stretched vertically, increase Fold Amplitude until folds overlap.
origin.confidence: medium

bedform-strata.look: Default section reads as cross-bedded sandstone: stacked wedge and lens sets of inclined foresets, each cut off by a curved bounding surface, thickness varying from set to set, some sets thinning out between neighbours. Smallest test: climb 0.1 gave climbing-ripple sets with only the lee laminae kept, climb 0.4 gave continuous laminae climbing over the crests with the stoss side preserved, the behaviour the entry predicted (I compared to the description, I did not view the USGS frames). Morph with no wobble or amplitude change does nothing, it needs amod to vary the sets. The 3D plan slice looks like wood grain: sinuous lines with eye-shaped closures, more than the U-shaped festoons the entry promised. The 4x wide view shows horizontal banding from the slow tone drift, which looks like bedding packages. Orientation: Eval2 has y up in world, and images grow downward, so the youngest sets are at the bottom of the picture.
bedform-strata.dims: 2D measured (vertical section, x along flow, y up). 3D measured (Eval3: check range -0.924..0.965, XZ slice in the sheet). 4D not written; an extra coordinate would only be passed to Bed, so it is cheap to add.
bedform-strata.range: -0.996..0.991 over 8 seeds/offsets, mean -0.055; far coords (4e4) -0.995..0.993, no NaN
bedform-strata.artifacts: Laminae output is discontinuous by design: proto_scan default real jumps 14991 crossings (seam length about 165), worst 0.902, all of which I attribute to lamina lines and truncations; hist in 0.4 bins 12210 2780 1 0 0 0. c0 and jumps confirm jumps do not shrink fast with h. Bounding output (out=2) is now close to C0: c0 plain 49.2, c0 straddled 1.04 with the 1e-3 step at 1.92 but 1e-4 0.0041 and 1e-5 0.00053, so slopes, yet proto_scan still reports 127 real-jump crossings (seam length about 1.4, worst 1.97) out of 38777 steep ones; I expect these at the tips where a truncation surface starts because a local minimum is born, which I did not confirm one by one. soft=1,bd=1 (no lamina step, full darkening on surfaces) gives 78 crossings, worst 1.33, jumps 0.656 / 0.172 / 0.017. Tap aliasing is not obvious at K=28 in the sheet; K below about 16 was not tried. Very steep lee faces need more taps.

master.one_liner: Cross-bedding as the exact deposit of a migrating bed: for any point, find the last time a moving, climbing bed surface passed it, with K taps and no stamps, so foresets, truncations, climbing ripples and trough sets all emerge from one height node.
master.look: Straight crest bed: climbing ripple lamination, sets of parallel inclined foresets stacked up the climb line. Sinuous crests with Morph: trough cross-bedding, festoon arcs on the plan face and scoops in section, sets truncating each other where the bed scoured deeper, as on Navajo Sandstone cliffs. Using BurgersSteepen as Bed gives steep slip faces and long stoss erosion. Sampled on a terrain, cliffs get coherent strata. In 3D a real solid: any slice is consistent.
master.algorithm:
Rubin 1987 and Rubin and Carter's Bedforms model: a fixed bed shape moves downstream and slightly up at each step, laying a lamina; where the surface cuts earlier laminae, they are eroded. Rubin's code marches in time over a grid. HOW IT BECOMES POINTWISE (my derivation): the rock at height y was laid at the LAST time the bed was at or below y.
S(x,t) = Bed(x - t*dir, MorphRate*t) + Climb*t   // bed moves one world unit per time unit, Climb is tan of climb angle
tau(x,y) = sup{ t : S(x,t) <= y }
If |Bed| <= A, then for t > (y+A)/Climb the bed is always above y and for t < (y-A)/Climb always below. So only t in [(y-A)/Climb, (y+A)/Climb] matters, with no global time and no start state, and the field is stationary in y.
dt = 2*A/(Climb*K); lastBelow = false; tb = t0; s0 = s1 = 0; low = +inf
for k in 0..K:   // oldest first
  t = (y - A)/Climb + k*dt
  S = Bed(x - t*dx, z - t*dz, Morph*t) + Climb*t
  below = S <= y
  cross = lastBelow & !below
  tb = Select(cross, t - dt, tb); s0 = Select(cross, Sprev, s0); s1 = Select(cross, S, s1)
  low = Select(below, +inf, min(low, S))   // lowest the bed got after the last crossing
  lastBelow = below; Sprev = S
tau = tb + dt*(y - s0)/(s1 - s0)   // linear root in the last bracket
Laminae = tone(saw(tau*LaminaFreq)) plus hashed tone for floor(tau*LaminaFreq)
Bounding = sat(1 - (low - y)/Width)   // goes to 1 on the truncation surfaces
Keep K about 16*A/(Climb*wavelength), so low climb costs more taps; that is the honest cost.
master.why_new: Different mechanism from the CrossBedding idea in raw_volume-and-time, which stamps scoops and fills them with a chosen lamination; here nothing is authored per set, and the laminae are the true past bed surfaces, so sets are as big as the bed's real scour and change with any bed node. The prototype that reads better should win. Other strata (StrataBands, StrataTerrace, FaultLines) have one lamination direction. The Half plane wave strata discovery has lenses but no truncation. A graph can't express last-crossing search with state across taps.
master.simd_plan: Fixed K loop with Select, no early out, taps per lane centred on y/Climb. No lattice unless Bed has one. 2D: x and y up, Bed sampled in 1 or 2 dimensions. 3D: full. 4D: extra coordinate passed to Bed; tiling only in plan. Cost K x Bed. Estimate with a 1-octave Perlin Bed, K = 24: 40 / 60 / 110 ns AVX2.
master.continuity: Discontinuous on purpose: Laminae and Age jump across truncations, as rocks do. Continuous inside a set. Bounding is C0.
master.params: Bed (required source, a 1D section in 2D, a plan map in 3D), Up Axis, Climb, Bed Amplitude A, Direction, Morph (morph rate through one more source dimension), Taps K, Lamina Frequency, Output (Laminae, Age, Bounding, SetTone).
master.risks: Tap aliasing at low Climb shows as staircase in tau. A wrong bound A gives wrong results silently; clamp the Bed. Fine laminae alias where tau changes fast. High total cost as a rock texture, and the look is not obvious from far away. I could not read Rubin's report PDF (403), so the claim that it matches comes from the model's description, not its equations.
sources: Rubin 1987, Cross-Bedding, Bedforms, and Paleocurrents, SEPM (not read, cited by the above)

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: K=28 taps x (one Perlin + one Value). About 45 / 90 ns 2D / 3D from handbook costs; 4D not written.

bedform-strata.changed_from_entry: 1) Taps locked to a lattice in t instead of sliding with y, so all heights at one x read one polyline. 2) The entry's low = min(low, S) marks a false line at every tap height on a rising limb, because the first tap above y counts; measured as about 23000 unit jumps. low now takes polyline local minima above y only. 3) The entry says Bounding is C0, but low alone is one sided and jumps across a truncation; added the younger side, y minus the local minimum the bed rose from, so both sides reach 0 on the surface. 4) Bed is an asymmetric wave sin(th - skew sin th) with Perlin phase wobble and Value amplitude variation in (s, morph t), not a Burgers source; amplitude variation is what makes sets differ. BurgersSteepen as Bed was not tried.

Then 3D with Bed = sin(x + 0.5*sin z), and view an XZ and a YZ slice for festoons.
origin.confidence: medium

cross-bedding.look: Read at the final tone (thumb): a stack of lens and wedge shaped sets, each filled with inclined fine laminae at its own angle, each cut by the smile shaped scour base of the next. It is immediately a cross-bedded section, somewhat like a clean engraving rather than a photo, since the laminae are very regular. The hillshade half is too busy to be useful because the laminae are fine, which is a value field shown as height. Read at previous tone (the image in the proto folder): the XZ plan slice shows overlapping elliptical scoops with ring laminae over straight planar stripes, so festoons do appear in plan, rings more than U shapes. The first render, with the entry's depth and per-cell dip, was mostly flat layers with rare bumps. The vol cliff test: the one vol I read had the wall facing away from the camera and showed only orange cut faces, so I flipped the wall and rendered again. A pixel count on it gives 19% lit non-orange surface, 18% orange, 63% background, which says only that a surface is visible, not how it looks. Whether relief reads on a cliff is not established.
cross-bedding.dims: 2D measured (the z = 0 vertical slice of the 3D form, with up = -y so that scoops are smiles in the picture). 3D measured (y up, check range -0.985..0.919, XZ slice read at the previous tone settings). 4D not written; the entry's w added to e2 and the dip dot would do it.

cross-bedding.artifacts: None measured at default: proto_scan real jumps 0, steep slopes 120805; c0 and straddle near 7; jumps shrink tenfold per decade of h, so all slopes. With w=0 (hard material boundary) it is discontinuous on purpose: c0 1.03, scan 2848 crossings, worst 1.364. Laminae alias if sp is small relative to pixel size; the hillshade already shows it at this window. Bugs found on the way, now fixed and measured: 460 real-jump crossings from dropping dv in 2D (rotated lattice row changes), 190 from a set search window that ignored the plane jitter.

master.one_liner: Cross-bedded sandstone as a vertical dead-leaves stack: each deposition set scoops a lens out of the older sets, fills it with its own tilted or trough laminae, and is truncated by the next set, so a cliff or slice shows real bounding surfaces with direction changing per set.
master.look: Vertical slice: stacks of wedge and lens shaped sets, nested smile arcs beside inclined parallel lines, each cut off flat or by a scoop at the next set. It reads at once as Navajo or Zion sandstone. Horizontal slice: festoon U shapes pointing downcurrent. On a 3D cliff, via a small density offset from Hardness, fine relief lines change direction at every bounding surface. Judge from stills: the XZ slice from a sheet, compared to a photo in the mind's eye, and a vol with Hardness * 0.05 added to a mesa density.
master.algorithm:
ys = y/SetH. Dmax = max scoop depth in sets, about 1.5. N = ceil(Dmax) + 2, a fixed loop, younger sets first.
j = ceil(ys + Dmax); hit = false; missMargin = BIG
for n in 0..N-1:
  rj = hash(j); (u,v) = Rot(table(rj))*(x,z)/LensL + offset(rj); v /= Aspect
  cell = floor(u,v); h = hash(cell, j); e2 = |(u,v) - (cell + 0.5 + 0.2*rnd2(h))|^2 / 0.25
  depth = Dmax*rnd(h,2)^2*sat(1 - e2)^2   // zero value and slope at the lens edge, confined to its cell, so bounding surfaces are continuous
  top = j + 0.3*rnd11(rj); bottom = top - depth
  inSet = ys > bottom
  take = inSet & !hit
  lamT = ys + TanDip(h)*dot((x,z), dir(h))/SetH   // tabular foresets
  lamS = ys - bottom                             // trough: laminae parallel to the scoop, festoon arcs
  lam = lerp(lamS, lamT, Foreset(h))/Spacing
  tone = saw(lam)*Contrast + rnd11(hash(floor(lam), j))*Vary
  value = Select(take, tone, value); above = Select(take, (ys - bottom)*SetH, above)
  missMargin = Select(!hit & !inSet, Min(missMargin, (bottom - ys)*SetH), missMargin)
  hit |= inSet; j -= 1
b = Min(above, missMargin)   // distance to the nearest bounding surface, from either side
out = lerp(BoundTone, value, smoothstep(0, W, b))
Outputs: Lamina (above), Hardness (for BedUndercut or a density offset), SetId, Bound (b).
master.why_new: Every strata idea so far (StrataBands, StrataTerrace, FaultLines, KnotFlow) has one lamination direction per region. This has several, in sets with erosional contacts. The Half plane wave strata discovery produced long lenses by accident, with no truncation or internal lamination. PebblePile and OcclusionStack are dead-leaves in plan; here the order is along y with an erosion rule, which also makes it window free.
master.simd_plan: N passes of one table rotation, one hash pair and a few ops, no window, no source. Estimate 1 ns per set on AVX2, 4 to 6 ns in 3D. 2D is a vertical section (x, y) with v dropped. 4D adds w to e2 and to dot(dir), which is enough for tiling to be continuous.
master.continuity: C0: both sides of a bounding surface fade to BoundTone inside W, and the surface itself is continuous because depth reaches 0 with zero slope at each lens edge. W = 0 gives a hard material boundary.
master.params: Set Height, Lens Length, Aspect, Dmax, Spacing, Foreset (0 trough to 1 tabular), Dip Range, W, Contrast, Vary, Output enum. Hybrid: Warp is left upstream.
master.risks: Laminae alias if Spacing is under about 2 voxels. A strong tell if all lens sizes match, so use a heavy tail. On its own it is a value field, not a shape, so it needs a density host to show in 3D.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: 5 sets x (3 lens lattices, each a hash and a few ops, plus one Perlin for the undulation). About 12 ns 2D, 20 ns 3D. und=0 removes the Perlin calls.

cross-bedding.changed_from_entry: 1) Foreset dip is per set rather than per cell: the entry's per-cell h jumps at each cell edge wherever two cells of a set meet above their lenses. 2) lam is continuous everywhere within a set and the lamina tone is 1D value noise in lam instead of a per-lamina step, so the field is really C0 at w > 0. 3) Three lens lattices per set rather than one, with a parabolic scoop (m instead of m^2, a kink at the rim like a scour edge) and r^1.5 depth rather than r^2, since the entry's version left most of the view flat. 4) Each bedding plane undulates with a low frequency Perlin rather than being one flat plane through the world. 5) Lamina spacing varies per set. 6) N and the start set account for the plane jitter and undulation.

origin.smallest_test: Eval3 with Dmax 1.5, Foreset 0.5, 5 sets in view: sheet, reading the XZ slice. If it shows one grid of lenses, raise lattice rotation per set before anything else.
origin.confidence: medium: I expect a very convincing vertical section; relief on a cliff may be too subtle at normal voxel sizes.

eigen-strata.look: Smallest test, Sep=1 Amp=0.6: three lines barely move and never approach, as the entry feared. At amp/sep from 1.6 to 7, most of all at 7, strands wander across the strip and at thumbnail size their avoided crossings look like crossings; zooming would be needed to see the veer. Section default: smooth wavy beds, thickness breathing, beds thinning to sharp tips between neighbours and reappearing, with laminae that crowd into each pinch. It reads as a tidy geological section, with big smooth shapes rather than rock texture. Volume vol: stacked wavy plates whose thickness varies, no plate ever crossing another. Gap: dark X shaped valleys with small conical pits. Outcrop: flat blobs with a few sharp cusps, not clearly better than a threshold. Beds come in groups of three inside a slab; I did not see the slab line in the Section thumb, because the top and bottom beds of neighbouring slabs share one tone.

Slab squash can flatten a surface against the slab line when amp is large; not measured.
