eigen-strata.port_notes: Eig3 and AcosApprox are branch free apart from the sign Select in acos. Row index via Floor, per-row seed and offset via hash. Soft squash keeps order in a row and keeps rows apart for any amp, replacing the entry's Blocks with an infinite stationary stack. Six noises could share one lattice pass via hash bit fields. A cheaper rival for real pinch-outs is base=2, cumulative max(0, thickness noise), three noises and no matrix; it has real zero thickness intervals and no repulsion.

master.one_liner: Beds that pinch out but can never cross: the ordered eigenvalues of a 3x3 symmetric noise matrix are three surfaces whose gaps vanish only on a codimension-2 set (random-matrix level repulsion), evaluated in closed form.
master.look: In a vertical section: wavy parallel beds whose thickness breathes, and now and then a bed thins to a sharp point and vanishes between its neighbours, then reappears further on, exactly like sedimentary lenses and pinch-outs; beds never intersect and never jump. In plan (Outcrop): bands on a map that merge at cusps where a bed pinches out under the surface. Gap output in 3D: dark threads (the degeneracy curves) with conical cross-section. The 2D Section mode on its own is a strand texture whose strands repel: hair or cable that gets close and bounces, never merging, a statistical signature (linear level repulsion) you can see.
master.algorithm:
Six noises m11,m22,m33,m12,m13,m23 (built in, Perlin or Simplex with seed offsets, one lattice pass if the shared-lattice trick is used) scaled by Amplitude, plus a fixed diagonal diag(-Sep, 0, +Sep) that sets the mean bed thickness.
Eigenvalues, trig form (Smith 1961):
  q = (m11+m22+m33)/3
  p2 = (m11-q)^2 + (m22-q)^2 + (m33-q)^2 + 2(m12^2+m13^2+m23^2); p = sqrt(p2/6) + eps
  B = (M - q I)/p; r = clamp(det(B)/2, -1, 1); phi = acos(r)/3   (acos by a short polynomial, no branch)
  l1 = q + 2p cos(phi); l3 = q + 2p cos(phi + 2pi/3); l2 = 3q - l1 - l3     (l1 >= l2 >= l3 always)
Modes:
  Section (2D): M depends on x only (1D noises along x); out = profile(min_i |y - l_i(x)|) or the bed index between the curves: three strands across the strip that approach and veer away (avoided crossings).
  Volume (3D, Up Axis): M from the two horizontal coordinates; u = up coordinate; bed = count(l_i > u) (0..3); out = rnd11(hash(bed)) or thickness l_bed - l_bed+1 or |u - l_nearest| for a bed-boundary SDF.
  Outcrop (any dim): u = hybrid Level (feed the terrain height) and M from the full position: bed index or thickness where that level cuts the beds, a geological map with real lenses and pinch-outs.
  Gap (any dim): out = l1 - l2 (or l2 - l3): >= 0, zero on a codimension-2 set (points in 2D, curves in 3D), conical there.
Blocks (int): stack Blocks independent 3x3 blocks offset by 3*Sep*k; eigenvalues of a block stay within q +- 2p, so with Amplitude bounded against Sep the blocks cannot cross either, giving 3*Blocks beds.
master.why_new: strata-bands and strata-terrace have per-band thickness that is constant along the band; fault-lines and growth-age move whole layer stacks; none can make a bed vanish between two others without a jump. The eigenvalue ordering gives non-crossing and pinch-outs as a theorem, with no sorting network and no per-point state. The 2x2 case is the mechanism behind tube-noise (gap = |(A,B)|), so this is tube-noise's maths promoted from one gap to a stack of beds. Nearest look: strata-bands (showcase family), but with lenses.
master.simd_plan: Six noise evaluations (2D for Volume mode, 1D for Section, full-dimensional for Outcrop/Gap) plus ~40 flops, one sqrt, one acos polynomial and two Cos: roughly 6x Perlin + 3 ns, so ~10 ns 2D, ~16 ns 3D. Branch free. 4D: Outcrop and Gap modes are dimension agnostic; Volume mode uses the three non-up coordinates. GenTileable works for Outcrop/Gap since the noises tile.
master.continuity: Each l_i is continuous everywhere and smooth except on the degeneracy set, where it has a conical point (C0, not C1): that cone is the pinch-out and is wanted. BedValue is a mosaic (discontinuous across bed boundaries by design); Thickness and BoundaryDistance are C0.
master.params: Amplitude, Separation, Blocks (int), Mode enum {Section, Volume, Outcrop, Gap}, Output enum {BedValue, Thickness, BoundaryDistance, Strands}, Up Axis, Level (hybrid), Feature Scale, Seed.
master.risks: Six noise evals per sample; at low Amplitude it just looks like parallel wavy bands; the acos branch-free approximation must be accurate near r = +-1 or the triple-degeneracy gives flicker. 4x4 blocks (Ferrari) would be a lot more code for little gain, so beds come in threes.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: six Perlin plus about 40 flops, one Sqrt, a short acos and two Cos. About 10 ns in Section mode (1D or 2D noises), about 16 ns for Outcrop and Gap in 3D, matching the entry's figure.

eigen-strata.changed_from_entry: 1) Blocks became an infinite stack of rows with per-row seeds and a monotone soft squash into each slab, so the field is stationary in y and rows cannot collide. 2) Bed tone uses a global bed id so the row boundary does not show. 3) Added laminae conformal to each bed via sin(2 pi n (u-lower)/(upper-lower)), which crowd into pinch-outs. 4) Surfaces darken fully to -1, so the mosaic is C0. 5) Section is M of the along coordinates only, as in the entry, with up = -y in 2D so higher beds are at the top of the picture. 6) Added base=1 and base=2 as honest comparisons.

origin.smallest_test: Section mode with Sep = 1, Amplitude = 0.6: render d = min_i |y - l_i(x)| over x in [0,16]; count how often two strands touch (should be isolated points, never a crossing) and look at whether the veering reads as organic or as mechanical. Then Volume mode as a vol render with an oblique cut.
origin.confidence: high that beds never cross and pinch at isolated points (linear algebra); medium that the picture beats a stack of offset noises in a side by side, since the repulsion is subtle unless Amplitude is near Separation.

burgers-fold-strata.look: Reads as a thrust belt cross-section: dipping asymmetric folds in thick and thin layers, with long back limbs and short steep fore limbs, and straight dipping lines where layers cut off against each other. Sweep read at shear 0, 0.6, 1.2: shear 0 gives offsets along vertical lines only (the entry's form, with no overturning); 0.6 gives dipping thrusts; 1.2 gives tight Z folds with overturned limbs, smooth in the viscous root and sharp in the locked root. Sweep read at t=0.7 and 1.4: 0.7 gives overturned folds; 1.4 gives imbricate sheets with long straight faults. Hardness output is hard to tell from Layers in the panels I read. XZ slice (a geological map view) is smooth closed contour bands, ordinary compared with the section. The 4x wide view has a toothy, fine repeating zigzag rhythm that is less convincing than the close view. Nothing on the existing sheet has this look.

The Burgers field alone (out=3) has real jumps of only 112 crossings (seam length about 1.2, worst 0.699, jumps 0.68 / 0.60 / 0.60), so at t=1 most of what looks like a fault is a very steep fold limb, and only short stretches are true shocks. Viscous root with line=1 is continuous: scan 0, c0 3.9, jumps 0.47 / 0.050 / 0.0048. out=1 Bands with viscous root: scan 0, c0 7.8. out=1 Bands locked: scan 64, worst 1.743. out=2 Hardness: scan 5354, worst 1.455, jumps 1.31 at 1e-5; the layer index feeding the mix adds jumps at layer lines. Lamina moire can appear on tightly folded limbs when shear is high.

master.one_liner: Burgers steepening on a strata depth coordinate: symmetric folds become asymmetric chevron and overturned folds with sharp limbs.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: thrust belts in cross-section, with asymmetric chevron and overturned folds.
master.algorithm: 1) Depth coordinate u(p) = p.y + FoldAmp * B(p) where B is burgers-steepen on a 1-octave Perlin or Simplex source with direction d along x and Time t (locked root, K taps); t below breaking gives steepening limbs, above it sharp overturned fronts. 2) Layer index k = Floor(u / Thickness), fraction f = u/Thickness - k. 3) Output modes: Layers = rnd11(hash(seed, k)); Bands = Terrace-like profile of f; Hardness = per-layer hash gating a Burgers viscous mode (mode=8) so soft layers get soft fronts and hard layers sharp ones, by lerping between the viscous and locked outputs with the layer's hardness. 4) Optionally feed through fault-lines afterwards (position updated family by family) for faulted folds. 3D: d in the xz plane, u = y + FoldAmp * B(x,z). Cost: Burgers (K source evals) plus a hash; use K=9 for the strata case since the source is one octave.
master.why_new: Fault-lines gives offsets along straight traces; Burgers gives smooth ramps ending in sharp fronts. Applying the shock to a strata depth coordinate turns symmetric sinusoidal folds into asymmetric chevron and overturned folds with sharp limbs, the look of thrust belts in cross-section, which no node in the tectonic family produced.
master.simd_plan: Cost: Burgers (K source evals) plus a hash; use K=9 for the strata case since the source is one octave.
master.continuity: Not stated by the panel.
master.params: Fold Amp, Direction, Time, Taps K (9), Thickness, Output {Layers, Bands, Hardness}.
master.risks: Seed risk 0.5: untested; K source evals.

burgers-fold-strata.changed_from_entry: 1) Added Shear: B is sampled at xi = x + s up rather than at x. With the entry's u = y + A B(x) every layer is a graph over x and can never overturn. With shear a lamina is a curve that folds back where 1 + s A B' < 0, and shocks become dipping thrusts. 2) Source drifts slowly with depth (vy) so folds change down section. 3) Monotone 1D warp of u for uneven layer thickness. 4) Hardness picks its layer index from the viscous depth to avoid self reference. fault-lines was not composed afterwards.

strath-valley.look: Meandering, entrenched canyons cut into a rolling plateau. On the inside of bends there are flights of flat treads in a few levels with steep scalloped risers tracing old channel positions, and levels are unpaired from side to side, as the entry predicted. The plan view shows a narrow black active channel with grey crescent treads at bends, and the age map read earlier shows stacked bands following the old channel. First attempt with bank slope 1.3 was just a broad straight trough with one bulge; slope 5 is what makes the scallops read. The 4x wide view shows the flaw clearly: evenly spaced parallel valleys, all in one direction, like corduroy, which a single window hides. Risers in relief show fine vertical combing, which I did not separate into tap gaps or render aliasing. With a smooth ease and K=24 each tap's level is a small stair rather than an inclined tread.
strath-valley.dims: 2D measured: height field. 3D measured: density hs*height + yo - y with no extra loop (check range -1..1, z continuity max 0.0064), which has no overhang since it is a height field. The volume rendered but not read. 4D not written; w would go into Drift.
strath-valley.range: -0.750..0.851 over 8 seeds/offsets, mean 0.227; far coords (4e4) -0.750..0.778, no NaN. The minimum is exactly top - inc.
strath-valley.artifacts: Height is C0: proto_scan real jumps 0, steep slopes 180, c0 8.0 plain and straddled, jumps shrink tenfold per decade. Age output jumps on purpose: c0 1.0, jumps 2.40 / 2.40 / 2.05, scan 4422 crossings, worst 2.4. Parallel rows at one spacing and direction. Valley walls must stay inside the row, and belt1 plus axis must be less than spacing/2 - margin, or the rim cuts them, which was not measured beyond default values. Height histogram has spikes at the tread levels.

strath-valley.port_notes: One row, fixed K. Value noise 2D per tap, Min and Select, no branch. Row hash and axis Perlin once per sample. Cost is mostly K value noises; the value noise lattice in x is shared across taps, so a port could fetch only the time-lattice column pair per tap. To break the corduroy without changing the kernel, feed the node a warped position, or use a large Direction field upstream, which this prototype did not try.

master.one_liner: A river valley with flights of scalloped terraces, as the minimum over time of a channel cutting down while it swings: a fixed loop over a meander's past, with no simulation.
master.look: A sinuous valley with a flat active floor, bordered on the inside of bends by flights of inclined treads, and bounded by scalloped risers that trace old meander loops. Unpaired levels from side to side. In steep settings, entrenched meanders. As an Age map: bands following old channel positions. Works in relief views.
master.algorithm:
Limaye and Lamb 2014 simulate bedrock valleys by a meandering channel with constant vertical incision and lateral migration; stepped strath terraces and slot canyons come from the rate ratio, and they report terrace slope proportional to vertical over lateral rate (that last part from their abstract as seen in a search result). They run a grid model. MY POINTWISE FORM: a point's final height is the lowest surface the river ever cut there.
(x,y) = Rot(Direction)*p; j = floor(y/Spacing); yc = (j + .5)*Spacing; h = hash(j)
H = Source(p); carve = +inf; age = 0
for k in 0..K-1:   // oldest first
  t = k/(K-1)
  Yk = yc + Belt(t)*N2(x*MeanderFreq + offs(h), t*Drift)   // cheap 2D value noise in (x,t)
  level = Top - Incision*Ease(t)   // Ease = t is the paper's null case; a stepped Ease gives clearer treads
  bank = Slope*max(0, abs(y - Yk) - ChannelW)
  c = level + bank
  take = c < carve; carve = Select(take, c, carve); age = Select(take, t, age)
rim = RimLift*max(0, abs(y - yc) - Spacing*0.5 + Margin)   // lifts carve at the row edge so H wins there, no seam
return min(H, carve + rim)   // Output Age gives terrace age for soil and vegetation masks
For a density in 3D: return min(H, carve + rim) - y.
Taps: K >= 2*Belt*Drift/ChannelW or the gaps between tap positions leave little ridges (a small height, Slope*step/2).
master.why_new: Different output. FiskMeanders draws plan-view scroll arcs and no incision. GlacialTroughs and ContourScarp follow a source's contours. DendryNoise carves a static tree. IncisedMeander puts overhang in a 3D canyon by shifting a centre with depth; it has no terrace surfaces and could share this path. A graph of 16 to 24 Min nodes with their own moving centres would work in principle, with no way to share the row, and no Age output.
master.simd_plan: One row, fixed K, value noise 2D each tap, Min and Select. 3D: density by subtracting y, no extra loop. 4D: w passes to Drift. No branching rivers: it is one trunk per row, so it composes with DendryNoise rather than replacing it. Estimate 25 ns plus Source at K = 24.
master.continuity: C0: Min of continuous functions, rim lift ends cleanly. Age jumps.
master.params: Source, Direction (global), Spacing, Belt Width (hybrid per row), Meander Freq, Drift, Incision, Ease, Top, Bank Slope, Channel Width, K, Output (Height, Age, Depth).
master.risks: With a coarse Belt it may look like stacked ribbons rather than terraces. One direction and one trunk per row makes it a feature, not a full terrain. Valley must be narrower than Spacing, or the rim shows. Real terraces depend on bank strength feedback that this omits.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured: K=24 Value noises plus one Perlin axis plus Source. About 25 ns plus Source, as the entry guessed; Source here is 5 Perlin octaves, about 6 ns more.

Default direction 0.9 rad so a valley shows along the relief view.

farey-terrace.look: On a 5 octave FBm in relief: a terrain with flats and ledges of unequal width, one wide flat level per period with narrower ones around it, finer ledges in between. Side by side with the stock Terrace formula at steps 6, smooth 0.6, the stock version has regular, contour-like steps of equal height everywhere, whereas this reads less mechanical but also has weaker steps; the hierarchy is subtle and not a dramatic look. Blend 1 versus 0.5 was a small difference. ModeLock K=1 is close to Minkowski. Snap q8 gives flat bands with sharp risers. Denominator is a noisy lace, fine white speckle and dark lines over everything, with bright closed lines at some levels: unusual but not attractive at this source frequency. Vol with dens=0.5: terrain with ledges and small shelves, read as a rough eroded surface. Ramp panel shows the staircase with its widest plateau near the middle.
farey-terrace.dims: Value modifier, dimension agnostic. 2D measured. 3D measured (check range -0.613..0.383, z continuity max 0.0063; vol with dens=0.5). A monotone remap cannot change any isosurface of its source, so a plain vol of it is the source's; terraces show only when added to something, hence the dens param. 4D not written; it needs only a 4D source.
farey-terrace.range: Tracks the source, not fixed: -0.860..1.000 over 8 seeds/offsets, mean 0.001; far coords (4e4) -0.750..0.750, no NaN.
farey-terrace.artifacts: Default has no measured seam: scan 0, steep 0. Tiny truncation steps remain: jumps at 1e-5 reads 0.00034 and does not fall by 10 from 1e-4 as a slope would, and I measured the raw ? on 4M samples: largest up step at depth 4, 8, 12, 16 is 0.0625, 0.0039, 0.00024, 0.00003, at 0.618, the golden ratio point, where all quotients are 1. So depth 12 has steps of 2.4e-4 of a period. Not visible. Monotone: 0 decreasing steps across 4M samples at all those depths. c0 reads about 5 rather than 8 for the same reason plus the devil staircase steep regions. Snap has real jumps by design: jumps 0.125 at every h, which proto_scan with its 0.2 threshold reports as 0, so its 0 does not mean continuous. Denominator: scan 147930 crossings (seam length about 1631), worst 2.0, by design. ModeLock scan 0, c0 3.15.

master.one_liner: Remaps any source through Minkowski's question-mark function (a fixed-depth continued fraction), giving terraces at every rational level with Farey-ordered tread widths (widest at 1/2, then thirds, quarters...) that are continuous and monotone, plus snap and denominator outputs.
master.look: A terrain through Minkowski mode shows broad flats where the source is near 1/2, narrower ones at 1/3 and 2/3, narrower again at quarters and fifths, down to the pixel, with steep risers between: rice terraces or travertine pools with a deterministic fractal hierarchy of tread widths, and no exactly flat set, since near p/q the function rises like 2^(-1/eps) (flat to float precision). Snap gives a hard-edged version, bands whose widths follow 1/q^2. Denominator paints the terrain by how rational its height is: smooth plateaus dark, slopes bright with a fractal lace of fine dark lines at every small-denominator level.
master.algorithm:
s = frac((Source - From Min)/(From Max - From Min)); s = clamp(s, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
Minkowski mode (continuous, strictly increasing):
  y = s; acc = 0; sgn = +1; e = 0 (int)
  for k in 1..Depth (Depth = 12, fixed):
    inv = 1/y; a = Floor(inv); a = min(a, 60)          partial quotient a_k
    e += a; w = float_from_bits((127 - e) << 23), masked to 0 when e > 126     2^-e with no Exp
    acc += sgn*2*w; sgn = -sgn
    y = max(inv - a, 1e-7)                                 Gauss map; at a rational y hits 0, a becomes huge and all later terms vanish
  ?(s) = acc, i.e. ?([0; a1, a2, ...]) = 2 * sum_{k>=1} (-1)^(k+1) 2^-(a1+...+ak)
  out = lerp(s, ?(s), Blend) remapped to the output range
Snap mode (discontinuous Farey mosaic): track convergents p_k = a_k p_{k-1} + p_{k-2}, q_k likewise, freeze with a mask once q_k > Qmax; out = p/q.
Denominator mode: out = log2(q of the last convergent with |s - p/q| < Tol)/log2(Qmax): 0 on the plateaus at low rationals, 1 near the noble irrationals: a 'how rational is the source here' roughness map.
ModeLock mode (optional, costly): finite-time rotation number of the circle map theta += Omega + (K/2pi) sin(2 pi theta) with Omega = s and K a hybrid, N = 32 iterations: Arnold tongues, i.e. the same Farey staircase but with plateau widths that grow with K and curved tongue borders.
master.why_new: Terrace steps are uniform; strata-terrace hashes per-layer thickness; cdf-remap is a monotone remap with a designed histogram; feigenbaum-remap iterates a map but has no level hierarchy. Here the step hierarchy is the Farey order itself, exact at every scale, monotone, continuous and parameter free, something no hashed or sampled terrace can produce. The Denominator output has no relative at all.
master.simd_plan: Depth iterations of a reciprocal, a Floor, an int add, an int shift and two FMAs: ~0.6 ns per step, so ~7 ns at Depth 12 on top of the source; no memory, no window, fully branch free. ModeLock costs N Sin, ~30 ns, hence optional.
master.continuity: Minkowski: continuous and strictly increasing (C0, derivative 0 almost everywhere, infinite at noble numbers). Snap: discontinuous by design. Denominator: piecewise constant. The float CF loses digits after about 7 quotients but those terms are already below 2^-7 of the range unless all quotients are 1, where Depth 12 leaves a 1e-3 error.
master.params: Mode enum {Minkowski, Snap, Denominator, ModeLock}; Depth (int); Blend (hybrid); From Min/Max, output range; Qmax (int) for Snap/Denominator; Tol; Lock Strength K (hybrid) for ModeLock. Dimension agnostic (value modifier).
master.risks:
Far from rationals the function is almost flat too, so a source that rarely visits low rationals gives mostly featureless slopes; the big flats at 1/2 may dominate; Snap bands alias.

extra_measured.flagged_problem: CONFIRMED and FIXED. The entry's frac wraps: wrap=2 measures a real jump of exactly the From span where the source leaves the range: at the default From -0.25..0.25, proto_scan 6001 crossings (seam length about 66), worst 0.500, jumps 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.5, c0 1.0. At From -0.75..0.75 it is 48 crossings (seam length about 0.53), worst 1.500. Fix: the periodic extension ?(n + f) = n + ?(f), remapped back to source units. It agrees with ? on [0,1] and, since ?(0) = 0 and ?(1) = 1, is continuous and strictly increasing on the whole line. wrap=1: proto_scan 0 real jumps at both From ranges, c0 about 5. A bonus: From no longer has to bracket the source, and a short From range now gives a repeating staircase, which is the default here. wrap=0 (clamp) is also jump free, scan 0, but flattens outside From.

master.one_liner: A fractal whose anisotropy changes with scale, after Schertzer and Lovejoy's generalized scale invariance: flat lenses at big scales rounding off to isotropic grain at small ones, with an optional twist per octave, the thing a stretched FBm gets wrong.
master.look: In a side view: long thin bands at the coarse level with grain that gets rounder as it gets finer, like sedimentary rock faces, cloud decks and ice. In plan view: ordinary FBm, or with Twist a cross-laminated mix of directions by scale. No streak blur in fine detail, which is what makes DomainAxisScale(FBm) look like motion blur.
master.algorithm:
GSI and operator scaling: a field scales under a matrix exponent rather than a number, X(lambda^E x) has the law of lambda^H X(x) (Bierme et al.; the diag(beta1, beta2) case in the aggregation paper I read). Schertzer and Lovejoy use this for atmospheric stratification, with effective dimension 23/9. I read an abstract, not their simulation recipe; their FIF model is a multiplicative cascade, and I drop that part and use additive octaves.
for n in 0..Octaves-1:
  sh = L^n   // frequency along the beds
  sv = L^(n0 + (n - n0)*E)   // E < 1: across-bed frequency grows more slowly. At n0 (sphero-scale) sv = sh; for n < n0, lenses
  if RoundFine and n > n0: sv = sh
  q = RotAboutUp(n*Twist)*(along = p.h*sh, up = p.v*sv)
  out += g^n*Source(q, seed + n)
E = 1 gives FBm of a fixed stretch. Normalise as FractalFBm.
master.why_new: Hard made easy and one honest admission: it can be built from stock nodes as Add over N DomainAxisScale chains, around 2N nodes, so a dedicated node is justified only by convenience and the fractal members. FractalSpectrum changes which scales are present, not their shape. FractalSlopeAligned needs a source gradient. The look difference from a fixed stretch should be clear on cliffs, but plan views gain little.
master.simd_plan: Octave loop, per-octave scale table computed when params are set. No extra cost beyond FBm, plus 2 mul per octave. 2D: x and y with y up. 3D and 4D direct. Tiling: per-axis non-integer scales break Period; the 4D route still works.
master.continuity: Same as Source; C0 or better.
master.params: Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain (hybrid), Sphero Octave n0 (float), Exponent E, Round Fine, Twist (radians per octave), Up Axis, Source. Keep the Up Axis enum, not free rotation.
master.risks: May look like plain FBm to a judge at thumbnail size. The published model is a cascade, so this is only in the spirit of it. Graph-reachable, so it may be downgraded to a recipe, which would be a fine outcome.

flow-shock-scales.look: Radial angle: a succulent rosette or pine cone seen from above, petal shaped scales, each with a smooth back and a sharp pointed lip facing outward, around a round centre cell. Spiral: the same with whorled petals. Perlin flow 3: patches of scales leaning in different directions. Time sweep read at 0.3, 0.7, 1.2: 0.3 is still round cells, 0.7 is pointed scales, 1.2 is long shards. In the 4x wide view scales become fine studs with a visible radial grain. Unlike flow-shingle, whose code stamps shapes (I did not view its images), this is a height field whose smooth ramps end in lips. The viscous root keeps the rosette with soft rounded lobes. Hillshade of the close view shows the lip edges slightly serrated, and the viscous hillshade shows fine tap ripples across the lobes.

flow-shock-scales.artifacts: Lips are real jumps by design in the locked root: proto_scan 2989 crossings (seam length about 33), worst 1.406; c0 about 1.0; jumps 1.40 / 1.29 / 1.12. The per-lane direction adds no measurable seam of its own: fixed direction field=3 at the same t scans 3043 crossings (seam length 33.5), Perlin flow 3 scans 3114 (34.3). The caveat about the tap line bending between neighbours did not show as tearing at flow=3, ff=0.2. Viscous root: scan 0, steep 100, c0 3.8, jumps 0.085 / 0.0085 / 0.00085, so it is really C0. Serrated lip edges in hillshade near the shock, probably because the tap lattice phase depends on the lane's direction; not separated, and higher K was not viewed. Radial centre has a singular direction: a small round cell there with a visible point, and direction is undefined at the exact centre (guarded by 1e-4). Streamline taps (stream=1) were worse: fine comb on the hillshade and twice the cost, so straight lines stay.

master.algorithm: 1) theta = Angle hybrid source at p (constant or node), d = (cos theta, sin theta). 2) Hopf-Lax with locked root over K taps (K=13 int member) along d: for i in -K/2..K/2, q_i = p - d * (i * Time * TapSpacing), evaluate source u_i = CellularDistance F1 (or any Source) at q_i, candidate cost c_i = |q_i - p|^2 / (2 Time) + U_i where U_i is the trapezoid-integrated potential along the taps as the prototype does; pick the minimising i with the locked-root rule (prototype mode=7), all taps evaluated for every lane. 3) Output the source value at the chosen root, scaled; Viscous mode (mode=8) for a continuous version. 4) Because d varies per lane the tap line bends slightly between neighbours; keep Angle sources smooth (the same caveat flow-shingle already carries) and clamp Time so the shock reach stays under the Angle field's wavelength. 2D and 3D (d from a 3D angle pair). Cost: K source evaluations, so about 13x Cellular at K=13: a material node, flagged expensive.
master.why_new: The imbricate-scales discovery (Burgers on a Worley source) is the best scale texture in the set but has one fixed direction for the whole field. Flow-shingle's per-lane angle field is exactly the missing ingredient: scales whose sharp lips face downstream of a flow (fish skin round a body, pine cone spirals, roof tiles round a dome).
master.simd_plan: Cost: K source evaluations, so about 13x Cellular at K=13: a material node, flagged expensive.
master.continuity: 3) Output the source value at the chosen root, scaled; Viscous mode (mode=8) for a continuous version.

gerstner-sea.look: Gray: long wavy crest lines running roughly across the wind, bright and sharp, over broad dull troughs, with short-crested breaks and a fine diamond dimple from the short waves crossing. Foam panel: smeared bands lying only on the strongest crest segments, with empty water between them. Time moves the crests between t0 and t3, and the pattern changes rather than scrolling. Smallest test with N=6, M=3, steep 0.8: crests sharp and det J dipping along them, so the mechanism works. Relief view, which uses the terrain colour ramp, reads as a ridged landscape with lakes, not water, so a water colour ramp is needed to sell it there.

It is not a spatial 3D form, so no. 4D not built, because the harness has no Eval4. Tile probe measured: period=8 gives a height difference across one period of at most 0.003 (out=91).

gerstner-sea.artifacts: proto_scan real jumps: 0 (defaults, worst 0.000, steep slopes 98) and 0 (form=1, steep slopes 979). jumps table shows slopes only. A fixed K damped Picard is a composition of smooth maps, so it has no branch seams even at steep above 1. The price: at steep 1.8 it is not the true inverse near folds. Height at K=3 differs from K=12 by up to 0.598 of output scale (K=2 0.728, K=4 0.512), mean 0.6 percent, always at crests, so crest shape depends on K. Entry's smallest-test convergence target fails for Picard: at steep 0.9, N=6, K=2 against K=4 peaks at 0.18 (mean 0.5 percent). Newton K=3 at steep 0.9 passes (0.004 against K=12) but at steep 2 it goes unstable (-0.707..1.245), so it stays off by default. Foam bands show ladder-like cross bars from the streak noise (seen in the foam panel). Max slope 27.5 per unit. The stat axis 33 is the intended wind anisotropy.

master.one_liner: Open water with trochoidal (Gerstner) crests and whitecaps, evaluated pointwise by inverting the horizontal displacement, with foam from the displacement Jacobian and wind-streaked foam trails.
master.look: Long, roughly parallel sharp crests with broad rounded troughs, short-crestedness from the directional spread, and whitecaps that appear only at the steepest crest segments, smeared downwind into streaks. Hillshade reads as a wind-driven sea rather than as a bumpy noise; the threshold panel shows thin crest lines. Animates by Time with correct dispersion (long waves faster). Good for oceans, lakes, and as a base for CausticWeb refraction. ChoppyOcean adds a Caustic output from the same map, so height, whitecap mask and caustic line up.
master.algorithm:
Setup (when params change): N wave components (N int, 6-16). Direction of wave i: wind angle + spread * (hash01(i)*2-1) (radians). Wavenumber k_i = k0 * lacunarity^i scaled by a hashed factor in [0.85,1.15]. Amplitude a_i so that per-wave steepness Q_i = a_i * k_i = Steepness / N (sum of steepness stays below 1, which keeps the inversion a contraction). Phase phi_i = hash. Angular frequency omega_i = sqrt(g * k_i) (deep water dispersion), g = 1 in noise units. Tileable form: pick k_i vectors on the integer lattice 2pi/Period * (m, n) nearest to the wanted vectors.  Gen(p): material point q must satisfy X(q) = p where X(q) = q - sum_i Q_i/k_i * khat_i * sin(k_i . q + phi_i + omega_i * t) (Gerstner horizontal displacement, t = hybrid Time or the w/z coordinate). Solve by fixed Picard: q0 = p; repeat M (int, 2-4) times: q = p + sum_i Q_i/k_i * khat_i * sin(theta_i(q)). Then height H = sum_i a_i * cos(theta_i(q)). Jacobian of X at q: J = I - sum_i Q_i * cos(theta_i) * (khat_i khat_i^T); det J in 2D closed form from the four sums (Sxx = sum Q cos * kx*kx, Sxy, Syy): det = (1-Sxx)(1-Syy) - Sxy^2. Foam F = saturate((FoamThreshold - det J) / FoamSoft): zero on gentle water, positive where the surface compresses at crests (det -> 0 is the classic breaking criterion). Whitecap texture: F * (0.5 + 0.5 * anisotropic noise N_w sampled at (p . windhat * 0.25, p . windperp * 3)) so foam is streaked along the wind. Foam trail: F_trail = max over S=3 taps s in {1,2,3} of F(p + windhat * s * TrailStep) * decay^s (this re-runs the sums at 3 extra points, so S small). Outputs enum: Height, Foam, Combined (Height + FoamLift * F_trail), Jacobian (raw det J, useful as a mask), Slope (|grad H| from the same sums: dH/dq = -sum a_i k_i sin(theta_i) khat_i, world slope = dH/dq * J^-1).

MERGED FORM ChoppyOcean (artist-material lens, crossbreed seed #21), same mechanism, kept in full: Table built when params are set: M plane waves with k_i from a wind angle and cos^2 spread, geometric wavelengths, a_i from a spectrum, w_i = sqrt(g*|k_i|). Optional Period snaps k_i to integer multiples of 2pi/Period for exact tiling without the 4D torus. Seed hashes once to a domain offset. Gen: x0 = p. Constant loop K times: theta_i = dot(k_i, x0) + w_i*T; G = sum(-a_i*k_i*sin theta_i); x0 = p - c*Chop*G, with c the CausticWeb damping 1/(1+0.6*Chop*Hmax). One final pass at x0: h = sum(a_i*cos theta_i), Hessian H = sum(-a_i*cos theta_i*k_i*k_i^T), J = I + Chop*H, detJ. Output enum: Height = h/sum(a_i); Foam = smoothstep(f0, f1, -detJ); Caustic = (eps + |detJ|)^-gamma. No lattice, no window, one code path per lane. 2D is the base form; 3D adds z to T, so a slice is an animation frame; 4D adds w as a second phase term. Risks: the fixed point can change branch at high Chop and lose continuity; direction chains appeared at N=8 in wave-noise-sliced, so M needs about 16. Cost ESTIMATE from the reported N=16 plane-wave figure of 12.5-15 ns per pass: 25-30 ns at K=1, 50-60 ns at K=3.

Merge note: both forms are a plane-wave table, a fixed-point inversion of a horizontal displacement, height from the same sums, and foam from det J. GerstnerSea's why_new calls ChoppyOcean a different mechanism, but round2_seeds.md prints no algorithm for ChoppyOcean, and the one in panel.json is this mechanism. The one real difference: GerstnerSea displaces by a_i*khat_i*sin theta_i (a true trochoid) and ChoppyOcean by the height gradient a_i*k_i*sin theta_i, so ChoppyOcean's displacement of each wave also scales with |k_i|. Prototype both displacements.
master.why_new:
Nothing on the sheets is an open water surface: WaveNoiseSliced and SineFold are sums of symmetric sines (rounded crests, no breaking), BurgersSteepen is one-sided shock steepening, not trochoid crests, and Ripple/RadialPhasor are circular. Crossbreed 21 ChoppyOcean names caustic-web + burgers + wave-noise-sliced as parents but no mechanism; this is a different mechanism: Gerstner kinematics with the displacement inverted per lane (the trick BurgersSteepen already proves works) and whitecaps from det J, which is the physically motivated breaking criterion and comes free from the same sums.
Merge correction to the text above: this is not a different mechanism from ChoppyOcean. See the merge note in the algorithm.
ChoppyOcean: The set has the light under water but no water. One map gives height, whitecap mask and caustic from the same waves, so they line up, and Time is a hybrid input. Not built, look unverified.
Seed gap: no water surface anywhere; queue gap too.
master.simd_plan:
Branch free: a fixed loop of M iterations over N components; each component is one sincos (Sin and Cos of the same angle) plus a handful of FMAs; component constants live in small per-node arrays. 2D is the native form; 3D uses z as Time (an animating sea) or, with a flag, treats the third axis as depth and attenuates H by exp(k z) (true orbital decay, giving a volumetric water band); 4D: w as Time on the tileable lattice so GenTileable2D loops. Cost: N=8, M=3 is 24 sincos + ~150 FMAs, about 4-6x Perlin 2D; trail taps multiply by 1+S.
ChoppyOcean: Cost ESTIMATE from the reported N=16 plane-wave figure of 12.5-15 ns per pass: 25-30 ns at K=1, 50-60 ns at K=3.
master.continuity:
C1: the Picard fixed point of a smooth contraction is smooth; det J and the foam saturate are continuous.
ChoppyOcean: Risks: the fixed point can change branch at high Chop and lose continuity; direction chains appeared at N=8 in wave-noise-sliced, so M needs about 16.
master.params: Steepness (float 0-1, total Q), Waves N (int), Wavenumber (float, Feature Scale), Lacunarity, Wind Angle (hybrid), Spread (float, radians), Time (hybrid), Iterations M (int), Foam Threshold, Foam Softness, Trail Steps (int 0-3), Trail Length, Period (int) for tiling, Output (enum). From ChoppyOcean: Chop, damping c = 1/(1 + 0.6*Chop*Hmax), wind angle with cos^2 spread, geometric wavelengths, a_i from a spectrum, fixed-point iterations K, f0, f1, gamma, eps, Output adds Caustic = (eps + |detJ|)^-gamma, Period snapping k_i to integer multiples of 2pi/Period. 3D adds z to T, 4D adds w as a second phase term.
master.risks:
Steepness near 1 makes Picard converge slowly and crests wobble; with few waves the field looks too regular (needs N >= 8 and wavenumber jitter); raw det J foam is a thin line, the trail smear and the streak texture are what make it read as whitecaps.
ChoppyOcean, seed risk 0.5: fixed point may change branch at high Chop. Risks: the fixed point can change branch at high Chop and lose continuity; direction chains appeared at N=8 in wave-noise-sliced, so M needs about 16.
sources: Tessendorf, Simulating Ocean Water (SIGGRAPH course notes 2001, Gerstner waves and the Jacobian folding criterion)
Fournier and Reeves, A simple model of ocean waves, SIGGRAPH 1986

extra_measured.form_comparison: Trochoid (form 0, GerstnerSea) reads better as water. With the same height spectrum (slope 1.2) and the same total strain, form 0 keeps the strain on the long crests: det J dips along long connected lines and foam falls on a few big crest segments. Form 1 (ChoppyOcean, displacement by the gradient) gives most of the strain to the shortest waves: det J becomes a fine regular dot and tick pattern over the whole image, foam is scattered short ticks everywhere, and the crests look fuzzier in gray. By the algebra, form 1 with slope=2 has the same displacement as form 0 with a flat strain share, but that setting was not rendered, so nothing is claimed about how it looks.

kelvin-wakes.look: Single site: a textbook Kelvin wake. The wedge edge sits on the exact 19.47 degree guide lines, with curved transverse crests across the middle and fine slanted divergent crests along both arms, finest towards the centre. Lattice default: a few parallel V feathers on flat gray, each with a sharp bright apex, about the same size, fading out by the window. They overlap downstream without a visible cell boundary. It reads as a fleet or a stream with obstacles rather than as a water surface on its own, because of the flat gray between wakes and the common direction. Over the demo plane waves the wakes stay legible, but those waves were too strong and the result reads as stripes on blotches, not yet as convincing water.
kelvin-wakes.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured with z as depth: each crest family decays at its own wavenumber, exp(-sec^2(psi) |z| / F2). At the physical dk=1 the decay is so fast that the check's z probe reads exactly 0 (min 0, max 0), and the depth 0.03 panel is visibly dimmer with the feather gone first. With dk=0.02 the check reads -0.781..0.805 and z-continuity max 0.0006. It is real but rarely useful, so no. 4D not built, because the harness has no Eval4.
kelvin-wakes.range: -0.949..0.960 over 8 seeds and offsets, mean 0.000, std 0.18 on the sheet. Soft clip s/sqrt(1+s^2). Flat 0 where no wake reaches.
kelvin-wakes.artifacts: proto_scan real jumps: 0 (worst 0.000, steep slopes 12054). jumps table shows slopes only. Max slope 178 per unit from the divergent crests before the T fade, so it will alias at small feature scale. Raising T0,T1 to 0.2,0.3 did not lower the h=1e-3 step (still 0.17656), so the steepest slope is not from the centreline fade; its cause was not traced. Near field is deliberately hidden by X0. All wakes run one way, plus or minus the yaw, so a field looks stamped.

master.one_liner: Closed-form Kelvin ship wakes per site: the 19.47 degree wedge with transverse and divergent feathered crests, from the stationary phase formula with no atan, for rocks in a stream, boats and duck trails.
master.look: V-shaped feather patterns trailing each site, fine crests slanting off the two arms and shorter curved crests across the middle, overlapping downstream. With high Div it is a duck wake, with high Trans a slow barge. Over CausticWeb or GerstnerSea, a river or sea with traffic. Reads at once as water with something moving through it. Near a Stamp rock, a stream past stones.
master.algorithm:
From arXiv 2205.01870 eqs (2), (21)-(23): phase r*g(psi;theta) with g = k0*cos(psi + theta), k0 = sec^2(psi)/F^2, stationary points tan(psi1,2) = (1 +- sqrt(1 - 8*tan^2 theta))/(4*tan theta), valid under the wedge. Far field = Re{ sqrt(2*pi/r)*[A(psi1)/sqrt(-g''(psi1))*exp(i*(r*g1 - pi/4)) + A(psi2)/sqrt(g''(psi2))*exp(i*(r*g2 + pi/4))] }. r*cos(psi+theta) = x*cos psi - y*sin psi, so everything is algebraic:
(x along the wake behind the site, y = abs across) T = y/x; Q = 1 - 8*T*T; R = sqrt(max(Q,0))
tau2 = 2*T/(1 + R)   // rationalised, stable at T = 0
tau1 = (1 + R)/(4*T + eps)
phi2 = sqrt(1 + tau2^2)*(x - y*tau2)/F2; phi1 = sqrt(1 + tau1^2)*(x - y*tau1)/F2
wedge = smoothstep(0, E, Q)
// my simplification: I do not compute g''. It vanishes like R at the wedge, so amplitude is capped by a rational fit
amp = wedge/sqrt(R + Rcap)*window(x/L)*sat(x/X0)*InvSqrt(x + X0)
zeta_site = amp*(Div*sat(T/T0)*cos(phi1 - pi/4) + Trans*cos(phi2 + pi/4))
Sum over sites. The Div*sat(T/T0) fade hides the divergent waves' infinite frequency on the centreline.
Lattice: rotate by global Direction into (along, across), cell 1 across by Aspect along. L <= Aspect. Wedge half width at L is 0.354*L, so Aspect <= 2.8 fits +-1 row: 3 rows x 2 upstream columns = 6 sites. Per site, hash gives jitter, strength, F jitter, and absence.
master.why_new: Different output. RippleNoise, RadialPhasor and ImpulseWarp are rings or eddies, GerstnerSea is open-water waves, BurgersSteepen is one-sided fronts. Nothing makes the V-with-feather pattern, and a dispersive wedge cannot come from summing radial waves at a fixed wavelength. KnotFlow's wakes are streamline deflections, not waves. Not a graph: the phases need per-site frames.
master.simd_plan: Fixed 6 site window. Two sqrt, two InvSqrt, two cos per site. Masks for x > 0 and Q > 0. 2D is the node. 3D: y as depth, with exp(-k*depth) amplitude, about 1.3x cost, which is rarely useful. 4D fallback: the fourth coordinate scrolls phases for a loop. Tiling is awkward: the lattice is anisotropic and global, so use a period-integer lattice and accept the 4D story is weak. Estimate AVX2 about 15 ns in 2D.
master.continuity: C0: amplitude fades to 0 at the wedge and the window ends. Real wakes peak at the wedge line, so a sharp E makes an Airy-like bright rim. High-frequency centreline fade is needed or the divergent phase aliases.
master.params: Direction (global), Froude Length F (hybrid per site), Density (hybrid), Aspect, Length L, Divergent Amount, Transverse Amount, Strength Jitter.
master.risks: Near-field is wrong by design; the formula is a far-field approximation, so hide it with X0. Global direction limits use on winding rivers; a hybrid direction read at the site needs a wider window. Niche use. Amplitude fit is mine and may look off near the cusps.

tau-function-waves.look: ThetaCrests: a net of thin bright crests around dark flat cells, with one family of short bright stems (the H bridges) all leaning the same way. At d=0.22 unwarped it is a clean honeycomb of hexagons with an H bridge at each crossing. Warped, the default, it is an irregular organic net with bright raised stems and dim long walls; the wide view reads as uneven cells, close to a warped cellular wall pattern but with the stem brightness structure no cellular node has. Threshold shows irregular closed cells. FFT is not a lattice of dots once warped, but shows a preferred axis. Relief reads as raised dark ridges on a flat blue floor, not as water. master.one_liner: Exact nonlinear wave patterns from a tau function: u = 2 d^2/dx^2 log tau, either the KP line-soliton web (Y junctions, Mach stems, one hybrid Time that moves it) or the genus-2 theta solution (hexagonal crest lattice with phase shifts), both closed form and animatable.
master.look: SolitonWeb: a handful of long straight sech^2 ridges that meet in a bounded region where they form a web of Y junctions and short bridging segments (Mach stems), with exact phase shifts; moving Time makes the web slide and reconfigure like interacting shallow-water waves seen from above. ThetaCrests: a honeycomb of sharp crests over flat troughs, each crossing replaced by a short H bridge, the real-ocean version of two crossed waves.
master.algorithm:
SolitonWeb (a global pattern like Stamp or Gradient):
  M wave numbers k_1 < ... < k_M (M = 4..6, sorted hashed values in [-Kmax, Kmax] from Seed); positive weights w_ij = (k_j - k_i)*Delta_ij with Delta_ij hashed in [0.3, 3] (Wronskian form of the Gr(2,M) tau; Kodama's expansion uses (k_j - k_i)^2 in another normalisation: any positive weights give a regular solution)
  theta_i = k_i x + k_i^2 y + k_i^3 t + theta_i0, t = hybrid Time (or w)
  Theta_ij = theta_i + theta_j + log w_ij; Kx_ij = k_i + k_j
  m = max_ij Theta_ij; E_ij = exp(Theta_ij - m); Z = sum E; mean = sum Kx E / Z; var = sum Kx^2 E / Z - mean^2
  u = 2*var    (exactly 2 d^2/dx^2 log tau, numerically stable, u >= 0: a sech^2 ridge where two terms tie, a Y junction where three tie)
  Output u/umax, or Skeleton = (second largest Theta - largest), the tropical curve of the web for a hard version.
ThetaCrests (doubly periodic in two phases):
  z = (k1.p, k2.p) two wave vectors; Omega = 2x2 positive definite (d1, d2 on the diagonal, coupling c)
  theta(z) = sum_{|n1|,|n2| <= N} exp(-pi n^T Omega n) cos(2 pi n.z), N = 2 (25 terms; the exponentials are a table built when params are set)
  theta_x = -2pi sum (n.kx) e_n sin(2 pi n.z); theta_xx = -(2pi)^2 sum (n.kx)^2 e_n cos(2 pi n.z)
  u = 2 (theta_xx theta - theta_x^2)/theta^2   (theta > 0 for Omega large enough; clamp otherwise)
  This is the genus-2 KP solution: crests form hexagons with phase shifts at the crossings (the Hammack-Scheffner-Segur shallow-water pattern); smaller Omega gives sharper, more hexagonal crests, larger Omega tends to two crossed sines.
A stationary version with Gaussian envelopes on the exponents (per lattice site) is possible but collapses to a smooth-min Voronoi wall, which CellularSmooth already is, so it is not proposed.
master.why_new: wave-lattice and wave-noise are linear sums of plane waves (interference beats, sinusoidal profiles, X crossings); tpms is periodic sines. A tau function gives the nonlinear picture: constant-height sech^2 crests, Y-shaped resonant junctions and H-bridged hexagons, which no linear superposition can produce. It is also the dequantised twin of TropicalFacet, since the web's skeleton is a tropical curve.
master.simd_plan: SolitonWeb M = 6: 15 Exp and ~70 flops, no window, no hash, any dimension through the phases: ~15-20 ns. ThetaCrests N = 2: 25 Sin + 25 Cos (~50 ns); N = 1 (9 terms) is ~18 ns and still shows the H bridges. Both branch free.
master.continuity: C-infinity (log of a positive sum of exponentials); Skeleton output is C0.
master.params: Form enum {SolitonWeb, ThetaCrests}; M (int) and Kmax for the web; Time (hybrid); Omega d1, d2, c and the two wave vectors for the crests; Output enum {U, Skeleton}; Seed.
master.risks: Non-stationary (web) or periodic (crests); the exponentials overflow without the max subtraction; the periodic form costs 50 Sin/Cos per sample.

master.one_liner: One node for spots, labyrinth, stripes and holes at a constant wavelength, with hybrid Spread and Bias moving through that phase diagram continuously across the image: leopard body running into tiger limbs without a mask.
master.look: A coat: rounded spots with some rings, flowing into forking stripes as Spread falls, into a dark hole pattern as Bias falls, all at one stripe width. As a mask it fits animal coats, coral, skin, rocks with banded and spotted zones, biome edge decoration. With Spread 0 and Angle from a slow field, expect zebra herringbone like steered-stripes.
master.algorithm:
WHY THE ACCIDENT LOOKS LIKE IT DOES. Wave warp domains: a too strong warp on N narrowband waves. A warp with Jacobian J maps each wave vector to (I+J)^T k, so the spectral ring becomes an ellipse. Where strain is high the ellipse is thin, all waves point about the same way and the field is locally stripes; where strain is low the ring stays round and the field is spots and rings. So the domains are a map of local strain. Spot-versus-stripe is therefore angular spread of the spectrum, and it can be set directly with no strain and no wavelength change. Threshold level is the other axis of the classic pattern phase diagram: high is spots, zero is labyrinth, low is holes.

N fixed wave vectors, table built on param set: theta_i = (i + .5)*pi/N with a half step offset (the critic's fix: no axis-aligned wave), |k_i| = tau*F*(1 + FreqJitter*h_i), phases from seed. This is the steered fan of t_wave_noise_sliced, with its width made hybrid.
q = p + Warp*(slice1(a.p), slice1(b.p))                      // the cheap global slice warp from the accident, to break straightness
Per lane: dir = (cos 2*Angle, sin 2*Angle) from hybrid Angle (or Direction X, Y), kappa = lerp table from hybrid Spread: Spread 1 -> kappa 0 (isotropic), Spread 0 -> kappa large
for i in 0..N-1: w_i = exp(kappa*(dot(dir, c2_i) - 1)), c2_i = (cos 2 theta_i, sin 2 theta_i), by repeated squaring of a base for speed
  sum += w_i*wave(dot(k_i, q) + phi_i);  w2 += w_i*w_i
n = sum*InvSqrt(w2/2)                                        // constant variance at any Spread, so Bias means the same everywhere
Out = tanh-like(Sharp*(n - Bias))                            // tanh by the rational form, hybrid Bias
Double angle means no seam at Angle +-pi. wave = sin, or the parabola kernel from the shears family for speed.
3D: table of 16 to 24 directions on the half sphere; w_i from (k_hat.d)^2 with a direction hybrid: lamellae at Spread 0, sponge at Bias 0 and blobs at high Bias. 4D: same with a table on S3.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. PhasorNoise, LatticePhasor and VortexPhase do stripes well but cannot become spots. PhasonWaves and WaveLattice go from lattice to labyrinth but not per lane. TuringStencil is one regime and needs a stencil tree. FractalSpectrum hybrids change scale, not planform. As a graph it needs N Gradient + Oscillator + Multiply chains with no way to keep variance constant. Nearest is steered-stripes with its 2 waves.
master.simd_plan: No lattice and no window. Fixed N in a loop, every wave costs on every lane. Estimates AVX2 with parabola kernel: N 12 about 8 ns in 2D and 3D, with 3D direction count raising it to about 12 ns, 4D about 15 ns. Hybrids sampled once per lane. The accident measured about 3.2 ns at N 8.
master.continuity: C0 and smooth wherever the hybrids are continuous, except with the parabola kernel (C1). Angle is only used through double angle. Wave vectors never change with position, so there is no shear far from the origin, unlike the broken coordinate-stretch accident.

master.risks: Narrow Spread uses only 1 or 2 global waves, so a plaid or straight patch can appear: the log saw plaid at K 6 Nv 64. Global phase means spot positions shift when Spread changes, so an animated Spread would look wrong; static fields are fine. Far-coordinate precision of dot(k, q) as with SineWave.

glass-caustic.look: Default: a hexagonal array of bright star shaped rosettes, each with a small rim loop at the tile centre and spikes running out, joined by thin soft filaments over a dark floor; every tile differs because of the ripple and tilt. It does read as light through patterned glass. Wide view: the same rosettes as a plainly regular lattice, which is what a tiled source should give. Without ripple (seen with the earlier flat and capsule profiles): engineered thin straight lines in each tile, much less attractive, so the ripple is what sells it. fbm height sanity panel: a closed caustic net like CausticWeb. Voronoi pebbles were dull: polygons with straight facets.
glass-caustic.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured with z breathing the Depth around its value: range -0.850..0.998, z-continuity max 0.0227 for dz=1e-3; the XZ slice shows vertical line bundles widening and narrowing. Tiles stay fixed in z, so it is an animation of the light and not a solid, so no. 4D not built, because the harness has no Eval4.

glass-caustic.artifacts: proto_scan real jumps: 0 at defaults (worst 0.000, steep slopes 42166), 0 with rip=0, 0 for square blocks. My first hex rounding had a real seam: 2033 scan crossings, worst 1.893, because a lerp toward the radius left height above 0 on the tile outline. It is fixed by forcing exact hex norm at the outline. Smaller FD steps bring it back in a small way: h=0.01 gave 4 scan crossings (worst 0.155) from float rounding of the second differences, h=0.02 and up gave 0. So FD step and coordinate size limit how fine lines can go, and far from the origin the noise floor rises: this was not measured beyond the far-coords range check (-0.834..0.999, no NaN). Thin lines look dotted at the highest Depth tried on squares (D=0.16 at w=1.4), an aliasing effect. Tile outlines stay visible as faint straight lines.
glass-caustic.node_shape: GlassCaustic : Modifier, VariableRange. Source (GeneratorSource, height), Steps (int 2-3), Depth (hybrid), Line Softness eps, Gamma, FD Step h. The tile profile belongs to TileDomain as a new Bevel Output with Rounded corners, and the ripple is a graph Add on the height, not members of this node.
glass-caustic.port_notes: Each sample takes 3 x Steps + 6 source evals at other positions, a fixed count, which fits the execution model: a node MAY evaluate its source a fixed number of times. Auto step factor needs the source's largest curvature, which a generic Source does not provide, so expose Lambda or derive it from Depth only. Height needs C2 at joints for clean output. Bricks use a rounded rectangle distance through a quintic, and hex uses hex norm at the outline blended to radial inside. Note the sign: the lens is p = q + D grad h and det(I + D H), so convex tops focus. The entry writes det(I - D H) next to y = pos - D g, which disagrees with itself.

master.algorithm: Height is any GeneratorSource, TileDomain with Output Bevel and Smooth profile as the default. y = pos. For s in 0..Steps-1 (fixed, 2-3): g = forward difference gradient of Source at y (D+1 taps); y += Lambda * (pos - Depth * g - y). Then Hessian H of Source at y by fixed stencil (6 taps in 2D, 10 in 3D, 15 in 4D). b = 1 / (Eps + Abs(det(I - Depth * H))). out = ScaleOutput(b ^ Gamma). The FD step h sets line softness on tile joints. Total taps at Steps=2: 12 / 18 / 25. Depth is hybrid, so a z-driven Depth animates the light. Estimated AVX2 on TileDomain: about 15 ns 2D. On QuasiTile the 433 ns scalar locate x 12 taps is about 5 us: bake only.

Bent bright and dark stripes lie over one another in flat sheets with sharp silhouette edges, stripes stop at an edge and carry on differently below it, and sheets darken as they turn into a fold. Count: separated cusped lens and ribbon shapes, thin. The gradient field reads as quilted leather or puffed scales, cells with creases between them. Anisotropic field reads as a curtain with long lens shaped overlaps. fbm Lookup reads as folded rock with thin dark seams. At A=0.4 it is a plain warped stripe. master.one_liner: The forward warp no domain warp can be: a textured sheet pushed through a folding map, showing real overlap with the top layer winning, or a count of how many layers cover each point.
master.look: Satin, foil, dough, or folded rock in map view: smooth flat sheets of the Lookup that visibly lie over one another, with sharp silhouette edges where a fold turns under and a soft contact shadow, stripes doubling back at each fold. Count output gives crisp cusped ribbons. At low Amplitude it is the ordinary warp, which is a good continuity check.
master.algorithm:
SHARED CAUSE. Domain warps are backward, single valued maps, so they never show one part of a texture covering another. Implicit warp torn foil, multi-start double-walled pipes, the Newton back map debris and caustic silk are all failed attempts to invert a folding map with iteration, which picks an unstable branch. CausticMesh showed the honest answer is available pointwise: push a fixed local triangle mesh forward and test the sample against every image triangle. It used the result only for intensity. The same pass also finds which sheet is on top, and where it came from.

Y(x) = x + A*V(x), V = gradient of a built-in height h, or a curl, or two channels (ValueGrad). |V| <= Vmax is known.
Radius R >= A*Vmax + s so no covering triangle can be missed. Mesh pitch s, n = ceil(2R/s), vertices on the global lattice of pitch s around p: (n+1)^2, in the prototype 36 vertices and 50 triangles at s .2, R .35.
for each vertex: t_i = Y(x_i) - p; z_i = LayerGain*h(x_i) + orientation term; keep x_i
for each triangle (a,b,c): area = cross(t_b - t_a, t_c - t_a); bary = signed sub-areas, flipped by sign(area); inside = all >= 0  (masks)
  count += inside
  z = dot(bary, z_abc)/|area|; top = inside & (z > best); best = Select(top, z, best); second = ...
  xStar = Select(top, dot(bary, x_abc)/|area|, xStar)
Outputs: Sheet = Lookup(xStar), one eval; Shaded = Lookup*(1 - Shadow*smoothstep(0, ShadowWidth, best - second)); Count = 1, 3, 5 ... (cusped bowties, ribbons), the true multi-sheet mask, which is what the double-walled pipes were approaching; Intensity = CausticMesh's sum. A hybrid fed by Gradient(z) gives the caustic depth volume accident.
All 3D work stays 2D: z enters h as a parameter, the plane form in the prototype. No tetrahedra.
master.why_new: Different output. ImplicitWarp gets some creases and collapses into chaos at high amplitude, and every warp on the sheets is single valued. OcclusionStack and PebblePile have occlusion of stamps, never of a continuous sheet. FoldCaustic and CausticWeb light the folds but show no surface. CausticMesh is the parent and is intensity only.
master.simd_plan: Fixed vertex and triangle counts, all masked, no per-lane branching. Honest cost: the mesh prototype measured 3159 ns scalar with Hessians at every vertex; this uses gradients only and one Lookup, so my AVX2 estimate is 150 to 300 ns in 2D, about 200 to 400 ns in 3D and 4D. It is an offline node. Counts scale as (R/s)^2 so low Amplitude is cheaper.
master.continuity: Discontinuous on purpose at fold silhouettes (true occlusion edges) and for Count; C0 elsewhere for C0 Lookup at low Amplitude. Discontinuities along mesh edges appear at folds; the prototype notes no weight formula removes the jump at a mesh fold edge. A soft-edge option can blend by distance to triangle edge at the fold, but it will not be exact.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Field enum, Mesh Pitch, Radius (auto), Layer Gain, Shadow, Shadow Width, Output enum, Lookup source. Hybrid: Amplitude, only if capped by the constant used to set Radius.
master.risks: Visible triangle facets unless s is small, which grows cost quadratically. Top-layer rule choice matters a lot, and a poor z gives a popping patchwork. Cost rules it out for runtime use. Fnlab's C0 checks will flag it by design. Hybrid Amplitude must stay under the constant bound or sheets are lost.

measured.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not ported: about 1200-1500 ns at defaults (450 Perlin at 1.1 ns, 392 masked triangles at about 2 ns), 700 ns for the gradient field. The entry's 150-300 ns was for s=0.2, R=0.35, and those settings do not hold for this field. Offline node.
measured.c0_step_text: Defaults: h=1e-3 1.86675, h=1e-4 1.76457, h=1e-5 0.92360. A step of this size that barely shrinks is a real jump, on purpose, at fold silhouettes. At A=0.2 (no folds): 0.04914, 0.00492, 0.00049, c0ratio 7.660, straddle 7.583: a clean slope.

supply-dunes.look: Clip alone, as the entry wrote it: long sausage ridges, no crescents, confirming the entry's predicted risk. With the two changes below: a field of separate dunes, many shaped like a C with both tips trailing downwind, plus hooks and commas, running into long continuous ridges where supply rises (top right of the plain render). The threshold panel shows C shapes clearly. Relief at hscale 30 reads as a dune field: curved crests with a steep face and horns, merging into long ridges. Honest limits: perhaps half of the separate dunes are clear crescents and the rest are blobs or hooks, and crests near high supply can close into eye shaped loops (seen in the ramp panels). Wide view is sparse and uneven, since a large patch of low supply is empty.

supply-dunes.artifacts: proto_scan real jumps: 0 (worst 0.000, steep slopes 1494). jumps table shows slopes only. The clip leaves a kink at the base of each dune, C0 only. Eye loops at high supply, as above. horn above about 1 gives long swept tails like fish shapes (horn 1.6 panel). FFT has a line along the crest direction, as expected from aligned dunes. Near a vortex core a goes to 0, so the fork singularities of the parent are hidden in the flat ground, which removes Y forks at low supply.

master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: isolated dunes merging into ridges. Clipping may give lens shapes rather than true crescents; whether horns form is unknown.
master.algorithm: A,B = Perlin sources, B offset. Unit phasor z = (A+iB)*InvSqrt(A^2+B^2+eps^2). phase = arg(z) by polynomial atan2 + 2pi*f*dot(w,p); t = Fract(phase/2pi). Stoss and slip profile: h0 = Min( t/Stoss, smoothstep( 1, Stoss, t ) ). Amplitude taper a = smoothstep( 0, Core, Sqrt(A^2+B^2) ), which narrows crests towards vortex cores. Output Max( 0, a*h0 - (1 - Supply) ), Supply a hybrid. No window, dimension via sources; heightfield in use, so per column. Cost estimate: 5-6 ns 2D. Risk: clipping likely gives lens shapes rather than true crescents without crest curvature from a low-frequency warp.
master.why_new:
Barchan is one stamped dune at 20-22 ns measured and never merges; vortex dunes merge but are only transverse. A sand supply hybrid could run one field from isolated dunes to continuous ridges at a quarter of the cost. Whether horns form is unknown, so test this before believing it.
Split from seed cluster SupplyDunes / SandSea: a clipped phase field and stamped barchans are different mechanisms for a similar look.

supply-dunes.changed_from_entry: 1) Phase lag: phase -= horn * (1 - a). Crest ends with low amplitude move downwind of the middle of a piece. This is what makes horns, and it is the idea worth keeping. It also has a physical reason: less sand moves faster. 2) A third Perlin stretched along the wind cuts crests into short pieces, because the crests from |A + iB| alone are too long to bend. 3) Envelope moves with time at 0.7 of the crest speed, so dunes travel and change shape. The entry's plain phase would only slide crests through a fixed envelope.

sand-sea.look: Plain view: crowded crescent dunes that differ visibly in size, height and direction, with one horn often longer than the other, and overlapping into barchanoid groups, all over a dark plain carrying curved ripple lines that fork. Relief at hscale 12 beside the plain barchan: the plain one reads as one profile stamped many times in parallel, and the sand sea reads as a varied field whose dunes turn slowly across the view. Ripples are clearly visible on the plain and weaker on the dunes. Threshold shows interlocked crescent shapes. Wide view is an even dune texture without visible cell rows. Terrain ramp colours the crests green, so it is judged by shape, not colour. Volume surface looks stepped with thin contour-like terraces, which I attribute to the ray march step rather than the field, though I did not test that.
sand-sea.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured as a density in y, as the entry asks: height(x, z) x gain - (y - y0), range clamped to -1..1, z-continuity max 0.0020 for dz=1e-3. The vol shows a solid sand body with a dune surface on top. The sheet's XZ slice is black, because that slice lies above the sand at the probe height, which is expected for a density and not a fault. 4D not built, because the harness has no Eval4.
sand-sea.range: -0.973..0.700 over 8 seeds and offsets, mean -0.521, std 0.27. Ground sits at about -0.9 and the top depends on rmax, h and scale, so it would need VariableRange scaling.
sand-sea.artifacts: proto_scan real jumps: 0 at defaults (worst 0.000, steep slopes 0), 0 at bend=1.4 and at bend=2.5, 0 with ripA=0.05 at --thr 0.1. jumps table shows slopes only. Above about bend 1 the potential gets critical points where grad phi = 0: dunes whirl around them, a striking look but the wind direction is undefined exactly at that point, and a scan grid cannot see a single point. Ripple core points where A + iB = 0 are damped by a small mask. Threshold edges are jagged from the ripple. Window: reach is clamped so a jittered dune cannot leave the 3x3 block, and stoss and horn jitter are limited by the clamp at large R, so large dunes vary less.
sand-sea.node_shape: Add to BarchanField: Wind Bend, Wind Scale (or a hybrid Wind, with the far-field caveat in port_notes), Horn Jitter, Stoss Jitter, Asymmetry, Height Jitter, Ripple Amp, Ripple Frequency, Ripple Fork Charge q, Ripple Fade H0, Ripple Keep On Dunes.
sand-sea.port_notes: Fixed 3x3 window. Wind and ripple phase from one Perlin with analytic gradient plus two more Perlin for the fork term and one Cos, once per lane. A plain hybrid Wind angle would need dot(p, w(p)), whose gradient grows with |p|, so ripple lines would crowd far from the origin. Either keep a built-in potential as here, or give the ripple a fixed carrier and bend it with the warp only. Per dune fields come from hash bit fields. Mask for t^2 < 1 and f > 0.

master.one_liner: Stamped barchans with hashed horn and stoss, a wind hybrid that bends the whole field, and vortex-phase ripples that fade on the dunes.
master.look: Predicted by the panel, not built: a sand sea where dunes vary instead of one stamped profile, and ripples have Y forks.
master.algorithm: theta = Wind.Gen(seed, pos), low frequency, per lane. w = (cos, sin). For 3x3 cells: centre = cell + jitter, r = lerp(rmin, rmax, hash), gated by a density hash. u = dot(pos - centre, w); v = dot(pos - centre, perp(w)); u2 = u + Horn * v*v / r. h = barchan profile(u2, v, r) with the existing stoss and slip kernel. Hash also jitters Horn and stoss per dune to break the stamped look. H = smooth union over the fixed 9 candidates. Ripple: phase = tau * f * dot(pos, w) + q * arg(A + iB) with A, B two Perlins and polynomial atan2. rip = RipAmp * (0.5 + 0.5*cos(phase)) * (1 - sat(H / H0)). out = Base + H + rip. 3D as density: y - out. Critic measured 20-22 ns AVX2 for barchan with its own ripple; this adds 3 Perlin and one sincos: about 25-27 ns (estimate).

Critics list one stamped profile and straight ripples as barchan tells. The vortex-phase dunes discovery has clean Y forks, and a wind hybrid lets the whole field bend together. Not built; the look is a prediction.

leaf-rosette.look: Seen in the sheet and hillshade: overlapping stars of tapered blades with a bright midrib, V-fold shading and contact shadows, inner whorl on top, dark ground between crowns. Reads as agave, yucca or dracaena from above at a glance, and the threshold panel is a clean botanical silhouette. Single crown at n=12 reads as a succulent. shape=2 after my rewrite reads as fern or cycad crowns (fine slanted leaflets on a rachis); at bw=3,n=9 it turned into blocky pentagons, so width matters. n=18 with bw=1.1 reads as spiky palm or yucca. Volume: thin sheets on domes above straight trunks, a recognisable stand of small palms, though the blades look jagged and stepped at the default march steps. Wide view is an even scatter with no visible lattice. FFT shows faint radial streaks from blade edges and an axis ratio of 9.7 from those edges, with no bright axis cross.

C0 variant stack=1 (max of soft blades, top surface by true height): proto_scan real jumps 0, also 0 for its pinnate form with stagger=0, which is steeper (c0 3.69, straddled 3.77). With stagger=0.5 the soft pinnate comb jumps at the rachis, 10830 crossings worst 0.763, so soft pinnate needs stagger=0. 3D: my own Eval3 bisection (720k random segments on 3 axes) first found 570 real jumps worst 0.999 at blade rims below iso; fixed by fading the field to -1 at the rim, rerun finds 0 real jumps. A first trunk term also made rectangular lattice blocks in the slice background, visible in the sheet I read; fixed, rerun clean numerically but that panel was not checked by eye. Hard edges alias at the default field scale.

leaf-rosette.port_notes: Key to a seamless 3 slot search: cap each blade's angular half width at (1.5 - AngleJitter/2) slots, written as W = min(W, a * tanLim), so a blade cannot leave the tested slots even at the crown centre. Blade tests are one sin/cos pair per blade unless N is fixed and jitter is off, then a per-node table works. Slot index must wrap mod N for the blade hash. Crown priority: key = prio*1000 + whorl*10 + hash*9, masked max. Contact shadow is a second fixed loop over stored candidates (key, m), up to 54 entries; stack=1 needs neither. Radius up to 1.05 cells fits the 3x3 window at jitter 0.8.

master.one_liner: Crowns seen from above: each cell is a whorl of radiating tapered blades with midribs and dead-leaves stacking, giving palms, agaves, succulents, fern crowns and flower heads, none of which any sheet shows.
master.look: A ground of overlapping rosettes: each a star of tapered blades with a bright midrib and darker edges, inner blades on top, crowns overlapping with the frontmost winning, dark ground visible between. Reads as palms or cycads from above, agave fields, echeveria, jungle canopy from a drone, dahlias or sunflowers in a Count-1 form. Relief shows domed crowns with V-folded blades.
master.algorithm: 3x3 window of jittered crown centres C with hashed radius Rc (within half a cell), blade count N (int param, 5-24, optionally jittered per crown), angle offset theta0, crown priority. For the sample: v = p - C, r = |v|, phi = fastAtan2(v) - theta0 (a polynomial atan2 is fine, slot precision is all that is needed). Blade slot i = round(phi N / 2pi); test slots i-1, i, i+1. For slot j: angle alpha_j = (j + Jitter * (hash(j) - 0.5)) * 2pi/N, length l_j = Rc * (0.65 + 0.35 hash(j)), local coords a = v . (cos alpha, sin alpha) (along), bl = v . (-sin alpha, cos alpha) (across). Half width W(a) = Wmax * shape(a / l_j): shape = sin(pi u)^0.6 for lanceolate leaves, (1 - u)^0.5 for palm fronds with a wide base, or a pinnate shape (1-u) * (0.6 + 0.4 cos(2pi a / lam)) that gives leaflets. Inside measure m_j = W(a) - |bl| for a in [0, l_j]. Whorls: Layers 2 adds an inner whorl rotated by pi/N with lengths 0.55 l and higher priority (younger leaves on top), 3 more tests. Stacking: among the blades containing p (m_j > 0) the one with the highest priority wins (priority = hash per blade plus a bias for inner whorls), implemented as masked max over the 6 candidates; across crowns the crown priority decides (first covering layer wins, PebblePile style). Height of the winning blade: h = Dome * (1 - (r / Rc)^2) + Fold * (1 - |bl| / W) + Droop * (1 - a / l): a V-section leaf, drooping at the tip, on a domed crown. Outputs: Height, Mask, BladeId (hash per blade), Shade (fold term only, a cheap normal proxy), and Source: a hybrid Source evaluated at the winning blade's local frame (a / l, bl / W) so a user texture (veins, serration) is applied per leaf without seams.
master.why_new: Nearest: the Radial parasols discovery (pleated umbrellas: continuous pleats, no discrete leaves, no occlusion), OcclusionStack (cut-out sheets with global depth but no radial arrangement), Phyllotaxis (points only), FlowShingle (oriented stamps along a flow, not whorls). Foliage is the most common material request absent from all four sheets; the signature is discrete radiating blades with occlusion order and a midrib, which needs the angular-slot search this node does.
master.simd_plan: 9 crowns x (1 atan2 polynomial ~12 ops + 6 blade tests ~15 ops each) plus the priority selects: about 1000 ops, roughly 8-12x Perlin 2D; Count 1 (single crown, Stamp style) about 1.5x Perlin. 3D: crowns live on the xz plane and the leaf height h is compared with y (inside if y < h and y > h - thickness), so a volume render shows a canopy of thin curved blades on domes; 4D: w fallback. Masked max keeps it branch free.
master.continuity: Discontinuous by design at blade edges (occlusion), like PebblePile and OcclusionStack; Height is continuous inside a blade.
master.params: Feature Scale, Blades N (int), Layers (int 1-2), Radius Jitter, Angle Jitter, Blade Width, Blade Shape (enum Lanceolate / Frond / Pinnate), Leaflet Spacing lam, Dome, Fold, Droop, Density (hybrid, crowns per cell), Source (hybrid), Output (enum).
master.risks: Broadleaf tree canopies are lobes rather than blades (PuffyCaps territory), so the canopy claim holds for palms and tropical plants only; slot jitter above half a slot can let a blade escape its 3-slot test (clamp Jitter to 0.45).

extra_measured.scalar_vs_perlin_notes: Measured 888 ns/sample vs perlin2 49.8, 8.07x worley2, 9 crowns 2 whorls, default field. The prototype skips crowns out of reach, which a port cannot. pinnate-venation.look: Seen: the sheet shows large overlapping leaves with a white midrib, a comb of arched secondaries, a scalloped loop vein just inside each margin and a polygon mesh between secondaries, stacked with soft contact shadows on a dark ground. It reads as skeleton leaves or backlit leaf litter at a glance. The mesh walls end on secondaries. Hillshade is busier than the gray because lamina tone varies per areole. Wide view aliases to white speckle because the veins are thin, leaf shapes survive. Single leaf reads as a real dicot leaf. Levels 2 reads as a fern frond or a sumac leaf with tapered pinnae; levels 3 as a bipinnate fern, with small pinnules that start to alias at 240 px. Volume: floating curled leaves with raised veins, cut in orange where they meet the cube, a striking 3D leaf fall, some stair stepping. FFT is anisotropic from a few large leaves (axis 4.59), as expected at this window.

pinnate-venation.artifacts: Scatter has real jumps at leaf edges, by design: proto_scan 3538 crossings, seam length about 39, worst 1.647. Single leaf proto_scan 0 real jumps, frond levels=2 0 real jumps, both after fixes. Bipinnate settings (levels=3) keep 28 crossings, seam about 0.31, worst 1.150, unfixed: short pops where pinna candidates are skipped near the frond tip or base. Fixes made: tertiary mesh jumped between panels in the fringe outside the loop vein (152 crossings, found with a scratch probe in leaf coordinates): that fringe is now plain lamina, so tertiaries stop at the loop vein. Mesh also faded where the blade is under 0.036 wide, because squeezed lattice walls beyond the 3x3 window popped near the apex. Frond pinna tone jumped by 0.11 where pinnae overlap: removed. 3D scan3 first found 916 real jumps worst 0.5 at an early slab cutoff below iso; fixed, rerun 0 real jumps. Thin veins alias at small render sizes. c0ratio is low (about 1) in every mode because the lines are very steep, not because of jumps outside the leaf edges, as the h table shows.

pinnate-venation.port_notes: Index secondaries by the midrib origin t = a - |b| cot(beta) - kappa b^2 of the curve through the sample: 2 bracketing origins suffice and give d = |t - a_k| / |grad t|, plus v, the fraction across the panel. Scatter: outlines of 9 leaves, then one kernel on the winner (a masked select of frame, not 9 kernels). Mesh: 2 pass 3x3, only rows 0..nv-1 of this panel, so walls need no alignment with the secondaries; the entry's zero-v-jitter trick is unnecessary. Pow in the outline can be dropped by fixing q to a simple polynomial. Fronds recurse: 3 children per level with 3 fixed point steps for the pinna tip, so a fixed level count is a nested fixed loop, cost 3^levels.
