master.one_liner: Leaf venation with the real hierarchy: a midrib, evenly spaced secondaries that curve toward the apex and loop near the margin, and a tertiary reticulum whose walls end on the secondaries, plus a fern frond mode that repeats the kernel per pinna.
master.look: A single leaf: the midrib, a comb of parallel curved secondaries that arch and join each other just inside the margin, and a fine polygonal mesh of tertiaries filling the panels between them, exactly the network a backlit leaf shows. Frond mode gives a fern with pinnae and pinnules. Scatter mode gives leaf litter with correct venation on every leaf. Threshold panel shows the areole mosaic.
master.algorithm: Leaf local frame (a along the midrib in [0,1], b across, leaf length 1, half width Wl). Outline: M(a) = Wl * sin(pi a)^q (q from 0.6 blunt to 1.4 pointed) with hashed base/apex asymmetry; inside measure dm = M(a) - |b|, approximate margin distance dm / sqrt(1 + M'(a)^2). Midrib: d0 = |b|, width w0 (1 - a). Secondaries: spacing Delta0; vein k leaves the midrib at a_k = (k + 0.5) Delta0 + 0.2 Delta0 (hash - 0.5) and follows a = a_k + |b| cot(beta) + kappa b^2 (angle beta to the midrib, bowing toward the apex). Nearest index k* = round((a - |b| cot beta - kappa b^2) / Delta0 - 0.5); for k*, k*+-1 distance d1 = |a - a_k - |b| cot beta - kappa b^2| * sin(beta) (first order perpendicular distance). Marginal loops: an intramarginal vein at |b| = M(a) - lam with distance d_im; within the band dm < 2 lam the secondary distance becomes min(d1, d_im), which closes every secondary into a loop (brochidodromous). Tertiaries: in the inter-secondary coordinates u = |b| / M(a) in [0,1] and v = fractional position between secondaries k* and k*+1 (from the same expression, v in [0,1]), run a 3x3 jittered cellular edge distance on (u / Du, v) with jitter in u only and zero jitter in v; the cell walls at v = 0 and v = 1 then coincide with the secondaries, so tertiaries end on secondaries with T junctions (percurrent) and areoles close. d3 = exact edge distance (iq two pass) scaled back to leaf units. Field: vein = min(d0 / w0, d1 / w1, d3 / w3) with per-order widths, masked to dm > 0; background outside the outline. Order output = which term won. Areole output = the cell hash value (for per-areole shading). Fern frond mode (Levels 2-3): the leaf becomes the frond outline, the secondaries become pinna rachises; for k* and k*+-1 evaluate the same kernel in the pinna frame (a2 = distance along the secondary / its length to the margin, b2 = signed perpendicular distance) with its own outline M2 and spacing; take the min over the 3 children; Levels 3 repeats for pinnules. Placement: Count 1 puts one leaf at the origin (a Stamp), Scatter mode uses a 3x3 window of hashed leaf frames (position, rotation, size) with first-covering-wins stacking for leaf litter.
master.why_new: Nearest: PhacelleNoise (constant width stripes following a direction field: no hierarchy, no areoles), RootVein (fractal line tiers with tapering but random, not pinnate), DendryNoise (river trees), CellularEdge (areoles only, not bounded by secondaries). The pinnate signature, parallel evenly spaced curved secondaries closing in loops with a reticulum that terminates on them, is what makes it read as a leaf, and it needs the aligned-lattice trick (zero jitter in v) to make tertiaries end on secondaries.
master.simd_plan: Single leaf: outline, 3 secondary distances, one 3x3 cellular edge distance (about CellularDistance cost), masks: about 6-8x Perlin 2D. Frond Levels 2: 3 child kernels, about 25x. Scatter: 9 leaves but only the first-covering leaf needs the full kernel: scan outlines for all 9 (cheap), then evaluate the kernel once on the winner, about 10x. 3D: leaves as thin slabs in hashed 3D frames in Scatter mode (volume leaf litter); the kernel itself is 2D. 4D: fallback.
master.continuity: C0: min of distances; index switching is covered by testing k*+-1; the v coordinate is continuous across secondaries because v wraps exactly where the next k starts.
master.params: Leaf Width Wl, Apex q, Secondary Spacing Delta0, Secondary Angle beta, Bow kappa, Margin Loop lam, Tertiary Scale Du, Tertiary Jitter, Widths w0 w1 w3, Levels (int 1-3, frond), Placement (enum Single / Scatter), Density (hybrid), Output (enum Veins, Order, Areole, Outline, Along, Across).
master.risks: The first-order secondary distance distorts where the bow is strong (use two Newton steps on the curve if visible); very dense tertiaries alias at the leaf scale; Scatter in 3D is a slab stamp, not real 3D leaves.

pinnate-venation.changed_from_entry: Tertiaries: instead of a global lattice with zero v jitter, each panel owns its sites and the panel edge simply is the secondary, which gives T junctions with full jitter. Alternate left and right offset added. Fringe outside the loop vein has no mesh. Added a contact shadow in scatter, and in 3D a curl, a V fold and vein thickness (lam3).

frost-feathers.look: Seen, Stellar at 240 px: unmistakable six-armed snowflakes, varied per crystal, overlapping at jitter 0.8, on black. Seen, volume: real looking 3D crystals with tubular arms and side branches, three axes, cut in orange at the cube faces. Seen, Spangle before the fold fix: Voronoi plates of flat gray, each with a dendritic flower, dark grooves between them, a convincing galvanised steel read. Seen, Window sheet: curved white lace feathers with stems and hatched side branches, more like frost ferns or skeleton leaves than a sheet of window frost: they are isolated with black gaps rather than sweeping and overlapping, and the vane fill shows as a soft gray halo that reads as a smudge and dominates the threshold panel. Window is the weakest mode, which is why I made Stellar the default.
frost-feathers.dims: 2D measured for three modes. 3D measured for Stellar only: octahedral fold after a hashed rotation, so arms along 3 axes with side branches in planes holding the arm, read in a vol render. 4D not written (fallback, non tiling).

frost-feathers.artifacts: proto_scan real jumps 0 for all three modes, scan3 0 real jumps in 3D. Reaching that took fixes. Long sub branches missed by the 3 branch test gave 1278 crossings worst 1.72; capping sub branch length at the branch spacing cut that to 272. The rest came from the sub branch index slipping along long sub branches; indexing each family by its own line invariant removed them. c0ratio stays about 2 because the lines are steep and thin, the h table shows slopes. Hard thin lines alias in the wide view. Window stems are capped at 0.95 cells by the 3x3 window, which is why feathers cannot sweep far: longer needs more stems per cell or a bigger window. Window flow direction samples a perlin per stem. Spangle assumes F1 from 3x3 at jitter 0.8.

frost-feathers.port_notes: Hex fold is abs on both axes plus two conditional reflections, at 60 and then 30 degrees, no atan2. Branch index from s0 = s - |t| cot(angle). Sub branches: two families with invariants an = py / sin(angle) and an = (px sin2a - py cos2a) / sin(angle), 2 candidates each, length capped at the branch spacing so 3 branch candidates cover them: 3 x (1 + 4) segments per crystal instead of the entry's rough count. Only the sample's side of the stem is tested; the stem line hides the side switch at t = 0. 3D fold is abs plus a 3 element sort by masks. Per crystal values (L, D, Lb) come from hash bit fields.

master.one_liner: Crystallographic dendrites: stems with side branches at exactly 60 degrees and parallel sub-branches, as window frost feathers, 6-fold stellar snowflakes, or galvanised-steel spangle, from one folded stem evaluation per crystal.
master.look: Window mode: ferny frost feathers sweeping across the field, each a stem with a comb of 60 degree side branches that shorten toward the tip, filled near the root, overlapping like real window frost; threshold panel is a lace of feathers. Stellar: a scatter of unique six-armed snowflakes with side branches. Spangle: flat grains each holding a dendritic flower, the galvanised steel surface. Useful for ice, frost, frozen glass, snowflake overlays, metal spangle, and as a mask for frozen edges.
master.algorithm: Core kernel: a feather in local coords (s along the stem, t across), stem from s=0 to s=L. Side branches at spacing D along the stem: branch j has origin O_j = (j+0.5)*D on the stem, direction rotated +60 deg on the t>0 side and -60 deg on t<0 (hexagonal ice), length l_j = Lb * taper(s_j/L) * (0.7 + 0.3*hash(j)), taper(u) = (1-u)^1.5 (feather outline). For the sample, j* = floor(s/D); test branches j* and j*+1 on the sample's side (the other side cannot be nearer than its own stem distance in the 60 deg geometry unless |t| < tiny, so test both sides only when |t| < 0.5*D). Distance to a branch = point-segment distance in the branch frame (a = (p-O_j).b, c = (p-O_j).bperp, a clamped to [0,l_j]). Level 3: sub-branches on each tested branch, spacing D2, direction parallel to the stem (true for hexagonal dendrites: side-branch children are parallel to the neighbouring primary arm), lengths tapering along the branch; test the 2 nearest indices. Field f = min over levels of dist_level / width_level (widths w0 > w1 > w2). Fill option: vane = smoothstep(0, D, l(s) - |t|) * Plate gives a sheet between the branches near the base (frost feathers are filled near the root and open at the tip); Sheen output multiplies the fill by a per-crystal hashed constant (crystal facets reflect differently). Modes. Window: 3x3 cell lattice, each cell owns one stem: jittered root point, hashed direction, L in [0.6,1.4] cells; evaluate the kernel for all 9 and take min; roots may be forced onto a Seed source level set (frost grows from scratches) by placing the root at the nearest point of the source zero set via one Newton step from the cell centre. Stellar: one site per cell, 6 arms: v = p - site, rotate by -theta0 (per crystal), fold into a 60 deg sector by the hex Coxeter fold (reflect across the 3 mirror lines: 2-3 conditional reflections, mask + Select), then run ONE stem kernel along +x; the result is an exactly 6-fold stellar dendrite with per-crystal hashed D, Lb, taper and arm length, all arms identical as in real flakes. Min over the 3x3 window lets flakes overlap. Spangle: Stellar with the arms clipped by the Voronoi cell of the site (distance to the nearest bisector is computed anyway) and the Fill replaced by the cell value, so each grain is a flat plate with a dendritic flower inside, the galvanised look.
master.why_new: Nearest: FernFold (recursive coordinate folding, random angles, no stems or crystallographic branch angles), FiberNoise (plain capsules, no branches), CoralNoise (3D random-angle branching capsules, hierarchical not pinnate), DomainKaleidoscope (6-fold symmetry of a source but no arm structure). Nothing on the sheets reads as ice or frost; the signature that makes dendrites read as ice is the fixed 60 degree branch angle with parallel sub-branches and tapering length, which no warp or fractal of a noise produces.
master.simd_plan: Window mode: 9 cells x (1 stem + 2 branches + 4 sub-branches) = 63 segment distances, each ~12 ops, plus hashes: about 10-14x Perlin 2D. Stellar: 9 x (hex fold ~10 ops + 7 segments): about 8-10x Perlin 2D, no atan2 anywhere. 3D: Stellar uses the octahedral fold (arms along +-x,+-y,+-z after a hashed rotation) with side branches in the two planes containing the arm, 27 cells, about 30-40x Perlin 3D: expensive but real 3D snow crystals; Window mode in 3D keeps stems as 3D segments with branches in a hashed plane. 4D: fallback (drop w), noted as non-tiling.
master.continuity: C0: min of segment distances; branch index switching is seamless because both neighbouring indices are tested and each branch's existence depends only on its own hash, not on the sample.
master.params: Mode (enum Window/Stellar/Spangle), Levels (int 1-3), Branch Spacing D, Branch Length Lb, Taper, Width per level (3 floats), Fill (hybrid), Sheen, Jitter, Arm Angle (float, 60 default; 90 for cubic salt-like crystals, 45 for decorative), Seed source (optional GeneratorSource in Window mode), Output (enum Lines, Filled, Sheen, Plate).
master.risks: Window mode may look like regularly spaced combs rather than frost if D is uniform; per-stem hashed D and slight branch length noise fix that. Level 3 doubles cost for a subtle gain. The side-only branch test needs care at |t| < D/2 to avoid a missed nearer branch (test both sides there).

spider-web.look: Seen: unmistakable orb webs. Dense radial hub, straight spokes, a capture thread that scallops toward the hub between spokes, irregular polygonal frame with reflex corners, torn gaps, strings of dew beads on the capture thread only, and webs overlapping where their frames cross. The threshold panel is a clean line drawing. Wide view (32 units) aliases to speckle bounded by frame polygons because threads are under a pixel there. FFT shows radial streak families per web. Volume: a single web in an inclined plane, round threads, very clean, reads as a wire sculpture of a web; another web barely enters the cube at the top. The XZ slice shows dotted lines, as a plane cut through threads should.

spider-web.artifacts: A few short real jumps remain, unfixed: proto_scan scatter 6 crossings, seam length about 0.07, worst 0.754; single web 5 crossings, seam about 0.06, worst 0.19; jump size mostly under 0.25. Their source was not traced after the fixes below; the positions are scattered. scan3 finds 0 real jumps in 3D at 240k segments with beads off. Fixed along the way: first scan had 149 crossings without tears or beads. Those came from the spiral's inner end dropping out, which now ends through a distance term; turn numbers that differed across the angle wrap (sector index normalised); beads outside the frame (seen in my first render); threads that ended on a missing spoke where a neighbour was torn (a segment can now tear only where both spokes are present); and lab::fastAtan2, which steps by 0.00075 rad across the 45 degree rays and produced a short radial seam on thin threads. Thin lines alias at wide views. The web is a stamp with empty cells at density 0.6, so large black gaps appear on purpose.

spider-web.port_notes: Must use an atan2 polynomial scaled so its end value equals pi/4: multiply by 1.0004787, or fastAtan2 leaves a radial step. Normalise the bracketing spoke index to 0..N-1 and unwrap phi into that sector, so turn numbers and tear hash agree across the wrap. Frame: 4 chords per web, only the bracket chord gives Rframe, all 4 are distance tested. Spoke tests 3, turn tests 3, bead test 1 per turn. Costly per web: 6 hashes for spoke angles, 8 for anchors, plus segment hashes; a per-node table of spoke angles is possible when N is fixed. Beads are domes, dew = sqrt(1 - d^2), radius capped at 0.45 of the slot.

master.one_liner: Orb webs in closed form: a hub, jittered radial spokes, an Archimedean capture spiral that sags inward between spokes, a polygonal frame, torn segments and dew beads, found with angular-slot and turn-index lookups.
master.look: Unmistakable orb webs: a dense hub, straight spokes, a spiral whose every segment sags inward between spokes, an irregular polygonal frame, some torn gaps, and when Beads is on, strings of dew drops along the threads. Scatter mode gives overlapping webs in a corner. Threshold panel is a clean web line drawing.
master.algorithm: Per web (one at the origin, or a 3x3 window of jittered centres with hashed radius, rotation and spoke count): v = p - C, r = |v|, phi = fastAtan2(v) - theta0. Spokes: N (int, 12-40); slot i = round(phi N / 2pi); spoke i angle alpha_i = (i + Jit (hash(i) - 0.5)) 2pi / N; distance to spoke line d_r = r |sin(phi - alpha_i)|, tested for i-1, i, i+1, valid for Rhub < r < Rframe(phi). Sector fraction f = (phi - alpha_i) / (alpha_{i+1} - alpha_i) using the two bounding spokes (recomputed for whichever pair brackets phi). Capture spiral: r = R0 + b theta; turn index n* = round((r - R0 - b phi) / (2pi b)); for n*, n*+-1 the thread radius at this angle is rho_n = R0 + b (phi + 2pi n) - Sag * b * 4 f (1 - f) (the thread bows toward the hub between spokes, maximal at mid sector, zero at the spokes: the scalloped look that makes a web a web); d_s = |r - rho_n| cos(atan(b / r)) ~ |r - rho_n| for small pitch; valid for Rfree < r < Rframe. Hub: the same spiral with small b and R0 = 0 for r < Rhub (dense hub mesh), and a free zone with spokes only between Rhub and Rfree. Frame: A anchors (int 4-8) at angles (m + hash) 2pi / A with radii R_m; the frame thread between consecutive anchors is a straight chord; sector m = round(phi A / 2pi) (test m and m+-1); distance to the chord d_f = |v . n_m - c_m| where n_m, c_m define the chord line; Rframe(phi) = c_m / (unit(phi) . n_m), so spokes and spiral stop at the frame. Tear: hash(i, n) < Tear removes spiral segment (sector i, turn n) and hash(i) < TearSpoke truncates a spoke beyond a hashed radius; removed segments leave their neighbours sagging more (Sag * 1.5 on the adjacent segments, continuous because f(1 - f) vanishes at the spokes). Dew: beads of radius Bead at spacing Ds along every thread: along a spoke index by r / Ds, along the spiral by f * sector length / Ds; distance to the nearest bead centre, test 2 indices; thread field = min(d_r, d_s, d_f) / Thread, bead field = min over beads of d / Bead; output = min(thread, bead) or the bead field alone. 3x3 webs combine by min (webs overlap like real webs in a corner). Outputs: Thread (distance, for width), Beads, Which (spoke 0 / spiral 0.5 / frame 1, for shading), Sector (hash per sector-turn cell, a stained glass look).
master.why_new: Nothing on any sheet is a web. Phyllotaxis gives Fermat spiral points, LogPolarVortex log spirals of a source, RadialPhasor rings; none has spokes, the sagging Archimedean capture thread and a chord frame. The sag term 4 f (1 - f) in the sector fraction is the small geometric signature that makes it read as silk rather than a target, and it needs the spoke-slot search.
master.simd_plan: Per web: one atan2 polynomial (~15 ops), 3 spoke distances, 3 turn distances, 3 chord distances, hashes, 2-4 bead tests: about 120 ops; Single about 1x Perlin, Scatter 9 webs about 8-10x Perlin 2D. 3D: Scatter places each web in a hashed plane (two basis vectors per cell) and adds a slab thickness, so webs float in a volume; the 2D kernel is reused on the projected coordinates. 4D: fallback.
master.continuity: C0: min of distances; the sector fraction and sag are continuous across spokes because the sag vanishes there; tears are per segment and change nothing at segment ends (the segment ends at a spoke where the sag is zero and the spoke itself remains).
master.params: Feature Scale, Spokes N (int), Spoke Jitter, Spiral Spacing b, Sag, Hub Radius, Free Zone Radius, Anchors (int), Frame Radius Jitter, Tear (hybrid), Spoke Tear, Thread Width (hybrid), Bead Radius, Bead Spacing, Placement (enum Single / Scatter), Output (enum).
master.risks: Mostly decorative rather than a general noise; the atan2 approximation must be continuous across the branch cut (fold by octant first); the spiral turn test near the hub needs r clamped above R0.

spiral-galaxy.look: Seen: a dark telescope plate with galaxies of several sizes and tilts, bright core, arms with a crisp inner edge from the dust lane, faint outer arm fragments, and sharp stars of which the bright ones carry a four point cross. The wide view is the strongest panel, a convincing deep field with no lattice visible. A single face-on 3 arm galaxy shows knotty arms and reads as a barred spiral. The 2 arm galaxy at 50 degrees reads clearly but is a little clean and swirly: arms are thin ribbons rather than a mottled disc, and there is no flocculent detail between arms. Volume at iso -0.8: a large ribbon spiral, like a rose of thin twisted sheets, cut in orange at the cube; striking but it reads as a sculpture of a spiral, not as a gas disc. Threshold at P50 is a poor view of it: elliptical cutoff discs and star crosses, since the median is exactly black. Slices in 3D are faint streaks at the default exposure.

spiral-galaxy.artifacts: None measured: proto_scan 0 real jumps, jumps table is a slope, scan3 0 real jumps at the vol settings. Reaching that: first scan had 21 crossings, worst 0.45, from two causes that I fixed: galaxies of radius up to 0.62 cells overflowed the 3x3 window (rmax now 0.5, reach 2.2 R), and the arm index jumped by m across the phi branch cut so clump hashes disagreed on that ray (index now wraps mod m). lab::fastAtan2's 45 degree step exists here too but is under the scan threshold on these smooth arms. The P50 threshold panel shows hard ellipses because the median is exactly -1, so any light above zero reads as white out to each galaxy's own cut; the field itself is C0 there. Dust lane side was wrong in my first code for one handedness, fixed.

spiral-galaxy.port_notes: Arm phase Psi = hand * m * (phi - cot(pitch) * ln r). Clump arm index must wrap mod m. Dust phase is Psi - hand * delta, the inner edge. Light fades by (1 - r^2 / 2.2^2)^2 so a galaxy of radius R fits the window when 2.2 R <= 1 + (1 - jitter) / 2. pow(wave, k) with integer k can be repeated squaring; the bulge's r^(1/4) can be sqrt(sqrt()). Stars are separable: 2 lattices x 9 cells, could be a separate node combined by Add. Tone mapping 1 - exp(-I * Exposure) keeps Add of many galaxies in range.

master.one_liner: Galaxies as stamps: inclined discs with logarithmic arms of fixed pitch, star-forming clumps strung along the arms in log radius, a dust lane on each arm's inner edge, a bulge and bar, plus a power-law starfield with diffraction spikes.
master.look: A dark field with inclined spiral galaxies of several sizes, each with bright knotty arms trailing from a bar, a smooth bright bulge and dark dust lanes hugging the inside of each arm, among sharp stars of which the brightest carry diffraction spikes. The Arm Phase and Dust outputs let a ramp colour the arms blue, the bulge yellow and the lanes brown. For skyboxes, telescope textures, and in 3D a volumetric galaxy slab.
master.algorithm: 3x3 window of jittered galaxy centres C with hashed: size R, position angle PA, inclination incl (cos incl in [0.3,1]), arm count m (2 mostly, sometimes 3-4), pitch angle alpha (12-25 degrees), bar length, brightness, handedness. Local frame: rotate v = p - C by -PA, de-project y' = y / cos(incl); r = |v'| / R clamped above eps, phi = fastAtan2(v') (continuous polynomial, fold by octant). Arm phase Psi = m (phi - ln(r) / tan(alpha)) * handedness. Arms: Aarm = (0.5 + 0.5 cos Psi)^k (k 3-6 sets arm width) * exp(-r / h) (exponential disc) * (1 - exp(-(r / rbar)^2)) (arms begin at the bar ends). Dust lane: Dust = (0.5 + 0.5 cos(Psi - delta))^kd * exp(-r / h) with delta ~ -0.6 rad (the inner, concave edge of each arm). Clumps (HII regions): along each arm the natural coordinate is xi = ln(r) (positions equally spaced in log radius, which is what real arms show); arm index j = round(Psi / 2pi), clump lattice c_n = (n + hash(j, n)) Dxi; test n*, n*+-1 where n* = round(xi / Dxi); clump = B_n exp(-((xi - c_n)^2 / sx^2 + (Psi - 2pi j)^2 / sp^2)) with B_n hashed and biased toward brighter clumps at mid radius. Bulge: Bulge = exp(-c (r_sky / rb)^0.25) on the sky radius (not de-projected, a round spheroid). Bar: elongated Gaussian along the bar axis in the de-projected frame. Intensity I = Brightness * (Bulge + Bar + Aarm * (1 + ClumpGain * sum clumps)) * (1 - DustStrength * Dust * cos-incl term), clamped at 0; a Halo output = exp(-r_sky / rhalo) alone. Galaxies combine by Add (optically thin) with a per-cell presence hash (Density). Starfield output: a finer lattice (two octaves of cell size), one star per cell with brightness Bstar = hash^(-1/gamma) (power law), rendered as exp(-d^2 / s^2) plus a four-spike cross exp(-|dx| / ls - |dy| / lt) + exp(-|dy| / ls - |dx| / lt) scaled by Bstar^2 so only bright stars spike; a Nebula output = the arm kernel at the window scale without the bulge for diffuse filaments. Count 1 puts one galaxy at the origin (a Stamp).
master.why_new: LogPolarVortex gives one log spiral of a source per Voronoi cell packed edge to edge (no arms with pitch, clumps, dust, bulge or inclination); DomainMobius makes a vortex pair that merely resembles galaxies; ClusterCellular is a clustered point process. A recognisable galaxy needs the log-arm phase with a dust lane offset and clumps spaced in log radius, which is a specific kernel rather than a warp of noise. The sheets have no astronomy at all.
master.simd_plan: Per galaxy: atan2 polynomial, one Log, 3 Exp, 2 Cos, 3 clump Gaussians (each an Exp): about 100 ops; 9 cells about 10x Perlin 2D; Count 1 about 2x. Starfield adds 2 lattices x 9 cells x ~20 ops. 3D: the disc gets a vertical profile exp(-|z'| / hz) with z' the coordinate along the disc normal (hashed per galaxy), so the volume is a flattened spiral spheroid and slices through it look like galaxies cut at different depths; 4D: fallback.
master.continuity: C1 away from the clump lattice (C0 there) and the centre (ln r is clamped and arms fade inside the bulge).

running-drops.look: Seen: rain on a window. In the hillshade the moving drops are dark glossy teardrops with bright specular heads, each with a thinner wavering wet streak above it, on a field of fine condensation beads. The gray panel reads as well, with bright round heads and pale trails. The wide view looks like falling rain streaks. Threshold is a clear drop and tail map with static beads. Satellites are small and easy to miss. Corridors cleared through the condensation are visible but subtle at this scale. Frames: heads move down and trails lengthen along a fixed path, plausible as motion from a row of stills; speeds vary by size. Relief: lens bumps on a pebbled plate, fine but not its strength. Time solid: worldline tubes, each head path a slanted tube; a curiosity, included because it is real data, not a spatial form.
running-drops.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: z is Time as the entry prefers, so the volume is a space-time solid, its slices are the frames and it is C0 (scan3 0 real jumps). There is no spatial 3D form of the idea, and the reason is physical: drops run on a surface. 4D not written; the entry wants w as a second time axis for loops.
running-drops.range: -1.000..0.962 over 8 seeds and offsets; the bare glass is exactly -1, mean about -0.95, so most values sit near the bottom. Far coords max 0.805
running-drops.artifacts: proto_scan 0 real jumps at t=0 and t=1.3. scan3 0 real jumps in 3D at thr 0.2 and thr 0.1, also with tscale=0.5. Time wrap is hidden by a fade, so a drop and its trail fade out together at the end of a trip, then a new one fades in at the top of the cell: a whole trail vanishing is not physical, and I did not see it in stills, but it will show in motion. Drops respawn every cell height, so paths cannot be longer than one cell (2.2 units). Columns are not visibly lattice aligned in the wide view; FFT has an axis ratio of about 20 from the vertical streaks, as expected. Lens rims have vertical tangents, which alias a little in hillshade.

running-drops.port_notes: Everything on the glass is a function of glass y: path noise, satellites on a lattice in y with a hashed existence, so per lane scan order does not matter. The head is at (centre(y_d), y_d) with y_d = (j + frac(t v + phase)) ch. Life hash per trip: floor(t v + phase). Window 3 columns x 4 rows because the trail is capped at 1.15 ch; capping at 0.75 ch gives 3 rows. Max of lens heights is C0 without any sort. The corridor needs one more path evaluation per cell but the same value as the trail's xc when s is in the trail. The static layer reads the corridor (clear), so cells run before the static layer in a fixed order; that is fine as a data-flow, no state between samples.

master.one_liner: Rain on a window: drops with bulbous heads and thinning, meandering wet trails above them, satellite droplets left along the trail, and a layer of static condensation, animated by Time.
master.look: Rounded drop heads of mixed sizes, each with a thinner wavering wet streak above it dotted with tiny droplets, over a fine mist of static beads; the big drops are lenses in relief. Animated, drops slide down and their trails lengthen. Nothing else is needed for the rain-on-glass look except a refraction shader.
master.algorithm: Gravity along -y. Column lattice along x of width Cw, rows of height Ch (window 3 columns x 3 rows, trails are capped at 1.2 Ch). Cell (i, j) hashes a running drop with probability Density: head position (x_d, y_d) = cell centre + jitter, radius r = Rmin (Rmax / Rmin)^hash (power law sizes), trail length Lt = r * TrailK * (0.5 + hash), meander amplitude r * Meander. Time t (hybrid or w): y_d(t) = y_top - v(r) t wrapped inside a tall cell with a soft fade in at the top and out at the bottom (speed grows with r, big drops fall faster, and the trail length is min(Lt, distance travelled) so a trail grows behind a moving head). Head shape: smooth union (polynomial smin) of a disc radius r at (x_d, y_d) and a disc radius 0.7 r at (x_d, y_d + 0.6 r): a teardrop with a round front; height of the head h = Flatness * sqrt(max(0, r^2 - dd^2)) where dd is the smin distance (a lens of liquid, contact angle via Flatness). Trail: centre line x_t(y) = x_d + Meander * r * noise1D((y - y_d) / (2 r), cellhash) for y in [y_d, y_d + Lt]; half width w(y) = lerp(0.8 r, 0.15 r, (y - y_d) / Lt); trail height h_t = WetHeight * w(y) * sqrt(max(0, 1 - ((x - x_t(y)) / w(y))^2)) (a thin liquid film ridge). Satellites: along the trail at spacing Ds, index n = round((y - y_d) / Ds), test n and n+-1: droplet at (x_t(y_n), y_n) with radius 0.15-0.3 r if hash(cell, n) < 0.6, height as a small lens. Static layer: a finer lattice (Feature Scale / 4) of condensation droplets, jittered, radius power law, lens heights, Max combined. Combine all by Max of heights (liquid lenses union). Outputs: Height (for the user's refraction normal via SurfaceProbe), Mask (wet area, soft), Trail (trail and satellites only), Age (0 at the head, 1 at the trail top, for drying).
master.why_new: FiberNoise gives tapered capsules (no head, no meander, no satellites); BubblePack gives static beads only; StreakSmear Uneven drips smears a source down into drip streaks without heads. The signature of a running drop is head plus thinning meandering tail plus satellites, in gravity columns, and that composition is a dedicated kernel: the trail must be indexed from its own head.
master.simd_plan: 9 cells x (2 discs + smin + trail with one 1D noise + 3 satellites) ~ 9 x 60 ops, plus the fine static lattice 9 x 10 ops: about 8-10x Perlin 2D. Dimension story: 2D is the glass; 3D uses z as Time (preferred), or treats z as depth with the drops as lenses on the z = 0 plane (slab); 4D w as a second time axis so loops tile. No atan2, all masks and selects.
master.continuity: C0 (Max of smooth lens heights, smin inside the head); the Time wrap is hidden by the fade so no pops.
master.params: Feature Scale (column width), Row Height, Density (hybrid), Radius Min / Max, Trail Length K, Meander, Satellite Spacing, Satellite Density, Flatness, Wet Height, Static Density, Static Size, Time (hybrid), Fall Speed, Output (enum).
master.risks: Trails longer than the row window are cut (cap Lt); fast drops in a tall cell need a bigger row window at high speed; without refraction the material is subtle in flat gray (judge with the hillshade).

running-drops.changed_from_entry: Added the corridor: a drop wipes the condensation along its whole path, which is the visual signature on real glass and costs little. Path, satellites and trail are anchored to the glass rather than to the head, so the trail stays put as the head moves; the entry's noise1((y - y_d) / 2r) would make the trail slide along with the head. Head respawns within its own cell instead of a tall cell, which keeps the window at 4 rows. Screen down is +y, so drops run toward +y, with the trail at lower y.

ink-drop-layers.look: Seen: packed round drops with nested rings, older ones dented into crescents and curved slivers against newer ones, crisp boundaries. Reads as agate, marbled stone, or cell tissue. The smallest test passed: at reach 1.01 rings are just clipped, at reach 2 and 3 older ring sets are visibly squashed against newer drops. With a comb stage it turns into real marbled paper: strands dragged into feathered wisps between round drops, the strongest look of the set. Capsule strokes give rounded stadium shapes that nest and deform. Threshold panel is a striking ring and crescent mosaic. Wide view is even with no lattice visible, across 32 rotated lattices. Volume (20 layers): a cube with spherical cavities, shells and rings on its cut faces, with some moire on steep surfaces. Relief: very cliffy cratered ground with vertical walls, not useful as terrain at this height.
ink-drop-layers.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured: spheres on rotated per layer lattices (vol read, slice read, scan3). The same loop gives 4D with one more coordinate; not written.
ink-drop-layers.range: -0.998..0.997 over 8 seeds and offsets, clamped to [-1,1], mean about 0
ink-drop-layers.artifacts: Reporting plainly: the scan counts real jumps in 2D. Default: 583 crossings, seam length about 6.43, worst 1.269. Comb (combevery=6): 2256 crossings, seam about 24.9, worst 1.688; its --window 2 table reads h=1e-6 1.675, h=1e-7 0.136. Capsule: 375 crossings, seam about 4.1, worst 1.272. soft=0.03,eps=0.03: 63 crossings, seam about 0.69, worst 0.41. Reach 1.01: 1539 crossings, worst 0.92. I profiled three of the default's reported spots in 6e-6 steps (with the earlier offsets): each is a continuous ramp over about 3e-5, passing through intermediate values, not a step. Cause: each drop's map stretches older ink strongly just outside its edge and the stretches multiply through nested layers, so older ink forms very thin steep bands. They line drop edges rather than lattice lines, and act as hard edges at any render size. So: C0 in principle, jumps in practice, as with any crisp ink boundary. scan3 finds 0 real jumps in 3D at layers=20,soft=0.01 with 240k segments, with many steep slopes (35927). Fixed along the way: comb sign flip (5762 crossings) replaced by Lu's one direction form; capsule arc measured from the wrong end (14726 crossings); capsule transport leaving its cell; layer offsets growing with the index, which cost float precision at old layers (923 down to 583 crossings). Thin bands alias, and the entry's risk is real: thin rings alias through compression.

ink-drop-layers.port_notes: Own-cell lattice per layer, no window. Keep R2 layer offsets fractional, and rotate each layer by a table of cos and sin. Newest first; accumulate accum += trans * a * tone, trans *= 1 - a, with masks, no early out. Transport: t = sat((d - r) / (Rt - r)), e = r (1 - t), eps' = eps (1 - t), s = sqrt(max(d^2 - e^2, 0) + eps'^2) - eps', which is the identity at Rt, so it needs no neighbour. Capsule: Rt = R - L/2, L <= 1.2 (R - r). Comb: Lu eq 1 with a direction per stage, cheap: one floor, no hash. A port could offer Layers as a constant per node so rotation tables are built when it is set.

master.one_liner: Real paper marbling (suminagashi, ebru): an ordered stack of ink drops and capsule strokes where each new deposit pushes all older ink aside by a closed-form map, so the last drop is round and older ones are squeezed into nested rounded polygons.
master.look: Round new drops with nested rings, older drops dented by them into rounded polygons, oldest ones reduced to thin curved slivers between the others, all with crisp ink boundaries. With a comb stage, classic nonpareil and bouquet marbling. With Source = FBm the background is carried around each drop as if it floated. Good for marbled paper, agate and jasper slabs, cell tissue, oil on water, pebbly lava. In relief with Rings it reads as nested terraces squeezed together.
master.algorithm:
Lu, Jaffer et al. 2012 give the drop map: forward P' = C + (P-C)*sqrt(1 + r^2/|P-C|^2), inverse for rendering Q' = C + (Q-C)*sqrt(1 - r^2/|Q-C|^2) when |Q-C| > r, otherwise Q is inside the drop. Evaluating the inverses newest first is already pointwise. Liu et al. 2026 generalise the disc to a capsule of segment length L: sigma = C/(L + sqrt(L^2 + pi*C)), C = (sigma' - r)*(2L + pi*(sigma' + r)), with sigma the distance to the segment and arclength fraction along the parallel curve preserved; L = 0 reduces to sigma = sqrt(sigma'^2 - r^2).
WHAT I CHANGED TO FIT: the exact map has an infinite 1/d tail, so a lattice of drops would need a huge window and the sum diverges. I fade the inserted radius to zero at Reach*r, confined to the drop's own cell, so one site per layer and no window. The cost is that older ink is compressed in an annulus instead of being pushed to infinity, so it is not area preserving beyond the near field.
accum = 0; trans = 1; q = p
for i = N-1 down to 0:   // fixed loop, newest first
  g = Rot(i*2.39996)*q*scale + R2(i); c = floor(g); f = g - c; h = hash(c, seed + i*prime)
  r = lerp(Rmin, Rmax, rnd(h,0)^2); R = min(r*Reach, 0.5); o = 0.5 + (0.5 - R)*rnd11D(h)   // the disc of radius R stays in this cell
  active = rnd(h,2) < Density; v = f - o; d2 = dot(v,v); d = sqrt(d2)
  a = active * sat((r - d)/Softness + 0.5)
  col = RingTone(rnd11(h,3), d/r)   // base tone + RingContrast*tri(Rings*d/r + phase), or Source read in the drop's own seed
  accum += trans*a*col; trans *= 1 - a
  t = sat((d - r)/(R - r)); e = r*(1 - t); s2 = max(d2 - e*e, 0)   // s(r)=0, s(R)=R, ds/dd>0, so it is a homeomorphism of the annulus onto the disc
  v2 = Select(active, v*sqrt(s2)*InvSqrt(d2 + eps), v)
  q += Rot(-i*2.39996)*(v2 - v)/scale
  every CombEvery layers apply a tine family (Lu eq. 1, an area preserving shear, inverse is minus the shift): d = dot(q-A,N); dp = spacing/2 - abs(fmod(d,spacing) - spacing/2); q -= (alpha*lambda/(dp + lambda))*M
return accum + trans*Source(q)   // bottom layer is any node, carried through every drop
Capsule shape: frame on the stroke, fold to the first quadrant by abs. Flank when |x| < L/2: sigma' = |y|, arc = |x|. Cap otherwise: sigma' = dist to (L/2,0), arc = L/2 + sigma'*angle. Map sigma' with the formula above using e for r, set arc2 = arc*P(sigma)/P(sigma') with P(s) = (L + 2*pi*s)/2, then rebuild the point. One polynomial atan and one sin/cos per layer.
master.why_new: Different output. Nearest are StampLayers, DomeHeap and PebblePile (stack with no displacement, so older shapes are only clipped, never deformed), ScatterWarp source stamps (a summed forward warp with no order and no deposit, so nothing can be inside a drop), and DomainWarpFlow or DomainWarpShear Marble (fluid look with no ink bodies). None gives the signature of marbling: later ink dents earlier ink and contours stay sharp at any resolution. A graph cannot do it because each layer needs the position left by the layer before it plus a per-cell hash.
master.simd_plan: Own-cell lattice per layer, no window. Coverage and transport with Select, no early out. Rotation per layer so layers do not share axes. 2D, 3D and 4D use the same disc code; for exact volume in 3D use s^3 = d^3 - e^3 (Solid Mathematical Marbling), the s^2 form also works visually and avoids Pow. 4D needed for tiling: spheres in 4D. Estimate AVX2: 1 to 1.5 ns per disc layer in 2D, 2 to 3 ns in 3D, so N = 16 about 20 / 40 / 60 ns plus one Source eval; capsule about 3x per layer.
master.continuity: C0 with Softness > 0: the transport fades to identity inside each cell and coverage is continuous. With Softness near 0 ink edges are jumps by design.
master.params: Layers (int), Density (hybrid, read at the sample), Radius Min/Max, Reach (1.2 to 3), Rings (int), Ring Contrast, Softness, Shape (Disc, Capsule), Stroke Length, Comb Every, Comb Spacing, Comb Amount, Comb Wave, Source (hybrid; constant gives a flat tank). Output: Ink, Layer Index, Ring Coordinate.
master.risks: Compact reach pinches rings harder than real marbling, so low Reach may look like dents rather than flow. R <= 0.5 limits drop size to the layer lattice. Near a drop edge the older pattern is radially stretched and may show streaks when Softness is tiny. Many thin rings alias through compression, since the mapped frequency is unbounded near s = 0.
sources: https://www.pubmed.gov/24807307/ (Solid Mathematical Marbling, search snippet only)

ink-drop-layers.changed_from_entry: Added the eps softening of the square root, because the exact form's infinite slope at s = 0 compounds across layers; it is a small change to the look and does not end the steep bands. Capsule arc runs from the flank mid point through the cap to the tip, P(s) = (L + pi s) / 2, since the entry's (L + 2 pi s) / 2 did not match a quarter perimeter of the parallel curve. Capsule transport is shortened by L/2. The 3D form uses the s^2 map. Layer Index and Ring Coordinate outputs not built. Reach default 2.

Equirect: the same cells, stretched into wide bands only toward the top and bottom rows, as the projection does. Lookup: patchy continents of flat tiles. fibonacci-cells.artifacts: Entry's 9 candidates: REAL short seams, Edge 11 crossings up to 0.68, Stamp 39 crossings up to 0.26, wrong F2 0.02 to 0.3 percent at the entry's jitter. Fixed by a 13 candidate window; now 0 real jumps by bisection for Edge and Distance at J <= 0.5 and N from 50 to 200000, including with the pole in view. At J = 0.8 seams come back (29 crossings, worst 0.60), so Jitter must be capped near 0.5 spacing. Stamp reach must stay inside the window: size=0.62 gave small real jumps up to 0.065 in layers above the first (33 crossings at thr 0.02), size=0.5 gave 7 (worst 0.029), size=0.45 gave 0, at J=0.5. Value and Lookup are mosaics. plain c0 on view=1 reads 1.0 only because of the globe limb. Stamp layers: the crater is C0 with a crease at the rim and the bowl edge. Spiral pattern at jitter 0 not looked at; rot moves the pole by seed.

fibonacci-cells.port_notes: Branch free: log, floor, 2 rounds, 2x2 solve, 4 candidates with sincos, then 13 candidates by angle addition. Keep a = (2i+1)/N so 1 - z^2 = a(2-a) has no cancellation at the poles. Indices from i * 2654435769u wrap exactly. Masks for candidates outside [0,N). A crater's frame costs a normalise and a cross per candidate; a port could use a frame from q and a hashed in-plane angle.

master.one_liner: Cells native to the sphere: O(1) nearest point on a spherical Fibonacci set, giving near equal-area cells with no cube seams and no pole pinch, plus Lookup and a tangent plane Stamp, so craters stay round and plates stay even at any latitude.
master.look: On an equirect map, cells that stretch toward the poles only as the projection does; on the globe, even polygons of one size, with no slivers. Jitter 0 shows a sunflower spiral around the poles, which jitter and a random rotation hide. Stamp with a crater profile gives a moon whose craters are all truly round.
master.algorithm:
Points i in [0,N): z_i = 1 - (2i+1)/N, phi_i = 2 pi * frac(i*Phi), from i*2654435769u in 32 bit wraparound so it is exact (the Phyllotaxis trick).
Inverse for unit p, after Keinert et al. 2015, written from memory of the paper, to be verified by brute force in the smallest test:
  phi = atan2 approximation, z = p.z
  k = max(2, floor( log(N*pi*sqrt5*(1-z*z)) / log(Phi^2) ))
  F0 = round(Phi^k/sqrt5), F1 = round(Phi^(k+1)/sqrt5)
  basis columns j in {0,1}: dphi_j = 2 pi*( frac((F_j+1)*Phi) - (Phi-1) ), dz_j = -2*F_j/N
  c = floor( B^-1 * (phi, z - (1-1/N)) )
  candidates: i = clamp( F0*(c.x+u) + F1*(c.y+v), 0, N-1 ) for u,v in {0,1}; keep the nearest by chord.
That gives F1 with 4 candidates. Jitter or F2: take the nearest i0 and its 8 lattice neighbours i0 +- F0, +- F1, +- (F0+F1), +- (F0-F1); site q_i moved along the tangent by J*spacing*rnd2(h_i), then F1 and F2 over the 9.
spacing = sqrt(4 pi/N). Hash on i.
Outputs: Value rnd(h_i). Distance: chord/spacing. Edge: F2-F1. Lookup: Source(q_i), the planet form of CellularLookup. Stamp: frame e1 = normalize(cross(q_i, axis from hash)), e2 = cross(q_i, e1); out = Source( dot(p-q_i,e1)/spacing, dot(p-q_i,e2)/spacing ) called in 2D with seed + i, so a Stamp or crater node works unchanged on the surface. Layers: independent nodes with N*4 per level.
master.why_new: Clearly different output on a sphere. Nearest: DomainMap Sphere samples a 3D Cellular, so cells are slices of 3D cells: sizes vary, some are slivers cut by a sphere and a crater stamp at a 3D site has its centre off the surface. Phyllotaxis is the planar Fermat version of the same trick. Evidence read: forum advice converges on evaluating 3D noise on the sphere, since per face 2D noise makes seams at cube edges (Unity, Stack Exchange, Three.js threads). Nothing I read gives surface features of controlled size; Panda3D threads prefer the spherified cube for even spacing, not exactly even. Red Blob does not cover spheres. Planet games such as No Man's Sky and Elite are the audience, though I found nothing on how they place surface features.
master.simd_plan: Branch free: log, floor, 2 round, 2x2 solve, 4 or 9 candidates. Direct: 4 sincos, about 6-8 ns. With jitter 9 candidates: 2-3 sincos for the local basis then complex multiplies and 9 sqrt, about 10 ns, similar to 3D CellularDistance at 12 ns (estimates). 2D Gen reads x and y as equirect longitude and latitude, for sheets. 3D normalises p. 4D: w passes to Source as a third coordinate, for animation; it cannot tile, which is correct for a sphere.
master.continuity: Distance C0, Edge C0, Lookup and Value piecewise constant, Stamp C0 if the stamp reaches 0 inside the cell. At the poles the clamp on i keeps it continuous; check there first.
master.params: Count N (int), Seed Offset, Grid Jitter, Output enum (Value, Distance, Edge, Lookup, Stamp), Source (hybrid), Output Min/Max
master.risks: Float32 precision: paper mentions GPU float issues; N above 1e6 is untested and the wrap multiply only saves part of it. The 4 candidate claim is from memory. Local lattice shape changes with k, so the look changes bandwise at low jitter. Spiral visible without jitter. Costs as much as 3D Worley once jittered, so its case is shape, not speed. Hybrid N is impossible. Sphere only.

sphere-charts.look: Plain render: a globe covered in Dendry river trees carved into terrain, dark branching channels of the same kind as on the flat sheet next to it, with no pole or cube mark visible at Sharp 3. Rivers end in soft crossfades in the blend bands instead of connecting across them; at the globe's centre one network dims where a neighbouring chart takes over. FBm source looks like plain fbm on a sphere, no visible structure. Cells at Variance: polygons stay readable, with soft double outlines near chart corners. Cells at Height: charts cut in over each other, with no ghost lines but some cut cells. Mask at Mean blend: crisp coast on most of the globe, grey gradient patches in blend bands. At Sharp 10 and Cut 0.3 the cube becomes visible on Dendry as a square patch, since each chart has its own low frequency terrain, so a narrow band is worse for sources with large scale content.
sphere-charts.dims: 3D (normalises p) measured working, including through vol. 2D is a view here; the real node's 2D Gen would pass through (view=2). 4D not built.
sphere-charts.range: FBm source (std about 0.49): -1.66 to 1.78 over 8 seeds in Variance blend, which keeps std but not the range bound. Not normalised to -1..1 in the prototype. No NaNs.
sphere-charts.artifacts: No seam from the charts: 0 real jumps on three continuous sources and on Height after its fix. The default Dendry source has real seams of its own, 22 crossings, worst 0.37 on the sphere and 12 crossings, worst 0.32 on the flat sheet with no charts at all, from the lite 3x3 window in this copy with the carve output (the parent's carve view uses a larger window). Hard edged sources double up in blend bands. Rivers do not join across bands. Height blend biases the mean upward near chart corners (mean +0.35 at corners against +0.03 at centres on an FBm source of std 0.49), since it takes a max of up to three values.

master.one_liner: Puts any 2D-only graph on a planet with no pinch and no seam: three area preserving Lambert charts blended by the normal, three source evals, feature size within about 13 percent, and area share preserved.
master.look: A sphere covered with whatever the 2D graph draws, at consistent size and at the same character as on a flat sheet: Dendry rivers, ErosionFilter drainage, TileDomain, roads. Blend zones around the 8 cube corner directions and 12 edge arcs read as soft crossfades for smooth sources and as double exposures for hard edged ones.
master.algorithm:
n = p/|p|. For each axis a with other two axes b, c:
  s = sign(n_a); k = sqrt(2/(1+|n_a|)); u = R*k*n_b, v = R*k*n_c      // Lambert azimuthal, exactly area preserving
  seed_a = seed + Stride*(2a + (s>0))
  v_a = Source(seed_a, u, v) in 2D
  w_a = max(0, |n_a| - Cut)^Sharp
Blend: Variance: sum w_a v_a / sqrt(sum w_a^2). Mean: sum w_a v_a / sum w_a. Height: Max of v_a + Sharp2*w_a, as HeightBlend does it.
Chart scale at colatitude theta is cos(theta/2) radially and its inverse across. At the cube corner, the worst point where all weights are equal, theta = 54.7 degrees, so the scale is 0.888 by 1.126.
The seed jump at n_a = 0 is invisible because w_a is already 0 there, and seeds are per lane so it is branch free.
3 evals for every lane; a lane with w_a = 0 still evaluates unless the whole batch has none, in which case that chart is skipped.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Nearest: DomainMap Sphere runs the source in 3D, which is fine for isotropic noise and useless for nodes whose look or cost is 2D: DendryNoise's 3D is the coarsest level only, ErosionFilter needs an up axis, and a 3D cellular costs 3x its 2D. The cube sphere users get seams; forum threads repeat this. Nearest in spirit, StochasticPatch: blends frames in the plane. Stock graph: three Fades plus a nonlinear offset per chart, roughly 30 nodes (estimate). Area preservation means a mask's share carries to the globe, unlike gnomonic cube faces, which stretch up to 3x at a face corner. Evidence read: MathWorks on pinching where several radii map to one spot, Panda3D on cube maps, libnoise on pole artefacts in wrapped maps.
master.simd_plan: One sqrt per chart plus 3 Source calls in lower dimension, plus small math. Cost 3x 2D Source plus about 2 ns. Against 3D Source: tie for Cellular (11.7 vs 12 ns), loss for Perlin (3.3 vs 2.2), and win only because the look is available. 2D Gen passes through. 4D gives Source (u,v,w) in 3D, so animated planets work; no tiling, correct for a sphere.
master.continuity: C0, with weights at 0 where seeds change. C1 with Sharp >= 2 and a C1 Source.
master.params: Source, Radius (world units), Sharp, Cut, Blend enum (Variance, Mean, Height), Stride
master.risks: Hard edged sources double up in the blend bands. Fractal hierarchy of a 2D network will not connect across a blend band: rivers end in a crossfade. Variance blend preserves contrast but moves mean height slightly near corners. Three evals are not a saving. A small Cut with high Sharp narrows bands but raises the visible scale step.

measured.scalar_vs_perlin: FBm source 6 octaves: 17.89x perlin2, 904 ns; the same source flat: 6.78x, 359 ns, so the wrapper costs 2.52x its source here (the prototype skips zero weight charts, a port would not). Dendry source: 70.98x, 3760 ns; flat 30.36x, 1533 ns. Measured.

modular-cusps.look: Plain render: the textbook Ford circles, big discs at integers, then 1/8 radius at the half, and rapidly smaller ones along the bottom axis, all tangent. Ford spheres in vol: big spheres on a floor with smaller spheres in the gaps; the Eisenstein form has a visibly hexagonal arrangement in the cut face. Strip CuspValue: tall pointed arches like cathedral windows in flat greys, refining toward the bottom edge. Strip Eta: smooth white domes on black, soft version of the same arches. Strip J: bold black and white zebra arches that break into dense moire and pixel noise in the lower half, striking and heavily aliased. Source Eta: white wandering ribbons and rings on dark, like agate or smoke, with dotted fine fringes running along contours; those dots are single pixel scale at this window.
modular-cusps.dims: 2D measured for HalfPlane, Strip and Source. 3D measured: Ford spheres on the Picard group and on the Eisenstein group, and Source mode through vol. 4D not built (Source mode is dimension agnostic, Hurwitz form unchecked).
modular-cusps.range: Horoball, Height, Eta clamp to -1..1. Source Eta over 8 seeds: -0.987 to 1.000, mean -0.517. No NaNs. Position mode ignores the seed except for CuspValue, measured seed sensitivity 0.000. 3D in position mode reaches -48 with ceil=1 far above the packing, since ceil is a slope for the vol view, not a clamped output.
modular-cusps.artifacts: No seams: 0 real jumps on all continuous outputs, including across unit arcs and x = +-1/2 for Eta. CuspValue jumps by nature. Source mode has very steep slopes near B = 0 (it pulls the whole cusp hierarchy into a thin band) and reads as dotted aliasing there; a port cannot prefilter it. Strip J aliases heavily in the lower half. Position mode is non-stationary and has no seed in its geometry. In 3D the unit horoball at infinity is a lid over the spheres, so ceil=1 removes it and leaves a tiny flat where a sphere touches t = 1.

master.one_liner: Gauss reduction of the sample into the modular fundamental domain, done as a fixed loop, gives exact Ford circles, the Farey horoball mosaic and seam-free modular invariants (Dedekind eta, j) from one kernel; the Picard group gives Ford spheres in 3D.
master.look: The famous pictures, computed exactly and cheaply: Horoball gives the Ford circle packing (big circles at integers, 1/8 at halves, 1/18 at thirds, down to pixel size at the axis), the 3D form a packing of tangent spheres resting on a plane with the same fractal depth. CuspValue is a mosaic of curvilinear cells that refine without end toward the axis. Eta is a smooth field of bumps at every image of rho: a hyperbolic frost or bubble carpet where each bump is a scaled copy of the big one, smooth everywhere. Source mode threads beads of all sizes along any contour of B: fractal fringing on a coastline, frost along a crack, horoball pearls on a vein network. Good for ornament, glass, foam against a wall, fractal fringes, and as a hierarchy signal (log H) without any lattice.
master.algorithm:
Position mode 2D: tau = (x, y) with y = |y| + eps (HalfPlane) or y = exp(-k*y) (Strip: spreads the interesting band 0<y<1 over the whole axis).
Ints a=1,b=0,c=0,d=1 (gamma, reduced = gamma*tau; the cusp whose horoball wins is -d/c).
for i in 0..Steps-1 (Steps=10, fixed):
  n = Round(x); x -= n; a -= n*c; b -= n*d                 (T^-n)
  r2 = x*x + y*y; inv = r2 < 1
  x = Select(inv, -x/r2, x); y = Select(inv, y/r2, y)      (S: tau -> -1/tau)
  (a,b,c,d) = Select(inv, (-c,-d,a,b), (a,b,c,d))
H = y   (cusp height = max over the orbit of Im; exactly SL(2,Z)-invariant once reduced, and the loop only ever increases y)
converged = (r2 >= 1) at exit; near the real axis (y below ~1e-3) 10 steps may not reduce: H is then a lower bound and Eta is faded to 0 there, which is its true limit anyway.
Outputs:
  Height   : saturate(log2(H)/Range). C0, creases on geodesic arcs.
  Horoball : smoothstep(Level-soft, Level+soft, H). H >= 1 is exactly the union of the Ford circles (open discs of radius 1/(2 q^2) tangent to the axis at p/q); Level = c gives radius 1/(2 c q^2), so one float sweeps a whole family of tangent packings.
  CuspValue: rnd11(hash(c,d)) with (c,d) sign-normalised: every point belongs to the cusp whose horoball is highest there, an infinitely refining mosaic bounded by geodesic arcs (the Ford/Dirichlet domains).
  Eta      : on the reduced tau (y >= 0.866): m = exp(-2 pi y); q = m*(cos 2 pi x, sin 2 pi x); etaAbs = exp(-pi y/12)*|1-q|*|1-q^2|*|1-q^3| (|q| <= 0.0043 after reduction so three factors are exact to 1e-8); out = y^(1/4)*etaAbs/0.7764 (its max, at rho = exp(2 pi i/3)). Real-analytic and invariant: no creases anywhere.
  J        : j = 1/q + 744 + 196884 q + 21493760 q^2 (complex, 3 terms are enough after reduction); out = tanh(Re j / S) or log(1+|j|)/L.
Source mode (any dimension): tau = (A(p), |B(p)| + eps) from two source nodes, same loop and outputs; the cusps then sit on the zero set of B and the whole modular picture is pulled back along it.
3D position mode (Picard group PSL(2,Z[i]) on H^3): z = x + i y horizontal (Up Axis enum picks t), t = |up| + eps. Per step: m = Round(z) componentwise (Gaussian integer); z -= m; r2 = |z|^2 + t^2; if r2 < 1: z = -conj(z)/r2, t = t/r2. gamma entries are Gaussian integers (8 int lanes). H = t; H >= 1 is exactly the union of the Ford spheres, radius 1/(2|q|^2) tangent to the plane at Gaussian rationals p/q, which are tangent or disjoint (Northshield 2015). Height, Horoball, CuspValue carry over; Eta has no cheap 3D analogue. Lattice enum: Gaussian (square rounding) or Eisenstein (hex rounding, PSL(2,Z[omega]), tetrahedral sphere packing).
4D: Source mode (dimension agnostic). A Hurwitz-quaternion version on H^5 should exist (same loop with quaternion rounding and inversion) but I have not checked it.
master.why_new: Nothing on the sheets is hyperbolic-arithmetic. Nearest: domain-hyperbolic-tiling (Poincare disk {P,Q} fold, a kaleidoscope of a source) and cellular-circle-packing (Apollonian corner circles by Descartes, a few levels in a window). This node needs no source and no window, has infinite depth at fixed cost, and its Eta and J outputs are seam-free because they are true modular invariants, which no fold-and-sample domain node can give. The Ford packing is itself an Apollonian gasket (curvatures 0,0,1,1) obtained for the price of ten complex reciprocals.
master.simd_plan: One fixed loop of Steps iterations: Round, two FMAs, one reciprocal, two float Selects, four int Selects and two int FMAs per step: about 1 ns per step, so ~10 ns 2D and ~14 ns 3D at Steps=10 (6 steps is enough for the strip above y=0.01). No window, no hash except the cusp id. Eta costs one Exp, one Sin/Cos pair and three complex products extra. Position mode is non-stationary like Gradient or SineWave; Source mode is stationary and dimension agnostic, so 4D and tiling come from the sources.
master.continuity: Height and Horoball C0 (max of smooth functions, creases on geodesics); CuspValue discontinuous by nature (a mosaic); Eta and J C-infinity in theory, in practice continuous down to the unreduced band near the axis, where they are faded to their true limit 0.
master.params: Mode enum {HalfPlane, Strip, Source}; Output enum {Height, Horoball, CuspValue, Eta, J}; Steps (int, 6..14); Level (hybrid, horoball cut); Softness; Strip Rate k; Up Axis; Lattice {Gaussian, Eisenstein} for 3D; sources A, B for Source mode; Seed only affects CuspValue hashing.
master.risks: Non-stationary in position mode (a strip picture), so its use is ornament and fringes rather than general noise. Float32 CF depth: beyond about 8 inversions x loses digits, so circles smaller than ~1e-5 are wrong, below the eye at any sane scale. Eisenstein rounding needs care to get the right fundamental cell.

modular-cusps.changed_from_entry: Eta output is -log of the normalised form, since the raw form spans only 0.989..1 over the floor of the domain, so the 'bumps at images of rho' are invisible and what shows is a dome on each cusp. Normaliser 0.7723, not 0.7764. HalfPlane reads y from the bottom of the harness window so the axis is at the bottom edge. 3D gets a ceil to take the infinity horoball off. Height output is -1..1 from H = sqrt(3)/2. Steps default 12.

tropical-facet.look: Curve: dark straight cracks that only run horizontally, vertically or on the diagonals, with faceted bright cells whose tops read as cut gems or chamfered roofs; no curved edge anywhere. Hillshade reads as Art Deco stained glass. Facet: square flat tops at random heights with chamfered ramps of the same few slopes; the relief looks like eroded mesas or an abstract city plan. Site: flat grey octagon-like paving, walls in 4 to 8 directions. 3D Curve: polyhedral grains with flat faces and almost constant cracks, like sawn or fractured rock. The entry's Barrier form: an axis aligned collage of rectangles with diagonals inside them, closer to Cubist collage than tropical curves, because the descending plates fill out to their barrier.
tropical-facet.dims: 2D and 3D measured working (3D through vol and check; 3D speed not measured). 4D not built: 81 terms at A <= 0.31 or 256 at A <= 0.75.
tropical-facet.range: Curve, Facet, Soft clamp to the output range, -1..1 over 8 seeds. Curve mean -0.288. Facet's native range depends on A. No NaNs.
tropical-facet.artifacts: No seams: 0 real jumps on all continuous outputs at the defaults. The window rule A <= 0.75 (4^D) and A <= 0.31 (3^D) is a proof of safety; the scan did not catch failures above it, but the clamp at Curve's top hides far ones. Strong lattice alignment: crease directions come from the lattice, the sites sit on it, cell sizes and rows stay readable as a loose grid in the Facet relief. Bright Curve tops show a central cross where the winner changes. Crack width varies by a factor of |q-p| since t2-t1 has slope 2|q-p|.

master.one_liner: A windowed min-plus (tropical) polynomial with integer slopes: concave piecewise-linear plates whose crease graph is a true tropical curve (rational-slope edges, balanced 3-valent vertices), with a temperature parameter that dequantises it smoothly and a crease-distance output that needs no search.
master.look: Cubist or woodcut ground: flat tilted plates with straight creases that can only run in 8 (or 16) directions, meeting in Y vertices with the integer balancing look of a tropical curve, i.e. a crystalline, hand-cut version of a Voronoi. Curve output thresholded is a linocut crack net of constant width with angular Y junctions. Soft at mid temperature is a smooth polygonal landscape with no creases; sweeping h is a continuous morph from blobs to crystal. In 3D: angular polyhedral grains with integer-normal faces, like a sawn mineral.
master.algorithm:
Window: the 3^D lattice points p around Round(x). For each p:
  h = hash(p); a_p = A * rnd11(h); v_p = integer vector with components in {-S..S}^D from hash bits (S = Slope Set, 1 or 2): the rational slopes are the tropical point
  d = x - p; t_p = a_p + Scale*dot(v_p, d) + K*max(0, Cheb(d) - 1)     with Cheb(d) = max_i |d_i|
  The barrier is itself a max-plus expression, so every t_p is piecewise linear and the result stays tropical.
  K = 2*(2A + 3*S*Scale) + 1: any term at Cheb(d) >= 1.5 (the window edge) is then larger than the smallest possible winner, so terms enter and leave the window only while losing and the min is continuous without any blend.
Keep the two smallest: t1 <= t2 (compare-swap chain over the window).
Outputs:
  Facet : t1, normalised. Concave piecewise linear: tilted flat plates meeting in V creases only. MaxPlus enum negates everything for ridges.
  Curve : t2 - t1. Zero exactly on the tropical curve and growing linearly away from it: constant-slope V valleys, so a threshold gives constant-width cracks with no distance search. Vertices are 3-valent and satisfy the balancing condition; edge directions are the normals of the differences v_p - v_q, a finite set (8 directions for S = 1).
  Soft  : t1 - h*log(sum_p exp(-(t_p - t1)/h)) (Maslov dequantisation, stable): h -> 0 recovers Facet, large h gives smooth blobs. SoftCurve uses only the two smallest terms.
  Site  : rnd11(hash(argmin)): a mosaic whose walls are straight with slopes from the finite direction set.
3D: the same with 27 terms, planes with integer normals, the Curve output is distance-like to the 2-skeleton of a tropical surface: a polyhedral crystal mosaic. 4D: 81 terms.
master.why_new: simplex-facet gives piecewise planar interpolation with arbitrary slopes and both ridges and valleys; cellular-planes gives tilted planes per cell with jumps or a smooth blend; poly-gauge gives pyramids to the walls. None restricts slopes to a lattice, none gives the balanced rational-slope crease graph, and none has the exact crease distance t2 - t1 for free. The temperature output makes the tropical point visible: CellularSmooth is already -h log sum exp(-d/h), the dequantisation of Voronoi; this node dequantises a polynomial with integer slopes instead of a distance.
master.simd_plan: 3^D window like CellularDistance but each term is a hash, a dot with small ints, one max and a compare-swap: cheaper than a Euclidean cell. Estimate ~3-4 ns 2D, ~10 ns 3D, ~35 ns 4D. Soft adds one Exp per term. Branch free; 4D via GenT over the window.
master.continuity: Facet, Curve and Site-free outputs are C0 by the barrier argument (piecewise linear, creases only); Soft is C-infinity for h > 0; Site is a mosaic.
master.params: Amplitude A, Scale (slope magnitude), Slope Set enum {Axis: v in {(+-1,0),(0,+-1),0}, Octant: S=1, Knight: S=2}, Temperature h (hybrid), Output enum {Facet, Curve, Soft, SoftCurve, Site}, MaxPlus (enum), Feature Scale, Seed.
master.risks: The Chebyshev barrier can show square rims around isolated low sites; a quadratic or L1 barrier changes the look. Integer slopes with S = 1 may feel too regular; with S = 2 the direction set grows to 16 and the crystalline feel weakens.

tropical-facet.changed_from_entry: The entry's barrier form gave square rims as the entry warned, and its K was too small for the second best term in 2D (it needs 4A + 5 D S Scale + 1, not 4A + 6 S Scale + 1). Default is now t_p = 2 a_p + Scale |x-p|^2, an additively weighted power diagram on the lattice, which equals a true tropical polynomial plus a global quadratic. Slope sets are replaced by the lattice itself: crease normals are q - p. Facet removes the global quadratic with a periodic term, which makes it exactly piecewise linear with a finite slope set; Barrier stays as form=0.

lens-ridges.look: Plain render: vertical furrowed bark, thin dark fissures wandering and crossing at shallow angles, enclosing grey to bright lenses, with a finer second family of fissures over them. Relief with hscale 40: clumps of pointed scales over dark furrows, like pine bark, a bit lumpy. 3D at an earlier setting: stacked sheets that pinch out and rejoin, with orange cut faces showing lens-shaped beds, like boudinaged rock, the strongest image of this idea. Rank bands: flat toned strata that pinch at crossings. Beside the stock comparison, DomainAxisScale on F2-F1 with x stretched 8x: stock is cleaner and has blunt strip-like cells with bright axes; LensRidges has needle ends and irregular crossing, more organic but busier. With only low Freq (0.15 as in the entry's smallest test) it reads as a stack of wavy lines, not interlocking lenses, as the entry feared.

It jumps on the vertical line through every crossing above or below the sample. In Plate's Tone that gave 142 real jump crossings, worst 0.76, visible as rectangles in the first render. Fixed for Plate and Lens by a tone keyed on rank (count of curves below) which is constant in a face. No pointwise per-lens id was found: rank separates faces across a curve, not along a band. Second, D with the slope correction jumps slightly where curves cross away from the sample, so slope correction is off by default and width is vertical. Row rhythm is visible as a preferred direction by design: axis 10.70.

master.one_liner: Long curves that wander and cross at shallow angles leave lens-shaped gaps, and a gap-based dome makes each lens taller where it is fatter: braided river bars, furrowed bark, tendons, mylonite, with no cell search and no Voronoi corners.
master.look: Long tapered ridges that interlock: each ends in a sharp point where its two bounding curves cross, and neighbours fill the space. Low Freq: thick oak or pine bark furrows, split firewood. High Wander: braided channels with eyot-shaped bars when inverted. Thin Width: tendons, muscle, sheared rock. Upstream warp bends the whole bundle around knots. In 3D, boudin-like lenses inside rock.
master.algorithm:
Target looks from tools: Gaea's Anastomosis node (the changelog only names it), Houdini 21 Grunge Pine Bark and Birch Bark (layers of elongated cells), Lefebvre and Neyret's Synthesizing Bark (fracture-based, abstract only). None gives a pointwise form. Mechanism is mine, prompted by the Cyclic slice shear creases discovery.
(x,y) = Rot(Direction)*p*scale; i0 = floor(y); yUp = +inf; yDn = -inf
for i in i0-K..i0+K:
  h = hash(i, seed); (n, dn) = Noise1D(x*Freq + offset(h), h)   // value and derivative
  yi = i + 0.5 + Wander*n; si = Wander*Freq*dn
  mask = yi > y
  update min yUp, sUp, idUp where mask; update max yDn, sDn, idDn where !mask
g = yUp - yDn; t = (y - yDn)/g
D = min((yUp - y)*InvSqrt(1 + sUp^2), (y - yDn)*InvSqrt(1 + sDn^2))
Network = sat(D/Width)
Lens = 4*t*(1-t)*pow(g, Gamma)   // zero on every curve, tallest in the widest part
Plate = pow(sat(D/Width), Round)*(1 + Tone*rnd11(hash(idUp, idDn)))
The lens's identity is the unordered pair of curves bounding it, which is constant inside it.
Window rule, worked out from the bounds on |n| <= 1: Wander <= 0.5 needs K = 1 (3 rows); Wander <= 1 needs K = 3 (7 rows). Below that an outside curve could be the nearest and leave a seam.
3D: yi depends on (x,z) through 2D noise, giving pillows and pinching sheets. Strands mode: rows on (y,z), 1D in x, D as a tube distance, giving crossing fibres; 49 curves, so offline only.
master.why_new: Different output. Stretched Voronoi gives elongated polygons with blunt corners and Y junctions; a lens has two curved sides and needle ends. FlowNetwork and DendryNoise merge and never rejoin. WaveLattice crosses lines at symmetric wide angles. StreakScatter and FiberNoise are short strokes. SignCodeRegions has X junctions but round blobs. EigenStrata pinches beds in 3D at codimension 2 and never crosses; this is a single cheap curve family per row in 2D. The gap dome is C0 by construction and needs the two ordered neighbours, so a graph cannot do it.
master.simd_plan: Fixed row window with masks, Min and Select. Rotation is global, with no hybrid direction: use an upstream warp, since hybrid rotation would shear. Noise1D is 2 hashes, a quintic and its derivative. Estimate AVX2: 7 rows about 8 ns in 2D, 7 rows of 2D noise about 20 ns in 3D, 7 rows of 3D noise about 35 ns in 4D. Tileable only through the usual 4D route, and row direction is not preserved around that torus, so tiling is an open question.
master.continuity: C0 for Network, Lens and Plate: identity changes only where the height is 0. C1 not expected: Lens has a kink at curve lines. Lens ID jumps.
master.params: Direction, Wander (hybrid read per lane is possible but changes which K is safe), Freq, Width (hybrid), Gamma, Round, Tone, Row Scale. Output: Network, Lens, Plate, Lens ID.
master.risks: With a single noise per row the row rhythm may show as even spacing; add jitter and a second octave. Crossings are true X, whereas real channels merge along a stretch, so close-ups may read as woven not braided. K = 3 for good wander is 7 curves, not the cheap 3. Direction must be global.

master.one_liner: A p-adic isometry as a domain map: hashed swaps of the two halves of every dyadic block at every level (or the bit-reversal Monna map) scramble the source into a recursive quilt whose pieces stay intact at all finer scales.
master.look: The source cut into a hierarchy of squares and reassembled: large quarters swapped, inside them halves swapped, down to small tiles, so a smooth noise becomes a glitch quilt or a patchwork whose seams exist at every power of two and whose pieces each still carry a coherent fragment of the original. BitReverse turns a gradient into a fine interleaved comb at every scale. Good for glitch art, cut-and-reassembled fabric, circuit-like panels, deliberately broken continuity.
master.algorithm:
per axis (Coupled enum uses the D-dimensional block id in the hash so squares move as squares):
  u = x/Period; i = Floor(u); f = u - i; m = int(f*2^Depth); g = f*2^Depth - m (sub-block fraction)
  for level l = 0..Depth-1 (coarse to fine, fixed): block = m >> (Depth - l); flip = hash(axis, i, l, block) & 1; m ^= flip << (Depth - 1 - l)   swap the two halves of the 2^-l block containing the point
  (BitReverse mode: m = reverse of the Depth bits of m, the Monna map; Gray mode: m ^= m >> 1)
  x' = (i + (m + g)/2^Depth)*Period; sample Source at x'.
Swapping the halves of a dyadic block preserves the 2-adic distance between any two points (the length of their shared prefix), so every block keeps its interior continuity down to the finest level while its placement is scrambled at every scale: a recursive quilt. Output distribution equals the source's.
master.why_new: tile-split and quad-stamp lay out hierarchical squares with their own content; stochastic-patch and cell-frame scatter patches with new frames. None permutes the domain while keeping multi-scale internal coherence, and none is an ultrametric isometry; it costs about one nanosecond. Honest limits: deterministic lattice, discontinuous on all dyadic lines, no natural look.
master.simd_plan: Depth iterations of shift, hash and xor per axis, all integer: ~1 ns per axis plus the source; any dimension; branch free; tiles with Period.
master.continuity: Discontinuous across every dyadic line that was flipped; continuous inside the finest unflipped blocks; the source's own continuity is preserved within pieces.
master.params: Period, Depth (int, 3..8), Mode enum {RandomSwaps, BitReverse, Gray}, Coupled (enum), Levels Min/Max (restrict which scales are scrambled), Seed, Source.
master.risks: A one-trick decorative effect; lattice-locked; could be judged a graph-recipe-like curiosity.

nested-fbm.merged_into: FractalFBm (real node): a Nest Rule enum plus Max Octave and First Octave members. It looks like FBm by design, and stock FractalFBm over Perlin at lacunarity 2 already has the exact vanishing on dyadic grids, measured below.

master.one_liner: FBm whose octave lattices nest through an integer rotation matrix, so every finer octave is exactly zero on coarser lattice vertices: a coarse mesh gets its exact final height from a few octaves, with no alias, no pop at shared vertices and no axis aligned octaves.
master.look: FBm, with less axis cross in the FFT at Rot45x2 than lacunarity 2. Slightly gappier octave spacing at 2.83, so a lower Gain is likely better. Not a new look: the point is the coarse mesh sits on the fine one.
master.algorithm:
Gradient noise is exactly 0 at its lattice points: at a lattice point the corner dot is zero and the other weights are zero. If x_(i+1) = M*x_i with M an integer matrix, then lattice points of octave i map to lattice points of octave i+1. So L_0 is a subset of L_1 is a subset of L_2... and all octaves j >= k vanish on L_k.
Rules (2D):
  Aligned2: M = 2I. Lacunarity 2. This is what stock FractalFBm over Perlin already does.
  Rot45x2: M = [[2,-2],[2,2]], lacunarity 2.83, rotates 45 degrees. M^k = 2^(k+floor(k/2)) * (unit or [[1,-1],[1,1]]), so every dyadic grid nests: octave k vanishes on spacing S/2^j when j <= k + floor(k/2). Spacing S/2 needs 1 octave, S/4 and S/8 need 2, S/16 needs 3, S/32 and S/64 need 4.
  Rot45: M = [[1,-1],[1,1]], lacunarity 1.41, 2 octaves per doubling, twice the cost.
  Pyth5: M = [[2,-1],[1,2]], lacunarity 2.24, rotates 26.57 degrees, 5-adic grid when alternated with its transpose.
3D: Aligned2 for dyadic octrees. Rot3: M = [[1,2,2],[2,1,-2],[-2,2,-1]] (quaternion 1+i+j), lacunarity 3 with a real rotation, nesting on 9-adic grids when alternated with its transpose. I found no integer similarity that rotates and nests dyadically in 3D.
Gen: sum = Base Value*ValueNoise(x_0); for i < MaxOctave(p): sum += A_i*Grad(seed+i, x_i); x_(i+1) = M*x_i. Base Value keeps level 0 vertices from all reading 0.
Max Octave is hybrid, batch level loop break like FractalForecast. Ridged: 1-|n| at a vertex is 1 for all skipped octaves, so a coarse vertex gets a known constant tail sum and stays exact.
First Octave member: evaluate only a band, so an engine can compute only the octaves a finer LOD adds.
master.why_new: Hard made easy. Nearest stock node: FractalFBm over Perlin at lacunarity 2 has the vanishing property by accident and nobody documents it, and fixing its axis alignment with DomainRotate destroys it. Nearest idea: PeriodicFBm. Coarse LOD by octave dropping normally samples the wrong surface and aliases if you do not drop; here sampling a coarser grid costs fewer octaves and is exact at those vertices. Evidence read: Proland keeps levels consistent by upsample plus residual tiles, which needs stored data and a matched filter; Godot Voxel Tools and Cinevva describe popping, seams and cracks between LODs, with stitching and dithering as remedies at mesh level. A search found no write-up that uses this vanishing property for LOD, so I may have missed one.
master.simd_plan: FractalFBm loop plus 2x2 or 3x3 integer multiply per octave, in float32v, about 0.1 ns per octave over FBm (estimate). Built-in gradient kernel per dimension. 4D uses Aligned2, or quaternion pairs if anyone wants it; tiling follows PeriodMember since integer M maps a period onto itself.
master.continuity: C2 from Perlin's quintic, plus C2 Base Value with quintic. Hybrid Max Octave needs a fractional fade if it varies across a surface, which loses exactness only inside the fade.
master.params: Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Rule enum, Octaves, Max Octave (hybrid), First Octave, Gain, Weighted Strength (hybrid), Kind enum (FBm, Ridged), Base Value, Output Min/Max
master.risks: Exact only on vertices: between them the coarse mesh is still wrong by up to the tail. Regular zeros of octave 0 still imprint a lattice, reduced by Base Value. Float rounding of x_i far from the origin eats exactness at large coordinates, about 1e5 features. Only for gradient kernels; a warped source breaks it. 3D octrees get no rotation.

fractal-forecast.look: Plain ramp: left of the window, soft grey blobs with no detail; across it they sharpen until the right side is a crisp fractal coastline, with the same shapes in the same places. Frames at gain 0.7, t 1.5: at Detail 1 wide soft smudges, at Detail 2 and 3 the same places tighten, at 5 and 8 fine islands, and each frame matches the previous one in place. Below it the truncated threshold row at Detail 1 shows a few small hard blobs, clearly less area than Detail 8. Relief with Floor and Perlin Detail: smooth low-detail beaches and shallow plains sit next to rough islets, with a flat sea, reading like a terrain with a focus field. 3D at Detail 3: ordinary smooth caves, nothing special to see. In the ramp's hillshade I saw a faint vertical line where Detail crosses an octave.
