master.one_liner: A fractal that evaluates only the first k octaves and outputs the exact expected value of what the full fractal would do at that point, so masks, sea level and ridges keep their area and height at every LOD instead of drifting when octaves are dropped.
master.look: Coverage at low Detail is a soft mask that matches a box filtered image of the full thresholded fractal: forests and coasts look the same size from far away, and detail sharpens in place when Detail rises. Floor keeps coarse terrain from sinking or rising at the shoreline. With Detail from a distance field, near lanes are crisp and far lanes soft and cheap, inside one tree.
master.algorithm:
F = S + R. S = sum over evaluated octaves A_i n_i(p), R = the tail. n_i = Source(seed+i, p*lac^i) with known std sigma. Tail variance comes from a prefix table V_i = sum_{j>=i} A_j^2 sigma^2 computed when Gain, Octaves or sigma are set.
Gen:
  D = Detail(p), hybrid, in [0,N]
  S = 0
  for i in 0..N-1: m = D > i; if !AnyMask(m) break; w = clamp(D-i,0,1); S += w*A_i*n_i
  i0 = floor(D), f = D - i0
  s = sqrt( (1-f*f)*A_i0^2*sigma^2 + V_(i0+1) + Soft^2 )
Then, treating R as N(0,s^2), which is exact when n_i is ExactGaussianNoise:
  Coverage(t): P(F>t) = Phi(z), z = (S-t)/s
  Floor(t): E[max(F,t)] = t + s*( phi(z) + z*Phi(z) )     // sea level, water table
  Abs: E|F| = s*sqrt(2/pi)*exp(-S^2/(2 s^2)) + S*(2*Phi(S/s)-1)     // billow and ridge octave, whose truncated mean is otherwise biased
  Upper, Lower: S +- Z*s
  Expected: S. Sigma: s.
Phi from A&S 7.1.26 as in the ExactGaussianNoise entry, phi = exp(-z^2/2)/sqrt(2 pi).
master.why_new: Hard made easy. The bug it fixes: thresholding a truncated fractal changes the area and hardens the edge. With 64 percent of the variance kept (std 0.8), a one sigma threshold covers 10.6 percent instead of 15.9, so a third of a distant forest vanishes and pops back at the next LOD. By my arithmetic the mean drift is small at gain 0.5 once 2 octaves are in, and about a third at gain 0.7 with a 1.5 sigma threshold and 2 octaves (4.3 against 6.7 percent), so the case is strongest at high gain, rare classes and very coarse LODs; the soft edge helps at any gain. Nearest: SuperSample (brute force footprint, many taps), IsoFocusFractal (octaves only near a level, for a look), FractalSpectrum (moves the band, keeps total variance, no conditional output), FBm plus a Remap, which works by hand for one fixed LOD but has no per lane cutoff, needs the tail std worked out, and cannot do Floor or Abs. Evidence read: Godot Voxel Tools documents popping on LOD change and uses a screen dither fade as a workaround; a search found no write-up of keeping coarse and fine noise consistent. Proland keeps coarse and fine consistent only by upsample plus stored residual, which is not pointwise. FN2 issue 16 asks to reason about distributions.
master.simd_plan: FBm loop with a batch level break, then one sqrt, one exp and a polynomial. Cost is octaves actually needed times Source plus about 2 ns (estimate). Dimension agnostic GenT, so 2D, 3D, 4D and tiling follow the Source. Zooming out reduces cost, which an ordinary fixed octave fractal cannot do.
master.continuity: C1 in S and s while s > 0, since Phi and phi are smooth; Soft keeps s positive at full Detail. C0 in Detail through the fractional octave weight, whose variance term is matched so coverage stays continuous. Hard edge only if Soft is set to 0 at D = N.
master.params: Source, Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain, Source Std (float), Mean (float), Detail (hybrid), Level t (hybrid), Output enum (Expected, Coverage, Floor, Abs, Upper, Lower, Sigma), Z, Softness, Output Min/Max
master.risks: Exact only for Gaussian octaves. Perlin octaves are bounded and kurtosis differs, so tails will be a little off, and a warped Source breaks independence between octaves. Weighted fractals have amplitude that depends on S, so the tail table no longer applies; out of scope here. The expectation is over the tail, so a coarse mask is a smooth average, not a preview of each small island.
